Also in this pass, from the same review: a revoke is stamped `GREATEST(at, issued_at)` so the `revoked_at >= issued_at` check never blocks revoking a leaked link under clock skew (the check stays); the unique-violation on the one-live-token index (`quote_token_live`) from a concurrent issue answers `TokenError::Busy` instead of `Database`; `LinkSalt`'s `Debug` is redacted; `LinkToken` equality compares SHA-256 hashes, not the token text; and the property test's always-true "no salt" assertion is replaced by a zero-salt guess and the stored salt under another secret. Tested by `a_revoke_stamped_before_the_issue_still_revokes`, `a_concurrent_issue_that_loses_the_race_answers_busy`, `weak_secrets_are_refused_and_nothing_secret_is_printed` and `secret_and_job_alone_never_reproduce_a_token`. Reason: re-deriving after a rotation would orphan every reference to a stored ID, and pinning plus per-version keys keeps replay exact (CARD-017).
- **D-840** Question (plan change, October 30, 2026; T024 QUEUED after its second attempt): why did T024's second attempt fail the runner's path check, and how does T024 own a test for its carrier-restricted word list? Finding: T024 owns `app/catalog/src/restricted_words.rs` (the CARD-010 list, D-492) but owned no test file for it in the `catalog` crate. The crate layout puts in-crate tests under `src/tests/`, one file per task, each declared by one `mod` line in the shared `src/tests/mod.rs` (`docs/architecture.md:109`, D-481), so the worker on attempt 2 (branch `claude/task/T024-ai-adapter-a2`, head 36cd224b197edd93454fcdae897572e36d3d3841) wrote `app/catalog/src/tests/restricted_words.rs`, and `runner/verify.py` `check_paths` failed the attempt with "app/catalog/src/tests/restricted_words.rs: not owned by T024" (attempts 2 of 3; attempt 1, PR #142, failed earlier on an unrelated `Cargo.toml` update conflict). A task that owns a source file in a crate must be able to own its in-crate test: a plan gap, not the worker's fault. Kind: conflict. No other task owns `app/catalog/src/tests/restricted_words.rs` (T021 owns `app/catalog/src/tests/loader.rs`, T177 owns `app/catalog/src/tests/question_bank_load.rs`, and `app/catalog/src/tests/mod.rs` is a shared path). T024 already owned 10 paths, the build-task limit (`scripts/validate_tasks.py:186`, `MAX_OWNS = 10`, D-485), and `budget.files` must equal the number of owned paths (`scripts/validate_tasks.py:394`), so the test file cannot simply be added. Dropping `app/ai/Cargo.toml` (a shared path) instead was tried and ruled out: rule V12 (`scripts/validate_tasks.py:653`, D-493) needs some task to own each crate's `Cargo.toml` as its creator, T024 is the only owner of `app/ai/Cargo.toml`, and without it the validator reports that T025 and T163 own `ai` files "but no task owns app/ai/Cargo.toml (V12)". Choice, the plan (a change to `kit/tasks.json`, T024's `owns` and `decisions`, and `kit/prompts/T024.md`, regenerated alone with `scripts/gen_prompts.py`'s own `derive_context`, because a full run recomputes the twin tasks' context budgets, D-520, as in D-677): `app/ai/src/api.rs` leaves T024's `owns`, and `app/catalog/src/tests/restricted_words.rs` is added after `app/catalog/src/restricted_words.rs`; `app/ai/Cargo.toml` stays owned, so V12 holds; the owned count stays 10 and `budget.files` is unchanged at 10. The regeneration also refreshes T024's derived `budget.context_pct` from 14 to 18 (under the 20 limit, `scripts/validate_tasks.py:190`); 18 is what `main`'s own T024 prompt already measures, because its reads (`docs/architecture.md` and the brains) grew after the 14 was stored, so the rise is not this change's. Nothing is lost: `app/ai/src/api.rs` is a shared path every task may edit to add its own public functions (`kit/tasks.json` `shared_paths`, `scripts/validate_tasks.py:153`, D-484), `runner/verify.py` `check_paths` accepts a path that is owned or shared, and the prompt's shared-paths line names each crate's `src/api.rs`, so T024 still creates and writes `app/ai/src/api.rs`, as it creates the shared `app/ai/src/lib.rs` (D-492). T024 lists this decision. If T024 reaches its attempt cap, `python3 -m runner --requeue T024 --plan-fix D-840 --reason "..."` gives it one more attempt, on Opus (D-677); attempt 2's branch was never pushed (the runner pushes only after the path check passes), so the next attempt starts fresh from `main` and writes the test file again. `kit/plan.lock` is rewritten. Reason: the test belongs beside the list it checks, at the path the worker already chose, and the swap keeps every validator limit and every crate's creator. Source: `docs/architecture.md:109`; `scripts/validate_tasks.py:153`; `scripts/validate_tasks.py:186`; `scripts/validate_tasks.py:394`; `scripts/validate_tasks.py:653`; `runner/verify.py` `check_paths`; D-481; D-484; D-485; D-492; D-493; D-520; D-583; D-677.
- **D-810** Question (T024, October 30, 2026): AI-023 retries a 429 only when it carries `retry-after`, alerts on a spend-limit 400 and AI-024 stores the provider's request ID, but `adapters`' `AiAdapter::create_message` (T176) returns only the status of an error and the response body of a success, and the stand-in picks its fault modes from an `x-stand-in-fault` header the client cannot send; how does `ai` meet AI-023 and TD-AI-14? Choice: `ai` defines its own `Transport` trait (one POST to an allowed `Endpoint`, returning a `Reply` or a `Fault` carrying status, `retry-after` and a spend-limit flag), so the retry, timeout and alert rules are one code path. `AdapterTransport` wraps the adapter client: a 429 through it counts as having no `retry-after` and any 400 as a possible spend limit, both failing toward the owner alert and no retry (the stricter reading), and the request ID stored is the reply's message `id`. TD-AI-14's fault modes run in `app/ai/src/tests/adapter_calls.rs` on a scripted transport that plays the stand-in's `FAULTS` table under Tokio's paused clock, and one test reaches the real stand-in over HTTP through `StandInAi`. A plan gap for the runner: the Phase 2 real client (or a harness change to `app/adapters/src/ai.rs`) should return the `retry-after` and `request-id` headers and the error type so `AdapterTransport` can stop assuming the worst. Each call (retries included) must end within the timeout setting, so a `retry-after` longer than the time left ends the call. The idempotency key is derived from the AI job code and the subject record, so two AI jobs on one record never share a key (D-814). The other plan gaps T024 found against the stand-in and the API (the schema keywords, the stand-in's non-catalog trades) are in D-812. Source: `docs/spec/ai.md:27`, `docs/spec/ai.md:28`, `app/adapters/src/ai.rs:24`, `stand_ins/ai.py:9`.
- **D-811** Question (T024, October 30, 2026): AI-021 names a length cap and a global daily AI-call cap, and AI-023 a 20-second timeout, without the cap numbers; what are they? Choice: settings `ASKHAVA_AI_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` (default 20, 1 to 120), `ASKHAVA_AI_DAILY_CAP` (default 2,000 calls per Arizona day, about 40 times the pilot's expected volume, 1 to 1,000,000) and `ASKHAVA_AI_MODEL` (default `claude-haiku-5-5`, AI-024). Length caps in code by kind of text: a reworded question or follow-up 320 characters (two text segments), a job card 1,200, a project file 4,000. Reaching the daily cap records a `daily_cap` row in `ai.call_stat` and raises the `ai.daily_cap` alert once that day; key and spend alerts (`ai.key_rejected`, `ai.spend_limit`) are likewise raised once a day per kind, so a broken key does not flood Casey. All are High alerts. The day is counted with the database clock in Arizona time. Source: `docs/spec/ai.md:25`, `docs/spec/ai.md:27`, `docs/brains/ai-intake.md:166`.
- **D-812** Question (T024, October 30, 2026): AI-022 says the request's `output_config` sends `schemas/intake_reading.json` and a test fails on any difference, but `docs/brains/ai-intake.md` section 2 says the Messages API refuses `minimum` and `maximum` in a structured-output schema with a 400, and the file holds both on the two confidences. Choice: the spec wins on what: `output_config.format.schema` is the file exactly as committed, and the 0-to-1 range is also checked in code (`parse_reading`). Flagged for the runner and the Phase 2 real-AI task: if the real API refuses the keywords, the fix is a logged plan change to the schema file (drop the two keywords, keep the code check), never a silent strip in the request. Also noted: the stand-in's trade list (`plumbing`, `heating_ac`, ...) and its job type equal to the trade are not catalog codes, so every stand-in reading is discarded by the AI-005 catalog check; T167's stand-in should return catalog category codes and job types. The adapter-side gaps (no `retry-after` or `request-id` headers, no stand-in fault header from the client) are in D-810; both entries are runner follow-ups for the Phase 2 real-AI task. Source: `docs/spec/ai.md:26`, `docs/brains/ai-intake.md:26`, `stand_ins/ai.py:27`.
- **D-813** Question (T024, October 30, 2026): what is on CARD-010's carrier-restricted list, and how does it match? Choice: `app/catalog/src/restricted_words.rs`, read through `catalog::api` (`RESTRICTED_WORDS`, `restricted_match`): about 80 English and Spanish words and phrases over the SHAFT categories plus cannabis and other drugs, matched as whole words in any case, the hit naming the entry only. Words that are everyday trade words are left off so a card or question about real work is not cut: "weed", "joint", "pot", "crack", "gun" (nail and caulk guns), "pistol" and "pistola" (spray and heat guns), "wine" and "vino" (wine fridges). Slurs are not written into the source; the hate entries are named groups and slogans, and a later list change is a decision entry. Source: `docs/spec/job-cards.md:14`, `docs/brains/sms-compliance.md:85`.
- **D-814** Question (T024 review, October 30, 2026): AI-021's screen ran on the raw AI text, so a zero-width or soft hyphen (`s\u200Bex`), fullwidth letters or an ideographic full stop (`evil。com`) hid a restricted word or a domain, and a link with a path or query (`evil.com/pay`, `bit.ly/abc`, `evil.com?ref=1`) was missed; and `missing_info` was AI-written text with no screen and no item limit. Choice: `screen_text` first normalizes as `privacy`'s scrubber does (NFKC through the already-approved `unicode-normalization` crate, D-491; Unicode format characters dropped; U+3002 written `.`), screens that copy and returns it, so what was checked is what is sent; `privacy` does not export its normalizer, so `ai` keeps the same Cf list beside its own. A word is a link when any piece of it, cut at `/`, `?`, `#`, `:`, `@` or `,`, is a bare domain. `missing_info` holds at most 8 items (more discards the reading, AI-005), each item passes `screen_text` (an item that fails is dropped), and it is for records and question choice only: never sent to a person or put into a template (`app/ai/CLAUDE.md`). `Transport::post` takes the AI job code, and `AdapterTransport` derives the idempotency key from the job and the subject (SEC-018, D-810). Source: `docs/spec/ai.md:25`, `docs/spec/ai.md:9`, `docs/spec/job-cards.md:14`.
- **D-820** Question (T018, October 30, 2026): how are Twilio, Stripe, Resend and Lob webhooks checked "in the adapter before any module sees them" with "403 and a log line on failure" (SEC-016, SEC-039, SEC-051), when `adapters` is layer 1 with no web framework and the Rust checklist keeps HTTP status codes in `server` (`docs/brains/rust-production.md` R3)? Choice: `app/adapters/src/signatures.rs` holds one pure check, `verify_webhook(vendor, secret, Delivery { url, body, headers }, now)` (D-822), taking the raw body, the request headers, the secret and the time (unix seconds, so `adapters` takes no clock crate): Twilio base64 HMAC-SHA1 over the full URL plus the sorted, decoded form fields; Stripe hex HMAC-SHA256 over `<t>.<body>` against any `v1` (a secret roll sends several); Svix base64 HMAC-SHA256 under the decoded `whsec_` key over `<id>.<timestamp>.<body>`; Lob hex HMAC-SHA256 over `<timestamp>.<body>` (the formats `stand_ins/` signs with). MACs are compared with `Mac::verify_slice` (constant time); a timestamp more than 300 seconds from now either way is `Stale` (300 accepted, 301 refused, TD-SEC-03), checked after the MAC so a forgery always reads `Forged`. Only it builds a `VerifiedWebhook` (private fields; `Debug` shows vendor and event key, never the body, PRIV-016), so a module handler that takes one cannot run on an unchecked body; its `event_key()` is the Stripe or Lob body `id` or the `svix-id`, and a signed delivery without one is refused (`NoEventId`), while Twilio's module builds its own (MessageSid, MessageStatus) or (CallSid, step) key from `params()` (SEC-017, SEC-039). The adapter's one concession to R3 is `refuse(vendor, error) -> u16`: it writes the single `webhook refused` warn line with the vendor and reason codes and returns `REJECTED_STATUS` (403) as a plain number, no HTTP type, which the module's route turns into its response; the line is written once there, at the handling point (R5). The Stripe source check, `check_webhook_source(mode, client, stand_in_host)`, takes the address `core::api::ClientIpPolicy::client_ip` gives (SEC-040), canonicalises an IPv4-mapped IPv6 address, and allows in sandbox and live only the addresses of `app/adapters/data/stripe_webhook_ips.json`, Stripe's `ips_webhooks.json` copied verbatim on October 30, 2026 (15 addresses) so the nightly-main comparison can diff it byte for byte, compiled in with `include_str!` and never fetched; an unreadable copy gives an empty list, so every address is refused (fails closed). In stand-in mode only the stand-in's host passes (SEC-049, D-492). `adapters` now names `base64`, `sha1` and `tracing`, and `askhava-security` names `hmac` and `sha1` for its signing helpers: no new library, all are pinned in `[workspace.dependencies]` and listed in `kit/allowed_crates.txt`. Wiring the routes (`messaging`, `payments`, `calls`) and the `ReleaseProof` cases of TD-SEC-18 and TD-SEC-27 stay with the tasks that own those modules; TD-SEC-31 owns the route's address cases. Reason: a pure check with a proof type keeps the rule in one place for every module, and the vendors' own algorithms are matched to the stand-ins so the same code serves stand-in, sandbox and live (D-453).
- **D-821** Question (T018, October 30, 2026): the task prompt's size budget is 5 files and 400 changed lines; the change is 13 files and about 1,050 lines. Why? Reason: splitting the vendors across tasks would leave some webhooks unchecked, and SEC-039 asks for all four before any module sees them.
- **D-822** Question (T018, October 30, 2026): `tests/integration/tests/architecture.rs` (`check_payments_adapter`, D-595) fails any file outside `payments`, `adapters` and `server`, test crates included, that imports from `askhava_adapters` an item whose name contains `stripe` or is `payments`, while T018 must prove the Stripe signature and source checks from `tests/security/tests/` (TD-SEC-03, TD-SEC-27); the first draft's `verify_stripe`, `check_stripe_source` and `stripe_webhook_ips` failed it. Which gives way? - **D-841** Question (T025, October 30, 2026): how does AI-008's gate decide, per call, whether the live app may call the AI, and where do the records it reads live? Choice: `ai::api::ai_mode(db, env)` returns `AiMode::Ai` outside `Environment::Live` (build, `Ci` and the Railway test project run on fake data, D-040), and in live only when the newest `ai.provider_terms` row has a `zero_retention_signed_on` on or before today in Arizona (an older row's date does not count, so a newer row without one, or with a future date, keeps or closes the gate), or the newest `ai.switch_history` row is on and nothing is `Missing`; otherwise `AiMode::KeywordOnly`. `Missing` is checked in order: no terms row, terms not saying API inputs are not used for training, no flagged-content retention period, no Console spend limit or one above 3 times the expected monthly cost (`spend_limit_cents <= 3 * expected_monthly_cents` on the newest row), and the `ai.privacy_policy_version` in force today (newest `effective_on` not after today) lacking the AI-018 sentence. The same check runs on every call, not only when the switch first turns on, so a policy version that drops the sentence, or a newer incomplete terms row, closes the gate the day it takes effect (AI-008's "only on a day the privacy policy carries the matching AI-018 wording"). `ai::api::set_ai_switch(db, on, owner)` refuses on with `SwitchError::Refused(Missing)`, always allows off, and writes the history row and an `ops` audit row (`ai.switch_on` or `ai.switch_off`) in one transaction. `ai::api::read_intake` now takes the `Environment` and runs the gate first; with it closed it returns `AiOff::SwitchOff` without calling the adapter or writing an `ai.call_stat` row, and the caller runs the keyword-only path (keyword rules, the fixed question bank, cards from fields). The ungated `service::read_intake` stays crate-private. The four tables are in migration `0041_ai_provider_terms.sql`, append-only for the app role; the owner enters terms rows and policy versions (the policy text is T112's, D-491), and the owner-portal form that writes them belongs to the portal task, so until then they are entered by SQL. Once zero retention is signed the gate checks no privacy-policy version, on purpose: AI-008 gates only the period before the agreement, and the after-agreement AI-018 sentence is the policy text's (T112, TERMS-016), not a condition of the call. Source: `docs/spec/ai.md:12`; D-412, D-418, D-492.
- **D-842** Question (T025, October 30, 2026): TD-AI-04 needs `ai.reading` to have no text column, AI-013 wants trade, job type and flags written off-database, and `ops::api::StreamEvent::AiReading` takes fields as `&'static str` pairs that must each be a code name (D-734), while the trade and job type are runtime catalog values and a job-type name such as "evaporative (swamp) cooler repair" is not a code name; what is stored where? Choice: `ai.reading` holds the reading's ID, time, subject, both confidences and the emergency, urgent, major and Spanish flags (no text, JSON, array or bytea column); the trade and job type go only to the off-database stream, queued by `service::write_reading` in the same transaction as the call record. Each catalog value is written as a code name by `service::code_of` (lower-case letters and digits, each other run one `_`: `leak_repair`, `evaporative_swamp_cooler_repair`) and turned into a `&'static str` by `service::interned`, which keeps one leaked copy per distinct value; only values that passed the AI-005 catalog check reach it, so its size is bounded by the catalog. A field that still is not a code name is left out rather than failing the call record. Rejected: a dictionary table of codes in `ai` (more schema for no gain) and joining `catalog.job_type` for IDs (Arch 4 rule 3 forbids naming another module's schema). Proposal for a later `ops` change: let `StreamEvent::AiReading` take `&'a str` values, which would remove the interning. Weekly counts per trade are therefore not available from the database; AI-014 needs none. Source: `docs/spec/ai.md:17`; `docs/spec/privacy.md:33`; D-734.
- **D-843** Question (T025, October 30, 2026): what does AI-014's weekly summary take from `ai`, and the task's size budget is 4 files and 300 changed lines while the change is about 655 lines over the four owned files plus shared paths; why? Choice: `ai::api::weekly_counts(db)` returns `WeeklyCounts` for the 7 days before now, numbers only and built by code: AI calls (daily-cap refusals excluded), calls that ended without a reading, readings, emergency readings and Spanish readings; the `ops` weekly digest (a later task) reads it, and no AI call builds any part of the summary. - **D-851** Question (T179, October 30, 2026): JOB-024 says a job number texted to a homeowner is never reused, and TD-JOB-06 adds "including after a restore"; a PostgreSQL sequence or counter rolls back with the rest of the database on a restore, and `ops`' off-database stream carries record IDs and code names only, not the number; how is a number kept unique across a restore? Choice: every job gets its number in `create`'s transaction from the one-row counter `jobs.job_number_next` (numbers from 1001, so a texted number is never a short count, matching the spec's "CONFIRM 1042" examples); `jobs.job_number` holds it with the number as primary key and is append-only for the app role, so within one database a number is never issued twice, even for a cancelled job or after a lowered counter (the create then fails). A counter row rather than a sequence keeps numbering gap-free and lets the floor be raised by the app role with a plain `UPDATE`. After a restore, the replay (T110, OPS-015, which already reads Twilio's and the email provider's sent logs, OPS-017) calls `jobs::api::raise_number_floor(db, highest_texted)` with the highest job number those records show before the app takes new jobs; the counter only moves up (`GREATEST`). Rejected: putting the number in the off-database stream (an `ops` change outside this task, and the vendors' sent logs are exactly the record of what was texted), and a time-based number (long and still not collision-free). The replay keeping a re-created job's original number is T110's. `tests/integration/tests/job_numbers.rs` proves the restore case by rolling the counter back as a restore would, showing the next number would repeat a texted one, then raising the floor. Source: `docs/spec/lifecycle.md:28`; `docs/test-design.md:429`; D-092.
- **D-852** Question (T179, October 30, 2026): TD-SEC-12 asks for a source scan that fails on a `_ =>` arm, `matches!` or `if let` on a status enum outside its module's helpers, and `scripts/check_rust_rules.py` (D-590) already is that scan with its own pytest cases; what does the Rust test add? Choice: `tests/security/tests/status_enums.rs` runs the same script (no second scanner to drift) over the repository and over a scratch tree under `CARGO_TARGET_TMPDIR`, where a clean probe status module passes and each planted shape fails with a SEC-031 message: `_ =>`, `matches!` and `if let` outside the module, and `_ =>` and `matches!` in `status.rs` outside the enum's `impl`. It also checks that every `status.rs` under `app/` denies `clippy::wildcard_enum_match_arm` and that no first-party file (vendor adapters excepted) declares a `status` field as `String` or `&str`. The planted code is laid out as `cargo fmt` writes it, since the scan reads arms line by line; a one-line `match s { X::A => 1, _ => 2 }` is not caught, which `cargo fmt --check` makes unreachable on `main`. Proposal, not a rule here: the scan could join lines inside a `match` body to lose that dependence on formatting. Source: `docs/spec/security.md:35`; `docs/test-design.md:587`; D-453, D-488, D-590.

- **D-846** Question (T028, October 30, 2026): TXT-009 says "No text is sent to a past customer unless they write first", but `messaging` (layer 3) cannot read `jobs` or `intake` (layer 4 and above) to learn whether a request is closed, and the inbox that would hold her last text is a later task's. Choice: every `enqueue` takes a `Relation` (`Business`, `OpenRequest`, or `PastCustomer { closed_at, last_inbound }`) from the caller, who knows the job; a past customer is texted only when `last_inbound` is strictly after `closed_at` (a text at the very instant of the close does not count), and a refused text writes no row. `send` checks it again for a homeowner (`To::Homeowner` carries her `Relation` as of the send), so a text queued while her request was open but sent after it closed is refused and stays queued (D-849). When the inbox task lands, it should supply `last_inbound` from `messaging`'s own records rather than the caller. Reason: TXT-009, `docs/architecture.md` section 4 layer rule, `docs/brains/sms-compliance.md` section 2.
- **D-847** Question (T028, October 30, 2026): how does a resend carry the same key when `adapters::api::IdempotencyKey` has a private field and is built only by `derive` (SEC-018), so a stored key string cannot be turned back into one? Choice: `messaging.outbox` stores the IDs the key is derived from (`template_id`, `recipient_id`, `subject_ids`) beside the key itself (unique, the dedupe); `send` re-derives the key from them on every attempt, so the key always follows from what the text identifies and holds no personal data (TXT-011, R13); the subject IDs are sorted before hashing, so the order a caller lists them in does not change the key (review finding). `send` claims the row (`status` `sending`, `attempts + 1`) in one statement, calls the carrier with no transaction open, and marks `sent` only if still `sending`; a carrier error or a killed worker leaves it `sending` for a later resend, and a `sent` row is never handed to the carrier again. Known limit: if `ID_SECRET` changes between an attempt and its resend, the resend's key differs, so the carrier would not dedupe it; D-819 already keeps the old secret while anything made under it may be rebuilt, and the retry task (TXT-014, TXT-015) should finish unsent rows before a rotation. Two cases reach the carrier twice with the same key and rely on it to deliver once: a worker killed after the carrier accepted but before the mark, whose resend is TD-TXT-04's case, and concurrent sends of one row by two workers (no lease is added here). Both rest on Twilio honouring a repeated `Idempotency-Key` on a message create within the retry window (the stand-in's `IdempotencyStore` does), which is **verify with vendor** before Gate C; if it does not, the killed-worker resend can deliver twice and needs a different guard (for example looking the message up by the key before resending), and if it does not, the retry task adds a lease (owner and expiry on the claim, the finish fenced by owner, R12) before any live send. No refusal or failure in `send` makes a row terminal: a TXT-009 or recipient-kind refusal leaves it `queued`, a failed vault read or carrier call leaves it `sending`, and the retry task (TXT-014, TXT-015) decides when an unsent row is given up. Reason: TXT-011, SEC-018, `docs/brains/rust-production.md` R11, R13.
- **D-848** Question (T028, October 30, 2026): the prompt's size budget is 5 files and 350 changed lines; the five owned files hold about 625 lines (the test file about 230 after rustfmt, the two Rust files about 180 each, the migration 38), plus the required shared paths (`lib.rs`, `api.rs`, two `Cargo.toml`s, `Cargo.lock`, eight `.sqlx/` files, `CLAUDE.md`, `docs/architecture.md`, this file). Why? Choice: accept the overrun and record it, as D-821 did: the outbox and the sender directory are two features with their own queries, errors and tests, and every public function carries the `///` documentation `docs/code-docs.md` requires. Reason: BUILD_BRIEF.md section 12.
- **D-849** Question (T028, October 30, 2026): who gives `send` the number to text? The review asked that it be read from the vault for the row's recipient rather than taken as plaintext from the caller. Choice: `send` takes `To::Homeowner { vault, relation }` or `To::Business(phone)`. For a homeowner the row's `recipient_id` is her vault contact and `send` reads only her phone with `privacy::api::read_contact` under `(Reader::Messaging, Purpose::Send)`, audited, on the bare connection after the claim; a failed read is `OutboxError::Recipient` and the row stays unsent. A business main or staff phone is not vault data (it lives in `businesses`, layer 4, which `messaging` may not read), so the caller passes it. Each row stores `recipient_kind` (`homeowner` or `business`, from the `Relation` given at enqueue), and `send` claims it only when `To` names the same kind, else `OutboxError::RecipientKind` with the row untouched, so a homeowner's row can never be sent as `To::Business` and skip the vault read and the TXT-009 check (review finding). Reason: PRIV-003, PRIV-004, `docs/architecture.md` section 4 layer rule; review finding on T028.
- **D-850** Question (T028, October 30, 2026): `messaging.outbox.body` holds the rendered text, which may carry a bearer quote or action link (SEC-037); should it be sealed? Choice: keep it plaintext only while the row is unsent and set it to NULL when the send is marked (a table check makes a sent row's body NULL), so a link outlives its send only in the carrier's own log. Not sealed: the vault seals contact fields only, texts to anyone but the homeowner never hold her name, address or phone (TXT-036), and no sign-in or pick code is ever queued here (codes go through Verify, TD-TXT-19). The retry task should keep unsent rows short-lived. Reason: SEC-037, PRIV-002, `docs/brains/postgres-operations.md` P12; review finding on T028.
- **D-861** Question (T178, October 31, 2026): how are Twilio's inbound texts and status callbacks de-duplicated (TXT-012) and where is each text's delivery status (TXT-013) kept, given that a status callback can arrive before `send` has stored the provider SID (a worker killed after the carrier accepted, TD-TXT-04) and callbacks can arrive out of order? Choice: `messaging.webhook_event` in the shape `core::api::Dedupe` documents, written in the transaction of the effect (a savepoint inside a caller's own transaction): an inbound text is keyed on its MessageSid (`twilio_inbound`), a status callback on (MessageSid, MessageStatus) (`twilio_status`, SEC-039); `messaging.inbox` gets one row per first inbound delivery, unique on the MessageSid, holding no phone or body yet (the scrubbed text and flags are the inbound-routing task's). Each first status callback is appended to `messaging.delivery_event` keyed by provider SID, not by outbox row, so an early callback is kept and joins its row once the send is marked; `delivery_status` folds them by rank (queued, sending, sent, then the final delivered, undelivered or failed) so a late earlier status never moves a text back, and between two final ones the later wins. Twilio's `accepted` and `scheduled` read as queued, `read` as delivered, `canceled` as failed; a status that is not an outbound text's (`received`, `receiving`) is ignored without a record, so the route still answers 200. The error code is stored for the retry and suppression tasks (TXT-014, TXT-015, CON-014's 21610); nothing here retries or suppresses. A missing or ill-shaped MessageSid, status or error code is `InboxError::BadWebhook` and records nothing. The webhook routes themselves (`server`) are not added here: no route for them exists yet and the routing task wires them with `verify_webhook`. Rejected: a `delivery_status` column on `messaging.outbox` (an early callback would be lost and every callback would race the mark). Source: `docs/spec/messaging.md:16`, `docs/spec/messaging.md:17`; D-847.
- **D-862** Question (T178, October 31, 2026): the task's size budget is 5 files and 300 changed lines, and the owned files come to about 600 (the integration test about 260, `models.rs` about 160, `handlers.rs` about 120, `service.rs` 30, the migration 35), plus the shared paths (`lib.rs`, `api.rs`, `status.rs` holding `DeliveryStatus` (SEC-031), two `Cargo.toml`s for the `askhava-core` path dependency and the workspace `sha1` dev-dependency the signed test webhooks need, `Cargo.lock`, five `.sqlx/` files, `CLAUDE.md`, `docs/architecture.md`, this file); why? Source: `kit/tasks.json` (T178 budget); D-848.
- **D-863** Question (T178 review, October 31, 2026): `messaging.webhook_event`, `messaging.inbox` and `messaging.delivery_event` took `received_at` from the database's `now()`, so a test on the injected clock could not control or check it, unlike the pattern `app/core/src/webhooks.rs` documents (`received_at` bound as `$3`); and the early-callback case recorded only `queued`, which reads the same as an unsent row and so proved nothing. Choice: `receive_inbound` and `receive_status` take `now: Timestamp`, which the route (the routing task) takes from its injected `Clock`, and bind it as `received_at` on all three tables; migration 0043 (not yet on `main`) drops the three `DEFAULT now()`s so no insert can fall back to the database's clock. The integration test records `delivered` before the send is marked, checks the row still reads `queued`, then `delivered` once sent, and checks every row's `received_at` is the fake instant. The comment in `handlers.rs` now states the 200-answer rule as the routing task's contract, since no route exists yet (D-861). Source: `app/core/src/webhooks.rs:10`; D-861.
- **D-886** Question (plan change, October 31, 2026; T034 QUEUED after its second attempt): why did T034's second attempt fail the runner's path check, and how does T034 own the property test it wrote for its routing rules? Finding: T034 (`licensing-agency-rules`) owns `app/licensing/src/rules.rs` and two in-crate test files, `app/licensing/src/tests/agency_rules.rs` and `app/licensing/src/tests/scope_examples.rs`, but no property-test file. The crate layout puts in-crate unit and property tests under `src/tests/`, one file per task, each declared by one `mod` line in the shared `src/tests/mod.rs` (`docs/architecture.md:109`, D-481), so the worker on attempt 2 (started 2026-10-31T00:08:05Z, ended 00:28:08Z) wrote a property test at `app/licensing/src/tests/prop_rules.rs`, and `runner/verify.py` `check_paths` failed the attempt with "app/licensing/src/tests/prop_rules.rs: not owned by T034" (attempts 2 of 3; attempt 1, PR #151, failed earlier on an unrelated `Cargo.toml` update conflict). A property test of routing rules is a reasonable test for the worker to choose (T035 owns `app/licensing/src/tests/prop_handyman_never_gas.rs` for the same kind of check), so this is a plan gap, not the worker's fault, as in D-840. Kind: conflict. No other task owns `app/licensing/src/tests/prop_rules.rs` (T035 owns `app/licensing/src/tests/handyman.rs` and `app/licensing/src/tests/prop_handyman_never_gas.rs`, T037 owns `app/licensing/src/tests/license_lines.rs`, T153 owns `app/licensing/src/tests/class_map.rs` and `app/licensing/src/tests/class_limits.rs`, and `app/licensing/src/tests/mod.rs` is a shared path). T034 owned 8 paths, so a ninth stays under the build-task limit (`scripts/validate_tasks.py:186`, `MAX_OWNS = 10`, D-485), and `budget.files` must equal the number of owned paths (`scripts/validate_tasks.py:394`). Choice, the plan (a change to `kit/tasks.json`, T034's `owns`, `budget.files` and `decisions`, and `kit/prompts/T034.md`, regenerated alone with `scripts/gen_prompts.py`'s own `derive_context`, because a full run recomputes the twin tasks' context budgets, D-520, as in D-677 and D-840): `app/licensing/src/tests/prop_rules.rs` is added to T034's `owns` after `app/licensing/src/tests/scope_examples.rs`, `budget.files` goes from 8 to 9, and T034 lists this decision. The regeneration also refreshes T034's derived `budget.context_pct` from 13 to 19 (under the 20 limit, `scripts/validate_tasks.py:190`): `main`'s own T034 prompt already measured 18 (`scripts/gen_prompts.py --check` reported "stored 13%; regenerate to refresh" before this change), because its reads grew after the 13 was stored, and the one point more is this change's own (the new owned path, its test command and this decision's excerpt in the prompt). Attempt 2's branch was never pushed (the runner pushes only after the path check passes), so the next attempt starts fresh from `main` and writes the test file again. If T034 reaches its attempt cap, `python3 -m runner --requeue T034 --plan-fix D-886 --reason "..."` gives it one more attempt, on Opus (D-677). `kit/plan.lock` is rewritten. Reason: the property test belongs beside the rules it checks, at the path the worker already chose, and adding it keeps every validator limit. Source: `docs/architecture.md:109`; `scripts/validate_tasks.py:186`; `scripts/validate_tasks.py:190`; `scripts/validate_tasks.py:394`; `runner/verify.py` `check_paths`; D-481; D-485; D-520; D-677; D-840.
- **D-866** Question (T029, October 31, 2026): how does the app keep one suppression list, know whether the provider already sent the opt-out confirmation, and decide what still goes to a listed number (CON-008 to CON-010, CON-013, CON-015 to CON-017, CON-030, CON-035)? Choice: `messaging.suppression` holds each listed number as its blind-index digests under the existing `homeowner-phone` index key (one row per key version, as `sender_directory` does, PRIV-002, PRIV-024), and `messaging.optout_event` logs every opt-out and START with its channel, how it was detected (`word:<word>`, `phrase:<pattern ID>`, `provider`, `carrier:21610`, CON-036) and the time it took effect, append-only for `askhava_app` (CON-022). Whether the provider answered comes from the inbound webhook's `OptOutType` (`STOP` or `START`), which Twilio and the fake Twilio (T167) send when an Advanced Opt-Out keyword matched, so the app never re-implements the provider's matching to decide; the app queues `opt_out_confirmation` only when no `OptOutType=STOP` came, the number was not listed already (a repeat is logged but not confirmed again: "exactly one confirmation") and texting is not paused (`ops` switches `texting` or `all`; paused returns `email: true` for T094's email, CON-030). The 5-minute limit is enforced at send: `rules::may_send_to` lets only `opt_out_confirmation` within `CONFIRM_WITHIN` of the listing and `help_reply` (D-131) reach a listed number, so a confirmation held past 5 minutes never goes. A sole START or UNSTOP (or `OptOutType=START`) lifts the listing and returns `Resubscribed` (CON-015); "yes" and any other message return `Suppressed` and send nothing; an emergency flag raises a critical `messaging.opted_out_emergency` alert on the inbox row through `ops::api::raise_alert`, so `messaging` now depends on `ops`, which `kit/layers.json` allows (CON-017). Rejected: matching the provider's word rules in the app (any drift between Twilio's matching and ours would send two confirmations or none). Source: `docs/spec/consent.md:13`, `docs/spec/consent.md:34`, `docs/spec/consent.md:39`; D-130, D-131, D-372.
- **D-867** Question (T029, October 31, 2026): CON-035 says the app checks the list before every text, and CON-014 says a 21610 is never retried, but `service::send` (T028's file, not this task's) takes no vault for a business number and folds every carrier error into `OutboxError::Carrier`, losing the 21610 code. Choice: a new `messaging::api::send_checked(db, (secret, carrier, vault), id, (to, from), now)` reads the row's recipient and template, resolves the number (the vault for a homeowner, as `send` does; the given phone for a business), refuses a listed number with `OutboxError::Suppressed`, then calls `service::send` with the carrier wrapped in a watcher that notes a `Vendor { code: 21610 }` refusal; on one it lists the number (channel `carrier`) and marks the row `blocked` (body NULL) in one transaction and returns `OutboxError::Blocked`. Migration 0044 adds `blocked` to the outbox status check, and `models::claim` now claims only `queued` or `sending`, so a blocked row is never handed to the carrier again even through the raw `send`. `send` keeps its signature so T028's tests stand; every send task handler must call `send_checked` (the CLAUDE.md "Never break" list says so). Two follow-ups for later tasks: `delivery_status` (in `service.rs`) reads a `blocked` row as `Sending`, and a 21610 that arrives later on a status callback (the text was accepted, then failed) is stored in `messaging.delivery_event` but does not list the number yet; the retry task (T094) should list the number from it with `suppress(.., RevokeChannel::Carrier, ..)`. Source: `docs/spec/consent.md:18`, `docs/spec/consent.md:39`; D-849.
- **D-868** Question (T029, October 31, 2026): how does the detector read a message, and where do the word lists live, given D-020 keeps the Spanish list "in settings so words can be added" while D-493 requires the app's lists to equal `stand_ins/provider_optout.json`? Choice: `rules::detect_opt_out` lower-cases, folds Spanish accents (á, é, í, ó, ú, ü, ñ), drops apostrophes and turns every other non-letter, non-digit into a space; a sole-word opt-out is the whole folded message equal to a word, a phrase opt-out is a listed phrase on word boundaries; it runs on the scrubbed words (only `privacy` sees raw text, `docs/architecture.md` section 8), which keep these words. The lists are constants in `rules.rs`: `PROVIDER_OPT_OUT_WORDS` (the twelve CON-030 words, equal to the file), `APP_OPT_OUT_WORDS` ("opt out", an FCC word Twilio does not handle, so the app confirms it), `RESUBSCRIBE_WORDS` (start, unstop) and `OPT_OUT_PHRASES` (the fourteen CON-010 phrases, each with a pattern ID). A word added in settings alone would break D-493's equality and leave the provider and app answering differently, so adding a word is a code change made together with the provider file and the live Advanced Opt-Out; the brief's how (D-493, a test pins equality) wins over D-020's settings note. The caller passes `PROVIDER_OPT_OUT_WORDS` plus `APP_OPT_OUT_WORDS` to `privacy::api::InboundWords` so the reader's flag agrees. Source: `docs/spec/consent.md:12`, `docs/spec/consent.md:14`; D-020, D-493.
- **D-869** Question (T029, October 31, 2026): the task's size budget is 7 files and 500 changed lines; the change is about 1,100 lines in the owned files (`optout.rs` about 390, the integration test about 380, `rules.rs` about 190, `models.rs` about 160, the two unit tests about 260, the migration 42) plus the shared paths (`lib.rs`, `api.rs`, `tests/mod.rs`, `Cargo.toml` for the `askhava-ops` path dependency, `Cargo.lock`, a new `sqlx.toml` for jiff timestamps, eight `.sqlx/` files, `CLAUDE.md`, `docs/architecture.md`, this file, `docs/for-casey-review.md`); why? Choice: accept the overrun and record it, as D-821, D-848 and D-862 did: the goal covers detection, the list, the checked send, 21610 and four test-design entries, each case with its own test. Source: `kit/tasks.json` (T029 budget); D-862.
- **D-870** Question (T029 review, October 31, 2026): a fresh-eyes review of T029 found (1) a punctuated "Start." with no `OptOutType` re-subscribed in the app while the provider's block stayed, and `td_con_20_only_start_or_unstop_resubscribes` asserted that; (2) `messaging::api::send` stays public and skips the suppression check (CON-035); (3) two near-simultaneous opt-outs from one number could both read "not listed" and queue two confirmations; (4) `may_send_to` let any `opt_out_confirmation` row through in the 5-minute window, even one queued for an earlier listing; (6) an emergency flag on an opt-out from an already-listed number raised no CON-017 alert; and (7) D-867 names T094 as the follow-up owner for a 21610 that arrives on a status callback. Choice: (1) `rules::classify` re-subscribes only on `ProviderKeyword::Start` (`OptOutType=START`, the provider's own START or UNSTOP match), so the app's list and the provider's block always agree, as D-866 already takes "did the provider answer" from `OptOutType` rather than re-matching; `td_con_20_only_start_or_unstop_resubscribes` now expects `Other` for "Start.", "START" and "unstop" without `OptOutType` and `Resubscribe` with it, and the property test and `optout_flow.rs` pass the provider's keyword as the fake Twilio (T167) reports it. This is a spec-consistent correction of a wrong test, not a weakened one: CON-015 and CON-030 make START and UNSTOP the provider's re-subscribe words and CON-013 forbids any text before START, and the old expectation lifted the app's listing while Twilio still blocked the number (BUILD_BRIEF.md:69). (2) Declined within T029: `service.rs` is T028's file, and `tests/integration/tests/outbox.rs` (T028) and `inbox.rs` (T178) call `api::send` directly with a two-part `(secret, carrier)` argument and no vault or clock, so removing the export or moving the check into `service::send` would break those tasks' tests, which T029 may not change. The guard stays as D-867 set it: `models::claim` never claims a `blocked` row, the crate `CLAUDE.md` says every send goes through `send_checked`, and the task that writes the first send handler (T094's retry worker or the routing task) should make `service::send` crate-private once those tests move to `send_checked`. (3) `record` now reports whether its `INSERT .. ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` into `messaging.suppression` added rows; the second of two concurrent inserts waits on the first's uncommitted rows and adds none, so `on_inbound_text` treats it as already listed and queues no confirmation, and `suppress` returns "newly listed" the same way; `td_con_05_two_opt_outs_at_once_queue_one_confirmation` holds one opt-out's transaction open while a second runs, and fails if the check is removed. (4) `models::listing` returns the current listing's `since` and `event_id` (the earliest row), and `rules::may_send_to(listing, template, subject, now)` lets a confirmation through only if its outbox `subject_ids` hold that event (the confirmation is queued with the opt-out event as its subject), within `CONFIRM_WITHIN`; `td_con_05_only_the_current_listings_confirmation_goes` proves an earlier listing's confirmation is refused after START and a new opt-out. (6) `Outcome::OptedOut` gains `alert`, raised whenever an opt-out message carries the emergency flag, whether the number was listed before or is listed by this message: either way it can no longer be texted back, and CON-017's "a possible emergency from an opted-out number" is safest read to cover both. (7) Kept: T094 ("3 retries over 30 minutes, then email and portal, then call-back alert") is the task that reads failed delivery statuses to decide retries, so it is the right owner for listing a number from a callback 21610. Source: `docs/spec/consent.md:17`, `docs/spec/consent.md:19`, `docs/spec/consent.md:21`, `docs/spec/consent.md:34`, `docs/spec/consent.md:39`; D-866, D-867, BUILD_BRIEF.md:69.
- **D-871** Question (T032, October 31, 2026): JOB-010 to JOB-012 and TXT-042 send texts to the homeowner, but `jobs` holds no homeowner contact (it is `intake`'s, and `intake` sits above `jobs`), so how does a timer or the every-window-ended call send one? Choice: the move (or the call) queues a `core.task` event of kind `jobs.homeowner_text` in its own transaction, carrying only the job ID, the job's version, the template ID and the numbers the template needs (the job number; for TXT-042 `quoted` and `count`), run at the move's time (6 p.m. for JOB-010, D-030); its dedupe key `jobs.homeowner_text.<job>.<template>` queues each template at most once per job. The sender is `intake`'s handler (registered by the task that sends homeowner job texts): it finds the homeowner and her language, fills the quote-page link (`jobs::api::quote_token::issue`, never put in a payload, SEC-037), applies quiet hours (`messaging::api::decide`, QH-001, QH-006) and queues the outbox row. Until that handler is registered the event has none, which matters only once the worker runs live. The timeout texts are `JobStatus::timeout_text` (Open, No quotes yet, Quotes ready); the Intake close text is INT-019's task's, the confirm and payment returns are told by `picks`, and the Connected close sends nothing, so no review request (JOB-026, D-046). Source: `docs/architecture.md` section 4 rule 2 ("events go up"); `kit/layers.json` (`jobs` calls `messaging`, `catalog`, `ops` only).
- **D-872** Question (T032, October 31, 2026): T046's goal names `jobs::api::all_windows_ended(job, quoted, sent)`, but JOB-025 closes the job only when no choosable quote is left, which the two counts cannot tell (a failed pick's quote still counts as quoted, D-045); and TXT-042's "never after a pick or a close" must hold for a text held overnight by quiet hours. Choice: the entry point is `all_windows_ended(db, job, Windows { quoted, sent, choosable }, at)`: on a job not in Quotes ready it does nothing (`Guarded::MovedOn`); with `choosable` 0 it closes the job with the `closed_no_quote_left` note; otherwise it queues the one `all_quotes_in` text and the job waits under its 3-day timer. `picks` calls it again when a pick fails after every window has ended, so that job then closes; the text is never queued twice. The event carries the job's version and the sender calls `jobs::api::text_due(job, version)` before sending: after a pick or close the version has moved, so the text is dropped; a closing note's version is a final status's and stays due (QH-007's exception, D-461). The close is fenced on the loaded version and timer version; if the row changed under it (a restarted wait, D-807) it reloads once and retries while the job still awaits a pick, so a moved fence alone never loses the close. Each template's dedupe key is permanent: once queued, a text is never queued again for that job, even after its task is dropped as not due or dead-lettered; this is intended, since TXT-042 is "sent once per job" and a held text is delivered by the task's own retries and the sender's hold, not by a re-queue; a dead-lettered text is an `ops` alert, not a second send. T046 passes the three counts. Flag for the runner: `kit/prompts/T046.md:9` and T046's goal in `kit/tasks.json` still name the old `all_windows_ended(job, quoted, sent)` signature; both are locked or generated, so T032 does not edit them and the task graph's owner should update them to this one. Source: `docs/spec/lifecycle.md:29` (JOB-025), `docs/spec/messaging.md:46` (TXT-042), `kit/tasks.json` (T046 goal).

- **D-891** Question (harness plan change, October 31, 2026; stage C of two lanes, the part D-620 left out): why does a conflict between two tasks that finished close together cost a task one of its 3 attempts, and how is that stopped without guesswork? What happened on October 30: T024's attempt 1 (pull request #142) failed `update_conflict` in `Cargo.toml` and `docs/for-casey-review.md`, and T028's attempt 1 failed in `docs/architecture.md` and `docs/for-casey-review.md`; each retry then redid the task from a branch with `main` merged in or fresh from `main`. Finding: re-running the update merge on the two pushed branches (`claude/task/T024-ai-adapter` 0f5dbfe against `main` 6a92164, and `claude/task/T028-messaging-outbox` 2d4aa07 against `main` 8acf08c) shows every conflict was a pure insertion on both sides at the same place: one workspace dependency each (`askhava-ai`, `askhava-jobs`) after `askhava-privacy`, one review section each at the end of `docs/for-casey-review.md`, one bullet each in section 2 of `docs/architecture.md`. These are mechanical side effects of shared files (`kit/tasks.json` `shared_paths`), not defects in the work, and `runner/update_merge.py` resolved only `docs/decisions.md` and `kit/plan.lock`. Kind: conflict. `BUILD_BRIEF.md:224` ended "it never rebases and force-pushes, and a real conflict fails the attempt instead of being resolved by guesswork."; a conflict handed back to a worker without spending an attempt breaks that clause, and `docs/governance.md` section 4 forbids departing from a section 7 rule by a logged decision alone, so this plan change amends that line in place (one line, no cited line number moves): its end now reads "it never rebases and force-pushes, and a real conflict is never resolved by guesswork: the runner hands it to a worker on the same attempt (a resync, at most 2 per attempt), whose merge is reviewed again before it is pushed, and a further conflict fails the attempt (D-891)."; `kit/plan.lock` is rewritten. `BUILD_BRIEF.md:540` ("up to 3 attempts, Opus on the last one") is unchanged: a resync is not an attempt and never moves `attempts`. Choice, (1) the mechanical path widened (`runner/update_merge.py` step 4, `INSERT_ONLY`, `insertions_after_main`, `UpdateMerge._insertions`): a conflicting `docs/for-casey-review.md`, `docs/architecture.md` or `Cargo.toml` (also any `*/Cargo.toml`) is merged with `git merge-file -p --diff3 --marker-size=40` of branch, base and main, and resolved only when every conflict in it is a pure insertion: no base line between the markers (a side that changed or removed a line is a real conflict), both inserted blocks ending in a newline, and, when main's block opens a section (a Markdown heading or a TOML table header), the branch's block opening its own, so the branch's lines never move into main's new section. Both blocks are kept verbatim, main's first and the branch's after, the order `decisions_after_main` already uses, so the tree stays one deterministic function of the two commits and `reviewed_plus_main`, `update_merge_of` and `prepare_branch`'s merge accept exactly it. A resolved `Cargo.toml` must still parse with `tomllib`, which refuses a key both sides added (two tasks adding the same crate with different versions stays a conflict), and no line either side inserted may assign a dotted key (`dotted_key`: a `.` outside quotes before the first `=`, as in `serde.version = "1"`), because a branch's `serde.version` and main's `serde.features` parse into one dependency neither side wrote. No resolution is tried when the branch's, the base's or main's text of the file holds any line whose first word is one of the four 40-character conflict markers (40 `<`, `|`, `=` or `>`; `marker_shaped`, checked by `insertions_after_main` before it reads the merge), since such a line, a Markdown heading underlined with 40 `=` for one, would be read as git's own marker and the join corrupted; the file is then a real conflict and goes to the resync. A resolved `docs/architecture.md` must keep every locked section (`scripts/check_plan_lock.py` `LOCKED_SECTIONS`, sections 3 to 6) equal to the branch's or main's, so a resolution never writes locked text neither side had and never needs a lock it cannot vouch for; without the lock tool it stays a conflict. Other files (`Cargo.lock`, code) are never resolved: `Cargo.lock` is generated, and git already merges its independent hunks. Checked on the real branches: with this change both October 30 conflicts merge with no worker (trees a486b98 and 77acda2, main's lines first). Choice, (2) the worker resync (`runner/cycle.py` `_conflict_step`): a real conflict left after (1) no longer fails the attempt. While fewer than `RESYNC_LIMIT` (2) resyncs are recorded for the task's current attempt (`attempts + 1`), a pull request with auto-merge on is closed first with the `DROP_MARKER` comment and recorded in `runner_closed_prs` (exactly as D-584 and D-620 close one, so nothing unreviewed can merge while the task is away; a failed close keeps the task MERGE_PENDING with the reason, so any merge is judged), then the task goes to QUEUED with `attempts` unchanged, `resync` = {attempt, from (the reviewed head), main, paths, at} (also appended to `resyncs`, last 10), `last_failure` naming the paths, and the history entry closed with result `resync` (`RESYNC`); it is not a strike (no attempt ended). The task's own lane is freed by QUEUED like any failed attempt, so no new lease, lane or state machine was added: the next claim (`_next_step`, on any lane `lanes.compatible_ids` allows, with the usual lease, pacing, smoke and hand-off) sorts a task with `resync` first, `prepare_branch` (D-583) makes the local branch at origin's tip without `main` merged in, but only while that tip is still the resync's reviewed head and the branch's pull request was not merged or closed by anyone else (`_pr_end`), and still closes an open pull request whose auto-merge is on; the hand-off adds `resync` (the `resync_log` text: merge `main` in with a normal merge commit, resolve each conflict keeping both sides' intent, change nothing else, run the smoke test, commit, never redo the task) and a `branch_note` saying the branch is the reviewed work without `main`, and `backup-runner.yml` step 3c tells the session to pass it to the worker; with `RUNNER_WORKER_CMD` the same text is the worker's log. The worker runs on the attempt's own model (`attempt_model`, unchanged since `attempts` did not move); a docs-only model downgrade was not made, because `BUILD_BRIEF.md:244` names the task's model for every subagent and a resync that touches code would need it anyway. The hand-in then goes through `finish` unchanged: path check, model check, the fresh-eyes reviewer's evidence (step 4, over the whole diff against `main`), the review record (`reviewed_sha` = the merge, which drops the old `update_merges`), the branch push (a fast-forward of the reviewed head) and auto-merge for exactly that head; MERGE_PENDING follows as usual. `finish` removes `resync` whatever the outcome except a pause (`RETRY_AFTER_RESET`, `RETRY_LATER`, which resume it), `record_failure` removes it on any failure, and its history entry carries `resync: true` with the same attempt number. When the resync cannot start on the reviewed head (origin moved, the pull request was ended by someone, git failed), `_work` fails the attempt at once with the conflict and "the resync could not start on the reviewed head" rather than redo the task as if new, so the retry then follows D-583 exactly as before this change. A crashed or lease-expired resync re-runs for free like any crashed attempt (`release_expired` leaves `resync` set, and `attempts` never moved); when origin's tip already is the task's `reviewed_sha` (the session died after the resync's reviewed merge was pushed but before the release), `_work` (`_resync_gate`) clears `resync` under the live lease and the attempt goes on the normal path instead of failing. A conflict after `RESYNC_LIMIT` resyncs in the same attempt, a failed resync (tests red, a blocking review, an empty or off-path hand-in) and an update push that fails all fall to the existing rules (`_update_failed`, `record_failure`, a strike on a lane above 1 for `update_conflict`). `plan_since` (D-677) skips resync history entries, so a plan fix is still measured from the attempt's own start. `kit/state_schema.json` describes `resync` and `resyncs`; the chain step counts `resync` as a result that moved a task, so it refills. Loops: a resync record is only written from a real conflict on a reviewed head, at most `RESYNC_LIMIT` per attempt number, and every resync worker's hand-in either reaches MERGE_PENDING through review or ends the attempt; nothing reaches MERGE_PENDING without a review record. Design difference from the brief's sketch: the sketch kept the task on a `RESYNC` step and ran the worker "on that lane"; going through QUEUED reuses the claim, lease, lane, pacing, `prepare_branch`, hand-off, `--after` and review record unchanged, at the cost that the resync may be picked up on another free lane (its owned paths and stage rules still apply). One existing test changes, which `BUILD_BRIEF.md:69` allows only through a logged decision, so it is named here: `test_drill_a_real_conflict_fails_the_attempt_and_the_retry_continues_the_branch` in `tests/test_runner_two_lanes.py` pinned the behaviour this change replaces and is now `test_drill_a_real_conflict_is_resynced_on_the_same_attempt_and_reviewed_again`. New tests: `tests/test_runner_two_lanes.py` (the limit, a resync that cannot start, a resync whose close fails, a failed resync, the hand-off), `tests/test_runner_update_merge.py` (real git: `insertions_after_main`, T024's Cargo.toml and review insertions, a doubled Cargo key and an edited line, an insertion into a locked architecture section, the resync branch at the reviewed head, auto-merge closed first, each of the four marker-shaped lines on each side, a 40-`=` underline end to end through `UpdateMerge.commit` and `is_update_merge`, dotted keys from both sides), and the resync that crashed after its reviewed push in `tests/test_runner_two_lanes.py`. Documented in `docs/architecture.md` section 7 and `docs/for-casey-review.md`. Reason: an attempt should be spent on the task's own failures, not on another task's timing; the runner still resolves only what is provably mechanical, and everything else is done by a worker and reviewed before it can merge. First written as D-890; renumbered D-891 when T030 took D-890 on `main` first. Source: `BUILD_BRIEF.md:69`; `BUILD_BRIEF.md:224`; `BUILD_BRIEF.md:244`; `BUILD_BRIEF.md:540`; `docs/governance.md` section 4; `runner/update_merge.py` module docstring; D-583; D-584; D-620; D-677; D-723.
- **D-856** Question (T034, October 30, 2026): LIC-011 says a no-license business must match the city's active business-license spreadsheet "on its listed business name, trade name (DBA) or owner name" and "may enter its city license number when the list has one"; how exact is a match, and what does an entered number do? Choice: `licensing::api::city_list_standing` compares names after lower-casing and keeping only letters and digits (words joined by one space), so "Sample Vent Works, LLC" matches "sample vent works llc" but "Sample Vent" does not (no partial or fuzzy match, which could hand a card to the wrong business); any of the business's three names may equal any of a row's three names; an empty name never matches; and when both the business and the row give a city license number, they must agree, or that row does not match. With no matching row the business stays `Pending` and gets no card (D-177); the next daily list is read the same way. Activation with the identity code, keeping the join date, stays T081's. Source: `docs/spec/licensing.md:15`; `docs/test-design.md` TD-LIC-06; D-059, D-177, D-255.
- **D-857** Question (T034, October 30, 2026): the license map gives class coverage, which T153 loads later, and T034's rules need to know whether a business's ROC classes cover a job type (cameras "R-67 or broader", alarms "an ROC low-voltage class", appliances R-63, pool equipment R-6, gas heaters "licensed businesses only"); where does that come from now? Choice: `licensing::api::Holder::roc_covers` is a plain input meaning "the license map covers this job type for this business's classes", which T153's class map will fill; T034 never reads a class name. A job type the category lists under `refused` (gas pool heater, gas appliance work, a new outlet in holiday lights, a vent reroute in dryer-vent cleaning) is `Job::listed == false` and goes only to a covered license holder, never to a handyman or no-license business (LIC-029 to LIC-031); the matching examples are checked with the oracle's own `map_covers`. The handyman category's job types (a vent reroute among them) give a `HandymanCard`, as do listed job types of handyman-allowed ROC categories, so the under-$1,000 and no-permit checks (T035) know to run. Pest work reads only the sign-up attestation, never `agencies` or an ROC class (D-417). Source: `docs/spec/licensing.md:17`, `docs/spec/licensing.md:18`, `docs/spec/licensing.md:32` to `docs/spec/licensing.md:35`; `docs/catalog/license_map.yaml`; D-392.
- **D-858** Question (T034, October 30, 2026): the task budget is 9 files and 550 changed lines, and the owned files come to about 1,400 lines after `cargo fmt` (models 325, rules 169, the three tests about 440, 260 and 180), plus the crate `CLAUDE.md`, `tests/mod.rs` and the workspace entry; why? Choice: the overrun is accepted and recorded, as in D-821, D-843 and D-853. This task creates the crate, so its models (every type documented, with requirement IDs) land here; the rules are under 170 lines; the tests cover TD-LIC-06, TD-LIC-12 and TD-LIC-17 case by case and tie the `Agency` table to the license map, the catalog, the matching examples and the migration, so none can drift. - **D-859** Question (T034, October 30, 2026): `licensing.business_license` stores license numbers from two sources, the pest business's own sign-up entry (`self_attested`, LIC-047) and the inspector, alarm and septage-hauler agency records (`agency_record`, T036); the spec gives no number format for either, so what does the table check? Choice: a self-attested number must be letters, digits and `-`, at most 20 characters, the same rule `PestAttestation::new` applies on the form, so a typed number is something a homeowner can paste into the Department's license search and the LIC-047 card line stays short; this is a form-hygiene limit, not a claim about the Department's numbering. An agency-record number is stored as the agency shows it, only non-blank and at most 64 characters, since Ask Hava does not choose those formats and a stricter check could refuse a real record (T036 may tighten it per agency from the files it imports). - **D-860** Question (T034, October 31, 2026): rust-production R17 asks for property tests of pure rules, and D-886 gave T034 `app/licensing/src/tests/prop_rules.rs`; which properties guard the routing rules? Choice: over random businesses (ROC cover, any subset of agencies, an optional pest attestation with random record categories and pause, handyman, city-list standing) and random jobs (agency, no-license, ROC and handyman categories, termite, pre-emergent and other job types, every license kind, listed or refused, handyman-allowed or not): a `HandymanCard` only ever goes to a handyman on the city list for a listed job type of a handyman-allowed category; a no-license card needs the city list and a listed job type; an agency category's card goes exactly to its licensees (pest by an unpaused attestation holding the needed record category, alarms with ROC cover); a business with no license and no list match gets nothing; the city-list match ignores case and punctuation but not an extra word, and an empty list leaves the business pending; only a home inspection is ever fee-free and a yes always makes it so. The oracles are written from the requirement sentences, not by calling the rules' private helpers. Source: `docs/spec/licensing.md:15` to `docs/spec/licensing.md:20`, `docs/spec/licensing.md:32` to `docs/spec/licensing.md:35`, `docs/spec/licensing.md:51`; `docs/brains/rust-production.md` R17; D-886.
- **D-892** Question (T033, October 31, 2026): JOB-004 asks each status change to take a row lock and apply only if the job is still in the expected status; `models::guarded_move` (T031) already does both in one `UPDATE … WHERE status = from`. Does the move need an explicit `SELECT … FOR UPDATE` first, and how does TD-JOB-02 make "both orders" certain? Choice: no extra statement. The guarded `UPDATE` is the first statement of `service::apply`'s transaction, so it takes the row lock first; under Postgres's default read-committed isolation a second update waiting on that lock re-checks its `WHERE` against the committed row and matches nothing, so the loser writes no history, audit row, timer or text and answers `Guarded::MovedOn`; a lost move never retries from the job's new status. A separate locking read would add a round trip and change nothing. `tests/integration/tests/job_races.rs` stages each pair (a cancel and a Confirm, a Stripe notice and the payment deadline, a pick and the 3-day close, two picks) behind a third session's held row lock, starting the first event, waiting until it blocks (`pg_stat_activity`), then the second, then releasing, so the first in line wins in each order; it also runs unstaged pairs twenty times. The staged cases are meant to fail if a lost move retried from the re-read status; no mutation run is recorded in the repository. Source: `docs/spec/lifecycle.md:8`; `docs/test-design.md:424`; rust brain R11 and checklist item 12.
- **D-897** Question (T035, October 31, 2026): what goes in AI-012's gas keyword list, and how does it enter the locked catalog (D-157, D-493)? Choice: the new catalog file `docs/catalog/gas_keywords.yaml` holds `decision: D-157`, an `en` list and an `es` list. It starts with every word AI-012 and D-157 name (gas, propane, natural gas, pilot, pilot light, won't light, heater won't light, furnace, gas line, gas dryer, gas stove, gas range; propano, piloto) and adds, because the list overrides the AI and must be wide: wont light, will not light, pilot light out, gas leak, gas smell, smell gas, gas valve, gas meter, gas fireplace, gas grill, gas water heater, gas pool heater, butane, thermocouple; gas natural, luz piloto, fuga de gas, olor a gas, butano, calentador de gas, estufa de gas, secadora de gas. Matching is whole words in order, case ignored, a curly apostrophe read as a straight one, so "gas" never matches "gasket"; the Spanish "no prende" and "no enciende" were left out because they also mean a light or a switch that will not turn on. The file is compiled into `askhava-licensing` (`handyman.rs`) and parsed with `serde-saphyr` and `deny_unknown_fields`; a file that does not parse or lists nothing blocks every handyman card (fail closed). `serde` and `serde-saphyr`, both already on `kit/allowed_crates.txt` and in the workspace, move from the crate's dev-dependencies to its dependencies; no new crate enters `Cargo.lock`. The PR adds the file to `kit/plan.lock` with `python3 scripts/check_plan_lock.py --write`, as D-493 assigns. Reason: AI-012, LIC-021, D-157. Source: `docs/spec/ai.md:16`; `docs/spec/licensing.md:25`.
- **D-898** Question (T035, October 31, 2026): how are the handyman limits, the never-handyman block and the split-job check shaped, where the spec leaves the detail open (LIC-019 to LIC-025, LIC-036)? Choice: (1) the block runs only on a `HandymanCard`, through the new `licensing::api::eligibility_for_request`, which reads the scrubbed request text and every candidate job type (and the job type being matched) and never the AI's handyman reading; a gas word in a no-license, non-handyman card (a gas dryer's vent cleaning) does not block it, since LIC-021 names handymen and dryer-vent cleaning of a gas dryer is not gas work; a gas pool heater stays a refused `pool_repair` job type (LIC-031). (2) Smoke alarms ("smoke alarm", "smoke detector") and fire sprinklers ("fire sprinkler") match as words inside a candidate, so a lawn "sprinkler repair" is not blocked; permit-type job types are an exact list in code (water heater replacement, panel upgrade, panel, new circuit, re-roof, wall removal), the catalog's `refused` entries marked LIC-022, since `models.rs` and the catalog crate are not this task's to extend; a new permit-type job type is added there. A blocked card is `NoCard(RefusedJobType)`, the existing reason for licensed-only work, because `NoCardReason` lives in `models.rs`. (3) `check_quote` asks for the certification box on every handyman quote, trip fee included (D-035), and applies the $1,000.00 limit to a construction-type quote from a handyman or from any business in a no-license construction category, judged on the top of a range; an hourly quote reaches it as a range (FEE-043). (4) `split_job` takes the window in days from the caller, who reads the setting (D-027), because `licensing` may not call `core`; a job is near when its submission lies strictly less than the window away either side (29 days 23:59 blocks, 30 days does not, TD-LIC-10); a trip-fee quote counts $0 toward the $1,000 but still blocks on a shared job type; `quotes` passes only the same business's handyman jobs at the same address. (5) Refusals are `QuoteRefusal` variants with no words: the explanation of Arizona's handyman limit and the certification statement are the portal's copy (T148), since this task owns no customer copy; `HANDYMAN_CARD_LINE` is LIC-024's line word for word. Reason: LIC-019 to LIC-025, LIC-036, D-027, D-035, D-081, D-154, D-186. Source: `docs/spec/licensing.md:23`–`docs/spec/licensing.md:29`, `docs/spec/licensing.md:40`; `docs/test-design.md` TD-LIC-08 to TD-LIC-10.
- **D-907** Question (T038, October 31, 2026): CON-027 fixes the line a "who is this?" or "is this a real person?" reply gets, and CALL-022 the sentence the consent text gains once the safety voice call is on, but neither has a template, and every text must be a fixed English and Spanish template (TXT-001, D-491). Choice: two new keys in `app/messaging/templates/en.json` and `es.json`: `who_is_this`, "Ask Hava: " plus the CON-027 sentence word for word (its "2 days" and "24 hours" are the spec's fixed words, not the HELP reply's settings; English GSM-7 in 2 segments, Spanish UCS-2 in 4 because of "días"), and `consent_safety_call`, the CON-031 text with the CALL-022 sentence placed before "Reply STOP to opt out, HELP for help." so the STOP/HELP line and both links stay last (3 segments in each language; the Spanish says "a este teléfono" so it stays GSM-7). Both Spanish texts are drafts for native-speaker review; neither stays on while Spanish conversations are off. `intake::rules::consent_template` picks `consent_safety_call` only while the "safety voice call" setting is on, which CALL-022 allows only once its conditions are met (D-384).
