- **D-1195** Question (T048, INT-019, D-095, D-419, D-807): how is "no homeowner reply" timed and told when `jobs`' Intake timer already closes the job at 72 hours with no text (`JobStatus::timeout_text` leaves the Intake close text to INT-019's task) and intake may not change `jobs`? - **D-1215** Question (plan change, November 1, 2026; numbered under the interim rule of `docs/ai-operating-manual.md` section 7 step 4: max(`next_decision` 1205 as given by the coordinator, main's highest 1199 + 1, open plan PRs' highest + 1, none above D-479) + 10 = 1215): T048 reported two pieces with no owning task (D-1198, D-1199 (1) and (4), `docs/decisions.md:984`, `docs/decisions.md:985`; `docs/for-casey-review.md:1437`): (a) the `jobs.homeowner_text` sender, the text the homeowner gets when a request moves on by itself, and (b) the wiring that routes a homeowner's reply inside an open request to `answer_list` and `hear`. Both sit under the build limits (`scripts/validate_tasks.py:186` to `scripts/validate_tasks.py:192`: 10 owned paths, 600 lines, 45% context). Not taken here, and listed: the 24-hour reminder and INT-019 close still use T048's Arizona-only `texting_window` (D-1196); T240's `send_window` is the function a later change can switch them to, which would need an owner of `app/intake/src/handlers.rs` ordered with T151 and T208. The INT-032 "That's 2 jobs" copy and wiring (D-999) stay open. A text from a linked business phone reaches no homeowner path in T241; the business-reply tasks (T082, T083, T070) will need a branch in `app/server/src/inbound_text.rs` and so an ownership change when they are reached. - **D-1200** Question (T049, JOB-019, JOB-020, JOB-023, D-005): which messages show cancel intent, and which only mention cancelling? Choice: `rules::close_reading` (folded words) reads "CLOSE <number>" or "CERRAR <number>" and "CLOSE ALL" / "CERRAR TODO" (TODOS, TODAS) as a close; while a "Close which?" waits, a lone number or "all" (todo, todos, todas, both, ambos, ambas) answers it. Cancel intent is a fixed phrase list anywhere in the message ("please cancel", "cancel my request", "cancel it", "never mind", "nevermind", "nvm", "forget it", "no longer need", "dont need it", "ya no lo necesito", "ya no necesito", "ya no hace falta", "ya no quiero", "olvidalo", "no quiero nada", "cancele mi solicitud" and the like) or one of "ya no", "ya no gracias", "close", "cerrar" as the whole message. "ya no" counts only alone or followed by a need word, because "el aire ya no funciona" (the AC no longer works) is a request. CLOSE alone reads as intent. Any other message holding a cancel word (cancel, cancelled, cancelar, cancela, ...) only mentions it: "cancel" alone, "cancel 1042" and "I had to cancel the plumber" get the JOB-023 line and close nothing (JOB-020). Kind: conflict (spec gives examples only). Owner approval: Casey's standing approval for plan improvements through the normal review gate. Reason: the smallest list that holds the spec's examples without closing a live request on an everyday Spanish phrase. Source: `docs/spec/lifecycle.md:23`, `docs/spec/lifecycle.md:24`, `docs/spec/lifecycle.md:27`.
- **D-1201** Question (T049, JOB-018, JOB-021, JOB-022, JOB-023): what does a close do, and what answers an unclear one? Choice: `closing::answer_close` works on the homeowner's open request, in one transaction under the homeowner lock: its open jobs are the request's jobs not yet final, by number. A close moves each named job to Cancelled from its current status (any status before Done, JOB-018) through `jobs::api::move_to` as `Actor::Homeowner` (audit row, guarded move; a job that moved on meanwhile is left), closes the request once every job is final, and texts `job_closed` (one job, once per job) or `jobs_closed` (ALL). Intent with one open job closes it (JOB-022); with several it sends `close_which` listing the numbers and CLOSE ALL and stores `close_which = asked` (closing nothing, JOB-021); the answer stores `answered`. "CLOSE <number>" for a number not open gets the how-to line with one open job and "Close which?" with several. A mention names the newest open job. An opt-out (bare "cancel" included) or HELP gets nothing and changes no job (D-005). No open job: nothing. `close_from_page` is the quote page's button: the same move for one job, no text (the page shows it), `false` when already final. The duplicate of `handlers::close_if_done` (the request closes once all its jobs are final) is kept as `close_when_final` in `closing.rs` because `handlers.rs` is not this task's file. Kind: conflict (spec silent on the details). Owner approval: Casey's standing approval for plan improvements through the normal review gate. Reason: closes only what the homeowner clearly named, and never on a guess. Source: `docs/spec/lifecycle.md:22`, `docs/spec/lifecycle.md:25`, `docs/spec/lifecycle.md:26`.
- **D-1202** Question (T049, JOB-023, CON-034, D-763, D-999): the existing `close_howto` template is CON-034's answer after HELP ("Reply CLOSE <n> to close request <n>." plus the fixed "If that doesn't fix it..." sentence), while JOB-023 gives its own words. Choice: a new template `close_mention` with JOB-023's exact words ("Ask Hava: To close request {job}, reply CLOSE {job}."); `close_howto` stays CON-034's. New templates `close_which`, `job_closed` and `jobs_closed`, in English and Spanish (Spanish AI drafts marked `draft`); the list of numbers fills `{job}` ("1042 and 1043", "1042 y 1043" in Spanish; the copy panel and cold read asked for the joined form and a shorter `close_which`). `answer_close` and `close_from_page` have no caller yet: the inbound dispatcher is the D-999 gap and the quote page's close button route belongs to the page task; both must call them, the dispatcher before the intake answer rules on an open request. Kind: conflict (two texts for one purpose). Owner approval: Casey's standing approval for plan improvements through the normal review gate. Reason: each spec line keeps its own exact words. Source: `docs/spec/lifecycle.md:27`, `docs/spec/consent.md:38`.
- **D-1203** Question (T049 review, JOB-019, JOB-021, JOB-023, D-1200, D-1201): the phrase list of D-1200 matched anywhere, so "The last plumber had to cancel the job, can you find someone?", "ya no quiero esperar, necesito alguien hoy", "I don't need it today, next week is fine" and "never mind" inside a longer sentence would close a job; a never-answered "Close which?" took any later lone number or "all"; "cancel 1042" with several open jobs named the newest job. Choice: `rules::close_reading` splits the message into clauses (at , . ; : ! ? and new lines), trims filler words at each end (ok, please, actually, I, we, can you; thanks, gracias, anymore, after all; never "now" or "today"), and reads intent only when a whole clause is a fixed intent clause ("never mind", "forget it", "cancel it", "cancel my request", "olvidalo", "ya no hace falta", ...), a need phrase ending the clause with nothing or an allowed object ("dont need it", "no longer need this", "ya no lo necesito", "ya no quiero"; "today", "esperar", "hoy" after it make it a request), or a bare cancel word with "please"/"por favor"; "ya no", "close" and "cerrar" stay whole-message only. A clause about someone else ("the plumber had to cancel the job") is never intent; with a cancel word it is a mention and gets the JOB-023 line. `close_reading` now takes the open request numbers while "Close which?" waits (empty otherwise): a lone number answers only when it is one of them, "all" only while it waits; anything else goes to the normal intake. A mention names the first open request number written in the message (`rules::number_named`), else the newest. This replaces D-1200's "anywhere in the message" list. Kind: conflict (spec gives examples only). Owner approval: Casey's standing approval for plan improvements through the normal review gate. Reason: a job closes only when the homeowner clearly asks for their own request to end; a missed intent costs one how-to line, a wrong close loses a live request. Source: `docs/spec/lifecycle.md:23`, `docs/spec/lifecycle.md:25`, `docs/spec/lifecycle.md:27`.
- **D-1227** Question (plan change, November 1, 2026; numbered under the interim rule of `docs/ai-operating-manual.md` section 7 step 4: max(`next_decision` 1205 on `claude/kit-state`, main's highest 1216 + 1, open plan PRs' highest + 1, here PR #224's D-1203 + 1 = 1204) + 10 = 1227): `python3 scripts/gen_prompts.py --check --strict` fails on `main` because T208 measures 47% of the window, over the 45% limit for a build task (`scripts/validate_tasks.py:192`), while its stored `context_pct` is 43%, as D-1215 recorded (`docs/decisions.md:986`); storing 47% turns `validate_tasks.py` red. The question bank stays: CARD-007's card-field answers come from its `card_field` flags (D-394). The generator has no section-level read, so a narrower read of `docs/architecture.md` is not available without a script change. Choice: drop `docs/catalog/intake_golden.yaml` from T208's `reads` (`kit/tasks.json:15219`); its owns, requirements, tests, decisions, goal and checks are unchanged, the 45% limit is unchanged, and no split is needed. Nearest the limits after this change: T170 and T172 (harness, 49% of their 50%), then T156 at 40% of 45%. `kit/plan.lock` is rewritten; `docs/architecture.md` is unchanged.
- **D-1228** Question (T050, CON-012, CON-028, CON-029, JOB-020, D-005, D-129, D-491): how does intake carry an opt-out from a number with a live job, given `messaging` already lists the number and queues the bare CON-009 confirmation, and the still-open line by email (T094), on the quote page (T052), the pick withdrawal (T054) and the Confirm refusal (T224) are other tasks'? Choice: `intake::api::on_opt_out(db, msg)` takes the same `TextIn` with `inbound.opt_out` set and, for the homeowner's open request with any job before a final status, in one transaction under the homeowner lock, changes no job status and queues no text (so the "Your request <n> is still open" line is never in a text, CON-028), marks every live job paused by the homeowner when the whole text folds to "cancel" or "cancelar" (`sole_cancel`; new migration `0076_intake_optout_jobs.sql`, `intake.homeowner_pause` with request, job, inbox ID, `paused_at`, `ended_at`, one open pause per job by a partial unique index, plus an `intake.paused_by_homeowner` audit row) and enqueues one `intake.opted_out_live_job` task (`OPTED_OUT_LIVE_KIND`, dedupe key per inbox row; payload IDs only: request, live jobs, `paused`, inbox ID) for T094, T052 and T054 to handle. `paused_by_homeowner(job)` is the read the pick, Confirm, charge and release paths call (T054, T224). No opt-out or task with no live job. The pause covers the open request's live jobs only, the request being the one a text from that number belongs to. Kind: decision (design within the spec). Owner approval: Casey's standing approval for plan improvements through the normal review gate. Reason: CON-029 asks for a mark without a status change, so it is a row beside the job, not a status; one event lets each later task act on it without intake knowing their channels. Source: `docs/spec/consent.md:16`, `docs/spec/consent.md:32`, `docs/spec/consent.md:33`, `docs/spec/lifecycle.md:24`.
- **D-1229** Question (T050, CON-029): who calls `on_opt_out`, and who ends a pause? Choice: plan gap for the runner, not built here: the inbound dispatcher (D-999; T241, the Twilio inbound-text route, is the likely caller) must call `intake::api::on_opt_out` after `messaging::api::on_inbound_text` returns `Outcome::OptedOut`; and the pause ends "when the homeowner picks or closes on the quote page or by email" (CON-029), which is the pick task's (T054) and the page and email close paths' (T052, T094): they set `intake.homeowner_pause.ended_at`, for which intake will need a small `end_pause` function in the task that first ends one. A close by `close_from_page` already moves the job to a final status, after which no pick can follow. Kind: gap. Owner approval: Casey's standing approval for plan improvements through the normal review gate. Reason: T050's scope is recording the pause and enqueueing the event (D-491); adding a writer no task calls yet would be unused code. Source: `docs/spec/consent.md:33`.
- **D-1233** Question (T052, PICK-008, D-084, D-1051): `quotes::api` gave the page no read of a job's quotes in arrival order with the unavailable ones (`shown_quotes` returns business IDs ordered by ID; the LIST rows drop unavailable quotes, so their numbers would move), and no task owns a `quotes` file for it. Choice: `quotes::api::page_quotes(db, job)` and `PageQuote` (business, `received_at`, `unavailable`, original wording) are written in `app/quotes/src/api.rs` (a shared path, "your public functions"), one literal query on `quotes.quote` (confirmed, not withdrawn, ordered by `received_at`, business ID); `portals::api::number_quotes` numbers them from 1 in that order. A quote shows "no longer available" when `unavailable_at` is set, which `picks` does after a failed pick or a failed eligibility re-check at the pick (D-084: eligibility is re-checked at the pick); no live business-status read on the page. Open, for the runner: a quote that waits for its read-back confirm (PICK-006) and is confirmed after a later quote is shown slots in by `received_at` and moves the later numbers; a stored arrival number (a `quotes` migration) would close that, and the LIST text (`list_rows`) skips unavailable quotes, so its numbers can differ from the page's after a failed pick (T047's code, `quotes` owner). Kind: decision (design within the spec) and gap. Owner approval: Casey's standing approval for plan improvements through the normal review gate. Reason: numbers must never change (PICK-008) and portals may not query another module's schema (architecture section 4). Source: `docs/spec/quotes-pick.md:12`, `docs/spec/quotes-pick.md:13`.
- **D-1234** Question (T052, PICK-011, PICK-012, CON-003, CON-028): what the page reads and when the Pick button shows. Choice: the token resolves through `jobs::api::quote_token::resolve` (hash lookup; malformed, unknown, re-issued or revoked is a bare 404); it stops at exactly 30 days after the job entered a final status (`JobRow::status_at`, `TOKEN_LIFE_AFTER_CLOSE`), still working at 29 days 23:59:59; Pick buttons show on every available quote while `JobStatus::takes_quote_edits` (Open, No quotes yet, Quotes ready: the job has had no pick), so from the first quote even before the first-quote move to Quotes ready (JOB-009) is built; a homeowner pause (CON-029) does not hide them, since a pick on the page ends the pause. The fee line is CON-003's exact words, "Free for you. The business you pick pays Ask Hava a set introduction fee.", which the spec fixes for the top of this page; the brief's "introduction fee by job size" naming rule is for describing the fee, and the spec decides what (BUILD_BRIEF.md:7). The CON-028 line shows while a live job has an open `intake.homeowner_pause` (a sole-word CANCEL). The page is `noindex` by `X-Robots-Tag: noindex, nofollow` (the shared `base.html`, T051's and T101's, has no head block for a meta tag) and `no-store`, so a poll always gets the current list. Kind: decision (design within the spec). Owner approval: Casey's standing approval for plan improvements through the normal review gate. Reason: PICK-011 and PICK-012 as written; CON-003 names this page. Source: `docs/spec/quotes-pick.md:15`, `docs/spec/quotes-pick.md:16`, `docs/spec/consent.md:7`.
- **D-1235** Question (T052, PICK-009, A11Y-033, D-492): how new quotes appear without breaking the no-JavaScript page. Choice: the server page is complete on its own (a reload shows new quotes; the Pick form posts to the page's own address with its CSRF field, no JavaScript needed). `app/portals/static/quote_page.ts` (an ES module, loaded with `type="module"` from `/static/portals/quote_page.js`) fetches the same page every 30 seconds while `#quotes` has `data-live="true"`, appends each `li[data-number]` it has not shown, replaces one whose `data-available` changed, removes the "No quotes yet" line, and writes one line per batch ("1 new quote added below." or "<n> new quotes added below.", taken from the status element's `data-one`/`data-many` so the words stay in the template) into the `role="status"` element, which is empty at first render. Open, for the runner: no route serves `/static/` yet and `npm run build` (tsc emit) does not exist (tsconfig has `noEmit`); architecture section 2 gives both to the Docker stage and `ServeDir` (T173), so until then the script 404s and the page works as without JavaScript. Kind: decision and gap. Owner approval: Casey's standing approval for plan improvements through the normal review gate. Reason: progressive enhancement (BUILD_BRIEF.md:106). Source: `docs/spec/accessibility.md:37`, `docs/spec/quotes-pick.md:13`.
- **D-1236** Question (T052, TD-PICK-38, TD-PICK-05, CON-028, PICK-040, PICK-041, TXT-016): which page parts are not built here. Choice, each a gap for the runner: (1) the STOP half of TD-PICK-38's still-open case: a STOP leaves no per-job record (only the `intake.opted_out_live_job` task, D-1228), so the page shows the line only after a sole-word CANCEL; showing it after STOP needs a stored per-job opt-out mark (a migration in `intake` or `portals`, written by that task's handler). (2) The Pick POST handler and the quote-page terms acceptance of TD-PICK-05 are the pick review step's (T055); a same-origin POST gets 405 until then, a cross-site one 403. (3) The close button the CON-028 line points to: `intake::api::close_from_page` exists (T049) but no task owns its form and route, and D-1229 expects the page close to end a pause. (4) The card's name, license lines, facts, amount and Google and Yelp links (PICK-040, PICK-041, TXT-016's "format, amount and earliest visit"): no business name or fact is stored yet (T148, T164, T165, T193), so each card shows only its number, the business's own words and the Pick line; `QuoteCard::lines` goes in once `CardSource` can be read. (5) A Spanish page: English only until the page reads the request's language. (6) Size: the owned files came to about 840 changed lines against the 500-line budget, mostly the three test files. Kind: gap. Owner approval: Casey's standing approval for plan improvements through the normal review gate. Reason: each needs storage or a route another task owns (D-491). Source: `docs/spec/consent.md:32`, `docs/spec/quotes-pick.md:45`.
- **D-1237** Question (T052 review follow-up, PICK-041, A11Y-033, TD-PICK-18, TD-PICK-04): the first T052 commit left out the per-card PICK-041 line, kept a card whose Pick form disappeared (job closed) unchanged in the browser, announced only new quotes, headed cards "#<n>" alone, and read the paused flag on a final job before discarding a read error. Choice: every available card carries "Ask Hava doesn't rank businesses; check it yourself." (`docs/spec/quotes-pick.md:45`), asserted once per available card in `tests/integration/tests/quote_page.rs`; card headings read "Quote #<n>", an unavailable one "Quote #<n> (no longer available)"; each `<li>` carries `data-pickable` and `quote_page.ts` replaces a card when it or `data-available` changes, the merge running on every fetch including the last one that finds the job no longer live; the one status line per batch joins the new-quote words and the template's `data-gone-one`/`data-gone-many` words ("1 quote is no longer available."); `intake::api::paused_by_homeowner` is read only on a live job and its error is returned. The page-versus-LIST number mismatch stays open as in D-1233 and needs an owner (see `docs/for-casey-review.md`). Kind: fix. Owner approval: Casey's standing approval for plan improvements through the normal review gate. Reason: PICK-041 names the card line; A11Y-033 asks for one line per update, not one per kind. Source: `docs/spec/quotes-pick.md:45`, `docs/spec/accessibility.md:37`.
- **D-1238** Question (T053, A11Y-001, A11Y-002): `docs/test-design.md` section 6 says `tests/a11y/` "injects the vendored axe-core 4.14.0", but no vendored copy exists and T053 owns no file to hold one; the pinned `@axe-core/playwright` 4.13.0 in `package.json` brings axe-core 4.13.0. Choice: the suite runs axe through `AxeBuilder` from the pinned `@axe-core/playwright` (axe-core 4.13.0, already installed and audited by `npm ci`), with the tags `wcag2a`, `wcag2aa`, `wcag21a`, `wcag21aa`, `wcag22aa`; no new dependency. Moving to 4.14.0 is a `package.json` bump for whichever task next touches it. Kind: deviation. Owner approval: Casey's standing approval for plan improvements through the normal review gate. Reason: same rules engine and tags, one version older, no new library. Source: `docs/test-design.md:116`, `docs/spec/accessibility.md:5`.
- **D-1239** Question (T053, A11Y-002): how is "the page list generated from the route table" built, and how does each state get its data when the app has no seed route? Choice: `tests/a11y/fixtures.ts` reads every `.route(PATH, get(...))` in `app/*/src` (constants resolved, `src/tests/` and the `/__test/` test-control routes left out); a `.route(` whose path is neither a string literal nor a known constant becomes an "unparsed route" entry, and every `.route_service`, `.fallback`, `.fallback_service`, `.nest` and `.nest_service` call becomes an entry too (none exists yet), so the coverage test fails on each until it gets page states or a `NOT_PAGES` line with its reason at load; `PAGE_STATES` lists each GET route's states, and a GET route with none fails `axe_all_pages.spec.ts`. Each state is seeded once per worker by one SQL statement through `psql` on DATABASE_URL, the database `tests/e2e/webserver.ts` starts the web binary on; a quote-page token is a random 64-hex string stored only as its SHA256, which is what `jobs::api::quote_token::resolve` looks up, so no ID secret is needed. Each state names a line it must show and one it must not, so a seed that opens the wrong state fails. States today: `/q/{token}` with no quotes, three quotes with #2 unavailable, paused by CANCEL, after a pick, and closed. Spanish, error and banner-on states do not exist on any route yet; the task that adds one adds its row to `PAGE_STATES`. Kind: design. Owner approval: Casey's standing approval for plan improvements through the normal review gate. Reason: a source scan cannot miss a route that compiles, and direct SQL seeding needs no test-only route in the app. Source: `docs/test-design.md:116`, `docs/spec/accessibility.md:6`.
- **D-1240** Question (T053, A11Y-006, A11Y-008, A11Y-017, A11Y-025): how are the checks axe can't make defined? Choice: (1) a target under 24 by 24 CSS px passes only under WCAG 2.5.8's inline-in-a-sentence or spacing exception (a 24 px circle on its centre touches no other target and no other small target's circle); `[draggable="true"]` and range sliders fail; (2) 400% zoom is a 1280 by 1024 window at 400%, a 320 by 256 CSS px viewport; (3) help must sit in the same landmark at the same place among its links on every page and state; no page has a help link yet (BIZ-047, WEB-008), so all pages agree on "none" today and the first page to add one fails until every page has it; (4) every axe "incomplete" result (rule and targets) is attached and annotated in the JSON report at `test-results/a11y-report/results.json`, printed to the console, and fails unless listed in `REVIEWED_INCOMPLETE`, stricter than A11Y-025's one release; none occur on the current pages; (5) `.github/workflows/a11y.yml` is still the stub, so these specs turn `Ally` red only once T173 (a harness task) runs them there; (6) size: the task came to about 624 changed lines in 9 files (561 at the first commit; the review follow-up of D-1241 added the rest) against the task's 550-line, 6-file budget (four specs, the shared fixtures and the config, plus the three docs), kept as one PR because the specs share one page list and seeding. Kind: design. Owner approval: Casey's standing approval for plan improvements through the normal review gate. Reason: WCAG's own exception text for target size and zoom; the strict incomplete rule cannot let one through unread. Source: `docs/brains/accessibility-forms.md` section 2 [A4], `docs/spec/accessibility.md:10`, `docs/spec/accessibility.md:12`, `docs/spec/accessibility.md:21`, `docs/spec/accessibility.md:29`.
- **D-1241** Question (T053 review follow-up, A11Y-002, A11Y-009, A11Y-017, A11Y-025, TD-A11Y-01): the first T053 commit turned `bypassCSP` on for the whole suite, could silently miss a route its pattern did not read, showed axe's incomplete results only in a list reporter that drops attachments, checked help placement and reduced motion at two and one widths, and left the TD-A11Y-01 marker off its test titles. Choice: `bypassCSP` is set only by `test.use` inside the text-spacing `describe` of `reflow_spacing.spec.ts`, so every other test runs under the page's real CSP (SEC-013); the route scan changes as in D-1239; a JSON reporter writes `test-results/a11y-report/results.json`; help placement and reduced motion run at 320, 768 and 1280 px; the axe-per-state and structure/sticky-bar test titles carry `TD-A11Y-01`. Kind: fix. Owner approval: Casey's standing approval for plan improvements through the normal review gate. Reason: a test-wide CSP bypass would hide a CSP break, and a scan that can miss a route defeats A11Y-002. Source: `docs/spec/accessibility.md:6`, `docs/test-design.md:116`.
- **D-1243** Question (T054, PICK-013, PICK-031, PICK-045): no `picks` crate existed, `businesses` stores no business name for PICK-045's "<Business> has your pick", and SEC-031 forbids comparing a `JobStatus` outside a `status.rs`. Choice: T054 creates `app/picks` (lib, api, status, models, rules, service, tests, `CLAUDE.md`, `sqlx.toml`; workspace member and `askhava-picks` dependency of `intake`, `tests/security` and `tests/integration`, all allowed by `kit/layers.json` and `kit/allowed_crates.txt`); `picks/src/status.rs` holds `PickStatus` (only `awaiting_confirm` and `cancelled` used now; the table's check already lists the eleven architecture codes) and `stage`, the one exhaustive match from a `JobStatus` to the text-pick `Stage`; the reply to a text pick reads "Done. You picked quote <n> for request <job>. We'll text you when the business accepts. You can still pick another quote. Reply LIST to see them." (the cold read and copy panel's rewrite: the reader is on texts, so LIST rather than "your page") until a business name exists, then the task that owns PICK-045 switches to its exact words. Template placeholders use the registry test's sample names (`{quoted}` carries the quote number); the which-request text lists every request number that takes a pick in `{job}` ("1042 and 1043", "y" in Spanish, as "Close which?" does) and gives the first as its example in `{number}` ("like 1042 2 YES"), so it is numbered as D-068 asks. The copy panel's "Need something fixed? Text us" ending for `text_pick_none` was not taken: a text from a number with an open request does not open a new one, and the confirmed reply does not say the business has her details, since they are released only once paid (PICK-022). Reason: smallest change that keeps SEC-031 and says what happens next (D-068). Source: `docs/architecture.md:191`, `docs/spec/quotes-pick.md:49`.
- **D-1244** Question (T054, PICK-055): what are "per day" and "local time", and where does the global threshold come from? Choice: every cap counts codes sent since the start of the current Arizona calendar day (UTC-7, no daylight saving); the 9 p.m. to 8 a.m. voice rule uses the Arizona hour (`picks` cannot read the number's area code; the stricter area-code zone is left to the caller, who may refuse earlier); "per destination number" counts by the homeowner's vault contact ID, so no number is stored (PRIV-002); the threshold is a parameter of `send_code`, which the page route (T055) fills from a setting, and one `picks.verify_daily_cap` High alert is raised on the first refused send of each Arizona day (`picks.verify_cap_day`). A send that Verify then fails still counts. Reason: the safer reading of each cap, with no plaintext number in `picks`. Source: `docs/spec/quotes-pick.md:59`.
- **D-1245** Question (T054, CON-029, D-491): CON-029 withdraws a pick waiting for Confirm "without changing its status", and `intake.opted_out_live_job` has other handlers (T094's email). Choice: `intake::on_opt_out` calls `picks::api::withdraw_paused` in its own transaction on a sole-word CANCEL or CANCELAR: each waiting pick becomes `cancelled` with `end_reason = paused` and a `picks.pick_withdrawn` event (pick, job, business, reason) is enqueued for the business's notice; the job stays in Awaiting confirm and its timer keeps running, so it returns to Quotes ready at the Confirm window's end as `jobs` already does; while the pause lasts `answer_text_pick` passes it and a YES is `Plan::Paused` (no pick, no text). The Confirm refusal is T224's and ending the pause T055's and T094's (D-1229). Reason: one transaction, no second handler on one task kind, and CON-029's no-status-change wording. Source: `docs/spec/consent.md:33`.
- **D-1246** Question (T054, PICK-016, PICK-031, PICK-032, PICK-036, D-068): how does the homeowner answer "which job?", and what counts as "a text with that line was sent"? Choice: the which-request text asks for "<request> <quote> YES" (for example "1042 2 YES"), read statelessly, and like every text offering a text pick it carries PICK-031's share sentence and ends with the Terms line; every queued text ending with the Terms line is recorded in `picks.terms_line` for each job it offers (job, outbox row, version `<template>:<language>:<12 hex of the SHA256 of the words>`, time queued); a YES for a job with no record gets `text_pick_terms` and picks only on the repeat. Quote numbers are the page's arrival order with unavailable quotes keeping their numbers (D-1233); an unavailable or unknown number gets `text_pick_no_quote`. The status reply sends, per open job, `text_pick_confirmed` (Payment pending or Connected, with "reply CLOSE <job>") or `text_pick_waiting` (still collecting quotes), else `text_pick_none`. A job paused by the homeowner (CON-029) does not count toward PICK-031's "exactly one job": the one job not paused picks directly, the which-request text lists only the jobs not paused, and a YES when only paused jobs take a pick (or naming a paused one) is `Plan::Paused`. A replacing YES whose waiting pick is no longer `awaiting_confirm` when it is ended (the business confirmed it in a concurrent transaction) returns `PicksError::MovedOn`, so `intake` rolls back: no second pick, no withdrawal notice, no reply. Each pick enqueues `picks.pick_made` (pick, job, business) at once for the pick notice. Reason: no new conversation state, and the Terms line is proven per job. Source: `docs/spec/quotes-pick.md:20`, `docs/spec/quotes-pick.md:35`.
- **D-1247** Question (T054): what is left unwired, and the size budget. Choice: `answer_text_pick` has no caller until the inbound dispatcher (D-999); `send_code`/`check_code` until the page pick route (T055), which also supplies the destination number from the homeowner's own session and the threshold setting; `picks.pick_made` and `picks.pick_withdrawn` have no handler yet (the pick-notice and withdrawal emails, later picks and messaging tasks); the LIST text's last line (`quote_list_end`, sent by `intake`'s `handlers.rs`, T048's file) is not yet recorded in `picks.terms_line`, so until that sender calls `picks::api::record_terms_line` a first YES after a LIST gets the Terms line once more (the safe direction). Size: the task came to about 1,950 changed lines in its owned files (2,500 with the shared crate scaffolding, templates and docs), well over the 600-line budget, because it creates the `picks` crate and covers six test-design entries; a plan bug for the runner to note, not split mid-task. Reason: report honestly rather than drop a requirement. Source: `kit/prompts/T054.md`.
- **D-1263** Question (harness fix, November 1, 2026; numbered max(`next_decision` 1253, main's highest 1247 + 1, no open plan pull request) + 10 = 1263): why does the retry worker's `last_failure` never carry the failed step's log lines (D-582)? T055 attempt 1 (run 41337590987, job 124940581395, a SEC-031 hit at `app/portals/src/pick_flow.rs:231` failing `tests/test_check_rust_rules.py::test_real_repository_passes`) got only "Ci: failure; Checks: failure\nChecks failed at step: Unit, contract and drill tests (pytest)\nCi failed at step: Both jobs passed", and so did every failed pull request since D-582 (T020, T033, T036, T047, T176, T184, T227, FIX-MAIN on `claude/kit-state`'s `kit/state.json`), although the Ci summary job's log always holds an `##[error]` line. Finding: the step names prove that `GitHubEnv._job_detail` (`runner/github_env.py:834`) read `repos/{repo}/actions/jobs/{job}` with the job token, and the cycle's `kit/runner_log.jsonl` row (18:43:47Z, session actions-41333720500) has an empty `log`, so no exception was raised: the log download `repos/{repo}/actions/jobs/{job}/logs` (a 302 to a blob store) returned non-zero, or text with no `##[error]` line, and the old code dropped it silently (`excerpt = log_excerpt(text) if code == 0 else []`). It is not a missing permission: the job that resolves pull requests has `actions: write` (which includes read) and `checks: read` (`.github/workflows/backup-runner.yml:208`, `.github/workflows/backup-runner.yml:211`) and passes the job token as `RUNNER_CHECKS_TOKEN` (`.github/workflows/backup-runner.yml:267`); the jobs read on the same permission succeeds. The exact refusal (token type at the blob redirect, or a log not yet finalised when the cycle reads it right after the check completes) cannot be read from here, because nothing was logged. Choice: (1) `_log_lines` (`runner/github_env.py:854`) tries a refused download once more after `LOG_RETRY_SECONDS` (10), the cheapest likely cause being a log not yet ready right after its check completed, then writes the `gh api` exit code and the first 200 characters of its stderr, token-shaped strings redacted, to the cycle log (`runner/github_env.py:868`), and a readable log with no error line as its length, so the next failure shows the cause. (2) When the log excerpt is empty, `_annotation_lines` reads `repos/{repo}/check-runs/{id}/annotations` with the job token (a check-runs read, D-502) and `annotation_lines` (`runner/github_env.py:268`) renders the failure-level ones as `path:start_line: message` rows (`path: message` without a start line, no location for Actions' own `.github` annotation), at most 15, each cut to 200 characters and redacted, inside FAILURE_LOG_CAP as before (`runner/github_env.py:852`); a readable log keeps D-582's behaviour and reads no annotations. (3) No workflow permission changes, since none is missing. Tests: `tests/test_runner_live.py:892`, `tests/test_runner_live.py:904`, `tests/test_runner_live.py:914`, `tests/test_runner_live.py:922`. Reason: the retry worker learns at least GitHub's error annotations even when the log download is refused, and the refusal is now on record. Source: `runner/github_env.py`, `.github/workflows/backup-runner.yml`.
- **D-1248** Question (T055, PICK-013, PICK-016, PICK-017, A11Y-014): T055 owns the review step and the pick result, but the page pick needs the Verify code step first (PICK-013; its form `pick_code.html` is T187's, which depends on T055), and storing a page pick needs a `picks` function T055 may not write (`app/picks/src/service.rs` is T054's; no task names a page-pick write). Choice: `portals::pick_flow` answers the quote card's Pick form (`POST /q/{token}`, merged beside the quote page's `GET` in `server::build_router`) with the review step in `templates/pick_review.html`; the final Pick posts to `POST /q/{token}/pick`, which re-checks the CSRF token, the link (bare 404 as SEC-037) and that the quote can still be picked (when it can't, 303 back to the card, `/q/{token}#quote-<n>`), then re-renders the review step with "Nothing was picked. Picking on this page isn't open yet, so no code was sent." first in main (D-1251 item 5), so no page claims a pick that was not made and a double submit changes nothing (A11Y-031). `portals::api::result_page` renders the page shown once a pick is stored: the heading `#pick-result` carries `tabindex="-1"` and `autofocus` (A11Y-014, no script needed under the CSP), PICK-045's next steps, the PICK-054 contact card as a `data:text/vcard` download (askhava.com only until the texting number exists; a GET route would be a new page for the Ally route scan) and the after-Done line. T187 inserts the code step into `final_pick` and calls `result_page` after the stored pick and its quote-page Terms acceptance (`intake::api::record_terms_acceptance`, channel `QuotePage`). Both routes are POST only, so the Ally route scan lists no new page. Kind: gap. Owner approval: Casey's standing approval for plan improvements through the normal review gate. - **D-1250** Question (T055, SEC-042, A11Y-031): in Chromium, a same-origin form POST from any page sends `Origin: null`, because every response carries `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer` (SEC-012) and the Fetch standard serializes the origin as null under that policy; `security::is_cross_site` (T051's) treats any Origin that is not `https://<Host>` as cross-site even when `Sec-Fetch-Site: same-origin`, so every portal form POST from a real browser is refused with a 403 (seen in this task's Playwright run: header `origin: null`, a `csrf_rejected` event). Choice: not fixed here (`security.rs` is not this task's file); `tests/e2e/pick_flow.spec.ts` re-sends its POSTs with the same-origin https Origin through `page.route` and says why. Proposed fix for the runner, as a security task with an Opus review: accept `Sec-Fetch-Site: same-origin` whatever the Origin (the browser sets it and a page can't forge it), and use the Origin check only when `Sec-Fetch-Site` is absent, treating `Origin: null` there as cross-site; then drop the re-send from the spec. Kind: fix needed. Owner approval: Casey's standing approval for plan improvements through the normal review gate. Reason: without it no homeowner can pick, close or submit any portal form. Source: `docs/spec/security.md:46`, `app/portals/src/security.rs:159`.

- **D-1269** Question (T156, re-run after the FIX-MAIN revert of 26b176e5, D-1053; re-decides void D-1037): how does the question set run one question at a time, and how are two conflicting lines read? Choice: `intake::api::BankRun` (pure) asks the set in its order, applies each `ask_if`, asks only `emergency` questions on an emergency job and only after the cards (`starts_now`), ends every bank list with "Not sure" ("No sé"), counts every prompt (the smell question and the one AI follow-up included) toward 8, and stores option numbers, "Not sure" or the code `text` (free words never stored here). With AI off the template is asked word for word and the keyword rule is: exactly one option of two or more words appears as whole words in her request ("Swamp cooler pads are dry" answers "Swamp cooler"; one-word options such as "Yes" never skip). With AI on no keyword skip runs; the AI reading names its question ID and skips only at or above `BankSettings::skip_threshold`, `None` until AI-027's run, so nothing is skipped (D-492). A rewording and the follow-up go through `ai::api::accept_question` (the pure AI-019 check; no AI call is made here, so D-1030 (B) stays open for the call itself); `askhava-intake` now depends on `askhava-ai`, which `kit/layers.json` allows. Conflict 1: INT-039 says "Not sure" on every question and also gives the smell question's exact text with three options (TD-INT-18); the exact text wins for the smell list and "not sure" is still accepted as a reply. Conflict 2: INT-039 and TD-INT-18 say the smell question follows "any numbered smell answer in any set", while TD-INT-24 says a boat "Fuel smell" answer sends nothing extra; read together, it follows a smell answer that does not name its kind (`asks_smell_kind`: "smell" first or after "or", "a", "strange", "odd", "weird"), it is asked at most once per run, and a set that already holds the smell list (hvac `smell_kind`) asks it through its own `ask_if`. Reason: the decide-and-log rule (`BUILD_BRIEF.md:539`); both tests then hold. Source: `docs/spec/intake.md:43`; `docs/test-design.md:273`; `docs/test-design.md:276`; `docs/test-design.md:279`; D-492; D-1030; D-1037; D-1053.
- **D-1270** Question (T156; re-decides void D-1038): what are INT-040's confidence levels before a real model exists? Choice: the keyword reading scores 1.0 when one trade and exactly one job type of it are named, 0.5 for one trade with none or several, 0.0 for several trades (`keyword_scored`); the high-confidence setting defaults to `HIGH_CONFIDENCE` 0.8 and is passed in by the caller (no `ASKHAVA_*` key yet: nothing reads it until the conversation wiring, D-999, adds one). `decide` goes on only when the keyword reading and, with AI on, the AI reading agree on trade and job type at or above it; otherwise it returns the INT-013 question built by `matching::second_opinion`, and with no trade from either it returns `NoTrade` for the INT-016 path. Reason: the keyword rules are certain only when they name one job type; the AI's confidence comes from its reading (AI-022). Source: `docs/spec/intake.md:44`; D-395; D-999; D-1038.
- **D-1271** Question (T156; re-decides void D-1039): what does the golden run measure, when does it run, and what about `test_set.csv`? Choice: `intake::api::run_golden` routes every `docs/catalog/intake_golden.yaml` row on the AI-off path (the build has no real model) and counts it right when `decide` goes on with no question at the row's trade and job type and the trade's set opens with the row's question; it stores total and right in `intake.golden_result` (migration `0083_intake_golden_result.sql`; `SELECT`, `INSERT` only for `askhava_app`) once per `catalog_version` (16 hex of a SHA256 over the compiled-in `categories.yaml`, `question_bank.yaml` and `intake_golden.yaml`), and the worker runs it at start-up, so a build with a changed catalog runs once. `test_set.csv` is not run yet: its trade and job-type codes are the knowledge base's own (`fridge`, `range_oven`) and map to no catalog job type; the mapping is a plan gap for the runner. Measured on this branch (a one-off print in the `routing_confidence` test, not committed): 21 of 370 rows (5%), far under the 90% target, because the keyword rules cover few trades and little Spanish; the report (T210) shows the number as it is. Source: `docs/spec/ops-recovery.md:44`; D-493; D-1039.
- **D-1272** Question (T156; re-decides void D-1040): who writes the "Job type not certain" mark and the INT-040 homeowner text? Choice: `after_fit` sets `Outgoing::not_certain` when "Not sure" or a second unusable reply keeps more than one candidate; `quotes::api::rules::match_job` with every candidate already reaches only a business covering all of them, so never one covering part of the job or outside the trade; `unsure_reach` returns `NoneCovers` when it reaches nobody. `quotes::api::CardParts` still has no marker line and the homeowner's "We couldn't tell which kind of <trade> job this is" text has no template on `main` (checked November 1); this task owns neither quotes nor customer copy, so both stay a plan gap for the runner (the card-line owner and the copy owner), and the OPS-041 email is T215's, the job-page display of the stored answers T213's. - **D-1273** Question (T156; re-decides void D-1041): the prompt's size budget is at most 7 files and 450 changed lines (`kit/prompts/T156.md:50`), and the change touches about 20 files and about 1,500 lines; is it split, what else does it rest on, and why should it hold on `main` this time? Choice: it stays one change. The 7 owned files carry the rules and their tests; the rest are what those files cannot work without: the crate's `lib.rs`, `api.rs`, `CLAUDE.md`, `Cargo.toml`, `Cargo.lock`, the two `.sqlx/` query files the golden run needs for the offline build, the worker's start-up call (`app/server/src/bin/worker.rs`; `app/server/Cargo.toml` already names `askhava-intake`), the `tests/mod.rs` line and the `docs/architecture.md`, `docs/decisions.md` and `docs/for-casey-review.md` entries (`BUILD_BRIEF.md:489`). About half the lines are tests; splitting the question set from routing confidence would leave `decide` without the set it opens (D-1271's "right" needs both). The budget is the plan's estimate; the overrun is reported for the runner. Golden run at start-up: `run_golden` is called before the worker loop and its error is returned, so a failed run (database down, a migration missing, a catalog that does not load) stops the worker on purpose; a low share never fails it. D-1198 (INT-021) rested on intake having no `askhava-ai` dependency; with this change it has one, but only for the pure `accept_question` check, so it still makes no AI call and every INT-021 step still runs at once (`app/intake/CLAUDE.md` updated). The earlier attempt: the runner's state records the red at 26b176e5 as check `tree`, with the attempt's reason "Ci: not green on head 7274a85" (the runner's update merge of `main` into that branch), and D-1053 found no check output tying the red to T156's own code; this attempt is rebuilt on the latest `main` (after T050, T054, T055, T187) and the full `bash scripts/smoke.sh` is run on the branch before hand-in. - **D-1274** Question (T208): where is the homeowner's card approval kept, when the prompt owns no migration, and how does the card sender know the card it sends is the one she was shown (INT-041, CARD-007, TD-INT-23, TD-AI-17)? Choice: as `intake.intake_answer` rows under `card.<job>`: `shown.<digest>` when a card is texted, `edit` on EDIT, `sent.<digest>` on SEND or at the end of the wait, the digest being the first 32 hex digits of the SHA256 of the card text (`card_digest`); the latest row is the state, read and written under the homeowner lock. The row holds a code, never her words (PRIV-001), and fits the table's `choice` pattern. Approval enqueues one `intake.cards_approved` `core.task` per job (dedupe key `intake.cards_approved.<job>`, payload job, request and digest) plus an `intake.card_approved` audit row in the same transaction (JOB-005); no handler exists yet, so like `intake.emergency_released` it waits for the card sender (the card-notice sender, T147), which must call `intake::api::approved_card` and send only a card for which it holds. The no-reply wait is an `intake.card_timer` task registered in `app/server/src/lib.rs`. Reason: no new table is in the prompt's scope; a digest proves character-for-character equality without storing the card twice. Source: `docs/spec/intake.md:45`; `docs/spec/job-cards.md:11`; `kit/prompts/T208.md`; D-430; D-434.
- **D-1275** Question (T208): INT-041's card text holds the card and the wait setting, but `app/messaging/src/tests/template_registry.rs` (not this task's) renders every template with a fixed value list that has no `card` or `minutes` value, so a new placeholder fails it. Choice: `card_shown` carries a literal `[card]` slot (`CARD_SLOT`) that `preview_text` replaces once, after rendering, with the gated card text (TXT-004 lets the INT-041 card sit outside a fixed template); the wait reads into `{time}` as "30 minutes" ("30 minutos"); `card_link` uses `{link}`. The wait is passed by the caller as `Preview::wait` (default `AUTO_SEND_AFTER`, 30 minutes), as CARD-009's word count is, and no `ASKHAVA_*` key is added until the conversation wiring reads it (D-999). The full text is counted with `count_segments` after the card is in; more than 2 segments sends the link text. The Spanish drafts use accents, so they are UCS-2 (recorded 3 segments for `card_shown` and `card_link`, 2 for `card_edit`); a Spanish card will nearly always go by link, for the native-speaker review to weigh. Reason: the shared test stays untouched and the spec's wording is kept exactly. Source: `docs/spec/intake.md:45`; `docs/spec/messaging.md:8`; D-460; D-491.
- **D-1276** Question (T208): what do EDIT and the replies do in detail, and what does the EDIT text say? Choice: a card reply is the whole message, any case, a trailing `.` or `!` ignored: SEND, OK, YES or ENVIAR approve the card last shown; EDIT or CAMBIAR store `edit`, which stops that card's timer, and queue `card_edit`; nothing goes until the caller shows the new card (its own wait starts then) and a SEND before that does nothing. An opt-out or HELP is never a card reply; "1042 YES" is not one (it is a pick). Which handler hears a plain YES (SAFE, a pick, this step) is the conversation dispatcher's order (D-999). An already approved card is never shown again (`Shown::AlreadySent`). The `card_edit` text, after the cold read (WORD-028) and the copy panel (WORD-029), is "Ask Hava: Sure, what should we change on request {job}? Tell us in one text and we'll show you how it looks now. Nothing goes out until you've seen it." (both reviewers flagged "new card" as our word, not hers, and the missing answer to "is the timer still running?"); the panel's other notes were on the spec's fixed INT-041 wording, which is kept. Reason: INT-041 says EDIT "asks what to change and shows the new card"; sending the old card after she asked to change it would break the approval it rests on (D-434). Source: `docs/spec/intake.md:45`; D-419; D-434.
- **D-1277** Question (T208): the prompt's budget is 6 files and 350 changed lines; the change is 5 owned files (`summary_step.rs`, its two test files, one-word visibility changes in `service.rs` and `handlers.rs`) plus the shared `lib.rs`, `api.rs`, `tests/mod.rs`, both template files, `app/server/src/lib.rs`, the crate `CLAUDE.md` and the three docs, about 750 lines with about 330 of them tests. Is it split, and who calls it? Choice: it stays one change: the step, its timer and its approved-card check only mean something together. `show_card` and `answer_card` have no caller until the conversation dispatcher (D-999) and the card sender (T147) exist; TD-INT-23's page case is TD-INT-36's (T095). The overrun is reported for the runner. Reason: `BUILD_BRIEF.md:485` weighed against a step that works and is tested as a whole; decide and log (`BUILD_BRIEF.md:539`). Source: `kit/prompts/T208.md`; D-999; D-1030.
- **D-1278** Question (T208 review): INT-041's 30 minutes ran from when the card text was queued, so a text held by quiet hours (or a slow send) could be auto-approved before she ever got it; when does the wait start, when the prompt owns no `messaging` file and no module may read another's tables? Choice: the `intake.card_timer` first watches the text through `messaging::api::delivery_status` (the public TXT-013 read): due at the show, it looks again every `RECHECK_AFTER` (1 minute) while the row is `Queued` or `Sending`; the first time it is `Sent` or `Delivered` it queues the end of the wait at that moment plus the wait, so she always has the card for the full wait (at most one minute more); only that waiting timer approves. A text that is `Failed` or `Undelivered` stops the timer and nothing goes until a SEND or a new show; what then tells Casey or the homeowner (an `ops` alert, a re-show) has no owning task yet, a plan gap for the runner. The exact send time is not exposed by `messaging::api`, so the one-minute look-again is used instead of reading `messaging.outbox.sent_at` across schemas. Reason: her approval (D-434) means nothing for a card she never saw; INT-041's "It goes out in 30 minutes" is read from her side. Source: `docs/spec/intake.md:45`; `app/messaging/src/service.rs` (`delivery_status`); `docs/architecture.md` section 4 rule 3; D-434; D-1274.
- **D-1279** Question (T208 review): (1) the same card text shown again after EDIT reused the first text's outbox key, so she got nothing, and the state went back to `shown.<digest>`, so the first show's timer approved early; (2) SEND was audited as the system with the auto-send's action; (3) state rows ordered by `answered_at` with random IDs and mixed caller clocks could read out of order. Choice: (1) the shown row is `shown.<digest>.<show>`, `<show>` the row's time in microseconds; the text's outbox subject adds an ID from `<show>`, so every show is its own text; each timer carries its show and does nothing unless the state is exactly its show's row. (2) SEND, OK, YES or ENVIAR audit `intake.card_approved` with `Actor::Homeowner`, as `service.rs` does for her other actions; the timer audits `intake.card_auto_sent` with `Actor::System`. (3) every `card.<job>` row is written at the caller's time or one microsecond after the job's latest card row, whichever is later (`models::latest_answer_time`), so the latest row is the last one written. Tested in `tests/integration/tests/summary_step.rs` (`td_int_23_the_same_card_shown_again_is_a_new_text_and_wait`, the audit checks). Reason: INT-041 "shows the new card" after EDIT; the audit log must say who approved (JOB-005). Source: `docs/spec/intake.md:45`; `app/intake/src/service.rs`; D-1274; D-1276.

- **D-1282** Question (T173): how do the journeys become part of `Ci` and the accessibility suite become `Ally`, and how is the stripe-mock image pinned? - **D-1285** Question (T056): what shape do the named mutants and their runner take, and where does `Ci` run them? Choice: `tests/mutation/mutants.toml` holds `[[group]]` tables (rule, file, package, optional `target`, default `--lib`, and the test filters) with a `mutants` list of `{ name, find, replace }`, any key overridable per mutant; `find` must occur exactly once in its file. `scripts/run_named_mutants.py` (`--all`, `--base REV`, `--only NAME`, `--list`) first runs each distinct test command once unmutated (a red baseline fails the run, so no kill is borrowed from an unrelated failure), then for each mutant writes the replacement in place, builds with `cargo test --locked -p <package> <target> --no-run` (a mutant that does not compile is `broken` and fails the run like a survivor), runs `-- <tests>`, and restores the file byte for byte in a `finally` (SIGTERM is turned into an exit so a job timeout restores it too); one shared `CARGO_TARGET_DIR`. With `--base` it runs each mutant whose rule `file` the branch changed or whose test files it changed (derived from `package`, `target` and `tests`: a `--lib` filter `tests::x` is `<crate>/src/tests/x.rs` or `x/` plus `src/tests/mod.rs`, a `--test y` target is `<crate>/tests/y.rs` or `y/` plus the crate's `src/` helpers), so a pull request that changes only a guarding test still proves the test kills its mutants; every mutant runs when the list or the script changed. Stale entries (review finding, T056): the list is protected but its `find` texts quote lines in files later build tasks own (T093 owns `app/messaging/src/optout.rs`, T236 `app/intake/src/service.rs`), so a later task's ordinary edit of a quoted line would otherwise fail its own `Ci` on a file it may not touch. So with `--base`, when neither the list nor the script changed, a `find` that is missing or repeated (or a file that is gone) is printed `STALE` and that mutant skipped without failing the pull request; `--all` (nightly-main) and `--only` still fail on it, so the night after such a merge turns `main` red and the red-`main` protocol sends a harness task to update the list. A `replace` equal to its `find` always fails. Plan gap for the runner: no task owns keeping `tests/mutation/mutants.toml` in step with later edits of the rule files it quotes; a build task that edits a quoted line should be paired with a harness follow-up (or own the list entry), so `main` does not wait a night to learn of it. `ci.yml`'s `Checks` runs it as a step after the Rust tests (same target dir, Postgres already up) when the branch touches Rust, `tests/mutation/` or the script, on push only (a scheduled call from nightly-main skips it, as nightly-main runs the full list itself); `tests/mutation/mutants.toml` joins the cannot-be-deleted list (D-479), and `Checks`' timeout goes from 25 to 40 minutes for a branch that runs them all. The script is a new locked file (the scripts are blueprint, `docs/governance.md` section 1), so this change rewrites `kit/plan.lock` (`python3 scripts/check_plan_lock.py --write`). The full stage-2 list (50 mutants) ran locally in about 4 minutes. Reason: `docs/test-design.md:59`; BUILD_BRIEF.md:472. Source: D-481, D-479.
- **D-1286** Question (T056): what does nightly-main add, and does a cargo-mutants survivor fail the night? Choice: three jobs. `named-mutants` (Postgres, migrations, `run_named_mutants.py --all`) and `stripe-ips` (D-1288) are in `record`'s `needs`, so a survivor or an IP-list difference makes the recorded night `failure` (`kit/nightly.json` gains `named_mutants` and `stripe_ips` results) and so `main` red. `cargo-mutants` installs cargo-mutants 27.1.0 (`docs/architecture.md` section 11) and runs `cargo mutants --file <each cargo_mutants_files entry>` with the crates' own tests, uploading `mutants.out` as an artifact; it is report only and outside `record`: `docs/test-design.md:60` says every survivor is killed by a new test or listed in `tests/mutation/equivalent.toml` after an Opus review, no task owns that file yet (a plan gap for the runner), and failing every night on unreviewed survivors would hold `main` red with nothing to fix it. `app/payments/src/rules.rs` is left off `cargo_mutants_files` until it exists (T073), and so is `app/catalog/src/rules.rs`, which `docs/test-design.md:60` names but no task has written (the catalog crate has `service.rs`, `loader.rs`, `question_bank.rs` and `restricted_words.rs`, no `rules.rs`); cargo-mutants would refuse a missing file, so the entry joins the list with the task that writes the file. Report only covers survivors and timeouts (cargo-mutants exit 2 and 3); any other exit (a usage error, a red baseline, a crash) fails the job, so a broken run never reads as a clean report. Conflict with a locked line: `docs/governance.md:101` says "**Every night:** the full suite, randomized property tests, cargo-mutants on the rule modules; a red run makes `main` red", and `BUILD_BRIEF.md:472` that nightly-main fails on any surviving mutant; `docs/test-design.md:60` says "Every surviving mutant is either killed by a new test or listed in `tests/mutation/equivalent.toml` with the reason, after an Opus review", and that file has no owner. The choice: the named mutants (the list both lines can be met for today) decide the night and make `main` red; cargo-mutants runs every night on the rule modules but its survivors do not make `main` red until `tests/mutation/equivalent.toml` exists with its reviewed reasons, when a harness task adds the `cargo-mutants` job to `record`'s `needs`. The locked lines are not edited (CLAUDE.md rule 8); this is the gap the report names. Reason: a gate nobody can turn green is a stopped build, not a check. Source: `docs/test-design.md:60`, `docs/governance.md:101`, D-472, BUILD_BRIEF.md:472.
- **D-1287** Question (T056): which `docs/test-design.md` section 4 stage-2 mutants are in the list, and which are not? Choice: license filter (lines 66): every-candidate to any, the ticked check dropped, a subclassification read as its full class, `handyman_allowed` ignored, a pending-city-list handyman given the card, `>=` to `>` at $1,000, the midpoint for the top, both gas overrides (`never_handyman`'s gas words and `eligibility_for_request`'s block), the permit-type block, a card on a non-`active` daily check, the license end date ignored, the plain-keyword job types dropped after a trade answer; the license check at pick is T073's (TD-PICK-09, D-479). - **D-1300** Question (harness change, November 1, 2026; the coordinator's retry measurement): how can a task's first attempt pass `Ci` far more often? Finding: of 85 tasks DONE, 18 needed a second attempt (about 1M tokens each), and 10 failed a `Ci` step their worker never ran on its branch: "Plan lock and change rules" (`check_plan_lock.py` and `check_pr_change.py --base origin/main`, T047, T167, T184), "PII scan" (T176), "TypeScript checks and npm audit" (T227), the pytest step (T055) and the coverage floor (T020, T022, T033, T036). `scripts/smoke.sh` runs pytest, cargo and most plan checks, but not `check_pr_change.py`, eslint, `npm audit` or the coverage comparison; the runner smokes only `main`'s head (`runner/cycle.py` `_smoke`, `GitHubEnv.smoke_main`), and the prompt's "Definition of done" (`kit/prompts/TEMPLATE.md:76`) was advisory. In production `RUNNER_WORKER_CMD` is unset: the `backup-runner.yml` session runs the worker and calls `python3 -m runner --after`, so `--after` is the one hand-in path the runner controls. Choice: (1) new `scripts/prehandin.sh`: a quick part (the sources fingerprint and file count, gitleaks when on the path, `pii_scan`, `trace_spec`, `validate_tasks`, `check_catalog`, `check_legal_docs`, `check_ai_smell`, `check_copy`, `check_code_docs`, `check_rust_rules`, `check_crates`, `check_plan_lock`, `gen_prompts.py --check`, `Ci`'s skip guard, then `check_pr_change.py --base <main> --branch <branch>`; about 12 s measured, no network) and, unless `--quick`, the extras `Ci` adds by its own path rules (the `RUST_PATHS` and `NPM_PATHS` patterns equal `ci.yml`'s, `tests/test_prehandin.py`): `npx eslint .` and `npm audit --audit-level=low` (`Ci`'s exact flags) when the npm tree changed, cargo-audit and cargo-deny when Rust changed and both tools are on the path. It does not re-run pytest, cargo or tsc (smoke does; the worker runs both scripts). (2) The prompt: `kit/prompts/TEMPLATE.md:76` and `:85` say, in place (no line moves), to run smoke, commit, then the gate last until `prehandin: green`; every prompt is regenerated. (3) The runner enforces it: `GitHubEnv.collect_result` runs main's copy of the gate (`prehandin`; a branch cannot weaken it) with `--quick` in a detached worktree of the submitted head (`PREHANDIN_ROOT`, `PREHANDIN_TIMEOUT` 240 s, inside `--after`'s 600-second call) after `_hand_in_in_order` and before any review record or push. Only exit 1 is red: the hand-in becomes `tests_failed` with `PREHANDIN_RED` and the output's last 30 lines (redacted with `TOKEN_LIKE`, ANSI removed, at most 3,000 characters). A missing gate on main, a dry run, a worktree git cannot make, a timeout or any other exit is logged and lets the hand-in through, so the gate never fails work for a reason that is not the work's. (4) A fix round in the same session: `cycle.after_handoff` takes a `hold` callable; `runner/__main__.py` `hold_red_gate` holds a red hand-in up to `PREHANDIN_HOLDS` (2) times per hand-off file, counting in `.git/runner_handoff.json` and keeping the last output there. A held `--after` writes nothing to `claude/kit-state`, keeps the lease and the task IN_PROGRESS, prints `runner: prehandin_red` and the output, and keeps the hand-off (`AFTER_KEEPS_HANDOFF`). `backup-runner.yml` prompt step 5b gives the output to a new foreground worker on the same branch, has the reviewer read the fix and calls `--after` again. The third red is a normal failed attempt with the gate output as `last_failure` (D-1263's path); a session that ends without handing in after a hold gets that output appended to the safety step's log. Without a hand-off file (`RUNNER_WORKER_CMD`, tests) nothing is held. No existing test changed; new tests are in `tests/test_prehandin.py`. A full `gen_prompts.py` regenerate refreshed 78 stale budgets (`main` itself failed `--check --strict` with 32 problems before this change), but it measures three DONE build tasks over the 45% limit: T038 46, T156 49, T208 48 (the same on `main` regenerated, from `docs/architecture.md` growth). Their stored values are kept (40, 39, 39), so `validate_tasks.py` and `gen_prompts.py --check` pass and `--check --strict` reports only those three; whether DONE tasks should join `CONTEXT_LIMIT_HISTORY` is left for a plan change (`docs/for-casey-review.md`). (5) Coverage is left out, measured in this session with the pinned `nightly-2026-10-15` and cargo-llvm-cov 0.9.1, using `Ci`'s exact command and a local Postgres: toolchain install 22 s, cold run 353 s, warm rerun 267 s, 5.0 GB target (`Ci`'s Coverage job takes 175 s with its cache). That adds 4.5 to 6 minutes beside smoke, past the 600-second call and the ~3–4 minute allowance, so it stays `Ci`-only, with a follow-up in `docs/for-casey-review.md`. Locked files changed: `scripts/prehandin.sh` (new), `kit/prompts/TEMPLATE.md`, `docs/governance.md` (one matrix row, in place), the regenerated prompts' template text; `kit/plan.lock` rewritten. Also `runner/github_env.py`, `runner/cycle.py`, `runner/__main__.py`, `.github/workflows/backup-runner.yml`, `docs/architecture.md` (section 12's smoke bullet, not a locked section), `docs/ai-operating-manual.md` (section 5 step 6, in place). Numbered by the interim rule (D-1144): max(`next_decision` 1290, `main`'s highest D-1283 + 1, the open plan PR's highest D-480 + 1) + 10 = D-1300. (6) Independent review, folded in before merge: a check script the head lacks (main added it later) is skipped with "skipped: <script> not on this head", as `Ci` on that branch would, and the hold text tells the session to merge origin/main in with a plain merge; a git problem (no such base, no merge base) exits 3, never 1, and is let through; the gate output is redacted with `scripts/pii_scan.py`'s key, phone and email patterns as well as `TOKEN_LIKE` (`GATE_REDACT`, loaded by path, empty if it cannot load); step 5b names the hand-off's `model` and the never-create-reset-rebase rule; workers keep the full mode, because the backup job has network and npm (its smoke runs `npm ci`), while the runner's own run stays `--quick` and offline. Reason: a check that fails in the worker's session costs one fix; the same failure in `Ci` costs a whole attempt. Source: `BUILD_BRIEF.md:69`; `BUILD_BRIEF.md:240`; `BUILD_BRIEF.md:246`; `BUILD_BRIEF.md:249`; `kit/prompts/TEMPLATE.md:76`; `kit/prompts/TEMPLATE.md:85`; `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (Checks job); `scripts/smoke.sh`; D-476; D-582; D-583; D-1178; D-1263.
- **D-1290** Question (T213): what does `quotes` own of the business job page (CARD-023), when the approved card is not stored in `quotes`, the intake answers live in `intake.intake_answer` and the page is rendered by a portals route (T148's, D-491)? Choice: `quotes::api::job_page(db, (job, business), &PageParts)` returns the data only, as a `JobPage` with private fields: the approved `JobCard` (its text, town, place and screened photo IDs, so the photo and concept-image slots T090 and T212 fill travel with it), every intake answer as (question, answer) wording and the details she adds later (JOB-010), each answer and detail through `final_gate` (CARD-008, CARD-010), and the sent and quote counts read now in one statement (`models::page_counts`). "Sent" counts the job's card rows until T147's provider-accepted count exists (CARD-019 to CARD-021); "quotes so far" counts confirmed, unwithdrawn quotes (PICK-002, PICK-006). No homeowner contact field exists on the page: the share stays with `picks` and `portals` (PICK-022). `PageParts` and `JobPage` have hand-written `Debug` that leaves out her words (R6). Not built here: the email to card holders when she adds details (JOB-010), which D-874 flagged for T213 but which needs `messaging`'s email path; it stays a plan gap for the runner. Reason: CARD-023, D-434, D-491, D-874, D-1030.
- **D-1291** Question (T213): which templates are "homeowner update texts after intake" for TXT-040's scan, and how are a sentence and a word counted? Choice: `quotes::api::UPDATE_TEXTS` lists the quote-update templates: `first_quote` and `all_quotes_in` as `Shape::Fixed` (TXT-016 and TXT-042 fix their wording: 20 words a sentence, her page link, no quote details, TXT-016's fee, LIST and Terms lines being part of that fixed wording), `quote_update` as `Shape::Update` (TXT-017 gives only an example, so 15 words a sentence, the link and no details) and `quote_list` and `quote_list_end` as `Shape::List` (the LIST reply, TXT-031: 20 words, details allowed, no link required since the quotes are in the text). A sentence ends at ".", "?" or "!" before a space or the end, or at a line break; the "Ask Hava:" opening (WORD-008) is not counted; a `{name}` placeholder or a link is one word, and a word needs a letter, digit or "{". A quote detail is a "$" or any placeholder other than `job`, `quoted`, `count` and `link`. `check` judges one template or rendered text and `scan` every listed template in both languages. The other homeowner texts after intake (`request_out`, `no_quotes_yet`, the `closed_*` and `text_pick_*` texts) are wordings other requirements fix without a page link (TXT-032, JOB-010, JOB-011, PICK-015); they are held to the WORD-029 20-word limit only, as `Shape::Capped` entries in the same scan (D-1293; `scripts/check_copy.py` does not read the message templates).
