- **D-1292** Question (T213): which TD-TXT-25 cases are here, and was the budget kept? Choice: `app/quotes/src/tests/update_texts.rs` holds the template scan (every listed template passes in English and Spanish), the planted sentences (21 words fail and 20 pass under a fixed wording; 16 fail and 15 pass otherwise), the link and quote-detail cases, the rendered first-quote and update texts and the homeowner audience of each listed template; TD-TXT-25's Spanish TXT-041 line is T162's (it lists TD-TXT-25 too). TD-CARD-12 is T212's; `tests/integration/tests/job_page.rs` holds this task's CARD-023 data cases (card, answers and later details without contact, current counts, no page without a card). No template wording changed, so no customer copy changed. The 5 owned files changed plus the shared `api.rs`, `lib.rs`, `tests/mod.rs`, the crate `CLAUDE.md`, `docs/architecture.md`, this file, `docs/for-casey-review.md` and one `.sqlx/` file. The 350-line budget was not kept: about 655 lines changed, of which 250 are the two test files, 38 the generated `.sqlx/` file and 32 the documents; the code is about 340 lines, most of it `///` documentation the code-docs rule requires (the same overrun T056 logged, D-1289). Reason: D-491, D-493, `BUILD_BRIEF.md:485`.
- **D-1293** Question (T213, review finding): the first D-1291 said `scripts/check_copy.py` holds the texts after intake that are not quote updates to the 20-word limit, but it does not read `app/messaging/templates/*.json`; and how does a new homeowner template not slip past the scan? Choice: `UPDATE_TEXTS` gains `Shape::Capped` entries (20 words a sentence only; no link required and no quote-detail check, since other requirements fix their wording) for `request_out`, `request_out_held`, `request_out_today`, `request_out_slow`, `no_quotes_yet`, `closed_no_quotes`, `closed_no_pick`, `closed_no_quote_left`, `text_pick_terms`, `text_pick_which` and `text_pick_done`, and they pass. `quotes::api::NOT_UPDATE_TEXTS` names every other homeowner template (consent, opt-out, HELP and safety texts; intake questions and replies before the request goes out; the card review texts; the command replies that are not updates), and `td_txt_25_every_homeowner_template_is_scanned_or_left_out` fails when a homeowner template is in neither list or in both, so a new one must be placed. `Shape::needs_link` and `Shape::plain` (identical) become one `points_to_page`; `sentences` and `words` are crate-private. A rendered text's link counts only when it is her quote page, `https://askhava.com/q/<token>` (PICK-010); a Terms or help link, or the bare `/q/` address, is `NoLink`. Reason: TXT-040, WORD-029, D-482. Source: D-1291.
- **D-1294** Question (T213, review finding): the job page's `quoted` (`models::page_counts`) counts confirmed, unwithdrawn quotes, while `models::window_state`'s `quoted` (T046, D-1051) counts every confirmed quote, withdrawn too; should they agree? Choice: no, the difference is kept on purpose. The job page's "quotes so far" says what the homeowner can still see, so it uses `shown_quotes`' rule (PICK-002, PICK-051); TXT-042's "X of N businesses quoted" says who quoted, so a business that withdrew still quoted. `PageCounts::quoted` documents this. Reason: CARD-019, CARD-023, TXT-042. Source: D-1051, D-1290.
- **D-1301** Question (T240, QH-001, QH-006, CON-028, D-1196, D-1215): `intake` must hold a homeowner job text to 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. in both Arizona and her area-code zone and skip an opted-out number, but it may not read her phone (the vault grants `messaging` and `calls` only); what does `messaging::api::send_window` answer? Choice: `send_window(db, vault, contact, now)` reads the phone under `messaging`'s existing send grant (`Reader::Messaging`, `Purpose::Send`; one audited read, outside a transaction), checks the one suppression list by the phone's blind-index digests, and answers `SendWindow::OptedOut` for a listed number, `NotTextable` for a number that is not `+1` or whose area code is not in the table (QH-003), else the pure `window(table, phone, now)`: `rules::decide` for a `Kind::Update` text (no QH-004 night exception), `Now` or `Hold { until }`, `until` being the next instant both zones are open. A broken area-code table or zone data is `OutboxError::Template` (no new error type). The phone never leaves the file. Reason: PRIV-004, D-1196; one decision rule (`rules::decide`) for every text. Source: D-1215.
- **D-1302** Question (T240, D-1030 (A)): the handler needs the `ID_SECRET` as an `IdSecret` for `jobs::api::quote_token::issue` and a `Vault` for `send_window`, but the worker builds neither, and the end-to-end and smoke runs start the worker without vault keys. Choice: `server::job_text_keys(settings, id_secret, pairs)` reads `VAULT_KEY` and `VAULT_INDEX_KEY` (the names `docs/architecture.md` section 8 and 9 use; not `ASKHAVA_*`, so `Settings::from_pairs` does not see them) and builds `intake::api::JobTextKeys` with `IdSecret::new(1, ID_SECRET)` (link key version 1: no setting names a version yet) and the same secret as the outbox key; without both vault keys it answers `None` in dev and CI, so `register_handlers(stream, texts)` registers no sender there (the events then dead-letter with `NO_HANDLER`, as before T240), and refuses to start in the test and live projects. `askhava-server` gains the `askhava-privacy` path dependency (the composition root may depend on every module). Reason: SEC-002 (a missing key stops the process where texts are real), D-481. Source: D-1030, D-1215.
- **D-1303** Question (T240, TXT-042, SEC-037, TXT-011, D-993): how is the link issued so a retried task never sends a dead link, and which request owns a job? Choice: `job_text_step` checks the version, the request, consent and the window first, then in one transaction re-checks the version, issues the token (`issue` revokes her earlier live link, as T052's page already states: "a new link makes the old one stop at once"), renders and enqueues the outbox row (subject: the job, so one row per template, contact and job); when the row was already queued the transaction is dropped, so the new token is rolled back and the queued link stays live. The token is in the outbox body only (cleared at send, D-850), never in the task payload or a log. The request is the newest conversation, open or closed, whose `job_id` is the job or that holds a `job.%` answer with the job's 32-hex ID; T049's `models::request_of_job` was not reused because it finds open requests only. A held event is queued again under `jobs.homeowner_text.<job>.<template>.<until in microseconds>`, so a repeated run queues it once. Reason: SEC-037, TXT-011, R11. Source: D-871, D-993.
- **D-1304** Question (T240, size budget): the prompt allows 450 changed lines in 5 owned files; the work came to about 830 in those files (`job_texts.rs` 295, `send_window.rs` 106, the three test files 428) plus about 150 in shared paths. Choice: kept, not split: more than half is tests (TD-JOB-03 and TD-QH-01 cases on the database: the held text, the link, the second run, the Pacific number, the dropped held text and the close text, consent and opt-out) and most of the rest is the `///` documentation `docs/code-docs.md` requires; the handler has no part that stands alone. Reported to the runner, as T213 and T056 did (D-1289). Reason: `BUILD_BRIEF.md:485`, D-473.
- **D-1305** Question (T240 review, PRIV-004, SEC-047, D-1301): `messaging::api::send_window` reads her phone once under `(Reader::Messaging, Purpose::Send)` and the audit row says `send` even when the answer is a hold to the next window, an opt-out or an area code outside the table, so no text goes out on that read; is there a more accurate purpose? Choice: no; the read stays `Purpose::Send` and the limitation is recorded here. `privacy`'s `Purpose` (`app/privacy/src/models.rs`) holds `Send`, `Inbound`, `BridgeCall`, `CallReadback`, `Release`, `OwnRecord`, `CallbackAlert`, `HelpRequest` and `Rotation`; none names "decide whether a text may go", and `Send` is the purpose the grant table gives `messaging` for the phone. Adding a purpose (say `SendCheck`) means a new grant, its audit action name and a `privacy` change T240 does not own. The read is part of a send attempt: a held event reads again at its new time and an audit reviewer sees one `send` read per attempt, not one per text sent. Listed for the plan: a later `privacy` task may add a narrower purpose for window and suppression checks. `send_window`'s `///` comment states this. Reason: PRIV-004, SEC-047, PRIV-002 (intake never reads the number, D-1196). Source: D-1301.
- **D-1306** Question (T240 review, SEC-002, D-1302): `server::job_text_keys` answered "missing VAULT_KEY" when only `VAULT_INDEX_KEY` was missing, and with one vault key set but not the other it quietly registered no sender in dev and CI. Choice: a blank value counts as unset; neither key set is `None` (no sender) in dev and CI and the error "missing VAULT_KEY and VAULT_INDEX_KEY" in the test and live projects; one key without the other is an error in every environment, naming the missing one ("VAULT_KEY set without VAULT_INDEX_KEY", "VAULT_INDEX_KEY set without VAULT_KEY"), since a half-set pair is a configuration mistake, never a choice to run without texts. In-crate tests in `app/server/src/lib.rs` cover each environment, both half-set pairs, a weak `ID_SECRET`, and `register_handlers` registering the sender under `jobs::api::TEXT_KIND` only with keys; `app/intake/src/tests/job_texts.rs` covers `run_job_text` refusing a bad payload with its fixed sentence. Reason: SEC-002 (a bad configuration stops the process, naming a key, never a value). Source: D-1302.
- **D-1317** Question (harness change, November 2, 2026; the coordinator's B-to-A+ plan items 1 and 2): workers lose their prompt cache during the smoke wait and load large tool results early; what changes? Measured from T173's job log (job 124999533662, Claude Code 2.1.316): the worker started `scripts/smoke.sh` with `run_in_background` and tried `sleep 240` (refused by the harness), polled, then ran the second smoke in the foreground with a 3,600,000 ms timeout; the Bash call limit is 600 s, so it ran past it into the background and the worker sat idle 6 min 20 s (22:46:02 to 22:52:23); its next turn wrote 144,460 tokens of 5-minute cache, the whole context (the worker's cache writes are all `ephemeral_5m`, the orchestrator's `ephemeral_1h`). Choice: (1) `kit/prompts/TEMPLATE.md` Start step 2 starts smoke with the Bash tool's `run_in_background` (a shell `&` can be killed with the call) and checks it with a `timeout 200` until-loop, at most 4 minutes a call; with no `exit=` line by about 15 minutes the worker stops smoke, reports and does not hand in, and it stops smoke too if it leaves early (a foreground smoke is not safe: it may exceed the 600 s call limit, smoke's own budget being 540 s, D-1178, and then it moves to the background silently); End step 1 points to it. (2) `.github/workflows/backup-runner.yml` sets `CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_PROMPT_CACHE_TTL: "1h"` on the session step. The docs: subagents "fall outside the main-conversation TTL bucket, so they get five minutes even on a subscription until you choose a longer one", and the bucket's environment variable is the second control in precedence after `FORCE_PROMPT_CACHING_5M` (code.claude.com/docs/en/prompt-caching, "Which TTL each request gets" and "Choose the TTL yourself"; code.claude.com/docs/en/env-vars, which requires v2.1.242 or later). Verified here with the same CLI version: a haiku `-p` run with one foreground subagent wrote the subagent's 36,244 cache tokens as `ephemeral_1h` with the variable and none as 1h without it. A 1-hour write is billed at 2x base input against 1.25x for 5 minutes (platform.claude.com prompt-caching pricing), so a worker's writes cost about 60% more per token (0.75x base more on every write, about 108k base-equivalent a task on T173's numbers). With the poll in place the idle gap should mostly disappear, so the 1-hour lifetime pays only if gaps over 5 minutes still happen in more than about 60% of tasks (a long build, a slow test, a reviewer wait). It is kept for now, and the first 5 tasks after it merges decide: their `ephemeral_1h` writes against the re-writes after a gap that the 5-minute lifetime would have cost; if the gaps are gone, drop the variable. The pacer's weights count a cache write as 1.0 whatever its lifetime (`kit/pacing.json`), and plan usage, not the dollar price, is what is spent; whether the plan counts 1h writes higher is not published. (3) Start steps 2, 3 and 5 of the old routine are dropped (read `BUILD_BRIEF.md` sections 2 and 7 and `CLAUDE.md`; read `kit/state.json`, `PROGRESS.md` and 20 commits; confirm the task is next): `CLAUDE.md` loads by itself, the prompt pastes the rules, requirements, tests, decisions and cited lines, and the runner claimed the task from the state; the "matches the next task in `kit/state.json`" phrase stays in step 1 for `tests/test_gen_prompts.py`, and step 1 says the prompt wins over `CLAUDE.md`'s reading list because it pastes the rules the task needs. A retry's `last_failure` used to reach the worker through the state it read; `backup-runner.yml` step 3 now has the session give the hand-off's `last_failure` to the worker word for word, before the task prompt. New step 5: never `cat` or `Read` all of a file over 200 lines (`wc -l` gives the count); `grep -n`, then `sed -n 'A,Bp'` or Read with offset/limit; keep outputs under about 8,000 characters. The template is 7,647 bytes against main's 7,651, so no prompt's measured `context_pct` changed (229 prompts compared with `main` at 230517c: every change 0, tokens -2 to +2). `kit/tasks.json` does change: 68 stored budgets move to their measurements (most by 4 points). Those were stale on `main`: T213 (#241) and T240 (#242) grew `docs/architecture.md`, `main`'s own measurements already equal the new values, and a full `gen_prompts.py` on `main` alone writes the same numbers; `--check --strict` goes from 72 problems on `main` to 4. The stored budgets of T170 (50), T038 (40), T156 (39) and T208 (39) are kept as #240 kept them; those 4 are the remaining strict problems. (4) `backup-runner.yml` sets `BASH_MAX_OUTPUT_LENGTH: "15000"`. The documented control for the inline size is the `bashOutputMaxChars` setting (v2.1.261+, 4,000 to 128,000); `BASH_MAX_OUTPUT_LENGTH` alone "only sizes the read-back window" (the CLI's own setting text) and the tools reference says it "doesn't raise the inline ceilings". Tested here: in a subagent, `seq 1 4000` (18,893 characters) arrived inline by default and as a 2,000-character preview plus a saved-file path with `BASH_MAX_OUTPUT_LENGTH=15000`, and the same with `--settings '{"bashOutputMaxChars": 5000}'` for 3,000 numbers, so in 2.1.316 the variable does lower the inline cap; the variable was kept over a `settings` input because it is one line beside the cache setting and the docs promise it only for the read-back window, which a future CLI may make literal; if a run shows 30,000-character results again, move it to the action's `settings: '{"bashOutputMaxChars": 15000}'`. The orchestrator's own runner output (the hand-off JSON, 27k characters in T173's run, mostly the state diff) also passes 15,000, so step 3 tells the session to read the hand-off from `.git/runner_handoff.json` when the output was saved to a file. The runner's `branch_note` and step 3b now name start step 3, not 6. Changed: `kit/prompts/TEMPLATE.md`, every `kit/prompts/T###.md` (regenerated), `.github/workflows/backup-runner.yml`, `runner/__main__.py` (the step number in `branch_note`), `docs/architecture.md` (section 12's smoke bullet, not a locked section), `docs/ai-operating-manual.md` (a worker note after section 2), `docs/for-casey-review.md`, `kit/plan.lock`. Numbered by the interim rule (D-1144): first D-1316 (max(`next_decision` 1306, `main`'s highest D-1300 + 1, the open plan PR's highest D-480 + 1) + 10), re-taken after `main` gained D-1301 to D-1306 (T240, #242): max(1306, D-1306 + 1, D-480 + 1) + 10 = D-1317. Expected saving (the plan's measurement, not re-measured): 0.15 to 0.2M weighted per task from the cache, and as much again from the smaller early context. Reason: an expired cache re-writes the whole context, and a large tool result is read again on every later turn. Independent Opus review (approve with fixes) folded in: the retry's `last_failure`, the corrected `kit/tasks.json` statement, the bounded smoke poll, the cache arithmetic, `wc -l` and the reading-list precedence. Source: `BUILD_BRIEF.md:240`; `BUILD_BRIEF.md:493`; `kit/prompts/TEMPLATE.md:14`; `kit/prompts/TEMPLATE.md:83`; D-503; D-583; D-1178; D-1300.
- **D-1328** Question (harness change, November 2, 2026): T241's first attempt (run actions-41375403001, 02:02Z to 02:50Z) finished its work, passed the pre-hand-in gate (`pre-hand-in gate on 4377cd91: exit 0`) and was still failed with `no model evidence found; a run without evidence fails`, costing one attempt and about 1.8M plan tokens; why, and what changes? Cause, from the job log: the runner session ran `python3 -m runner --after --worker-agent a2999ce7af66ed1d2,a988abbda82417227 --reviewer-agent ...`, both worker agent IDs joined by a comma in one flag, where T240's session had repeated the flag; `find_transcripts` globbed `agent-a2999...,a988....jsonl`, found nothing, and `verify.check_model` read the empty evidence as "no model ran". The worker had not pushed either (the head 4377cd91 is not on GitHub), so the attempt also left no branch. Choice: `runner/github_env.py` gains `agent_id_list`, which splits every `--worker-agent` and `--reviewer-agent` value on commas and spaces, drops an `agent-` prefix and duplicates, accepts only `[0-9a-z]+` ids (a value such as `*` would otherwise be a glob over every transcript) and prints `runner: not an agent id, ignored: ...` for anything else, and `find_transcripts` reads through it and prints `runner: no transcript for agent <id>` for an id that matches no file, so the job log shows the gap (before, a mistyped id was dropped silently and the check passed on the other transcript); `backup-runner.yml` step 5 says "one `--worker-agent` per worker agent, the fix-round worker included"; a test covers the joined form (`tests/test_runner_live.py`). Not changed: the rule that a hand-in without evidence fails (D-170) stays; a lenient parser removes the way this one was lost, not the rule. Changed: `runner/github_env.py`, `tests/test_runner_live.py`, `.github/workflows/backup-runner.yml`, `docs/for-casey-review.md` (`kit/plan.lock` does not cover these paths and is unchanged). Numbered by the interim rule (D-1144): max(`next_decision` 1312, `main`'s highest D-1317 + 1, the open plan PR's highest D-480 + 1) + 10 = D-1328. Reason: the evidence check is there to prove which model ran, not to punish the shape of a command line; the attempt's work is lost either way, so the retry starts over on the same ladder. Independent Opus review (approve) folded in: the missing-transcript line, the id check against glob characters, the docstring naming both flags. Source: `BUILD_BRIEF.md:261`; D-170; D-503; D-1300.
- **D-1361** Question (plan change, November 2, 2026): the plan-health check (D-1350, `scripts/plan_health.py` on `claude/harness-plan-health`) reports that two DONE tasks own a file that is not on `main`, `app/catalog/src/tests/restricted_words.rs` (T024) and `migrations/0068_quotes_card_text.sql` (T045), so T057, which depends on T024, would be held as a plan gap; and that T148, T151 and T104 cite `tests/integration/test_emergency_card_email.py` and `tests/integration/test_no_business_calls.py` only through D-353, pasted as history (superseded by D-491, `kit/superseded_decisions.json:45`), which no task owns and which do not exist. Neither `.py` path is cited anywhere else (`docs/spec`, `docs/test-design.md`, `kit/tasks.json`); D-353 also stays listed on the DONE tasks T039 (#178) and T152 (#175), whose prompts still paste the paths as history, with no effect (a DONE task is not checked for decision paths and is not rebuilt). Numbered by the interim rule (D-1144): max(`next_decision` 1312, `main`'s highest D-1328 + 1, the open plan PR's highest D-480 + 1, and the numbers held by the T242 roadmap change, D-1339, and the plan-health change, D-1350, + 1) + 10 = D-1361. Independent Opus review (approve with fixes) folded in: the TD-CARD-11 reason, the T039/T152 clause. Source: `BUILD_BRIEF.md:261`; `BUILD_BRIEF.md:485`; D-353; D-491; D-840; D-1030; D-1033; D-1350.
- **D-1350** Question (harness change, November 2, 2026; the coordinator's A+ plan item 3, "plan-health check before a claim"): a worker that starts a task with a hole in its plan spends an attempt finding it (a test file no task writes, a dependency's file missing on `main`, a context budget over its limit); how does the runner catch that before the claim, and what accounting and limit rules change with it? Choice: (1) New `scripts/plan_health.py`, importable and a command (`T### [--json]`, `--all-eligible`, `--all`, `--state PATH`; exit 0 clean, 1 gaps, 2 unreadable inputs). It reuses `gen_prompts.context_bytes`/`percent`/`load_sources`, `validate_tasks.context_limit` and `check_pr_change.task_paths_check` (so `runner/verify.py check_paths`) rather than restating them. Checks: (a) the prompt on disk plus the loaded files, against the task's limit; (b) every backticked repository path in the requirement sentences and test-design rows the task names, and every file under its `reads`, is owned by the task, an ancestor in the dependency graph or the shared list, or exists; a path named by a live decision the prompt pastes only needs some task in the graph to own it or to exist (a superseded decision, pasted as "history only, build <successor>", never holds a task), because decisions name later tasks' files as background (the deploy notes from T013's SEC-040 decision, the README) and holding those would be noise (33 tasks name `docs/deploy.md` through decisions alone); the runner-written files (`kit/state.json` and the like) are never a gap; (c) each dependency DONE or SKIPPED, and each regular file a DONE dependency owns exists. `--all` drops the "dependency not DONE" lines (they only mean "not eligible yet") and adds every DONE task's missing owned files, since a DONE task with no waiting dependent is the plan's gap but no claim's. (2) `runner/cycle.py`: `Config.plan_health` (the checker, built once per run in `runner/__main__.py` with `pending_ok=True`, because `eligible` already judged dependency status and allows a proof-waiting cleanup dependency, D-551) and `plan_health_pass`, called in `_next_step` after the resync sort and before the smoke and the pacer: every candidate is checked (the pacer may pass over the first sound one); a task with problems stays QUEUED, `attempts` untouched, nothing in `history`, gets `plan_gap: {at, problems}` (at most 10 problems kept, then "and N more") and drops out of the candidates, so the next sound task is claimed, or the cycle ends `idle` when none is; an unchanged mark writes nothing; a sound task loses a stale mark, so a plan fixed on `main` frees the task with no state edit; FIX-MAIN is never checked; a checker that raises holds nothing (the claim goes ahead as before) and leaves the task's entry, any mark included, unchanged; a changed problem list keeps the mark's first `at`, so STATUS.md's "since" is when the hold began; a mark is judged only while its task is a candidate, so one that stops being eligible keeps its last mark in STATUS.md until its next turn (kept on purpose: the problem usually still stands). This builds on D-1058, which made a first "not owned by" hand-in free: that covered gaps a worker found by tripping over them; this one finds them before any worker starts. `plan_gap` is a new task key, so `kit/state_schema.json` gains it (object with `at` in the runner's time format and `problems` an array of strings); `scripts/check_state.py --state` passes a copy of the live state carrying one and fails a malformed one (D-1156). STATUS.md's "Needs attention" lists each task with a mark that is not DONE or SKIPPED as "PLAN GAP T### (since …, no attempt used; a plan change fixes it): …" (`runner/github_env.py` `_plan_gap_line`). (3) `gen_prompts.context_bytes` counts a read of `docs/architecture.md` as its section 2 (the crate layout every prompt's start step 4 names) plus the lines naming the task's `module` in backticks or as `app/<module>/` and every section the prompt itself cites ("architecture section 8", "sections 2, 4 and 11", "sections 7 to 12"; `cited_sections`) (`architecture_bytes`), not the whole 177,167-byte file (about 22 points of the window), which 215 tasks read and workers read only by section and range (D-1317's step 5); a task owning it would count it whole (none does). Measured: 215 stored budgets fall by 6 to 19 points (median 17), and counting the cited sections raises T057, T075, T100 and T142 to 23, T076 to 11 and T126 (cleanup, limit 65) to 60; T038 40→29, T156 39→33, T208 39→32 now fit their 45% limit, so their measured values are stored instead of the hand-kept ones. (4) `--strict` keeps judging every task: rather than skip DONE tasks (which would let any finished task's record drift unseen), T170 joins `CONTEXT_LIMIT_HISTORY` (75%): it finished on October 30 reading the whole brief, measures 51% today and stores 50, history like T005 to T007's; `tests/test_validate_tasks.py` pins the set and now names T170. `gen_prompts.py --check --strict` goes from 4 problems on `main` to 0. (5) Item 4 of the plan (trim T170 and T172; move T170 to Opus) does not apply: both are DONE on `claude/kit-state` (T172 on October 29, T170 on October 30, PR #93); the hand-off's "unstarted but eligible" line was stale. `attempt_model` runs the task's own model on attempts 1 and 2 and Opus on the last, so an unstarted non-Opus task would start on its own model; the only one left is T136 (Haiku, docs), left as it is (a judgement for the overseer). (6) `kit/pacing.json` `actions_minutes` is not changed here: it is a note plus four numbers that no script reads, so "unlimited" is not a single value; item 5 rewrites it. First run (`python3 scripts/plan_health.py --all` against `claude/kit-state` at `next_decision` 1312), before the review: T148, T151 and T104 each named `tests/integration/test_emergency_card_email.py` and `tests/integration/test_no_business_calls.py` through D-353 (superseded by D-491, pasted as history), which no task owns and which do not exist; superseded citations never hold since the review, so these three are clean with no plan change; T089 names `docs/deploy.md` through SEC-040 (owned by T135, not its ancestor); T057 has DONE dependency T024 whose `app/catalog/src/tests/restricted_words.rs` is absent; DONE T024 and DONE T045 (`migrations/0068_quotes_card_text.sql`) own absent files. None is fixed here. T057 will be held as a plan gap until a plan change drops the absent file from T024's `owns` or restores it; T089 is held only when it becomes eligible. D-1361 (#246, merged before this one) then took the never-written files off T024 and T045, so after the merge `--all` reports T089 alone; this entry sits after D-1361 because the log is append-only. `--all-eligible` at the time: no candidate (T241 in progress). Changed: `scripts/plan_health.py` (new), `scripts/gen_prompts.py`, `scripts/validate_tasks.py`, `runner/cycle.py`, `runner/__main__.py` (`plan_health_checker`: a checker that cannot be built prints `runner: plan health unavailable: <error>` and the runner runs without the check), `runner/github_env.py`, `kit/state_schema.json`, `kit/tasks.json` and every `kit/prompts/T###.md` (regenerated), `tests/test_plan_health.py` (new), `tests/test_gen_prompts.py`, `tests/test_validate_tasks.py`, `docs/architecture.md` (section 12 only), `docs/ai-operating-manual.md` (section 7 step 5), `docs/for-casey-review.md`, `kit/plan.lock`. Numbered by the interim rule (D-1144): first D-1339 (max(`next_decision` 1312, `main`'s highest D-1328 + 1, the highest on an open claude/ plan PR, #55's D-480, + 1) + 10); renumbered before the first push because the overseer gave D-1339 to the parallel plan change `claude/plan-prewar-review` (T242): max(1312, D-1328 + 1, D-1339 + 1) + 10 = D-1350, used whether or not that PR is open yet, to avoid a collision. Independent Opus review (approve with fixes) folded in: the checker built inside a guard in `runner/__main__.py`; superseded decisions never hold; a raising check leaves the mark as it is; prompt-cited architecture sections counted; tests for FIX-MAIN, a later gapped candidate, the shared list, a gate, a superseded decision and the kept `at`; the kept first `at`; stale marks on tasks no longer eligible documented, not cleared. - **D-1339** Question (plan change, November 1, 2026; Casey's instruction in chat, `docs/reviews/pre-war-games-review-brief.md`, committed here word for word as the requirement; his answer on scope at 20:25 Phoenix: "We will run it small market first with the plan to expand."): where does a mandatory "PRE-WAR-GAMES COMPETITIVE GAP ANALYSIS & FEATURE READINESS REVIEW" sit, in the sequence current approved build → build verification → competitive gap and feature readiness review → approved necessary enhancements → verification of enhancements → war games (`docs/reviews/pre-war-games-review-brief.md:314`), without removing, reordering or silently changing an existing milestone? So the build and spec stay Lake Havasu City only, and the review treats expansion (businesses in markets with no sign-ups, growth without human work per job) as planning questions whose answers may become later plan changes, not a change to this build. **The hold.** The approved enhancements cannot be tasks yet, because their content is unknown. This hold is an owner stop added on Casey's instruction, beyond the closed list of stops in `BUILD_BRIEF.md` section 16 (`BUILD_BRIEF.md:546` to `BUILD_BRIEF.md:551`, mirrored in `CLAUDE.md` "When Claude stops and asks Casey"); that list itself is unchanged by this decision. - **D-1307** Question (T241, November 2, 2026; SEC-016, SEC-039, TXT-012, CON-008, CON-018, D-861, D-999): how do Twilio's inbound-text and status webhooks reach the modules, in what order, and what does a failure answer? Choice: `server`'s `inbound_text::routes` adds `POST /webhooks/twilio/sms` and `POST /webhooks/twilio/status`; each builds the signed URL as `ASKHAVA_PUBLIC_BASE_URL` plus the request's path and query and passes only a delivery `adapters::api::verify_webhook` accepted (otherwise `refuse`: one log line with vendor and reason, 403). Each checked delivery runs in one database transaction (every module step opens its own savepoint), committed unless the database failed, answered 200, or 500 on a database error, so Twilio's retry finds nothing half done and the dedupe row and its effects commit together. An inbound text: `receive_inbound` (a repeat MessageSid stops), `privacy::api::read_inbound` over the raw `Body` (sole-word opt-out, HELP and START flags; the raw text goes no further), the sender (a linked business phone by `sender_business`, else the homeowner's vault contact, stored phone-only on her first text), `on_inbound_text` (an opt-out stops), `reply_to_help` (a HELP, INFO or AYUDA text stops after its reply; the reply also reaches a listed number, D-131, and any other text from a listed number stops, CON-016), then for a non-business number `intake::api::receive_reply`; a business phone's text stops after the HELP step (business replies are later tasks'). The provider's START (`Outcome::Resubscribed`) goes on to `receive_reply`, which opens a new request from the consent text (CON-015). A status callback runs `receive_status` alone. Kind: gap (no routing task existed, D-861). Reason: SEC-016, SEC-039, TXT-012, CON-008, CON-013, CON-015, CON-016, CON-018, D-861. Source: D-1215; D-1216.
- **D-1308** Question (T241; CON-018, CON-017, TXT-009, TXT-031, INT-002): the route must fill inputs no setting holds: the HELP reply's settings, the opt-out check's emergency flag and relation, and LIST's business names. Choice: `HelpSettings::new((2, 24), None, (None, To))`, D-887's example reply times, no away date and no help line, with the texting number taken from the delivery's `To` field (the Ask Hava number Twilio delivered to), until an owner setting holds them; the emergency flag is `intake`'s own 911-list screen of the scrubbed words (`intake::api::rules::check`), the screen `receive_text` runs anyway (INT-026), so `read_inbound` gets no emergency stems; a homeowner's relation is `Relation::OpenRequest`, since she has just written and TXT-009's "written first" holds for any reply; the business names are an empty list (`Webhooks::names`), as `businesses` holds no public name yet (D-1197), so LIST with a quoted job ends at `IntakeError::Quotes`, is logged ("intake") and answered 200 until a names source exists. `receive_reply` hears no opt-out or HELP text (both already answered by `messaging`), so neither restarts the no-reply wait. Kind: gap (no setting). Reason: CON-018, D-887, D-1197, INT-026. Source: `docs/spec/messaging.md:35`.
- **D-1309** Question (T241; SEC-002, SEC-016, D-493, D-1216): the shape of `ASKHAVA_PUBLIC_BASE_URL` and where its routes are tested. Choice: an optional typed setting (`Settings::public_base_url`), trimmed and without a trailing slash, an `http` or `https` origin with a host and no query or fragment, passing `check_base_url` (`https` to a non-local host in live); `server::webhooks` builds the routes' state only when it is set, then requiring `ASKHAVA_TWILIO_AUTH_TOKEN` (through `TwilioConfig`), `ASKHAVA_ID_SECRET`, `VAULT_KEY` and `VAULT_INDEX_KEY`; unset it is no routes in dev and CI (the e2e server runs without it) and the start-up error "missing ASKHAVA_PUBLIC_BASE_URL" in the test and live projects, which Twilio must reach. Because a test crate may not depend on `server` (T175's layer rule), `tests/integration/tests/inbound_text_route.rs` compiles `app/server/src/inbound_text.rs` with `#[path]`, as `offdb_stream.rs` does, so the file names no `crate::` item. Kind: gap. Reason: SEC-002, SEC-016, D-493. Source: D-1216.
- **D-1310** Question (T241 review; TXT-031, INT-019, TXT-012, D-1197, D-1308): with no business names yet (`Webhooks::names` empty), LIST with a quoted job failed at `IntakeError::Quotes`, the route ended it after the once-per-MessageSid row committed, so the text was never handled and the 72-hour wait never restarted. Choice: `receive_reply` runs `answer_list` inside a savepoint; on `IntakeError::Quotes` the savepoint rolls back and the text goes on as a LIST with no quoted job (heard, then `receive_text`), so nothing is lost; any other error still fails the whole text. This replaces D-1308's "LIST with a quoted job ends at `IntakeError::Quotes`, is logged". Kind: fix. Reason: TXT-012, INT-019, D-1197. Source: T241 review finding 1.
- **D-1311** Question (T241 review; PRIV-016, SEC-018, CON-018, D-1306): how the route reports a module error after the duplicate check, when it builds the HELP settings, and how `server::webhooks` checks its keys. Choice: a non-database error from `messaging`, `privacy` or `intake` after `receive_inbound` (`Halt::Failed`) is logged at warn with the step and the error's variant name only (no value, phone, body or URL) and answered 200; the HELP settings are built only for a text `messaging::api::keyword` reads as HELP, INFO or AYUDA, so a bad `To` field stops no other text; `webhooks` checks `ASKHAVA_ID_SECRET` with `IdSecret::new` as `job_text_keys` does, and a half-set vault key pair names the missing key ("VAULT_KEY set without VAULT_INDEX_KEY" and the reverse), both unset "missing VAULT_KEY and VAULT_INDEX_KEY", as D-1306. Kind: fix. Reason: PRIV-016, SEC-018, D-1306. Source: T241 review findings 2, 3 and 5.

- **D-1362** Question (T057 stage-2 cleanup, November 2, 2026; BUILD_BRIEF.md:488): the scans found no unused dependency, no commented-out code and no TODO, but a duplicate-function scan (bodies of 4 or more non-comment lines, whitespace-normalized, across `app/`) found two duplicates in rule code: `messaging`'s `optout::number` repeated `service::recipient_phone` line for line (the vault read of a homeowner's phone under `Reader::Messaging`, `Purpose::Send`), and `ai`'s `schemas::is_format` repeated `privacy`'s scrubber list of Unicode format characters, kept apart by D-814 only because `privacy` did not export it; and two in tests, struct-literal fixture builders (`Inbound` in three `intake` test files, `Outgoing` in two `messaging` test files). - **D-1378** Question (T094, November 2, 2026; TXT-014, TXT-015, INT-023): TXT-014 says important texts are "retried up to 3 times over 30 minutes", TXT-015 that "when a homeowner's texts fail 3 times with no email on file, Casey gets a call-back alert"; when are the retries, what counts as the 3 failures, and what happens to the text row? Choice: every failed text (TXT-015) is retried 3 times, 10, 20 and 30 minutes after its first failure (`retries::RETRY_AFTER`, `next_step`); "fail 3 times" counts the 3 retries, so the give-up comes after the first send and its 3 retries have all failed (`Step::GiveUp` on the 4th failed send). `record_failure` sets the failure count from the outbox row's claim count, so a repeated call counts nothing twice. `give_up` marks the row with the new terminal status `failed` (body cleared, SEC-037; `models::claim` never takes it again) in one transaction with its outcome: an important text (`IMPORTANT_TEMPLATES`: `first_quote` and `caller_missed` now; the who's-calling text and the business confirm request join when their templates exist) is listed in `messaging.portal_notice` and, with an email on file, queued as a `text_failed` email holding the text as sent; a homeowner with no email on file gets a call-back, its due time in `messaging.text_retry.call_back_due` (24 hours for `Urgency::Urgent`, which the caller sets for "Today, it's urgent", an emergency and a 911-list request before "How soon?" is answered; `NO_RUSH_CALL_BACK` 4 days otherwise, passed in as the INT-023 setting) and an `ops.alert` `messaging.call_back_due` on the outbox row, High when urgent so it reaches the OPS-032 push, Normal otherwise; anything else simply ends `failed`. `give_up` refuses (`OutboxError::RecipientKind`, nothing changed) a `Reach` or an email `Recipient.audience` naming a kind other than the text's stored `recipient_kind`, so a homeowner's text is never emailed with a business footer or the reverse. The homeowner's email is looked up before the transaction opens, since the vault refuses a read inside one (PRIV-003, D-753). Quiet hours for a retry stay the caller's (`rules::retry`, QH-008). Reason: "over 30 minutes" read as evenly spaced retries ending at 30 minutes; one give-up point keeps TXT-014 and TXT-015 consistent. Source: `docs/spec/messaging.md:18`, `docs/spec/messaging.md:19`, `docs/spec/intake.md:27`; D-226, D-236, D-308.
- **D-1379** Question (T094; OPS-038, D-381): how is "above 90% of the email provider's daily sending limit" counted, when is "the reset", and what does a provider refusal for a limit do? Choice: the day's count is the `messaging.email_outbox` rows marked sent since midnight UTC, and the reset is the next midnight UTC (`email::next_reset`; verify with vendor before Gate C how Resend counts its day). `DailyLimit::new(per_day, hold_above_percent)` (100 and 90 on the free plan; the caller passes both as settings, refusing a zero limit or a share outside 1 to 100) holds a `Bulk` email (open cards CARD-022, missed cards BIZ-044, the weekly digest OPS-030) while more than the share went: 91 of 100 holds, 90 does not. Every `Notice` email still goes. An HTTP 429 from the provider puts the row back in the queue with `waiting_for` `provider_limit` until the reset when the day's count has reached the limit, or for 1 minute otherwise (a per-second rate limit); nothing is dropped. `waiting_for` stays on the row after the send, so the notice log (`email_log`, BIZ-045) can show the wait, and `sent_at` is the provider's acceptance, so a window counted from the send (PICK-001, PICK-019) starts then. Reason: the database's own sent count needs no provider call; a 429 below the limit is a rate limit, not the daily cap. Source: `docs/spec/ops-recovery.md:42`; D-381; `docs/brains/email-deliverability.md` section 7.
- **D-1380** Question (T094; SEC-028, A11Y-034, SEC-018, D-491): what shape does the one email pipeline take, and what of it is left to later tasks? Choice: `messaging.email_outbox` holds each email once under an `email.send` key over its template ID, recipient ID and sorted subject IDs (no address in the key or any column; a homeowner's address is read from the vault at send time under `Reader::Messaging`, `Purpose::Send`, a business's comes from the caller); `send_email` claims the row, calls the `EmailAdapter` outside any transaction with the key re-derived from the stored IDs and marks it sent with its subject and both parts cleared (SEC-037). Every email is rendered in `templates/email_layout.html` through Askama (already a workspace dependency, used by `portals`; no new crate): `lang` on the root (A11Y-034), the message first, then the SEC-028 footer (the audience's why-line, "Manage email notices" linked to the person's portal, "Ask Hava LLC," and the postal address), and a plain-text part with the same lines. The postal address is a checked `PostalAddress` (a P.O. box or a private mailbox, never empty; there is no home-address kind); the caller passes it until a task adds the `ASKHAVA_*` setting. From is `"Ask Hava" <jobs@notify.askhava.com>`, Reply-To `help@askhava.com`. Email lines are Rust `Notice` variants (`TextFailed`, `OptedOut` for CON-035's email confirmation, `StillOpen` for CON-028's "Your request <n> is still open. Close it on your quote page."), each with a draft Spanish line that waits for the native-speaker review as the Spanish texts do (TXT-003). The homeowner's update channel (TXT-018) is `messaging.update_channel` behind `update_channel` and `set_update_channel`, text when no row exists. Left to later tasks, within this task's 7-file scope: the worker handler that sends due email rows and its `ResendEmail` wiring, the `core.task` kind through which modules above `messaging` ask for an email (D-491, the first such sender adds it), the Resend webhook route in `server`, and the `ASKHAVA_*` settings for the limit, the share and the postal address. The task ran over its 400-line budget (about 2,300 changed lines of code, tests and migration, before `.sqlx/` and docs) because TD-SEC-27's storage cases and TD-CON-28's email confirmation fell to it as well. Reason: one pipeline every sender uses; the address never rests in a `messaging` row (PRIV-002). Source: `docs/spec/security.md:32`, `docs/spec/accessibility.md:38`, `docs/spec/messaging.md:22`; D-385, D-490, D-491.
- **D-1381** Question (T094; SEC-050, SEC-051): what does `messaging` do with a verified email-provider webhook? Choice: `receive_email_event` takes only a `VerifiedWebhook` from Resend (the raw-body signature, constant-time comparison and 5-minute tolerance are `adapters`' `verify_webhook`, T018) and, in one transaction, records its Svix message ID in `messaging.webhook_event` (new source `resend`; a replayed ID is `EmailEvent::Repeat` and changes nothing) and the event in `messaging.email_event` with the provider's `created_at` and the injected receive time; it returns `Ok` only after the commit, so the route acknowledges only a stored event and answers 500 on `EmailError::Database` (the planted-failure case renames the table). `email_status` is the latest event by event time, so an earlier event arriving later never replaces a later one. An `email.complained` event raises `ops.alert` `messaging.email_complaint` (High) in the same transaction; `check_webhook_silence` raises `messaging.email_webhooks_silent` when emails were sent in the last 24 hours and no webhook arrived in them, for a scheduled task to call; only emails sent at least `WEBHOOK_GRACE` (1 hour) before the check count, so an email sent minutes before it, which has had no time to produce a webhook, never raises a false alarm (fix round: the first version alerted on any send in the window). A verified event whose type is not `email.*` (Resend also sends `contact.*` and `domain.*`) is `EmailEvent::Ignored`, acknowledged with nothing stored, and an `email.*` event that `messaging.email_event`'s checks would refuse (empty or over-long email ID, a type outside `email.[a-z_]{1,32}`) is `EmailError::BadWebhook`, both decided before the transaction, so a valid event never rolls back into a 500 the provider resends forever. Bounce and suppression handling of the address status (BIZ-040, BIZ-045) is a later task's. The Postmaster registration step (account checklist) and the owner portal's monthly review line are T122's and the owner-portal task's. Reason: storage and order are `messaging`'s; signature checks stay in the one adapter. Source: `docs/spec/security.md:54`, `docs/spec/security.md:55`; D-490, D-492.
- **D-1382** Question (T094 cold read and copy panel, WORD-028, WORD-029): what did the two reviews of the new email copy find, and what changed? Choice: the opt-out email's body is now the CON-009 confirmation text itself (`opt_out_confirmation`, rendered in the person's language), not a paraphrase, since CON-035's email confirmation is that confirmation; its "at this number" reads less clearly in an email, which a spec change would have to settle (listed for Casey). The failed-text email now reads "Ask Hava: A text to you didn't go through" / "This text to you didn't go through, so here it is by email: <text> You can also see it on your quote page." (business: "in your Ask Hava portal"), naming where TXT-014 shows it and using contractions; the Spanish drafts use "mensaje de texto" throughout ("Ask Hava: No le llegó un mensaje de texto", "Ya no recibirá mensajes de texto"). Not taken: adding the Ask Hava number to the START line (a new fact the template does not carry). AI-smell list: add the uncontracted "could not" and "did not" in short notices. Reason: fixed wording is never paraphrased; the reviews' plain-speech rewrites. Source: `docs/spec/consent.md:13`, `docs/spec/messaging.md:18`; `docs/voice.md`; `docs/copy/copy-panel.md`.
- **D-1398** Question (harness change, November 2, 2026): T225's first attempt failed `Ci` at the Coverage floor step (07:05Z), but the retry's `last_failure` carried only the step names, because both job-log downloads were refused: `gh api` answered "the response contains terminal escape sequences; pass --allow-escape-sequences to output it anyway" (cycle log, D-1263's diagnostics), so the worker on attempt 2 does not see which crate's coverage fell or by how much. Choice: `GitHubEnv._log_lines` passes `--allow-escape-sequences` on the job-log download (the flag of the `gh` on GitHub's `ubuntu-latest` runner, which printed that refusal; this session's gh 2.89.0 does not know it), and a `gh` that answers "unknown flag" is asked once more without it, so an older host loses nothing; because a refused log now reaches the retry's prompt, `log_excerpt` strips more than colour codes: `ANSI` now covers private CSI sequences (`\x1b[?25l`), OSC strings (hyperlinks, titles) and two-byte escapes, and a new `CONTROL` pattern drops the C0 controls other than tab; the one retry after `LOG_RETRY_SECONDS` and the annotation fallback stay as D-1263 made them. Tests: `tests/test_runner_live.py` `test_failure_log_download_allows_escape_sequences`, `test_failure_log_download_falls_back_when_gh_lacks_the_flag`, `test_log_excerpt_strips_osc_private_csi_and_control_characters`. Changed: `runner/github_env.py`, `tests/test_runner_live.py`, `docs/for-casey-review.md`. Numbered by the interim rule (D-1144): max(`next_decision` 1388, `main`'s highest D-1382 + 1, no open plan PR) + 10 = D-1398. Reason: a retry that knows the failing line is the point of D-1263; Coverage's log is coloured by cargo, so every coverage failure would have lost its excerpt. Independent Opus review (approve with fixes) folded in: the fallback for a `gh` without the flag, the OSC/private-CSI/control stripping, the gh version. Source: `BUILD_BRIEF.md:261`; D-582; D-1263; D-1300.
- **D-1383** Question (T225, FEE-028, D-092): how does `payments.ledger_entry` store an amount, and which entries name a business and a job? Choice: `amount_cents` is a `bigint` of whole cents, never negative; the `kind` says which way the money went, so no caller can get a sign wrong and a statement or the reconcile (T067) applies the direction once. The three $0 kinds (free first win, repeat customer FEE-013, fee-free job type FEE-045) are exactly 0 and carry no Stripe ID; every other kind is above 0. A payout names no business and no job; every other entry names its business; every kind but payout and credit names its job (a credit may be given to a business outside a job). The kind codes are the FEE-028 names in kebab case (`free-first-win`, `countering-fee-return`, `processing-fee`, ...). The migration's checks and `LedgerEntry::new` enforce the same rules, so the database is the last guard and the constructor gives a named error first (rust brain R2). `stripe_id` is optional on every non-$0 kind by design (a credit has no Stripe object, and a charge, refund or dispute row may be written before or without its Stripe ID); whether a missing ID is a reconcile mismatch is T067's call. Open for a later decision (T067 and the dispute tasks): how a won dispute's returned amount is recorded (a new kind or a `credit`), whether any fee can be negative, and whether an account-level processing fee with no business (as a payout has none) needs its own party rule; today `processing-fee` must name a business and a job. Reason: FEE-028 lists kinds and $0 entries but no sign convention; unsigned amounts plus kinds keep one source of direction. Source: `docs/spec/fees.md:32`, `docs/spec/fees.md:17`, `docs/spec/fees.md:49`.
- **D-1384** Question (T225, FEE-028, FEE-032, JOB-006): how is `payments::api::ledger_append` called, and what does a repeated call do? Choice: it takes the caller's `&mut PgConnection` (inside the caller's transaction, so the entry commits with the state change, R11) and a checked `LedgerEntry` carrying a caller-derived idempotency key (IDs only, `A-Za-z0-9._:-`, 1 to 200 characters, SEC-018), unique in the table. `INSERT ... ON CONFLICT (idempotency_key) DO NOTHING` needs only the insert grant; a repeated key with the identical entry returns `Appended::Already` with the first row's ID, and with different content `LedgerError::KeyReused`, so a task handler run twice appends once (JOB-006) and a key collision is never silently swallowed. The Stripe match, the reconcile and the architecture case of TD-FEE-16 are T067's and T175's. `LedgerError::Database` keeps no `sqlx::Error` source: the workspace's database errors carry no database message (D-698; `team`, `catalog`, `jobs` all drop it), a Postgres check failure's detail repeats the failing row, and `LedgerError` stays `PartialEq` for the tests; the caller logs the step that failed, not the database text. Reason: every money task (free win, refund, dispute, charge, reconcile) appends through one function, and task handlers must be safe to run twice. Source: `docs/spec/fees.md:32`, `docs/spec/fees.md:36`. Size (fix round): the task budget is 300 lines in 6 files; T225 landed about 500 hand-written lines in 7 main files (`CLAUDE.md`, migration, ledger, tests, architecture, decisions, manifest), and after this fix round about 640 lines in 11 files counting the workspace `Cargo.toml` line and the `lib.rs`, `api.rs` and `tests/mod.rs` stubs, plus the generated `.sqlx/` entries and `Cargo.lock`, because the crate is new and its tests cover every FEE-028 kind, the table's own checks, the database error branches and the grants (SQLSTATE 42501); splitting the crate skeleton from its first writer would ship an unused crate.
- **D-1399** Question (T058, FEE-001 to FEE-004, FEE-043, FEE-045, D-033): what does `payments::rules` take and return, and where do the edge cases go? Choice: `fee_for(FeeQuote, FeeJob) -> Result<Fee, FeeError>`, pure, amounts in unsigned whole cents. `FeeQuote` is `Fixed`, `Range`, `Hourly { rate, hours: Option<(u32, u32)> }` (whole hours, as `quotes::Price::Hourly` stores them) and `DiagnosticVisit { visit_fee }`; `payments` (layer 3) cannot import `quotes` (layer 5), so the caller maps its checked quote to this input. `FeeJob` carries the job's `diagnostic_visit` format flag, its category's `VisitTier` and its fee-free flag; `VisitTier::from_dollars` accepts only 25 and 75 (`VisitTierAboveCap` for 199, `NotATier` otherwise), so a $199 set tier fails wherever settings are read (TD-FEE-27). The midpoint is `low/2 + high/2 + (low%2 + high%2)/2`, the exact floor of the half sum with no overflow (D-033's rounding down); a low above its high and a rate times hours that overflows are `FeeError::Amounts`; an equal low and high is taken (one hour estimate). An hourly quote with no hours outside a `diagnostic_visit` job is `NeedsHours`, a diagnostic-visit quote there `NotDiagnosticVisit`, the same split as `quotes::intake::format_of` (D-1050). A fee-free job type returns `Fee::FeeFree` with the basis it would have had, so the ledger's $0 "fee-free job type" entry (T224, TD-FEE-40) and the free-first-win rule (no win used) can tell it from a charged tier. The tier amounts and edges are named constants with their requirement IDs; the owner's fee-mode switch (FEE-007, T060) decides how they become settings. Reason: one pure function the Confirm step, the quote-form preview and the twin's `rules_bridge` (T074) can all call; a checked set tier keeps FEE-004's $75 ceiling out of every caller. Source: `docs/spec/fees.md:5`, `docs/spec/fees.md:7`, `docs/spec/fees.md:8`, `docs/spec/fees.md:47`, `docs/spec/fees.md:49`.
- **D-1400** Question (T058, FEE-034, FEE-044, TD-FEE-02, TD-FEE-27): T058's goal asks every worked example to match to the cent, but the recurring rows (W11 to W20, W30, W33, W37: the 4-month rule, the $75 cap, the setup charge left out of the basis) need REC-002 and FEE-039, which are T188's, and the refused rows (W26, W27, W40) are the handyman limit, `licensing::api::check_quote` (its `tests::handyman` runs every row). Choice: `tests::worked_examples` runs every one-time, not-refused row (24 of 40) through `fee_for` and checks the basis and fee to the cent (for W24's free first win, the waived tier; W23's repeat-customer $0 is FEE-013's), and pins the 13 recurring and 3 refused IDs, so a new row cannot pass untested; T188 adds the recurring input and moves its rows into the checked set. FEE-044 holds here by construction: `FeeQuote` has no setup amount, so no setup charge can reach a basis; W37 ($75) and TD-FEE-27's "no setup amount ever changes the fee" property land with T188's recurring input. W18 and W30 (TD-FEE-02's monthly range and yearly rounding) likewise; their range midpoint and round-down are the same `fee_for` code tested by W31 and the range property here. Reason: building the 4-month rule here would take T188's owned work and REC requirements; the pinned lists keep the goal's "every example" checkable across both tasks. Source: `docs/spec/fees.md:38`, `docs/spec/fees.md:48`; `kit/prompts/T188.md`.
- **D-1404** Question (T188, REC-002 to REC-006, REC-010, FEE-039, FEE-044, D-010, D-037, D-159, D-265): how does a quote's period reach the fee without changing T058's `fee_for` or its `FeeJob` (built field by field in `tests::worked_examples`, which T188 does not own)? Choice: a second entry point, `period_fee_for(FeeQuote, Option<Period>, PeriodJob) -> Result<Fee, FeeError>`, where `PeriodJob` wraps the `FeeJob` with a `Service` (`NotRecurring`, `OneTimeJobType`, `RecurringJobType`; `Service::of(category.recurring, job type in one_time_job_types)`, REC-001) and a `RecurringCap` (a tier, `DEFAULT` $75, `from_dollars` takes 25, 75 or 199 so the capped fee is always one of the three fees). No period: a recurring job type is `NeedsPeriod` (bounced to the business, D-159), anything else is `fee_for`'s face value. A period: `PeriodNotRecurring` outside a recurring category (D-037); `NotRecurringPrice` on an hourly or diagnostic-visit quote (only a price or a range recurs); else the basis is `floor(price x a / b x 4)` with `Period::per_month` (52/12, 26/12, 1, 1/3, 1/12; a per-visit price with weekly visits is `Weekly`), a range using its exact midpoint, worked in `u128` and rounded down to the cent once at the end, as `scripts/check_catalog.py` does with `Fraction` (so $40 weekly is $693.33, not 4 x $173.33 = $693.32); overflow is `Amounts`. The tier of that basis is capped at `cap` for a recurring job type only; a one-time job type with a typed period still takes the 4-month basis (D-037: a period means 4 months) but is never capped (D-265). A fee-free job type is still $0. `RECURRING_MONTHS = 4` is the only multiplier (REC-006). No input carries a setup amount, so FEE-044 holds by construction and W37 matches. The cap is an input, not a `Settings` key yet: the owner's fee settings and the fee-mode switch are T060's (D-1399), which reads the setting and passes `RecurringCap`. `tests::worked_examples` still pins the 13 recurring IDs; `tests::recurring` runs those 13 rows and W32 through `period_fee_for` to the cent, and again with the cap at $199 to show W20 and W33 are held at $75 by the cap only (TD-FEE-21's "cap removed" mutant). Reason: keeps T058's one-time function and test untouched, makes every quote shape that cannot recur an explicit error, and matches the twin's exact arithmetic. Source: `docs/spec/recurring.md:6`, `docs/spec/recurring.md:14`, `docs/spec/fees.md:43`.
- **D-1405** Question (T188, FEE-040, D-197, D-261, D-288, D-465): how is the early joiner's price lock computed, with no fee schedule versions stored yet? Choice: pure `price_lock_until(LockDates { launch, joined, first_trade_on, activated: Option }) -> Option<Timestamp>`: none when the business joined 90 days (`90 x 24` hours) or more after launch, so 89 days 23:59 is locked and exactly 90 days is not; otherwise 6 calendar months, in Arizona time (`core::api::arizona_time`), from the latest of the join date, the first trade's switch-on and, for a business that waited on its city-list match, its activation. `locked_cents(lock_until, at, current, on_join)` charges `min(current, on_join)` strictly before the end and the current amount from the end instant on. The caller (T060's fee settings, with the fee schedule in effect on the join date) supplies both amounts. Reason: the rule is date arithmetic plus a minimum, testable without a database; the schedule history belongs with the fee-mode settings. Source: `docs/spec/fees.md:44`.
- **D-1406** Question (T188): the 4-month rule, the cap and the price lock need `jiff` and `askhava-core` in `askhava-payments` and run past the 300-line budget. Choice: `askhava-core` moves from a dev-dependency to a normal path dependency (layer 0, allowed by `kit/layers.json`) for `arizona_time`, and `jiff` (already in the workspace, `kit/allowed_crates.txt`, `Cargo.lock` and used by eleven crates; no new crate, so no new cargo-audit or license entry) is added for `Timestamp` and calendar months. The owned diff is about 500 lines (rules about 220, tests about 300) because FEE-040 and five test-design entries fall to this task; nothing outside its owned and shared paths changed. Reason: one Arizona offset in `core`, no hand-rolled calendar math; splitting would leave REC or FEE requirements without their tests. Source: `kit/prompts/T188.md`.
- **D-1407** Question (T188 review, REC-004, REC-010, D-010, D-159): `Period` names five schedules (weekly, every two weeks, monthly, quarterly, yearly); how is a per-visit price on any other visit schedule (for example twice a week, or every three weeks) priced? Choice: `period_fee_for` takes only those five `Period`s, no visits-per-month input. A per-visit price on a weekly, every-two-weeks, monthly, quarterly or yearly schedule is passed with that `Period` (weekly visits are `Weekly`, 52 / 12 a month). A per-visit price on any other schedule is converted by the caller (the quote form, which records the schedule) to a monthly amount and passed as `Period::Monthly`; the 4-month multiplier and the one round-down at the end are then this module's as before. Review fixes in the same round: the recurring cap's `match` on `Service` lost its unreachable `NotRecurring` arm (a period outside a recurring category already returned `PeriodNotRecurring`), so the cap is a plain test for `RecurringJobType`; `tests::recurring` now pins every price-lock end as a literal instant instead of re-deriving it with the code's own calendar arithmetic, has a TD-FEE-24 case worded as the test design states it (activated 3 months after joining, lock to 6 months from activation), and covers `price_lock_until`'s two overflow branches (a launch whose 90-day window, or a start whose 6 months, runs past `Timestamp::MAX`, gives no lock, never a panic). Reason: every worked example and the spec's only named per-visit case (weekly) fit the five periods; a free-form visits-per-month input would widen the pure API and its errors for a schedule no source names, and the caller already holds the schedule. Source: `docs/spec/recurring.md:14`, `docs/test-design.md:164`.
- **D-1409** Question (T059, FEE-009, FEE-014, FEE-015, FEE-036, FEE-048): how are Stripe customers, the card authorization and saved cards stored? Choice: `migrations/0093_payments_customers_cards.sql` adds `payments.customer` (primary key `business_id`, so a Stripe customer is always a business's and no column can hold a homeowner, FEE-009), `payments.card_authorization` (append-only for `askhava_app`: version, the exact FEE-015 text and `accepted_at`, so a later wording change is a new version, FEE-007) and `payments.payment_method` (`pm_…`, brand, last four only; checks `method_type = 'card'`, D-073, and `usage = 'off_session'`, FEE-048; `removed_at` for BIZ-051). `payments::api::ensure_customer` creates the customer at sign-up with no card, with an idempotency key derived from the business ID alone (SEC-018), and reads before and after the Stripe call so no transaction spans it (R11); `save_card` takes a checked `SavedCard` (any type but `card` is `CardError::CardsOnly`) and stores the authorization and the card in one transaction, a repeat being `Saved::Already` and another business's card `OtherBusiness`. The authorization text lives as `AUTHORIZATION_TEXT`, version 1, verbatim from FEE-015. `askhava-payments` gains `askhava-adapters` (layer 1, allowed by `kit/layers.json`), `secrecy` and `jiff-sqlx` (all already workspace crates in `kit/allowed_crates.txt` and `Cargo.lock`; no new crate, so no new cargo-audit or license entry) and a `sqlx.toml` mapping `timestamptz` to jiff (D-488). Reason: the smallest store that keeps FEE-015's version and time, refuses bank debits at both the type and the table, and gives TD-FEE-07 a schema with no homeowner in it. Source: `kit/prompts/T059.md`.
- **D-1410** Question (T059, TD-FEE-10 "through stripe-mock", FEE-048): `askhava_adapters::api::PaymentsAdapter` (T176) has no SetupIntent create, and `app/adapters/src/payments.rs` is not a T059 file; stripe-mock runs only in the e2e job. Choice: `payments::api::SetupIntentRequest::form` fixes the SetupIntent's fields (customer, `usage=off_session`, `payment_method_types[]=card`) and is tested in-crate and in `tests/integration/tests/setup_intent.rs`; the integration test drives `ensure_customer` through a recording fake of the adapter trait whose charge and refund methods panic, so saving a card provably makes no PaymentIntent. The adapter method that posts the form, and the stripe-mock round trip of the SetupIntent, are T132's ("Stripe test mode behind the adapter; contract and webhook tests against it"), and recording a card from `setup_intent.succeeded` is the webhook task's call to `save_card`. Reason: stays inside T059's files while leaving one place that defines what a saved card's SetupIntent carries. Source: `kit/prompts/T059.md`, `kit/tasks.json` (T132, T176).
- **D-1411** Question (T059 review, TD-FEE-07, TD-FEE-10, TD-FEE-32, FEE-014, BIZ-051, R11): T059's prompt sets a 550-line budget; the owned diff is about 970 lines outside `.sqlx/` (rules about 380: `models.rs`, `service.rs` and the migration; tests about 550: the in-crate TD-FEE-07 and TD-FEE-10 properties, `tests/integration/tests/setup_intent.rs` and `tests/security/tests/no_homeowner_charge.rs`), and touches more than 6 files. Choice: keep it as one pull request. The overrun is tests the test design assigns to this task: TD-FEE-07 (no homeowner is ever a Stripe customer or charged, at the type, the table and the routes), TD-FEE-10 (customer at sign-up with no card, the authorization's text, version and time, cards only, append-only rows) and TD-FEE-32's saved-card case each need their own database or route cases; nothing outside the owned and shared paths changed. Review fixes in the same round: the app role's UPDATE on `payments.payment_method` is limited to `removed_at` (the schema's default table-wide UPDATE is revoked, then `GRANT UPDATE (removed_at)`), and `tests::setup_intent` checks any other column is refused (42501) while `removed_at` may be set; a vendor ID's part after `cus_` or `pm_` is at most 200 characters in the checked types, as the table checks state (`'^pm_[A-Za-z0-9_]{1,200}$'`), so the code no longer accepts a 204-character `pm_` ID the table refuses, tested in-crate at 200 and 201 and through `save_card` at 200; `ensure_customer` returns its pooled connection before the Stripe call and takes one again to store the answer, so no connection is held across it. Reason: splitting would leave TD-FEE entries without their tests or a schema without its checks; the same shape as T188's overrun (D-1406). Source: `kit/prompts/T059.md:41`, `docs/test-design.md`.
- **D-1414** Question (T060, FEE-007, D-072): FEE-007 needs a logged owner switch between tiers and a flat fee per job type, and a new card-authorization version after any mode change, but T060 owns no migration and `payments` may not query the `catalog` or `ops` schemas (architecture section 4 rule 3); the owner-portal task (T108, "owner tools for pauses, fee mode, categories and settings") stores the setting as a `catalog` setting. Choice: `payments::api::FeeTerms` (pure, `rules.rs`) is the setting's value: the `FeeMode` in force (`Tiers` or `Flat`) and the authorization version a business must have accepted to be charged; `FeeTerms::switched` returns the new terms with the version raised by one, or none for the mode in force. `switch_fee_mode` writes the audit row through `ops::api::audit` in the caller's transaction (actor the owner, action `payments.fee_mode_switched`, subject `payments.fee_mode` with the fixed `FEE_MODE_ID`, `from_status`/`to_status` the mode codes) and returns the new terms for the caller to store in that same transaction. `accept_authorization` appends a `payments.card_authorization` row at the terms' version with the text the business was shown; `may_confirm` refuses (`ConfirmError::NewAuthorizationNeeded`) unless the business's highest accepted version is at least the terms' version, and `record_fee_at_confirm` calls it first. `payments` now depends on `askhava-ops` (allowed by `kit/layers.json`). A card saved after a switch still records `AUTHORIZATION_VERSION` (1), so the Confirm page asks for the new version once. Flat mode: `flat_tier` is the owner's edit for the job type, else its category's set tier (`trip_fee_tier`, `VisitTier`); the edit is always one of the three tiers; a fee-free job type stays $0. Reason: no charge under terms the business never agreed to (D-072) without a table T060 cannot add; the setting's storage stays with its owner. Source: `kit/prompts/T060.md` (FEE-007, D-072), `docs/architecture.md` section 3 (`catalog` owns the fee-mode switch), `kit/tasks.json` (T108).
- **D-1415** Question (T060, FEE-005, FEE-006, JOB-016, D-071): where is the fee "fixed at the pick" kept, and what makes a PROBLEM reply unable to change it? Choice: `fee_at_pick(chosen quote, period, job, mode, flat edit)` returns a `PickedFee` (private fields, only that function makes one): its inputs are the chosen quote's amounts and period, the category and job type and the fee mode, never an AI flag or another quote. `record_fee_at_confirm` writes exactly `PickedFee::cents` to the ledger at Confirm (kind `charge` with the succeeded charge's `ch_…` ID, or `fee-free-job-type` at $0), keyed by the job and business IDs only, so a repeat appends once; no `payments` function takes a final bill or a check-in reply, so no PROBLEM reply reaches the fee (the reply's listing for Casey is the digest's and OPS-032's). The picks task that holds the pick until Confirm (T063) keeps the `PickedFee` it computed at the pick; T062 makes the Stripe charge before calling `record_fee_at_confirm`. The AI's major flag is not stored on any table yet (INT-018 is a later task), so TD-FEE-04 shows it is no input in-crate and flips the quote's AI-read flag in the integration case. Reason: the smallest place that makes the rule structural; no table needed. Source: `kit/prompts/T060.md` (FEE-005, FEE-006, JOB-016, TD-FEE-04, TD-FEE-05).
- **D-1416** Question (T060, TD-FEE-04, TD-FEE-05, TD-FEE-06): T060's prompt sets a 450-line budget; the owned diff is about 810 lines outside `.sqlx/` (rules about 300: `rules.rs` and `service.rs`; tests about 510: `src/tests/fee_at_pick.rs`, `tests/integration/tests/fee_at_pick.rs` and `tests/integration/tests/fee_mode_switch.rs`). - **D-1417** Question (T060 review of f11b569d, FEE-006, FEE-007, FEE-039, D-072, D-1414, D-1415): (1) `record_fee_at_confirm` wrote a `charge` row with no Stripe ID when a charged fee came with `Confirmed.charge` none; (2) it called `may_confirm` after the Stripe charge, so a succeeded charge could fail to be recorded; (3) `payments.card_authorization.version` holds both the FEE-015 wording version (`AUTHORIZATION_VERSION`, written by `save_card`) and the fee-terms version (`FeeTerms`, written by `accept_authorization`), and `may_confirm` compares `max(version)`; (5) flat mode skipped the FEE-039 recurring cap; (6) TD-FEE-04's integration case flipped only the quote's AI-read flag. (5) `fee_at_pick` in flat mode caps a recurring job type's tier at its `RecurringCap`, as `period_fee_for` does; a one-time job type is never capped. (6) TD-FEE-04's integration case also appends `ai.reading` rows with the major flag unset and then set (the table exists, so D-1415's "not stored on any table" is corrected; the reading is not yet joined to a job, INT-018) and checks the ledger row's business, job and `ch_…` ID. - **D-1418** Question (T060 review, FEE-007, FEE-015, D-072): flat mode needs its own card-authorization wording (FEE-015's text quotes the tiers), but the spec gives none, and `accept_authorization` stores whatever text the caller passes. - **D-1419** Question (T061, FEE-010, FEE-011, FEE-012, D-019, D-151, D-152, D-195, D-491): how does `payments`, which cannot read `licensing`, `businesses` or `catalog`, give one free first win per entity key, checked at use, with the waived amount, given the ledger's $0 kinds must be exactly 0? Choice: (1) the caller hands everything in: `record_entity_keys` (T081's sign-up, and the card-save step for the card fingerprint) stores each `EntityKey` as `payments.entity_key` (kind plus an HMAC-SHA256 digest under the ID secret of the trimmed, lower-cased, single-spaced value, through `IdempotencyKey::derive` with action `payments.entity_key`; never the value, so no contact or owner name sits in a `payments` column, PRIV-002, postgres brain P12); keys are never removed. (2) `waive_at_confirm` (T224's Confirm page, before any Stripe charge, in the Confirm transaction) takes `JoinDates` (sign-up submitted, launch = Gate C setting, each signed-up category's switch-on): inside the window when the form was submitted strictly before launch + 90 x 24 hours or before any switch-on + 90 x 24 hours (Arizona has no daylight saving, so this is 90 days; exactly 90 days is out; activation is not an input, D-152). (3) At use, the win is refused when any of the business's keys is already in `payments.free_win_claim`; using it writes, in a savepoint, the $0 `free-first-win` ledger entry, a `payments.free_win` row (one per business) with `waived_cents` (FEE-012, so the ledger stays at exactly 0 per FEE-028), and a claim on every key; a claim taken by a concurrent Confirm rolls the savepoint back as `FreeWinError::Race`, and the caller's retry sees the win used. A repeated Confirm for the same job returns the same win (`Appended::Already`); a business's later job is not waived. A fee-free pick is never waived here (its $0 entry is `record_fee_at_confirm`'s), so it never uses the win. Reason: the unique `(kind, digest)` key makes "once per entity key" hold under concurrency; digests keep the D-151 contact and name keys out of plain storage; the caller-supplied inputs keep the layer rule (D-491). Source: `kit/prompts/T061.md` (FEE-010 to FEE-012, TD-FEE-08), `migrations/0090_payments_ledger.sql` (the $0 check).
- **D-1420** Question (T061, FEE-013, D-069, FEE-009): how does `payments` know a pick is repeat work from the same customer, when no `payments` code or column may name a homeowner (TD-FEE-07)? Choice: the Confirm page (T224) passes `same_customer_jobs`, the customer's other jobs still linked to the homeowner record in `jobs`; `payments` answers `Repeat` when its own ledger has a `charge`, `free-first-win`, `repeat-customer` or `fee-free-job-type` entry of the same business on one of them (any property; the confirmed introductions of D-069, a later refund included, since a refund does not undo the introduction), and writes a $0 `repeat-customer` entry keyed by job and business, before and without touching the free first win. After the 180-day contact purge (PRIV-007) the record no longer links the jobs, so the caller passes none and the pick is charged; no hash is kept to extend it (D-069). Repeat is checked before the free win, so a repeat never uses one. Reason: the ledger is the money truth for "already introduced", and the homeowner link stays in `jobs`, outside `payments`. Source: `kit/prompts/T061.md` (FEE-013, TD-FEE-09), `tests/security/tests/no_homeowner_charge.rs`.
- **D-1421** Question (T061, TD-FEE-08, TD-FEE-09, TD-FEE-32): T061's prompt sets a 450-line budget; the owned diff is about 900 lines outside `.sqlx/` (rules about 440: `free_wins.rs`, `models.rs` and the migration; tests about 460: `tests/integration/tests/free_wins.rs` and `repeat_customer.rs`). Choice: keep it as one pull request. The overrun is the tests: TD-FEE-08 needs the window edges, all five key kinds, the $0 row with its waived amount, the simultaneous claim and the append-only grants, and money code needs 95% branch coverage (BUILD_BRIEF.md:481). - **D-1422** Question (T061 review, FEE-011, FEE-012, FEE-013, FEE-053, D-151, D-1419, D-1420): (1) a key recorded after its business used its free first win was never claimed, so a second business with that key could get another win; (2) `waive_at_confirm` run again for a job already decided, with a different `same_customer_jobs` (for example after the purge), could write a second $0 line for the same pick; (3) the claim insert had no order, so two Confirms could deadlock, and a deadlock was a `Database` error; (4) the simultaneous-claim test slept 300 ms. Choice: (1) `record_entity_keys` claims the business's keys at once when it already has a `payments.free_win`, and the at-use check (`win_blocked`) also refuses a win when this business has a win, or any of its keys is claimed, or is shared with another business that has a win, so the guard holds even without the claim row; the claim table stays the guard against simultaneous Confirms. T081's sign-up (and the card-save step) must record every key through `record_entity_keys`, including keys learned after the win; a key never recorded cannot block anything. (2) `waive_at_confirm` first returns the answer the ledger already holds for that business and job (`free-first-win` or `repeat-customer` as `Appended::Already`, a `charge` or `fee-free-job-type` as `NotWaived`) and writes nothing. (3) Claims are inserted `ORDER BY kind, digest`; SQLSTATE 40P01 and 40001 in the claim are `FreeWinError::Race` (the caller reruns the Confirm). (4) The test polls `pg_stat_activity` (bounded, 10 s) until the second Confirm waits on the first one's lock. The review's notes on key normalization (only trim, lower-case and single spaces, so "ROC-123" and "ROC 123" differ) are left as they are: changing `EntityKey::new` later would orphan stored digests, so a stricter per-kind normalization is for T081 to apply before calling `EntityKey::new`, logged here for that task. Reason: FEE-011 is once per entity key whenever the key became known; FEE-053 is one line per pick. Source: T061 review findings.
- **D-1462** Question (harness, A+ plan item 6 of the 2026-11-02 evening hand-off; BUILD_BRIEF.md:276 to BUILD_BRIEF.md:281, governance section 6): STATUS.md on `claude/kit-state` gave the requirements table first and needed a reader to work out whether the build was running, stuck or out of tokens. How does it become Casey's dashboard without leaving GitHub? (2) "Needs attention" moves up and adds the build hold and `gen_prompts.py --check --strict` red on tasks still to run, problems on DONE or SKIPPED tasks folded into a count (run once per runner process, which is every cycle and every `--after`, measured 1.25 to 1.7 s, so no Ci-written flag is needed; a crash or a missing script shows nothing); (3) "Last 24 hours": one row per attempt whose `ended_at` is within a day (title from kit/tasks.json, result, attempt, duration, end), with the retry reason, the first 120 characters of the task's `last_failure`, redacted as the pre-hand-in gate's rows are (`TOKEN_LIKE` and the PII scanner's key, phone and email shapes), on its latest attempt only when that attempt is a retry or failed (history rows keep no failure text of their own, so an older attempt's reason is not available), plus plan and harness merge subjects on `main` from the same day (their decision numbers are in the subjects); (4) the progress block, pacing, throughput, running and last-usage sections follow unchanged; `README.md` links the page. `kit/state_schema.json` gains an optional `keeper` key ({`next_wake_at`, `last_run_at`}, object or null) so this change and the self-scheduling keeper (D-1451, built concurrently) agree on its name; the dashboard shows "keeper: unknown" while it is absent.
