Reason: Casey asked for an A+ build process he can follow without asking; every figure comes from state the runner already holds, at about 2 s per process. Found while building: `gen_prompts.py --check --strict` is red on `main` now with 9 stale stored budgets: T094, T225, T058, T188, T059, T060 and T061 are DONE (counted, not flagged), T189 and T079 are queued (real drift, flagged); a separate plan change will regenerate the stale budgets. Independent Opus review (approve with fixes) folded in: every dashboard section renders inside a guard that turns any error into one "unavailable" line, so a malformed state field (a non-number attempt, a None history row, a string lease; tested) never stops a cycle; failure text is redacted with the PII scanner's patterns as well as `TOKEN_LIKE`; the strict flag judges only tasks still to run; the attempt number is read defensively; the architecture bullet states the run frequency. - **D-1440** Question (harness change, November 2, 2026; the A+ plan's item 4, "first pass above 90%"): T225's first attempt (07:05Z today) passed the runner's pre-hand-in gate and then failed `Ci`'s Coverage floor, because the gate (D-1300) left coverage to `Ci`; and T154's attempts that "ended without handing in" (3 and 9 minutes, no model evidence) and D-503's safety hand-in show a session that does not know its deadline. What changes? Measured here, with `Ci`'s pinned `nightly-2026-10-15`, cargo-llvm-cov 0.9.1 (tarball checked against `Ci`'s SHA-256), `Ci`'s flags and a local Postgres 16, on 2 cores: `cargo llvm-cov -p askhava-payments` alone took 183 s cold and 9 s warm but measured `app/payments/` at 60.98% against a floor of 95, because most of its coverage comes from `tests/integration` (the workspace run measures it at 98.82%); `-p askhava-payments -p askhava-integration` took 324 s cold and 271 s warm (212 s of it the integration tests) and measured 98.82%, the workspace figure; `Ci`'s whole workspace command took 407 s and passed every floor (payments 98.82, privacy 96.80, licensing 95.96, `rules.rs` not measured). So a crate alone gives a false red, and a correct per-crate run is about 4.5 to 5.5 minutes, too long for `--quick` (the runner's 240 s `PREHANDIN_TIMEOUT` inside `--after`'s 600 s call). Choice: (1) New `scripts/coverage_floor.py`: `compare` is `Ci`'s inline comparison moved unchanged (branch coverage, lines when a part has no branches, the 0.005 slack, the lowered-floor refusal against origin/main) with `--only PREFIX` to judge some floors and not the workspace total; `select` reads the changed paths, finds the floored crates they touch (a change to the floor file selects all) and adds every workspace crate that depends on them, minus `Ci`'s two excluded trybuild crates. `ci.yml`'s Coverage compare step now calls `python3 scripts/coverage_floor.py compare "$COVERAGE_JSON"`, and its Rust path rule adds `scripts/coverage_floor\.py`, so a change to the comparison is measured. (2) `scripts/prehandin.sh` full mode (the worker's run, not `--quick`) runs `Ci`'s command (`--locked --branch --json --summary-only --ignore-filename-regex '(/tests/|/bin/)'`) over the selected packages and `compare --only` on the touched floors; without cargo-llvm-cov, the nightly or `DATABASE_URL` it says it skipped; a run past `PREHANDIN_COVERAGE_TIMEOUT` (360 s, so the whole gate fits one 600 s Bash call) says so and leaves the verdict to `Ci`; a test failing under coverage is red. The runner's `--quick` run is unchanged. `backup-runner.yml` installs `Ci`'s pinned nightly and cargo-llvm-cov (same URL and SHA-256) in its prerequisites step and keeps their build in `CARGO_LLVM_COV_TARGET_DIR`, outside the cached `target` so the Rust cache does not grow by about 6 GB: on `/mnt` (a separate disk on GitHub's runners) when it is writable, else `/tmp`, with `df -h` logged there and before each gate run. Plainly: both are fresh on every job, so **every backup run measures cold**. Payments takes 324 s cold against the gate's 360 s cap, about even odds; a privacy change selects 10 packages and a floor-file change every floored crate with its dependents, and those will almost always time out, print "skipped: not finished in 360 s (Ci measures it)" and leave the verdict to `Ci` as before. So today the gain is mostly for payments and licensing changes and for sessions with a warm build; a separate cache for the instrumented build is the follow-up that makes the rest pay. A floor whose path has no file is never selected: `app/catalog/src/rules.rs` (floor 95) does not exist on `main`, so every `app/catalog/` change would otherwise start a workspace-sized run to judge a floor with nothing to measure. That is a plan gap: no task in `kit/tasks.json` owns the catalog fee-rules file or its floor key, so its floor is never enforced (D-694 and D-1286 note the file); it is left for a plan change. `kit/prompts/TEMPLATE.md:74` and `:83` (in place, no line moves) list the coverage step among the gate's checks and tell the worker that a red `coverage floor` means more tests, never a lower floor, and that "skipped: ... (Ci measures it)" is not red but leaves the verdict to `Ci`; every prompt is regenerated, the stored budgets in `kit/tasks.json` and the prompts' "Size budget" lines are kept as `main` has them, and `gen_prompts.py --check --strict` reports the same 9 problems as `main`. Of 148 queued tasks about 23 touch floored code (the plan's count), so the others pay nothing. (3) `runner/__main__.py` `write_handoff` adds `hand_in_by`: the claimed lease's expiry less `HAND_IN_MARGIN` (30 minutes), as an ISO time, None without a lease; `backup-runner.yml` step 3 tells the session to give it to the worker, who must have committed, run both scripts and stopped by then so step 5 runs first. The hand-off is not part of `kit/state.json`, so `kit/state_schema.json` is unchanged. `coverage_floor.py` reads `[dependencies]`, `[dev-dependencies]` and `[build-dependencies]`, not platform `[target.*.dependencies]` tables (no workspace crate has one). Tests: `tests/test_prehandin.py` (selection with dependents and exclusions, a floor with no file never selected, the comparison's floors, slack and lines fallback, `Ci` and the gate equal on the script, flags, nightly, exclusions and pins, the gate skipping coverage it cannot measure without going red), `tests/test_runner_live.py` `test_the_handoff_says_when_the_worker_must_hand_in`. No floor or existing test changed. Changed: `scripts/coverage_floor.py` (new), `scripts/prehandin.sh`, `kit/prompts/TEMPLATE.md` and every `kit/prompts/T###.md` (regenerated), `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, `.github/workflows/backup-runner.yml`, `runner/__main__.py`, the two test files, `docs/architecture.md` (section 12's smoke bullet, not a locked section), `docs/for-casey-review.md`, `kit/plan.lock`. Numbered by the overseer, who assigned D-1440, D-1451, D-1462 and D-1473 among four concurrent harness changes under the interim rule (D-1144: `next_decision` 1429, `main`'s highest D-1422). Reason: a coverage failure found in the worker's session costs a fix; the same failure in `Ci` costs an attempt (D-1300's arithmetic). Independent Opus review (approve with fixes) folded in: floors with no file are not selected (with a test) and the catalog plan gap reported; the template lines; the plain statement that backup runs measure cold; `/mnt` for the instrumented build with `df -h` logged; docstrings, line lengths, the comment wrap, the `[target.*]` note and the hand-off's lease fallback comment. Source: `BUILD_BRIEF.md:69`; `BUILD_BRIEF.md:218`; `BUILD_BRIEF.md:481`; D-503; D-694; D-1300; D-1398.
- **D-1451** Question (harness change, November 2, 2026; the A+ plan item 5, "self-scheduling runner", `docs/handoff/2026-11-02-evening.md`; numbered by the coordinator for four concurrent harness changes tonight, D-1440 the coverage gate, D-1451 this, D-1462 STATUS.md, D-1473 machine proofs and the war-games gate, from `next_decision` 1429 and `main`'s highest D-1422 under the interim rule, D-1144): GitHub's cron fired 24 times in 123 hours (median gap 5 h, longest 7.9 h), so a build waiting on it sat idle for hours and an overseer had to dispatch it and schedule the weekly restart; how does the runner wake itself, and what else did the plan ask? Choice: (1) **The keeper.** New `runner/keeper.py` (standard library; `python3 -m runner.keeper arm|wake|clamp`, `key=value` lines for `$GITHUB_OUTPUT`). `backup-runner.yml`'s backup job ends with "Arm the keeper for the next cycle" (`if: always()`): it reads `kit/state.json`, `lease.json` and `kit/runner_log.jsonl` through the contents API and runs a copy of `runner/` taken from `main` at job start (the session may leave a task branch checked out), then dispatches the workflow with `lane` and `wake_after`. `wake_after` rules (`wake_after`): no keeper while `backup_runner` is not "on" or `main` is red with FIX-MAIN escalated to a person (`escalated_at`, D-1099); a live lease: its end + 2 minutes (the soonest lane); the pacer waiting: `waiting_until` + 5; the week's plan reading (`usage.session_reading.week`) at 0.97 or more: its `resets_at` + 5; work a cycle could act on (an eligible task by `runner.state.eligible`, which applies `build_hold` and FIX-MAIN, or a MERGE_PENDING task) and the arming cycle's own last result not `idle` or `fix_main`: 20; otherwise the soonest future `retry_after` + 5, else 340. Every computed value is capped at 340 minutes (5 h 40 m) and floored at 10. A dispatched run with `wake_after` skips the gate (a new clause in its `if`), so it runs no cycle and no backup job; it runs only the new `keeper` job (`concurrency: {group: backup-runner-keeper, cancel-in-progress: true}`, so one sleeper exists and a newer keeper replaces it; `timeout-minutes: 350`; permissions `contents: read`, `actions: write`; no Postgres). It sleeps `clamp(wake_after)` minutes (1 to 340), re-reads `claude/kit-state`, `claude/lease` and the workflow's last 50 runs and decides (`on_wake`): `stop` when no keeper may run or the run list could not be read (the cron is the backstop); `rearm` (dispatch a new keeper) when another run of the workflow is queued, waiting or in progress, a lease is live, the pacer waits, the week stopped or nothing could be claimed; `go` dispatches an ordinary run with an empty lane, which goes through the gate, the lane pick (D-620), the backup job's concurrency group and the lease like any start. A live run makes the keeper re-arm rather than stop, because a run whose gate starts no backup job arms nothing; the keeper group keeps that from multiplying (each backup job that ends arms a keeper that cancels the sleeper). The keeper holds no lock: the backup group and the lease stay the only locks on a cycle, and every existing step (the tick D-518, the chain D-500, the refill D-723) is unchanged. The cron stays at minute 37, already an odd minute. **Weekly reset:** at the 97% reading the keepers chain 340-minute sleeps to `resets_at` + 5 and then start a cycle, so the overseer comes off that path (`docs/ai-operating-manual.md` section 8 says the overseer only checks a keeper exists). Not done, and why: the plan's "the runner writes `handoff/<date>.md` on `claude/kit-state`" is left out (the overseer's brief says the hand-off doc is written through a reviewed PR); STATUS.md: D-1462 (merged first, so this entry follows it) added the optional `keeper` key ({`next_wake_at`, `last_run_at`}) and a dashboard line that says "unknown" while it is absent; after a successful dispatch the arm step runs `python3 -m runner --keeper-armed <minutes>` (`runner/__main__.py` `keeper_armed`, through `update_state` like the usage reading, D-1155), which records `last_run_at` (the arming backup run) and `next_wake_at` (its keeper's first wake; a keeper's own re-arm is not recorded, since the keeper job has read-only contents); a "week stopped at N%" line is not added (the week reading is already on the dashboard), and the keeper's reason is in its job summary. The repository is public by Casey's decision at 01:02Z on November 2 (unlimited standard Linux minutes), so the block now says `repository: "public"`, `included_per_month: null`, and keeps the old figures under `private`, with the warning that a sleeping keeper would cost minutes on a private repository. The cause is the start-routine smoke (`GitHubEnv.smoke_main`, `/tmp/tmpXXXX/main`, the exact path the worker saw), not the Actions cache key: the D-514/D-1178 key is not shared with any other checkout path. The pre-hand-in gate's worktree runs no cargo (`scripts/prehandin.sh` "Not here: pytest, cargo and tsc"). Fix, smallest that keeps D-1178's speed: `smoke_main` ends with `cargo clean --workspace` (`CARGO_CLEAN_MEMBERS`) in the smoke's target dir (`run_command` gives it `_smoke_env`), skipped without a `Cargo.toml`; dependencies stay built and only the workspace members rebuild on the worker's first cargo run. - **D-1424** Question (T062, FEE-047, FEE-016, D-490, D-1410): FEE-047 wants one PaymentIntent per pick, created once (key from `pick-<id>-intent`) and confirmed by every press with that attempt's own key, but `askhava_adapters::api::PaymentsAdapter` (T176) only has `create_payment_intent` with `confirm=true`, which would make a second intent on every retry, and `app/adapters/src/payments.rs` is T132's file, not T062's. Choice: `payments::api::IntentStripe`, a trait over `PaymentsAdapter` with `create_intent` (unconfirmed) and `confirm_intent(key, pi, pm)`; `confirm_and_pay` and `open_intent` take it, and the timer and check handlers take only `PaymentsAdapter` (they only fetch). The HTTP methods that post these calls and the stripe-mock round trip are T132's, as for the SetupIntent (D-1410); `tests/integration/tests/charge_attempts.rs` drives a scripted fake that panics on `create_payment_intent`. Because no Stripe client is built in `server` yet, `register_handlers()` registers only `picks`' card-fix notice handler and the `payments.pause_watch` handler (it needs no Stripe client, D-1427); the `payments.charge_check` and `payments.pay_timer` handlers (`run_charge_check`, `run_pay_timer`) are registered by the task that wires the Stripe client (T132 or T189). Each idempotency key is `IdempotencyKey::derive` (HMAC, SEC-018) over the label `pick-<id>-intent` or `pick-<id>-try<n>`, so the labels FEE-016 names never reach Stripe in plain form. Reason: stays inside T062's files and keeps one place, the trait, that says what the two calls carry. Source: `docs/spec/fees.md:20`, `docs/spec/fees.md:51`; `kit/tasks.json` (T132, T176, T189).
- **D-1425** Question (T062, FEE-016, FEE-017, FEE-019, FEE-037, D-153, D-365): how does a press become exactly one attempt, and what may start a second one? Choice: `payments.charge_attempt` has one row per press (`press_id`, the Confirm form's one-time ID, unique per pick) numbered `try_no` 1, 2, ... by one `INSERT ... SELECT max+1 ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING`, so two presses at the same moment make one attempt (the other answers `Pending`). A repeated press, reload or duplicate callback of the same press answers from its own attempt (asking Stripe if it is undecided) and never sends again. Before a new attempt, in this order, and before any Stripe call but the FEE-037 question: the caller's `PickNow` (the Confirm page reads the job's Payment pending status and the pick's current status, which `payments` cannot read) and `payments`' own record (another business's pick, pick ended, or already paid); the charging pause; an undecided latest attempt (`sent` after a timeout, or `processing`) is settled by `fetch_payment_intent`, and a new try goes only once Stripe says it failed (`requires_payment_method`, `requires_confirmation`, `canceled`), never while Stripe is unreachable (D-153); then the monthly fee limit (D-1427), so an earlier unanswered try is resolved first; only then is the PaymentIntent made if the page has not made it. The attempt row is inserted under the pick's `FOR UPDATE` row lock by an `INSERT ... SELECT ... HAVING` that refuses while any attempt is `sent`, `processing` or `succeeded` or the pick has ended, so "no try2 while try1 is undecided" is one step, and the same transaction queues that attempt's first 30-minute check. A `sent` attempt younger than `IN_FLIGHT` (60 seconds; the HTTP client gives up at 15) is never settled as failed by an intent that still wants a card, since a second press can ask Stripe before the first confirm lands; and a decline may still become a success (`AttemptStatus::may_become`: a success from Stripe always wins; a call that never left takes any answer Stripe gives). A confirm answered 402 is a decline; a request that never left, or a 429, is `unreachable` (nothing charged); any other 4xx (for example `payment_intent_unexpected_state`) charged nothing, so the intent is read again and an answer that decides nothing is a decline (`AttemptStatus::after_refusal`); a timeout or a 5xx stays `sent`. The bank-approval code is `needs_action` (the `ops` audit check allows only `[a-z0-9_.]`). `AttemptStatus` lives in `app/payments/src/status.rs` with every match (SEC-031). Every attempt start and answer writes an `ops` audit row in its transaction (JOB-005); no transaction is held across a Stripe call (R11). The release itself, the ledger entry and the verified webhook are T189's; the nightly refund of a second kept charge is T067's (FEE-037). Reason: FEE-016's key per attempt must never allow two successes (D-153), and the pick's one PaymentIntent (FEE-047) is the backstop: two confirms on one intent cannot both charge. Source: `docs/spec/fees.md:20`, `docs/spec/fees.md:21`, `docs/spec/fees.md:41`.
- **D-1426** Question (T062, FEE-018, FEE-019, FEE-020, FEE-038, D-135, D-270, D-807): where do the card-fix window and the 4-hour Stripe release run, given `payments` cannot call `jobs` (whose Payment pending timer D-807 says the owning task re-times) or `picks`? Choice: `payments.pay_timer` (one row per pick and kind, `card-fix` or `stripe-down`), each with a `payments.pay_timer` `core.task` at its due time. A decline or bank approval opens the card-fix window: 1 business hour by `core::api::add_business_minutes` (a 7:30 p.m. decline ends at 8:30 a.m.), 60 clock minutes when the pick's job is an emergency (PICK-044, stored on `payments.pick_intent`); a later decline keeps the running window. The first call Stripe does not answer starts the 4-hour clock release; any answer ends it. A processing or timed-out attempt queues `payments.charge_check` 30 minutes later (FEE-019). Every attempt has its check queued when it starts, and a check that finds it still undecided (or Stripe unreachable) queues the next round 30 minutes on, so a `processing` attempt never blocks the pick without a check. At a timer's due time Stripe is asked once more: a paid pick stays; the 4-hour release ends the pick only while Stripe still cannot be reached (once Stripe answers, that answer's own effects run, for example the card-fix window); the card-fix window ends the pick only on Stripe's word that the card still needs fixing; anything Stripe has not settled, or Stripe unreachable at the card-fix window's end, moves the timer 5 minutes on (`RECHECK_AFTER`) rather than failing the task or giving up (FEE-019, D-153). An ended pick raises `payments.pick_ended` `{pick, business, job, reason}`. Offering the homeowner the next quote, and moving the job and pick statuses, are the `picks` Confirm tasks' (T063, T190), which register a handler on that event; until then the worker has no handler for it, so each such task fails with `NO_HANDLER` and is dead-lettered after its attempts (`app/server/src/lib.rs`, JOB-006), and the handler's task must replay those dead letters when it lands. `sync_pause` stops each running timer with its time left (business minutes counted per minute, clock seconds otherwise) and resumes it with that time (FEE-038); the timer handler also calls it when it fires during a pause. Reason: one place owns the payment timers and the facts they rest on (the attempts); the job's own backstop timer stays `jobs`'. Source: `docs/spec/fees.md:22`, `docs/spec/fees.md:23`, `docs/spec/fees.md:24`, `docs/spec/fees.md:42`.
- **D-1427** Question (T062, FEE-038, FEE-041, OPS-024, D-135, D-204): what pauses charges, and how is the monthly fee limit counted? Choice: charges are paused while the `ops` `charging` switch or the `all` switch is on (`charges_paused`); safe mode (OPS-001) has no flag of its own yet, and the task that builds it adds its check to `charges_paused`. A press while paused answers `Paused` ("try again later", OPS-024) and charges nothing. Nothing that flips a switch calls `payments` (`ops` is below it and no switch page exists yet): instead the `payments.pause_watch` task (`run_pause_watch`, registered in `register_handlers()`) runs `sync_pause` every minute while any payment timer is open and queues itself again (one task per minute by its dedupe key; every new timer starts it), so a timer stops and resumes within a minute of the flip. The limit is `payments.fee_limit` (one row per business, set or removed by `set_fee_limit`; the portal and card-authorization field is T224's). A press is over the limit when the business's succeeded attempts decided since the start of this Arizona calendar month plus this fee exceed it; exactly at the limit is charged. Over the limit nothing is charged, Stripe is not called (the check runs before the PaymentIntent is made; a pick with no PaymentIntent yet still raises the event, `announce_end`) and the pick ends at once (`payments.pick_ended`, reason `fee-limit`); the reply with the portal link and the homeowner's text are T224's (D-492). A $0 pick (free first win, repeat customer, fee-free job type) never reaches `confirm_and_pay` (it refuses a $0 fee), so the limit cannot block it. Two presses on two picks at the same moment can both pass the check; FEE-041 is a business's spending guard, not a ledger rule, so this is accepted. Reason: the switches exist (OPS-003); the attempts are `payments`' own record of what was charged and carry the decision time. Source: `docs/spec/fees.md:42`, `docs/spec/fees.md:45`, `docs/spec/ops-recovery.md:28`.
- **D-1428** Question (T062, FEE-020, BIZ-019, D-308, D-491, D-492, D-1380): how does the FEE-020 notice reach the business, when `payments` cannot call `businesses` or `messaging`, and `messaging` has no `core.task` kind yet through which a module above asks for an email (D-1380 left it to "the first such sender", but `app/messaging/src/` is not a T062 file)? Choice: `payments` queues `payments.card_needs_fix` `{pick, business, job, try, approval, fix_by}` once per declined or bank-approval attempt; `picks::api::run_card_fix_notice` first asks `payments::api::card_fix_window` and sends nothing for a pick paid or ended since (for example at the window's own end), then (`app/picks/src/money_notices.rs`, registered in `register_handlers()`) resolves the owner and every "Confirm and billing" member through `businesses::api::notice_addresses(Money)`, reads the job number and queues `messaging.business_notice` `{template: "card_fix_notice", business, pick, to: [address IDs], values: {job, time}}` with a dedupe key per pick and attempt, `{time}` the window's current deadline (none while paused). A card waiting on the bank uses its own template `card_approval_notice`: "Ask Hava: Your bank wants you to approve the payment for job {job}. You haven't been charged yet. After {time}, the homeowner can pick another business's quote. Approve it here: {link}" (after the cold read and the copy panel). The template `card_fix_notice` is added in `en.json` and `es.json` (Spanish draft): "Ask Hava: Your card didn't go through for job {job}. You haven't been charged. After {time}, the homeowner can pick another business's quote. Try again or use another card: {link}" (rewritten after the cold read and the copy panel; `{time}` must carry the day when it is not today) The `messaging` handler that renders it by the business's chosen channels (BIZ-036), fills `{link}` with the Confirm page and `{time}` in Arizona time, and sends it through T094's pipeline is the next `messaging` task's; until it exists the worker has no handler for `messaging.business_notice`, so each notice task fails with `NO_HANDLER` and is dead-lettered after its attempts (`app/server/src/lib.rs`), the Confirm page (T224) shows the decline at once, and that `messaging` task must replay the dead letters it inherits. The task ran over its 350-line budget (about 1,900 changed lines of code, tests and migration before `.sqlx/` and docs, about 1,060 of them in `payments` code and 625 in tests), because the charge, the two timers, the pause, the limit and the notice handler each needed their own database cases. Reason: keeps the layer rule (events go up) and the one email pipeline. Source: `docs/spec/fees.md:24`; D-1380.
- **D-1474** Question (T189, FEE-042, FEE-015, TD-FEE-38): what does the evidence record written at charge time hold, when `payments` knows only its own records and the `Press` type (T062's, built in `charge_attempts.rs`, a test T189 does not own) carries no IP, signed-in person, terms version or page snapshot? Choice: `payments.charge_evidence`, one row per pick, written by `write_evidence` in the same transaction that stores a succeeded attempt (from the confirm answer, the 30-minute check, a timer or a verified event), holding IDs and timestamps only: business, job, press, attempt number, the idempotency label the key was derived from (`pick-<id>-try<n>`; the key itself is an HMAC and is re-derivable), Stripe customer and PaymentIntent, the FEE-015 authorization version (the business's latest acceptance at or before the press, D-1478), the fee, the press time and the success time; insert and select only for the app role. The other FEE-042 parts are append-only rows keyed by the pick, each written by the task that has the fact: the press facts (IP, signed-in person, terms version, the page as shown) by T224 at the press, the charge and receipt IDs and the payment-success event by the webhook (T224, T067), the release by `picks`, refunds and disputes by T067. Both lines: FEE-042 "each charge keeps an evidence record" and the T189 goal "IDs and timestamps only, append-only, in this task's migration".
- **D-1475** Question (T189, SEC-030, SEC-039, SEC-049, D-488): how does `payments` check the event's account, and how is the minter tested when only `privacy`, `payments` and `server` may name `release_mint` and the mint is taken once per process? Choice: Stripe puts `account` on an event only when it belongs to another (connected) account; an event that names an account other than the configured `acct_…` builds nothing, and one that names none came over this account's own signed endpoint and is then re-fetched with this account's key, which finds only this account's intents. The clearing and the minting are two steps: `paid_release` and `no_fee_release` do every check and return a `Releasable` (private fields, no `Clone`, made only there), and `Minter::mint(releasable, contact)` is the one line that calls the mint, so `tests/integration/tests/confirm_and_pay.rs` proves every refusal on the clearing without holding a mint, and `payments`' one unit test (`release_proof::tests`) takes this binary's mint and proves the proof names the pick, contact and basis. Exactly-once release (PICK-022) is the release's own record in `picks`; a proof is consumed by `read_for_release`.
- **D-1476** Question (T189, FEE-049, TD-FEE-38, D-491): where do the PaymentIntent's description and statement descriptor come from, when `IntentStripe::create_intent` (T062) takes no text and its fake lives in a test T189 does not own? Choice: `payments::api::IntentText::for_job(number)` builds the description "Ask Hava introduction service, job <n>", the suffix "JOB <n>" and the full descriptor `ASKHAVA* JOB <n>`, refusing a number below 1 or one that takes the descriptor over 22 characters (job numbers up to 999,999,999 fit). The trait is left unchanged here; T132, which writes the adapter's create form against stripe-mock, adds the text to `create_intent` (and to the `charge_attempts.rs` fake) and checks it there (TD-FEE-38's stripe-mock case).
- **D-1477** Question (T189, SEC-030, D-488): how does `register_handlers()` take the mint once when it is built more than once in one process (its own unit test builds it twice) and no Stripe client exists yet to register a release handler with? Choice: `server::release_minter()` returns a `&'static Minter` made from `privacy::api::release_mint()` the first time it is called (`OnceLock`), and `register_handlers()` calls it first, so the worker holds the mint from its start and a second minter fails the start rather than a payment. No task handler takes it yet: the webhook route that hands verified events to `paid_release` and `Minter::mint` is T224's (it uses `release_minter()`), and the charge check and timer handlers wait for the Stripe client (T132).
- **D-1478** Question (T189 review round, FEE-015, FEE-018, FEE-020, FEE-036, FEE-041, FEE-042, JOB-014, PICK-022): may a success event clear an ended pick, which authorization version does the evidence hold, and how is a $0 release tied to its pick? Choice: `paid_release` reads `payments.pick_intent.ended_at` before the Stripe fetch and again after storing the success, and an ended pick (the 4-hour release, the card-fix window, the monthly fee limit, a refund) is `ReleaseError::PickEnded` and clears nothing; the money such a late success took is the reconcile's to refund (T067). `write_evidence` stores the version of the business's latest `payments.card_authorization` acceptance at or before the attempt's `started_at`, not the compile-time `AUTHORIZATION_VERSION` (the attempt does not record which saved card, so its `payment_method.authorization_id` cannot be read); the column is nullable and holds null only when no acceptance is recorded (T062's `charge_attempts.rs`, a test T189 does not own, charges a customer with none; FEE-007's `may_confirm` keeps a real Confirm from getting there), and an insert that writes no row when the pick has no record is `ChargeError::Database`. `no_fee_release` refuses any pick that has a PaymentIntent (it has a fee to pay); `payments` holds no record linking a $0 pick to its business and job (no intent is made for it, and `picks` is above `payments`), so the caller, `picks`, passes the parties of its own pick, and that binding is the caller's (T224) to keep. Both lines: the T189 goal and the reviewer's findings. Size: the T189 diff is over the 300-line, 6-file budget (BUILD_BRIEF.md section 12) because the migration, the minter, the evidence writer, the `server` wiring and the TD-FEE-38/TD-SEC-18/TD-SEC-27/TD-FEE-25 tests are one goal that cannot ship in parts without an unused minter or an untested release path.

- **D-1495** Question (plan change, November 5, 2026; a finding in Casey's November 3 package (file 21 section 2, its draft "T246" with migration 0098), verified on `main` by this session; interim-rule number as in D-1494; TD-SEC-33): the payments schema's default privileges give the app role UPDATE and DELETE on every new table; should they? Choice: no. Verified: `migrations/0090_payments_ledger.sql:15` runs `ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES IN SCHEMA payments GRANT SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE ON TABLES TO askhava_app`, and each payments migration narrows by hand: 0090 `ledger_entry` SELECT, INSERT (revokes UPDATE, DELETE, TRUNCATE); 0093 `customer` and `card_authorization` SELECT, INSERT, `payment_method` SELECT, INSERT and UPDATE of `removed_at` only (table UPDATE revoked first); 0095 `entity_key`, `free_win`, `free_win_claim` SELECT, INSERT; 0096 `pick_intent`, `charge_attempt`, `pay_timer` SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE (DELETE, TRUNCATE revoked) and `fee_limit` SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE; 0097 `charge_evidence` SELECT, INSERT. New task T245 (build, payments, stage 3; deps T189, T224, T244, one payments task at a time) adds `migrations/0098_payments_default_privileges.sql` (`ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES IN SCHEMA payments REVOKE UPDATE, DELETE ON TABLES FROM askhava_app`, existing grants unchanged) and `tests/integration/tests/payments_grants.rs`, which checks the default ACL and every payments table against an explicit allow list (FEE-028 and FEE-042 cover the append-only tables; no new requirement is needed, the rule being D-092's). Number 0098: main's highest is 0097 (T189, an ancestor of T245); the lowest queued payments migration is 0102 (T066), then 0104 (T067) and 0196 (T210); no queued task owns 0098 to 0101; `architecture_migrations.rs` requires an ancestor's file to be lower-numbered, which 0097 is. Because tables T066 (0102), T067 (0104) and T210 (0196) create will get SELECT, INSERT only by default, their goals now say any wider privilege is an explicit GRANT in their own migration, which the T245 test reads and checks for tables outside its pinned list (a later build task cannot edit another task's test, so the test, not the task, carries the rule), and T066 depends on T245 so its code is written against the narrowed default (T067 and T210 already follow T066). Reason: an append-only money table should not depend on a migration remembering a REVOKE; a test that pins every table makes a forgotten one fail `Ci`. - **D-1479** Question (T224, PICK-021, FEE-047, FEE-014, SEC-039, SEC-049, TD-FEE-25, TD-SEC-31, D-491): T224's prompt asks for the served Confirm route (reading the pick, its fixed fee and job type, opening the pick's one PaymentIntent on the first load, charging each press, 3-D Secure in the page) and the Stripe webhook route; what can be built on `main` as it stands? Findings, each checked against the files: (1) nothing stores the fee fixed at the pick or a job's job type (`picks.pick` has no fee, `jobs.job` no job type), so the page's fee, tier, basis and the FEE-045 fee-free test have no reader; (2) `IntentStripe` (T062) has no implementation: the unconfirmed create and the confirm are T132's adapter calls (stage 6, after this task), so `open_intent` and `confirm_and_pay` cannot be called from a served route, and the adapter returns no `client_secret` for the in-page 3-D Secure step; (3) business sign-in and the business actor of a session are T084's (`Session` exposes no actor ID, `session.rs` is not T224's), and the test-control router (`app/core/src/test_control.rs`, not T224's) has no session seed; (4) `portals::api::security_headers` replaces every page's CSP with the own-origin one, so Stripe.js is refused in a browser until that layer allows `js.stripe.com` on the Confirm page (`portals/CLAUDE.md`: "needs that layer changed first", D-946), and `security.rs` is not T224's. Choice: build what rests on existing code and say plainly what waits. `app/payments/src/routes.rs` is the full webhook route (`stripe_webhook_routes`, `POST /webhooks/stripe`): source rule through `ClientIpPolicy::client_ip` and `check_webhook_source`, then `verify_webhook`, then T189's `paid_release`, and a `ReleaseSink` trait whose holder mints with `server::release_minter()` and releases once; 403 on a refused source or signature, 500 only when Stripe or the database failed (Stripe resends), 200 otherwise. `app/portals/src/confirm_pay.rs` and `templates/confirm_pay.html` render the Confirm review step from `ConfirmFacts` (every PICK-021 item, FEE-045's line, the unticked save box with `AUTHORIZATION_TEXT`, \"Next time it's one tap.\" on a $0 Confirm, the CON-029 refusal with no form) and `press_reply` maps T062's `ChargeOutcome` to what the page shows (a decline at once with a new press ID, so the next press is `try2`); `static/confirm_pay.ts` mounts Elements, posts the `pm_…` and the press ID, and runs `handleNextAction` for a bank approval. Tests: `routes::tests` (TD-SEC-31: forged signature 403, sandbox address off the list 403, stand-in mode other host 403 and the stand-in accepted, test-mode event at the live endpoint builds no proof; TD-FEE-25: a success that cannot be checked is resent, not released), `confirm_pay::tests` (TD-FEE-25, TD-FEE-37, TD-FEE-40 page cases, TD-SEC-04) and `tests/e2e/confirm_pay.spec.ts` (the script against a stand-in page and a fake Stripe.js: decline at once, next press ID, 3-D Secure in the page, no card data posted; and no Stripe.js on another served page). The spec's stand-in page (`confirmPage` in `tests/e2e/confirm_pay.spec.ts`) is a hand copy of the template's ids, fields and `data-paid`, not the rendered template; the two are kept in step by hand until the route is served (D-1482).

- **D-1500** Question (T063, PICK-019, D-345, D-381, D-807): where does the Confirm window live, and how is it "a setting" when `jobs`' Awaiting confirm backstop is a 4-business-hour constant? Choice: `picks::api::ConfirmSettings { window_minutes }` (default 240) is passed by the caller, so a 3-hour window is a value change, not code. The window counts from the pick notice's real send: the email sender calls `picks::api::notice_sent(db, pick, sent_at, settings)` (whole seconds), which, with the pick row locked, restarts `jobs`' backstop with `restart_timer` from `add_business_minutes(sent_at, window + 1 - 240)` (never below the send), so the backstop always ends one business minute after the window, and queues `picks.confirm_ends` at `confirm_by(sent_at)` with `{pick, job, from, due}`, deduped per pick and due. `run_confirm_ends` locks the waiting pick, acts only while the job is Awaiting confirm and its `timer_from` still equals the task's `from` (a later send, Hold or Away restart makes an older task stale), then moves the job to Quotes ready at `due` and stores the pick as `expired` (new `PickStatus::Expired`), in one transaction. An emergency job keeps `jobs`' own 60 clock minutes (PICK-044) and `notice_sent` returns none. `run_pick_notice` (registered on `picks.pick_made`) queues one `messaging.business_notice` per pick to `notice_addresses(PicksAndRelease)` (owner and "Confirm and billing" members) with template `pick_notice` or `pick_notice_emergency` and values `job` and `window`; `messaging`'s sender fills "Accept by <time>" at the send and then calls `notice_sent`. Reason: PICK-019 and TD-PICK-09 count from the actual send, which only the sender knows; D-807's `timer_from` fence makes the stale-timer check exact without a new picks column (no migration is T063's file).
- **D-1501** Question (T063, PICK-020, PICK-033 to PICK-035, D-056, D-196): how are the license checks, the fee line and the business's YES or CONFIRM answer built? Choice: `check_at_pick(conn, source, (business, ROC number), now)` makes the one live lookup through `licensing::api::lookup_at_pick` (which records a read answer) and answers `LicenseAtPick` (`Eligible` on Active, `Ineligible` on not Active, and on a failed lookup `Eligible` only when the latest stored check is Active and under 24 hours old, else `Waits`); `check_at_confirm(conn, (business, number), StoredFacts, (now, deadline))` makes no lookup and refuses `Expired` at or after the deadline, `Account` unless the account is Active, `License` on a reached license-end or bond date (LIC-009) or when the latest stored check is not Active and under 24 hours old. `fee_line(fee, Option<FeeBasis>)` gives "Fee $75", "Fee $75 (ongoing services count as 4 months: $125 x 4 = $500)" or "Fee $75 (ongoing services count as 4 months, capped at $75)" from the cents `payments` priced (monthly, 4-month basis, capped). `read_business_word` reads YES, SÍ, SI, CONFIRM, CONFIRMAR with an optional job number; `business_reply(linked, open)` gives the same `FeeAndLink` answer to YES and CONFIRM (a text never confirms or charges, D-365), `Expired` after the window and `Nothing` for an unlinked phone. The fee reply template `pick_fee_reply` is "Ask Hava: {number}. Confirm and pay here: {link}." with the fee line as `{number}`: the template registry test (not T063's file) renders every template with a fixed value set that has no `fee`, so a new placeholder would fail it. The expired reply `pick_expired` reads "Ask Hava: Time ran out to accept job {job}, so the pick expired. You weren't charged. Your quote can't be picked again for this job." after the cold read and copy panel (the panel's rewrites of the PICK-034 fee lines were not applied: they are the spec's own example strings, checked by TD-PICK-15). Reason: D-056 names the stored results; `licensing` already owns the lookup and the stored checks, and `picks` reads them only through `licensing::api`.
- **D-1502** Question (T063, TD-PICK-09, TD-PICK-15, TD-PICK-28, TD-PICK-33, PICK-037): which parts of this task's tests and requirements are not built here? Choice, each a gap for the runner: (1) the call sites: no task yet reads a business's ROC license number for `picks` (no `licensing::api` read of `licensing.business_license`), so `check_at_pick` is not yet called from `run_pick_notice`, and `check_at_confirm` waits for the Confirm route's handler (T224's wiring, D-1480), which also supplies the deadline; the move to the backup quote on an ineligible Confirm is the PICK-047 backup task's extension of `confirm.rs`. (2) `messaging`'s `business_notice` sender (T094's pipeline, D-1380) must fill `{time}` from `window` at the send and call `notice_sent`; until then the notice is dead-lettered with `NO_HANDLER` like the card-fix notice. (3) The email body, the "Can't take it" link (T214), the Hold link (T148), the reminders (T197), the bounce grace of 1 business hour (PICK-045) and backup addresses (T149) are those tasks'. (4) The business's inbound YES or CONFIRM text route (which phone is linked to which business) is the inbound-text router's; `read_business_word` and `business_reply` are its rules. (5) TD-PICK-28's review-step case here is only that the fee line carries no end time; the review page is T055's.
- **D-1503** Question (T063 fix round, November 5, 2026; a fresh-eyes review of commit c01a5f45): the window was `ConfirmSettings::default()` fixed in code, the backstop copied `jobs`' 240, a notice held past `jobs`' backstop or an emergency's 60 minutes left a dead pick waiting, a Spanish fee reply carried an English fee line, a zero fee still gave a line, "YES 1042." did not read, and a repeated send restarted `jobs`' timer again. What is fixed and what is still open? Choice, fixed: (1) the window is the setting `ASKHAVA_PICK_CONFIRM_WINDOW_MINUTES` (added to `core::settings` `KEYS` under D-493; whole business minutes 1 to 3,600, 240 when absent or empty; a bad value stops startup naming the key only), parsed by `picks::api::ConfirmSettings::from_pairs` once in `bin/worker.rs` and passed through `server::register_handlers(stream, texts, confirm)` to `run_pick_notice(pool, settings, task)`; the notice's `window` and the deadline come from that one value, and `notice_sent` returns the deadline that is the notice's "Accept by", so the sender must call it before rendering and send nothing on an error. (2) `jobs`' backstop length is read from `JobStatus::AwaitingConfirm.wait()` (`picks::status::confirm_backstop_minutes`), since `jobs::rules::CONFIRM_BUSINESS_MINUTES` is crate-private and `jobs` is not T063's file. (3) `notice_sent` loads the job before anything else: when the job is back in Quotes ready or ended (`status::pick_lost`: `jobs`' backstop or an emergency's 60 minutes fired before the send) it stores the pick `expired` at the send instant and returns `MovedOn`; Payment pending, Connected and Done are not treated as a dead pick. (4) A repeat with the same send leaves `jobs`' timer alone when its `timer_from` already equals the restart point. (5) `fee_line(fee, basis, Language)` returns `Option<String>`: none for a fee of zero or less, the English spec strings word for word, and in Spanish "Tarifa $75 (los servicios continuos cuentan como 4 meses: $125 x 4 = $500)" or "... con tope de $75)" (a draft until TXT-003's review, like the es templates). (6) `read_business_word` drops trailing periods and exclamation marks. Tests: `src/tests/confirm.rs` and `tests/integration/tests/confirm_window.rs` (a repeated send, a notice held past the backstop for a normal and an emergency job, an emergency still waiting). Still open, each a gap for the runner, adding to D-1502: (a) PICK-019 and PICK-020 are not enforced on any live path yet: nothing calls `notice_sent`, `check_at_pick` or `check_at_confirm` (D-1502 (1), (2)), so until `messaging`'s `business_notice` sender and the Confirm handler land, the window is only `jobs`' 4-hour backstop from the pick and no license is checked at the pick or Confirm; the sender must also skip a pick whose `notice_sent` errs. (b) When the backstop or the emergency's 60 minutes fire without any later send, the pick row stays `awaiting_confirm` (`jobs`' timer cannot touch `picks`); a later `notice_sent` or a Confirm attempt ends it, and a `picks` handler on `jobs`' timeout is the clean fix. (c) `run_confirm_ends` does not call `jobs::api::all_windows_ended`: its `Windows` counts (quoted, sent, choosable) are `quotes`' data, which `picks` cannot count without a `quotes::api` read, so a job whose expired pick was the last choosable quote is not closed here and the failed quote is not marked unpickable (D-045); the PICK-046 homeowner notice after expiry is not sent either. Those are the backup and failed-pick tasks' (PICK-046, PICK-047). (d) A zero fee has no fee line, so the caller must not send `pick_fee_reply` for it. Reason: the review's points within T063's files are fixed; the rest needs other modules' code and is logged rather than built around.
- **D-1504** Question (T063, size budget): the prompt's budget is 5 files and 350 changed lines; the first commit was 20 files and 1,105 lines, and this fix round adds 14 files and about 450 changed lines. Choice: kept, as D-809 and D-1481 did. Besides the five owned files the change needs the shared `api.rs`, `lib.rs`, `status.rs`, `CLAUDE.md`, both template files, the `.sqlx/` query data, `Cargo.toml`/`Cargo.lock`, `core::settings` (the new key), `server` (`register_handlers` and the worker) and the docs; about half the lines are the pure and database tests, each a named test-design case. Reason: the budget is a guide for small pull requests (`BUILD_BRIEF.md:485`); splitting the window, its timer and its checks would leave a half-working pick on `main`.
- **D-1515** Question (plan change, November 5, 2026; Casey's decision on his November 3 voice call, recorded in his handoff package (file 23 decision 2) and in `docs/reviews/2026-11-03-handoff-zip-review.md`, and confirmed by him in chat on November 5: "I do want the product to be national ready. We will start in one market but it will expand later"; approved for this repository by the overseer, who has the final say; numbered under the interim rule (D-1144): max(`next_decision` 1505 on `claude/kit-state` after T063's claim, main's highest D-1499 + 1 after PR #269 merged, no other open plan PR) + 10 = D-1515, because `--reserve-decision` is refused in this environment; INT-048, BIZ-058, CARD-024): is Ask Hava built for one market or for any market? Choice: national-ready is a standing design goal. The architecture and the code must support a national launch: every value that is Lake Havasu City or Arizona only today (the towns, the identity source for no-license categories, the licensing sources, the quiet-hours and business-clock time zone, tax treatment, a launch date) must be replaceable by data (a market row, a reviewed catalog file or a setting) without an architecture change. The launch market is open: Phoenix metro if a business partner is secured, Lake Havasu City otherwise; no requirement, task or code names either as settled. Phoenix metro (many cities, jobs across city lines) is the war-game stress market and Lake Havasu City the comparison and fallback scenario; D-1154's $40 AI cap for the war games stays. D-1339 keeps its sequence (the approved build, its verification, the T242 review, the approved enhancements, their verification, the war games) and its "small market first" for the launch; only its reading that the build and spec stay Lake Havasu City only gives way to this goal, and T242's goal now says so. Scope (the overseer's, final): one data-layer change now, T248 (markets as reviewed data, ZIP centroids, each business's service radius, D-1518) and T249 (radius matching, D-1519); the retrofit of the rules that are Lake Havasu City or Arizona only today is a required output of T242: an inventory (at least LIC-011's city list, QH-001's and JOB-007's Arizona time, the ROC lookup and other licensing sources, FEE-046's set-aside rate, INT-022's Arizona-only towns, the identity sources, the time zone, and what the Phoenix metro fixture needs for the war games) with how each becomes per-market data, whose items go to Casey under T243 as candidates for the approved-enhancements step before the war games (T242's goal and acceptance updated). A standing rule for workers is added to `docs/code-docs.md` section 4: new code takes market-specific values from data, never as a literal Lake Havasu City or Arizona value, except where a requirement line names one (for example JOB-007, LIC-011, QH-001, FEE-046), and such a literal's comment names that requirement; `CLAUDE.md` is not changed. Unchanged: INT-022 (Arizona towns only, and a new legal review before another state), LIC-011, QH-001, JOB-007 and FEE-046 as written. The review record's dispositions now name the tasks, and Casey's November 5 words are added to it. Reason: Casey's instruction; a market held as data makes a second market a data change, not a rebuild. Source: `docs/reviews/2026-11-03-handoff-zip-review.md:12`, `docs/reviews/2026-11-03-handoff-zip-review.md:68`, `docs/decisions.md:1054`.
- **D-1516** Question (plan change, November 5, 2026; a finding in Casey's November 3 package (file 25 section 3, its draft "T245"), re-verified on `main` by this session; interim-rule number as in D-1515; PICK-012, PICK-013, PICK-015, PICK-016, PICK-032, PICK-045, PICK-055, TERMS-016, PRIV-003, TD-PICK-45, TD-PICK-46, TD-PICK-47, TD-PICK-30, TD-PICK-14): no homeowner can pick on the quote page; who builds the page pick, and in which statuses may a homeowner pick? Verified on `main`: `app/portals/src/pick_flow.rs:214` `final_pick` re-renders the review step with `not_open` and stores nothing; the code step sends no code (D-1248, D-1264, D-1280); `server` builds `pick_flow_routes(pool, clock)` with no Verify client, vault or secret; no task owns the page-pick write; and three rules disagree on status: the quote page's Pick buttons use `takes_quote_edits` (Open, No quotes yet, Quotes ready; D-1234, `app/portals/src/quote_page.rs:190`), `pick_flow::takes_pick` uses `takes_quotes` (those plus Awaiting confirm; D-1251 item 1) and the text pick takes Quotes ready and Awaiting confirm (`app/picks/src/rules.rs:291`). Choice: one rule. A new `JobStatus::takes_pick` (Quotes ready, Awaiting confirm) decides the quote page's Pick buttons, the review step and the final Pick, and a test pins picks' text stage equal to it, so a homeowner may pick or re-pick until the picked business taps Confirm (PICK-032, PICK-045, PICK-017's "you can pick another quote") and never from Payment pending on; Open and No quotes yet drop out because the first quote now moves a job to Quotes ready (T247, D-1517). This narrows the Pick-button status list of D-1234 and the status list of D-1251 item 1 to that one rule; everything else in both decisions stands (the token, the CON-003 and CON-028 lines, a pause not hiding the buttons, the review step). New task T246 (harness, stage 3, Opus worker and reviewer, review areas privacy, security and accessibility; deps T247, T055, T187, T094, T053, T054, T022, T224) builds the page pick end to end: the shared pick core and `picks::api::page_pick` in `app/picks/src/service.rs` (a re-pick ends the waiting pick as `replaced` with its withdrawal event; no fee, free win or release before Confirm; `insert_pick` already writes channel `page`, so T063's and T069's `app/picks/src/models.rs` is untouched); the code without `portals` ever seeing the number, through a new vault grant `(Picks, PickCode, [Phone])` read only by `privacy::api::read_for_pick_code`, which only `picks` may name (an architecture change made in this plan change: `docs/architecture.md` section 8 records it); the code step, "Finish my pick" storing the pick and its TERMS-016 acceptance in one transaction, and the result page; and the `server` wiring, which keeps today's "Nothing was picked" lines word for word when the vault keys are absent (dev, `Ci` and the end-to-end runs set none), so `tests/e2e/pick_flow.spec.ts` and `tests/a11y/pick_forms.spec.ts` stay true. It is a harness task because it must take over three earlier tasks' tests, which only a harness task may do (BUILD_BRIEF.md:70): T055's in-crate case in `app/portals/src/tests/pick_flow.rs` (which asserted the four-status `takes_pick`), T022's `tests/security/tests/vault_readers.rs`, whose `READERS` list gains `read_for_pick_code` for `picks`, and T053's `tests/a11y/fixtures.ts`, whose "after a pick" quote-page state (Awaiting confirm) required no "Pick #" and so locked in the gap D-1251 named; that expectation tested a spec gap, not a spec rule, and now requires the Pick button there, with a new Payment pending state requiring none (BUILD_BRIEF.md:69). The harness limits (14 files, 800 lines) hold the whole change in one task of 11 files, so the package's optional split is not used. A paused job or a number that can't be texted gets no code; ending a pause by a page pick stays T095's email path (PICK-029). The contact choice and email (PICK-018) stay checked and unstored, and their storage still has no owner (open). New TD-PICK-45 to TD-PICK-47. Dep edits so no two tasks own a file unordered: T095 (`quote_page.rs`), T157 (`pick_flow.rs`; T214 follows it), T090 and T092 (`app/privacy/src/models.rs`) and T075 (stage 3's cleanup) gain T246. The package's claims checked here held on `main` (its line numbers within a few lines); its draft deps are kept with T247 in place of its draft "T244". Reason: PICK-012, PICK-013 and PICK-045 as written; one predicate ends the page, server and text mismatch. Source: `app/portals/src/pick_flow.rs:214`, `docs/decisions.md:996`, `docs/decisions.md:1013`, `docs/spec/quotes-pick.md:36`.
- **D-1517** Question (plan change, November 5, 2026; a finding in Casey's November 3 package (file 25 section 2, its draft "T244"), re-verified on `main`; interim-rule number as in D-1515; JOB-009, JOB-011, JOB-012, JOB-025, JOB-006, TXT-016, TD-JOB-11, TD-JOB-03, TD-PICK-40): is the first-quote move built? Verified on `main`: no. JOB-009 (`docs/spec/lifecycle.md:13`) is listed by T032 (DONE), but no code moves a job to Quotes ready on a quote: outside `app/jobs/src/status.rs` (the arrows and the waits) `QuotesReady` appears only as a text-pick stage and a check-in target; `submit_quote` and `confirm_quote` (`app/quotes/src/intake.rs:468`, `app/quotes/src/intake.rs:504`) store the quote and move nothing; D-1048 says the move "is not this task's and is not built here"; `app/quotes/CLAUDE.md:55` lists it as not here yet; and `tests/integration/tests/job_timers.rs` names JOB-009 but moves the job by hand. Choice: new task T247 (build, quotes, stage 3, Opus; deps T046, T186, T033, T240 (DONE) and T224) adds `JobStatus::moves_on_first_quote` and `jobs::api::first_quote` and calls it from `submit_quote` (a quote confirmed at once) and `confirm_quote` (an AI-read quote confirmed) inside the quote's transaction, after the window and status checks and before the quote row is written (job lock first, as D-1051 orders); the move bumps the version, so the old wait applies nothing (JOB-006), and Quotes ready's 3-day wait counts from it (JOB-012, JOB-025); `intake::job_texts` sends `first_quote` through T240's homeowner-text pipeline (quiet hours, opt-out, a fresh quote-page link, SEC-037). A second quote, an edit and a quote in Quotes ready or Awaiting confirm move nothing. It owns `app/quotes/src/intake.rs` and `app/intake/src/job_texts.rs` (only DONE tasks owned them) and the new `tests/integration/tests/first_quote_move.rs`; TD-JOB-11 is new; T246 depends on it and T075 gains it. `submit_quote` still has no production caller (the business quote form is T148's), so the move goes live with T148. Noted, not changed: `quote_token::issue` revokes a live token (SEC-037), so the first-quote link stops working once the all-quotes-in link is issued. Reason: JOB-009, JOB-011 and TXT-016 as written. Source: `docs/spec/lifecycle.md:13`, `docs/spec/messaging.md:20`, `docs/decisions.md:957`.
- **D-1518** Question (plan change, November 5, 2026; Casey's November 3 decisions on the national-ready goal and radius matching, D-1515; interim-rule number as in D-1515; INT-048, BIZ-058, BIZ-049, TD-INT-37, TD-BIZ-37): where do markets, job locations and each business's service radius live? Choice: new task T248 (build, catalog, stage 4, Opus) builds the data layer only, from the package's file 22 sections 1, 3.1 and 3.2 (its T253 to T258 bundle is not adopted: launch records, tax rules, category rules by place and the license display stay out, the tax and licensing ones going to T242's inventory): `docs/catalog/markets.yaml` (new, reviewed, owned by T248) with one market, Lake Havasu City, AZ, `America/Phoenix`, its identity source (LIC-011's city list) and its towns; `catalog.market` (ID, name, state, time zone, identity sources, `launched_at` empty until a later owner action records a launch), `catalog.market_town` and `catalog.zcta_centroid` in `migrations/0162_catalog_markets.sql`; a Phoenix metro market only as a test fixture, never in the reviewed file and never launched; job locations as ZCTA centroids copied from the US Census Bureau Gazetteer ZCTA file into `app/catalog/data/zcta_centroids_az.csv` (public domain; source, vintage and download date in its header; at least the ZCTAs of the Lake Havasu City market's towns and of the Phoenix fixture's towns; never typed or estimated, the task stopping BLOCKED if the file can't be reached), with `catalog::api::zip_location` and a great-circle `miles_between` (no geocoding service, no new crate); and each business's service radius (BIZ-058: a base ZIP and whole miles from 1 to 100, its own number, never one for a market or metro) in `businesses.service_area` (`migrations/0163_businesses_service_area.sql`), asked at sign-up beside towns served (BIZ-049 amended in place), with draft wording for the copy panel. A business based outside Arizona (for example across the river in California, holding an Arizona license) can still sign up: any well-formed 5-digit base ZIP is accepted, and one with no centroid in the table is stored with no location, so its radius is unused and its towns served decide its cards (the independent review's fix). The catalog tables have no foreign key to or from another schema, and the CSV's data rows do not count toward T248's line budget. Migration numbers: main's highest is 0097; queued tasks own up to 0161 (T228) in stage 4 and from 0169 (T103) in stage 5, and no task owns 0162 to 0168; T248's deps (T155, T165, T228, T250 and the DONE T041, T044, T177) and its file position after T215 keep 0162 and 0163 above every migration before them in the runner's serial order (V9). Stage 4, not the package's "after T110" slot: T110 is a stage-5 task, and a stage-4 task cannot follow it; that slot existed only for migration order, which these numbers keep; stage 4 also lands the radius with the sign-up work and long before the war games, and blocks no stage-3 money task. `docs/architecture.md` section 3 lists the new tables (a locked section; the lock is rewritten). T100 (stage 4's cleanup) gains T248. Reason: Casey's decisions; data, not code, decides the market. Source: `docs/reviews/2026-11-03-handoff-zip-review.md:12`, `docs/reviews/2026-11-03-handoff-zip-review.md:13`, `docs/spec/businesses.md:53`.
- **D-1519** Question (plan change, November 5, 2026; Casey's November 3 decision on radius matching; interim-rule number as in D-1515; CARD-024, CARD-001, CARD-002, BIZ-010, BIZ-058, PRIV-028, INT-032, TD-CARD-13, TD-BIZ-38, TD-PRIV-13): who gets a job card once businesses have a radius? Choice: new CARD-024: beside the towns rule (CARD-001, CARD-002), a card also goes to every business that meets every other CARD-001 rule and whose radius reaches the job's ZIP centroid from its base ZIP centroid, whatever town either is in; a business serving the job's town keeps the card, so a radius only adds reach; the licensing and category rules of the job's place still apply (the LIC rules are unchanged), a business whose base ZIP has no location (an out-of-state base, as D-1518 allows) is matched by its towns served alone, only Arizona towns are matched (INT-022), and the count intake tells the homeowner (INT-017, INT-032, D-1022) counts by the same rule. The radius is each business's, never market- or metro-wide. New task T249 (build, quotes, stage 4, Opus; deps T248, T214, T212, T149, T164) adds the location and the reach to `quotes`' caller-filled `CardJob` and `CardBusiness` (D-1013, D-1014), the radius test to `rules::card_for` and `coverage`, and the portal edit of the base ZIP and radius (BIZ-010 amended in place) in `app/portals/src/business_actions.rs` and its template; T158 (stage 5, which also owns those two files) and T100 gain T249. PRIV-028 is amended in place so `intake.property` may hold the 5-digit ZIP beside the town (the job's location, never a street address), and TD-PRIV-13's schema test with it. Found while verifying, recorded open and not fixed here: no task owns the ZIP-and-area step that writes `intake.property` from the homeowner's ZIP (only tests insert rows; no ZIP question template exists), and none owns the production caller that builds `CardJob` and calls `quotes::api::send_job_cards` (no caller outside `quotes`); until they exist a job has no location and matches by towns only. Reason: Casey's decision; a ZIP centroid keeps the address in the vault and is finer than a large city's centre. Source: `docs/reviews/2026-11-03-handoff-zip-review.md:13`, `docs/spec/job-cards.md:5`, `docs/decisions.md:921`.
- **D-1520** Question (plan change, November 5, 2026; D-1495's wider finding; interim-rule number as in D-1515; OPS-010, CON-022, TD-SEC-34): the other schemas' default privileges give the app role UPDATE and DELETE on every new table; should they? Choice: no. Verified on `main`: migrations 0019 (core), 0021 (ops), 0027 (catalog), 0031 (jobs), 0036 (privacy), 0040 (ai), 0042 (messaging), 0048 (licensing), 0053 (intake), 0055 (businesses), 0058 (portals), 0067 (quotes) and 0079 (picks) each run `ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES IN SCHEMA <schema> GRANT SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE ON TABLES TO askhava_app` (exactly the 13 D-1495 listed; no other migration sets a default, `payments` in 0090 being T245's), and their tables rely on per-table REVOKE statements. New task T250 (build, core, stage 4, Opus; deps T245, T075) adds `migrations/0110_schema_default_privileges.sql`, revoking UPDATE and DELETE from each of the 13 defaults (no existing table's grants change), and its own test `tests/integration/tests/schema_grants.rs` (only one build task may own a `tests/` file, so T245's `payments_grants.rs` is not extended), which pins every non-payments table's app-role privileges against an allow list built from the migrations, checks the append-only tables the spec names and every schema's default, and accepts a later table's explicit GRANTs parsed from `migrations/`, as T245's test does; a table the spec calls append-only that has UPDATE or DELETE today is revoked in the migration when no code changes its rows, and otherwise the task stops and reports. Number 0110: stage 3's last numbered migration is 0106 (T069) and stage 4's first is 0114 (T076); T250 sits in file order just before T076, which now depends on it, and after T075 (stage 3's cleanup). Every later migration in the 13 schemas descends from T250: the ten stage-4 tasks with such a migration that were not yet ordered after it (T081 0119, T193 0120, T082 0121 and T083 0122 in `businesses`; T084 0123 in `portals`; T090 0125 and T092 0127 in `privacy`; T093 0128, T147 0141 and T196 0142 in `messaging`) gain T250 as a dep and D-1520 in their decisions (T250 depends only on T245 and T075, both stage 3, so no cycle and no dep on a later stage), and a table they create that needs UPDATE or DELETE gets an explicit GRANT in its own migration. T076 (`calls`) and T109 (`recovery`) create their schemas later, so their goals now say the new default is SELECT, INSERT; the P5 line of `docs/brains/postgres-operations.md` (edited in place) says a table needing UPDATE or DELETE gets an explicit GRANT; T248's `businesses.service_area` grants UPDATE explicitly; T100 gains T250. Stage 4: its deps finish with stage 3, and it blocks no stage-3 money task. New risk R-22, open until T250 merges. Reason: D-092; a forgotten REVOKE should fail `Ci`, not wait for an audit. Source: `migrations/0019_core_db_migrations.sql:17`, `migrations/0079_picks_code.sql:15`, `docs/decisions.md:1103`.
- **D-1521** Question (plan change, November 5, 2026, the overseer's follow-up to D-1519; interim-rule number continuing this change's block (D-1144: `next_decision` still 1505 and main's highest D-1499, so D-1515 onward); INT-048, INT-049, CARD-025, INT-022, INT-029, INT-041, TXT-032, PRIV-028, TD-INT-37, TD-INT-38, TD-CARD-14): D-1519 recorded that no task owns the intake ZIP step or the production caller that sends job cards; is the gap real, and who closes it? Verified on `main` after merging #269 and #270: nothing outside `app/quotes/src/` calls `send_job_cards`, `send_cards` or `send_late_cards`; nothing builds the caller-filled `CardJob` and `Pool` (D-1013, D-1014; `Pool` reads businesses and licensing data no current caller assembles, and `intake` may not call `licensing`); the `intake.cards_approved` event of T208's approval step has no handler (D-1274: "no handler exists yet"; D-1277 expected a card sender from T147, whose goal covers card notices only) and neither has INT-029's `intake.emergency_released`; no template asks the ZIP and no production code writes `intake.property`; `submit_quote` also has no production caller (T148's, D-1517). So job cards never go out in production. Choice: new task T251 (build, intake, stage 4, Opus worker and reviewer, review areas privacy and licensing; deps T248, T147, T208, T039, T043, T184, T045, T240, T247) owns `app/intake/src/zip_step.rs` (the ZIP question, new INT-049, with draft English and Spanish wording for the copy panel; a ZIP Ask Hava does not know, such as a PO-box-only ZIP no one has reviewed, is asked once more and then waited on, never closing the request, as the twin does at `twin/app.py:514` to `twin/app.py:522`, while a known Arizona ZIP outside the service area closes it as INT-022 says; reviewed extra ZIPs with no centroid give their town and no location), `app/intake/src/models.rs` and `migrations/0164_intake_property_zip.sql` (the ZIP stored beside the town, as D-1519 amended PRIV-028), `app/quotes/src/card_pool.rs` (the business pool from `businesses`, `licensing` and `ops` APIs), `app/intake/src/cards_out.rs` (the handlers of both events: the approved card only, `send_job_cards` once and idempotently, T147's card notices held by quiet hours, then the TXT-032 text) and their tests, including the `intake.property` column assertion of TD-PRIV-13 (contact ID, town and ZIP, never an address); new CARD-025 states when the cards go out, and TD-INT-38 and TD-CARD-14 are new. So this entry supplies the owners D-1519 left open. INT-048 gains each town's ZIP codes from the US Census ZCTA-to-place relationship file plus reviewed extra ZIPs with no centroid (a ZIP under one town only) and T248 gains `catalog::api::town_for_zip` and the matching TD-INT-37 case. Ordering: T251 follows T248 in file order and runs before T249, which now depends on it and also owns `cards_out.rs` and `card_pool.rs` to fill the job's location and each business's reach; T162 (the intake order) depends on it and calls the ZIP step at step 4; T100 gains it; migration 0164 is free (T248 holds 0162 and 0163, T103 0169), keeping V9. T251 shares no file with T246 or T247 (it depends on T247 and runs after both, in stage 4). Left open: the trigger for late cards (CARD-018) stays with the tasks that make a business newly eligible; the neighbouring towns a job is offered to stay D-1014's later choice; R-23 now also names T251. Reason: without the caller no business ever gets a card, which would invalidate every journey and the war games. Source: `docs/decisions.md:1023`, `docs/decisions.md:1026`, `docs/spec/intake.md:45`.
- **D-1522** Question (T190, PICK-043, PICK-044, BIZ-034): T190 owns only `app/picks/src/confirm.rs` and its two test files, with no migration, sender or text route, so where do HOLD, Away and the emergency windows live? Choice: pure rules in `picks::confirm`, exported from `picks::api`: `hold_allowed(HoldAsk)` and `hold(ask, (now, due), rules)` (the owner or a "Confirm and billing" member, `Roles::confirm_and_billing`, a non-emergency job, the first HOLD, a clock not delayed by Away, refused in that order with `TimeRefusal::{Role, Emergency, AlreadyHeld, AwayDelayed}` and `Ended` at or after `due`; the new end is `add_business_minutes(due, hold_minutes)`, so a HOLD at 1:59 into a 10:00 window ends at 16:00, 6 business hours in all); `away_until(by, (now, until), rules)` and `away_for(by, now, hours, rules)` (after now and at most `away_max_minutes` business minutes ahead, so AWAY 3 at 10:00 is 13:00 and AWAY 0 or 5 is `TooFar`); `window_start(sent, away, emergency)` (a non-emergency pick sent while away starts at the away end and is marked delayed; an emergency pick never waits); `emergency_plan(picked, after_hours, rules)` and `emergency_fix_by(declined, rules)` (60 clock minutes at any hour, the reminder at 30); `read_time_word` for HOLD/ESPERA <job> and AWAY/AUSENTE <hours>. A "Today" answer is simply `emergency: false`, so it never blocks a HOLD (D-284). Reason: the task's files hold no storage or sender; the rules are the testable part, and the callers (the portal Hold and Away pages, the text route, `messaging`'s sender) apply them with `jobs::api::restart_timer` (D-807).
- **D-1523** Question (T190, PICK-043, PICK-044, BIZ-034): the 2 hours, the 4 hours ahead and the 60 and 30 minutes are each "a setting"; how, without changing `ConfirmSettings`' struct literal in files T190 does not own? Choice: a separate `picks::api::WindowRules { hold_minutes: 120, away_max_minutes: 240, emergency_minutes: 60, emergency_reminder_minutes: 30 }` (its `Default`), passed by the caller like `ConfirmSettings`; no `ASKHAVA_*` key is added until a caller reads one (no unused code). The emergency night rules: a business without the BIZ-007 tick picked when `core::api::is_business_hours` is false (8 p.m. to 8 a.m.) gets its notice at the next 8 a.m. with the window from then (`NightLine::SeesAtEight`); picked by day with the 60 minutes' last second at or after 8 p.m., the notice goes at once, the homeowner gets `NightLine::MayMissAfterEight` and the reminder waits for 8 a.m. if it falls at night; a window ending exactly at 8:00 p.m. warns nothing ("ends after 8 p.m."). The jobs timer agrees: `jobs::api::rules::timeout` gives the same 60 clock minutes (`tests/integration/tests/confirm_hold_away.rs`). Reason: the settings stay values, not code; the edges follow PICK-044's words.
- **D-1524** Question (T190): what does T190 leave for other tasks? Choice, each a gap for the runner: (1) no HOLD-used or away-until column exists, so `HoldAsk.held`, `away_delayed` and the away time must be stored by the task that adds the Hold and Away pages and the AWAY text (BIZ-038, D-309) with a `picks` or `businesses` migration; (2) nothing calls these rules yet: the Hold link, the HOLD and AWAY text replies (with English and Spanish templates, never read as opt-outs by `messaging`'s detector), telling the business the new end, and `messaging`'s pick-notice sender applying `window_start` and `emergency_plan` before `notice_sent`; `notice_sent` still starts an emergency job's window from `jobs`' own 60 minutes counted from the pick, not from a notice held to 8 a.m.; (3) the homeowner lines of PICK-044 and D-285 are named by `NightLine` but have no templates here; the copy belongs with their sender; (4) TD-PICK-20's loss-text count (D-263) and TD-PICK-23's HOLD line in the pick text are other tasks' cases. Reason: logged rather than built around, inside T190's files.
- **D-1525** Question (T190, size budget): the prompt's budget is 3 files and 350 changed lines; the change is 8 files and 627 changed lines at review, about 660 after this fix round. Choice: kept, as D-1504 did for T063. Besides `confirm.rs` and its two test files the rules need `api.rs` (the exports), `lib.rs` and `tests/mod.rs` (the module lines), the crate `CLAUDE.md` and `docs/decisions.md`, and the integration test that ties the emergency window to `jobs`' timer; over half the lines are tests, each a named TD-PICK-20, TD-PICK-21 or TD-PICK-23 case. Reason: the budget is a guide for small pull requests (`BUILD_BRIEF.md:485`); splitting HOLD, Away and the emergency windows would leave PICK-043 and PICK-044 half-built on `main`.
- **D-1526** Question (T190 review, BIZ-034, PICK-044): AWAY 0 at 22:00 was accepted, because zero business minutes from a night time is the next 8 a.m.; and a day emergency pick at 19:30 (window to 20:30) held its 20:00 reminder to 08:00 the next day, after the window ended. Choice: `away_for` refuses `hours == 0` (`TooFar`, after the role check) before computing an end; `EmergencyPlan::reminder_at` is `Option<Timestamp>`, `None` when the (possibly held) reminder time is at or after `confirm_by`; `EmergencyPlan::open_at(at)` states the window rule (open from the send, strictly before `confirm_by`) so TD-PICK-21's 23:59:59 and 00:00:00 checks test the rule, not arithmetic. Reason: AWAY 0 means no away time at any hour (D-285); a reminder after the window ends tells the business to confirm a pick that can no longer be confirmed (PICK-044).
- **D-1527** Question (T065, FEE-022 to FEE-026, D-491): where does the refund rule get its facts, and how does a refund happen only once? Choice: `payments/src/refund_rules.rs` is pure; `picks` hands it the call log (`CallRecord`: time, `Caller`, `Answer`), the release time, the emergency flag, the replies and whether the pick was already refunded; `refunded_before` returns `NoRefund(AlreadyRefunded)` first, and every refund of a pick uses the one key `refund_label(pick)` = `pick-<id>-refund`, so a repeated decision or task reuses Stripe's idempotency. The homeowner's side of a call is `Caller::Customer` and the DONE/PROBLEM failure `Unmet::DoneOrProblemReply`, because no `payments` code may name a homeowner (FEE-009, TD-FEE-07's scan). Reason: D-491 keeps job, pick and call tables out of `payments`; a fixed key per pick makes the Stripe call itself safe to repeat (FEE-026, rust brain R13).
- **D-1528** Question (T065, FEE-022, FEE-035, CALL-007): FEE-022's limits at their edges. Choice: an attempt counts from the release up to and including 72:00:00 after it, and inside 8:00 a.m. to before 8:00 p.m. Arizona (`core::is_business_hours`; any hour on an emergency); the gap is last counted attempt minus first, at least 3:00:00; any call answered by a person anywhere in the log, either way, blocks the refund; the no-show for call contact is judged from 72:00:00, and any business call in that time, answered or not, is not a no-show. Checks run in a fixed order (already refunded, talked, DONE/PROBLEM, email YES, attempts, missed-call notice) and the first failure is the reason given (D-336). Reason: FEE-022 says "within 72 hours" and "at least 3 hours apart"; FEE-035 says "never calls", which an unanswered call is not.
- **D-1529** Question (T065, FEE-022, D-336): the decision email must say which condition was or wasn't met; is its wording written here? Choice: no; `RefundDecision` carries a `RefundReason` or an `Unmet` value (`TooFewAttempts(n)` holds the count, so "only 1 call attempt was inside the homeowner's window" can be said) and T191, which sends the email, writes the wording in both languages. The FEE-025 charge after a cancel is refunded whatever the call log says, and `NothingCharged` covers a $0 pick. Reason: the email is sent where the decision is acted on (D-491); no customer copy lands without its sender.
- **D-1530** Question (T065, size budget): the prompt allows 2 files and 350 changed lines; the change is 8 files and about 580 lines. Choice: kept, as D-1504 did for T063. The two owned files hold about 555 lines, a little under half of them tests, each a named TD-FEE-13 or TD-FEE-24 case; the rest are the shared module lines, the `api.rs` exports, the crate `CLAUDE.md`, `docs/architecture.md` and these entries. Reason: the budget is a guide for small pull requests (`BUILD_BRIEF.md:485`); splitting the unreachable, cancel and no-show rules would leave FEE-022 to FEE-025 and FEE-035 half-built on `main`, and `cargo fmt` lays the test fact structs out one field per line.
- **D-1531** Question (T065 review, FEE-022, FEE-026, FEE-035, CALL-007): `decide_unreachable` did not check that anything was charged; `no_show` recorded a no-show for call contact when the homeowner called and a person answered, and for email contact on a day-3 NO even when the log showed an answered call; and FEE-026's block on a disputed charge is not in `refund_rules.rs`. Choice: `UnreachableFacts` gains `charged`, and `false` gives `NoRefund(NothingCharged)` first after `NotYet`, as `decide_cancel` does; `no_show` returns `No` whenever a call in either direction was answered by a person, for both contact methods, which changes D-1528's no-show line and the TD-FEE-13 no-show case (the homeowner's answered call was `Recorded`, is now `No`); FEE-026's hourly retry and disputed-charge block stay with T066 (`payments-refunds-disputes`, which owns `refunds.rs` and `disputes.rs` and lists FEE-026), and the crate `CLAUDE.md` says so. Reason: FEE-035's "never calls" targets a business that ignored the homeowner and its email branch rests on "not having reached them" (`docs/spec/fees.md:39`); an answered call is the call log's evidence that they were reached (CALL-007, D-141, the same test FEE-023 uses, `docs/spec/fees.md:27`), and a no-show closes the call line and alerts Casey, so recording one against a business that talked would be wrong. Refunding with no charge would write a refund that has no payment (FEE-025, `docs/spec/fees.md:29`).
- **D-1532** Question (T244, FEE-040 withdrawn by D-1494, TD-FEE-41): how is the early-joiner price lock removed from `payments`, and what proves it stays gone? Choice: `LockDates`, `price_lock_until`, `locked_cents`, `LOCK_JOIN_WINDOW` and `LOCK_MONTHS` are deleted from `app/payments/src/rules.rs` with their re-exports in `src/api.rs`, and the now-unused `jiff` import goes from `rules.rs`; their tests (`td_fee_21_the_early_joiner_price_lock`, `td_fee_24_activated_3_months_after_joining`, the `lock` helper, `price_lock_past_the_last_instant_is_none`) are deleted; `td_fee_41_no_early_joiner_price_lock` in `src/tests/recurring.rs` reads `rules.rs` and `api.rs` at compile time and fails if either names a lock item, `Timestamp` or `joined`, and pins the same quotes to $25, $75, $199 and the $75 recurring cap. The 4-month rule, the cap, every fee amount and the free-first-win window (`JoinDates`, FEE-010 to FEE-012) are unchanged; D-1405's lock computation is retired.
