- **D-1617** Question (T250, OPS-010, CON-022, TD-SEC-34, TD-SEC-35; D-1520, D-1632): how does `migrations/0110_schema_default_privileges.sql` narrow the 13 schemas' table defaults, and how does TD-SEC-10 let a `core` migration name them? Choice: 0110 is 13 plain top-level statements, `ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES IN SCHEMA <schema> REVOKE UPDATE, DELETE ON TABLES FROM askhava_app;`, one per schema 0019 to 0079 opened (core, ops, catalog, jobs, privacy, ai, messaging, licensing, intake, businesses, portals, quotes, picks), and nothing else; `payments` is 0098's. An earlier attempt's `DO` block that walked `pg_default_acl` and named no schema is dropped: it hid the schemas from the architecture test behind dynamic SQL, and D-1632 chose the named exception instead. `tests/integration/tests/architecture_migrations.rs` gains `core_revoke_only`: a file headed `core` whose every statement (tokens split on `;`, empty ones ignored) is exactly that REVOKE shape, with a non-empty comma list of `kit/layers.json` schemas and of table privileges (`select`, `insert`, `update`, `delete`, `truncate`, `references`, `trigger`, `maintain`; not `ALL`), skips the schema-reference scan; anything else in the file voids it and the file gets every finding it got before. No existing rule, case or message changed; the plant gains task T004 (deps T001) and its REVOKE-only `migrations/0006_core_defaults.sql` (two statements, a schema list, a quoted name, a comment), and `td_sec_35_core_default_revoke_exception_is_narrow` checks the real 0110 is REVOKE-only and that 11 planted voids (added GRANT, `CREATE TABLE`, `INSERT`, `DO` block, the REVOKE inside a `DO`, another grantee, `GRANT OPTION FOR`, `FOR ROLE`, `ON SEQUENCES`, a schema not in `kit/layers.json`, a `jobs` header) each give exactly the one `schema picks` finding. No table the spec calls append-only had UPDATE or DELETE (`ops.audit_log`, `intake.consent_record`, `intake.terms_acceptance`, `messaging.optout_event`, `quotes.job_card` are SELECT, INSERT), so no table REVOKE was needed. Reason: plain statements fail alone on a missing role (D-701) and read exactly as the plan states; the exception can only take a default away, so it cannot widen any module's reach. Source: `kit/prompts/T250.md`, `docs/architecture.md` section 4 rule 3, `tests/integration/tests/architecture_migrations.rs`.
- **D-1679** Question (T076, CALL-001, CALL-017, D-1520): how is a job's masked line stored, and what may the app role change? Choice: `migrations/0114_calls_pool.sql` creates the `calls` schema with `ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES IN SCHEMA calls GRANT SELECT, INSERT ON TABLES TO askhava_app` and the architecture's `calls.number_pool` as one row per line (job, homeowner and business by opaque ID, the pool number, `shared`, `assigned_at`, `closed_at`, an identity `seq`), one open line per job by a partial unique index. Its only wider privilege is `GRANT UPDATE (closed_at) ON calls.number_pool TO askhava_app`, given here because T079 closes lines (CALL-009) and owns no migration; no DELETE anywhere. `calls.pool_alert` is append-only. Homeowner and business are keyed by ID, never by phone, so no contact value is stored (PRIV-002). Reason: the default of D-1520 plus the narrowest grant the next tasks need. Source: `kit/prompts/T076.md`, `docs/architecture.md` section 3.
- **D-1680** Question (T076, CALL-017, D-231): "at most one number-pool alert is open at a time", but `ops` has no API to ask whether an alert is resolved, and `calls` may not read `ops.alert`. Choice: `calls` keeps its own record of each pool alert (`calls.pool_alert`, with the `seq` of the line that raised it) and treats an alert as open until a later assignment finds a free number (the shortage ended); a shared assignment raises a High `calls.pool_exhausted` alert, about that line, only when no alert is open. Assignments run under one advisory lock, so `seq` order is commit order and two alerts never open together. The alert is High, not Normal, because sharing means PIN routing and the fix is Casey buying numbers (D-077). Reason: keeps the rule inside `calls`' own schema (architecture section 4 rule 3); an `ops` resolve-state API can replace it later without changing the rule's effect. Trade-off: resolving the alert in `ops` does not re-arm it; while the shortage lasts no second alert is raised, and the next one comes only after a free number is assigned and a later job shares again (logged in `docs/for-casey-review.md`). The stored `shared` flag (and `Line::shared`) means "shared when assigned" and is never updated: an unshared line becomes shared in fact when a later line takes its number, so PIN routing (T077) must derive sharing from the open lines on the number, never trust the flag. Source: `docs/spec/calls.md:21`, `docs/decisions.md` D-231.
- **D-1681** Question (T076, TD-CON-28, CON-035, CALL-014, CALL-022): the T076 case of TD-CON-28 needs a suppression-list check before every automated call, but `messaging` exports no bare "is this number listed" query and the phone may not leave the vault reader. Choice: `calls::api::automated_call_gate(db, vault, (contact, AutomatedCall), now)` asks `messaging::api::send_window` (which reads the phone under `messaging`'s grant and checks the one list, D-1301) and answers `CallGate::OptedOut` for a listed number, `NotDialable` for any number `send_window` answers `NotTextable` (not a `+1` number, or a `+1` number whose area code is missing from the quiet-hours table, QH-003), else `Dial`; quiet hours do not apply to these calls, so `Hold` also dials. Only `AutomatedCall::Code { asked_on_screen: true }` skips the check (CALL-014). Side effects of reusing the text-send window: the vault audits the phone read as `Reader::Messaging`, `Purpose::Send` (a text-send read, D-1305) though no text is sent, and an untabled area code blocks a call it would not need to (D-1682 makes that visible for the safety call). T080 calls it before the safety and code calls; the masked calls a person places are not automated and do not pass through it. Reason: one list, checked in one place, with no new `messaging` surface; a mutant that skips the check fails `td_con_28_no_automated_call_after_an_opt_out` (run in this repo). Source: `docs/test-design.md` TD-CON-28, `docs/spec/calls.md:18`.
- **D-1682** Question (T076 review, CALL-019, CALL-022, QH-003, D-1681): the call gate answers `NotDialable` for every number `messaging` would not text, including a `+1` number whose area code is missing from the quiet-hours table, so a safety call to it would be blocked with no trace. Choice: when `automated_call_gate` answers `NotDialable` for `AutomatedCall::Safety` it raises one High `calls.safety_call_not_dialable` alert with subject `privacy.contact` and the contact ID (no phone, PRIV-006); a code call raises none (she is on screen and sees the failure). The gate still does not dial: widening dialing past the list `messaging` texts is a spec question, logged in `docs/for-casey-review.md`. Reason: the smallest change that makes the blocked safety call visible to Casey, inside `calls`' existing `ops` dependency; CALL-019's critical alert fires regardless. Tested by `td_con_28_an_untextable_number_is_not_dialled_and_a_safety_call_alerts` (run in this repo). Source: `docs/spec/calls.md:23`, `docs/spec/calls.md:26`, D-1681.
- **D-1684** Question (T077, CALL-003, CALL-004): CALL-003 needs a 4-digit job PIN, but no table holds one and T077 owns no migration. Choice: a line's PIN is `calls::api::job_pin(line_id)`, the line's random `gen_random_uuid()` ID modulo 10,000, four digits with leading zeros; `JobPin::parse` takes exactly four ASCII digits; `Debug` hides the digits. The PIN of a job is its open line's, so a new line after a close has a new PIN. Two open lines on one number with the same PIN (about 1 in 10,000 a pair) connect neither by PIN (`route` connects only on exactly one match), never the wrong one; a stored, unique-per-number PIN is a migration for a later calls task (T078 or T080). Line IDs are not secret (they appear in audit rows, alert subjects and, later, portal links), so anyone who sees a line's ID can work out its PIN; plan gap for the runner: the task that adds the stored PIN (T078 or T080) must make it random and independent of the line ID, and no line ID may reach a homeowner or a business before then. Reason: no new storage, deterministic for the portal and the voice handler, and a collision fails closed. Tested by `td_call_02_an_unlinked_phone_needs_the_pin_and_a_wrong_one_is_refused` (run in this repo). Source: `docs/spec/calls.md:7`, `docs/spec/calls.md:8`.
- **D-1685** Question (T077, CALL-025): "6 per calling number per pool number per day" needs a stored count, and T077 owns no migration (its owned files are `routing.rs`, `pin_routing.rs`, `readback_reader.rs`, `release.rs`). Choice: `calls::api::route` and `answer_call` take the counts as input (`CallTurn { tries_call, tries_today, .. }`) and apply the rule: a number with 6 tries that day is `Step::Refuse` before any prompt; the third wrong try of a call, or the sixth of the day, is `Step::HangUp` with one High `calls.pin_tries_exceeded` alert (subject the first open line on the number, no phone). Keeping the day's count (keyed by a blind index of the calling number, never the number) belongs with the call log migration (T078's `0116_calls_call_log.sql`) and the voice webhook (T080); a plan gap for the runner. Reason: the rule is built and tested now; storage waits for the task that owns a migration. Tested by `td_call_11_ten_wrong_pins_never_connect_and_the_7th_of_the_day_is_refused`, `td_call_11_a_hang_up_raises_one_alert` (run in this repo). Source: `docs/spec/calls.md:29`.
- **D-1686** Question (T077, CALL-005, D-026): `calls` (layer 5) cannot read `picks` or `payments`, so how does it know the caller's business holds a confirmed paid or $0 pick, and what is "the job it would connect"? Choice: a line opens only at the release (`picks::release`, which runs only on a `ReleaseProof`), so a business holding an open line on the number is the paid business; this holds only while lines open nowhere else and close when the pick ends, which T079 (line closing) must keep true, and until then a business whose pick moved on still holds its line; the caller's business comes from `messaging::api::sender_business` (linked main and staff phones), her own number from `privacy::api::find_by_phone`, and a line's `homeowner_id` is her vault contact ID. After the second wrong try on an A-attested call from that business's phone, `route` gives `Step::ReadBack` for its newest line on the number; `privacy::api::read_for_readback` reads name and address under the registered `(Calls, CallReadback)` grant (audited per field) and returns only the first word of the name and the address before its first comma. The voice handler (T080) connects that line only on the caller's key press. Any other phone, or attestation B, C or none, gets PIN routing only; `Attestation::parse` takes the bare letters `A`, `B`, `C`, so T080 must map Twilio's `StirVerstat` strings (such as `TN-Validation-Passed-A`) to them, anything else being no attestation. Plan gap for the runner: `read_for_readback` is a new vault reader and must be added to `READERS` in `tests/security/tests/vault_readers.rs` (allowed crate: `calls`); that file is not T077's to edit, so a harness or security task adds it. Reason: keeps the vault rule (D-026) inside the layer table. Tested by `td_call_02_the_read_back_goes_only_to_the_paid_business`, `td_call_11_only_attestation_a_gets_the_read_back` (run in this repo). Source: `docs/spec/calls.md:9`, `docs/spec/calls.md:29`.
- **D-1687** Question (T077, TXT-027, TD-TXT-29, TD-QH-04): can T077 send the who's-calling text? Finding: any new homeowner template must also be listed in `app/quotes/src/update_texts.rs` (`UPDATE_TEXTS` or `NOT_UPDATE_TEXTS`, D-1293), or `quotes`' `td_txt_25_every_homeowner_template_is_scanned_or_left_out` fails the smoke test; that file is T213's, not a shared path, so the change rules (`scripts/check_pr_change.py`) refuse it on T077's branch. "Retried as an important text" likewise needs the template in `messaging`'s `IMPORTANT_TEMPLATES` (`app/messaging/src/retries.rs`, T094's). Choice: T077 ships no TXT-027 template and no sender; TD-TXT-29 and TD-QH-04 stay open. The text was built and tested on this branch, then removed before hand-in; the branch's history may not survive the merge, so no later task should rely on it. Its design, for whoever rebuilds it: `calls::routing::send_whos_calling` sends at once on an emergency job, else at `messaging::api::send_window`'s window, else queues a `calls.whos_calling` task at the window's start run by a `server`-registered handler; templates `whos_calling` and `whos_calling_email` in both languages. Plan gap for the runner: TXT-027, TD-TXT-29 and TD-QH-04 have no owning task now; add one, and give it `app/quotes/src/update_texts.rs` and `app/messaging/src/retries.rs` (one line each), and a source for the business's public name (no table holds one; the caller must supply it). Reason: a green gate inside the task's paths beats a red one; nothing is half-built on `main`. Source: `docs/spec/messaging.md:31`, D-1293.
- **D-1688** Question (T077, CALL-001, PICK-022, TD-CALL-12): where does the release open the line? Choice: `picks::api::release` now takes `(vault, masked pool)`; only when it returns `Released::Shown` does it call `calls::api::assign_number` (homeowner: the proof's contact) on a bare connection; the who's-calling text waits (D-1687). An emergency job with no address is `WaitingForAddress`, so no line opens until a later release finds the address in. `Already` opens nothing, so a line closed after 30 days is never reopened. A line that fails to open (no pool, database error, `LineOpen`) never hides the release: `release` still returns `Shown(view)`, so the paying business always gets the homeowner's details, and raises one High `picks.release_line_failed` alert about the pick (`RELEASE_LINE_FAILED_ALERT`; a failed alert write is dropped, the view still goes back). Because the pick is then released, a later proof gets `Already` and opens nothing; reopening the line from the alert is for a later task (T079 or the release's caller, T224), a plan gap for the runner. Reason: one place opens lines, only after a proven release. TD-CALL-12's pure case is `td_call_12_no_masked_line_before_an_emergency_address` (run in this repo); the database path with a real proof stays untested (no test crate may mint one, D-1563). Source: `docs/spec/calls.md:5`, `docs/test-design.md` TD-CALL-12.
- **D-1689** Question (T078, CALL-007, CALL-008, D-141): what does the call log hold, and how does `payments`' refund rule (FEE-022 to FEE-024, `refund_rules::CallRecord`) get it, when `calls` (layer 5) cannot call `payments` (layer 3, `kit/layers.json`)? Choice: `migrations/0116_calls_call_log.sql` adds the append-only `calls.call_log` (default SELECT and INSERT only, D-1520): the line, the provider's call SID (unique, so a repeated status callback logs nothing twice, JOB-006), who called by role only (`business` or `homeowner`, no phone number), who answered (`person`, `machine`, `nobody`), the length in whole seconds, `reached_45s` (checked to equal `length_seconds >= 45`; for reports only, no rule reads it) and when it ended. `calls::api::log_finished_call` writes a row and `call_log` reads a line's rows back; the pure `talked` (a person answered, either direction, any length) and `business_attempt` (only the business's calls) live in `app/calls/src/rules.rs`. `picks`, which may call both crates, maps `LoggedCall` into `payments::api::CallRecord` (`Caller::Homeowner` to `Customer`, `AnsweredBy::Nobody` to `NoAnswer`, `AnsweredBy::Unknown` to `Machine`: never a person, still a business attempt) when it gathers the refund facts; that wiring is the refund task's, not T078's.
- **D-1690** Question (T078, CALL-008): how is "a person or a machine answered" read from the voice provider? Choice: `calls::api::answered_by(CallStatus, AnsweredBy)`: only a `completed` call was answered (busy, no-answer, failed and canceled are `Nobody`); only `human` is `Person`; a `machine_…` or `fax` detection is `Machine`; `unknown`, any other word or no detection on a completed call is `Unknown` (stored `unknown`), which `talked` never counts, since CALL-007 counts only a call answered by a person and a voicemail the detector missed, or a hang-up before the detector decided, must not deny the homeowner-unreachable refund (FEE-022); the log keeps `unknown` apart from `machine` so reports can see how often detection fails. `finished_call` takes a verified status callback's params and refuses anything without a `CA…` SID, a final status and a whole-second `CallDuration` (absent means 0); the length is a `u32` and the column `bigint`, so no length can fail to fit. For T080 (a requirement, not optional): `finished_call` must be fed the dialed leg's own final status callback (the `<Number>`'s child call: its `CallSid`, `CallStatus`, `CallDuration` and `AnsweredBy`), never the first (inbound or parent) leg's, whose status is `completed` whenever the caller was answered by our TwiML; T080 adds to `dial_twiml`'s `<Number>` a `statusCallback` with `statusCallbackEvent="completed"` (and the machine-detection result, through that callback or an `amdStatusCallback`) on its own signed webhook route, which does not exist yet; until then nothing is logged, and a call whose detection result never arrives is logged `Unknown`, never `Person`. The voice handler (T080) supplies who called, as it knows the party.
- **D-1691** Question (T078, CALL-006, TD-CALL-03): no TwiML existed yet; how is "no call request or TwiML ever asks for recording" proved? Choice: `calls::api::dial_twiml(pool number, phone)` is the one TwiML that bridges a masked call: `<Dial callerId=… record="do-not-record">` with `<Number machineDetection="Enable">` (so the log can say who answered, D-1690), returned as a `SecretString` because it holds a phone number, and `None` for a number that is not E.164, so nothing but digits reaches the XML; T080's bridging must use it. `tests/integration/tests/no_recording.rs` catches the voice adapter's real open and end requests on a fake vendor and finds no recording parameter, checks the TwiML, and scans the `calls` and voice sources for recording verbs and callbacks.
- **D-1692** Question (T078, size budget): the prompt's budget is 5 files and 350 changed lines; the change is 13 files and about 900 lines. Choice: kept as one pull request, as D-1504 did. Besides the five owned files it needs the shared `lib.rs`, `api.rs`, `src/tests/mod.rs` (new: the crate had no unit tests), `Cargo.toml` (proptest as a dev-dependency for the R17 property test), `Cargo.lock`, two `.sqlx/` files, `CLAUDE.md`, `docs/architecture.md` and this file; the integration test is about 250 lines because TD-CALL-03 needs a fake vendor to catch real requests.
- **D-1694** Question (T079, CALL-009, CALL-010): the app role may change only `calls.number_pool.closed_at`, and `jobs` (layer 4) cannot call `calls`; how does a line close, record why, tell the business of a cancel and keep it free of a strike? Choice: `calls::api::close_line(db, (job, job number), CloseReason, now)` sets `closed_at` on the job's open line and writes one audit row whose action names the reason (`calls.line_closed_cancelled`, `_no_show`, `_complaint`, `_expired`), in one transaction; a job with no open line returns `None`, so a repeat does nothing (JOB-006). Only `Cancelled` queues a notice: one `messaging.business_notice` task (template `line_closed_cancelled`, en and es: the call number for the job is off now, "This doesn't count against you. Nothing to do.") to `businesses::api::notice_addresses(PicksAndRelease)`, the owner and every "Confirm and billing" member, deduped per line, as `picks` does (D-491). `calls` records no strike for any reason. `close_expired(db, now)` closes every line open `LINE_DAYS` (30) days or more, with one audit row each. The callers are later tasks': the cancel, no-show and complaint flows in `picks` or `intake` (T191 and the complaint task) pass the job number, and the daily sweep that calls `close_expired` needs a scheduled task (not built here). Reason: CALL-009, CALL-010; only `closed_at` is granted (D-1679).
- **D-1695** Question (T079, CALL-012, BIZ-033, TD-CALL-08): no table stores an owner's approval of a member-linked phone (D-963's known gap), and T148, which owns the YES and Approve paths, adds no column for it; how is the gate built and tested here? Choice: the pure `calls::api::phone_works(PhoneStanding { linked_by_owner, owner_approved })` and `gate(Party, PhoneStanding)`, which turns a business phone that does not work yet into `Party::Unlinked`, so it hears the PIN prompt and never connects as the business; TD-CALL-08's case seeds the standing as values. `answer_call` (T077's `routing.rs`, not this task's file) still treats every linked phone as its business: T080, which extends `routing.rs`, must apply `gate` before `route`, and T148 must store the approval (a `businesses` migration) and the main/owner flag and pass them in. Listed for Casey. Reason: the task's files are `lifecycle.rs` and its test; the plan gives no task the approval column.
- **D-1696** Question (T079, CALL-011, D-078, D-311): what does a blocked call from an unlinked staff phone trigger, and what does the LINK text say? Choice: `calls::api::request_link(db, line, blocked phone, now)`, for T080's voice handler to call once a blocked call's line is known, queues one `messaging.business_notice` (template `link_this_phone`) whose `to` (the email list) is the owner and every "Confirm and billing" member and whose `text_to` is `"main_phone"` (`LINK_TEXT_TO`): the "Reply LINK <PIN>" text goes only to the business's signed-up main phone, and only when the business chose text, never to members' phones; it names only the last 4 digits and the line's PIN; it returns whether a notice was queued now (`false` for a repeat, a closed line or a number under 4 digits). It is deduped once per line with a key of IDs only (`messaging.business_notice.link_this_phone.<line>`, no digits, R13); a later blocked call on the same line from another phone queues nothing, as the business already has the line's PIN, and a line lives at most 30 days, so the key's life is bounded by the line's; the full number is never stored. Fix round: the first version sent one notice to every recipient's channels and keyed it by the last 4 digits. Gaps, recorded exactly: `calls` cannot read the main phone or the business's channel choice (both are `businesses`' and `messaging`'s, and no public read exists), so `messaging`'s `business_notice` sender (T094's pipeline, not built) must resolve `text_to: "main_phone"` to the main phone's sender entry and honour the channel choice; the email's "Link this phone" link needs T148's page, so until then the email carries the same words and the PIN. The test asserts the payload as built (`to`, `text_to`, the key). The template reuses the placeholders `{number}` (the last 4 digits) and `{job}` (the PIN), because `messaging`'s registry test renders every template with a fixed sample set that has no `pin` and that test is not this task's; rename them when it gains one. Not built: the 45-minute "call from your main phone" follow-up (it needs the voice handler's "got through" signal, T080), the LINK reply handler and the "Link this phone" page (T148). Reason: CALL-011; only consenting numbers are texted (D-078).
- **D-1697** Question (T079, CALL-020, D-227): how does a call to the Ask Hava number sound, and what is the Spanish? Choice: `calls::api::greeting_twiml()`: `<Say language="en-US">` with CALL-020's English, then `<Say language="es-MX">` with "Habla Ask Hava LLC. Trabajamos por mensaje de texto. Para hacer una solicitud, mande un texto a este número. Para ayuda, mande AYUDA. Si es una emergencia, cuelgue y llame al 911." (back-translation: "Ask Hava LLC speaking. We work by text message. To make a request, send a text to this number. For help, send AYUDA. If it is an emergency, hang up and call 911."; AYUDA is CON-018's Spanish HELP), then `<Hangup/>`: no `Record`, `Dial`, `Gather` or voicemail, so nothing is recorded or forwarded. The inbound-voice route that returns it is T080's. Reason: CALL-020, D-227.
- **D-1698** Question (T079, size budget): the budget is 2 files and 450 changed lines; the change is about 700 lines in the two owned files plus the shared `lib.rs`, `api.rs`, `Cargo.toml` (`askhava-businesses`, `askhava-core`, `serde_json`, all already workspace crates), `Cargo.lock`, three `.sqlx/` files, two template files, `CLAUDE.md`, `docs/architecture.md`, `docs/for-casey-review.md` and this file. Choice: kept as one pull request, as D-1692 did; the integration test is about 390 lines because each TD case needs a business with three members, a contact and a line on a fresh database. CALL-018 needs no code: `assign_number` never reads how the homeowner chose to be reached, and `td_call_05_an_email_preferred_homeowner_still_gets_a_line` proves it.
- **D-1699** Question (T081): how are the sign-up and identity records stored, and how is the identity letter's code checked, when Twilio Verify sends only texts and emails? Choice: one `businesses.signup` row per business holds the sign-up email's opaque mailbox ID (BIZ-019), the optional source answer and `g` code (BIZ-053), the identity step reached, the code and match ticks, the first flag, when it began waiting and was last told (BIZ-020) and the About us line (BIZ-022); `docs/architecture.md` section 3's `businesses.identity_attempt` and `businesses.signup_review` are folded into it, since one step and one review state per sign-up is all the rules read (as T182 kept the pause reason on the row instead of `pause_event`). Record contacts are passed in by the caller from `licensing`'s record as `RecordContacts` and never stored here (PRIV-001, D-059). The chain is `next_step`: a Verify text to the record phone when it gets texts, then a Verify email, then the letter; there is no voice step (BIZ-046, D-366). The letter's six-digit code is `letter_code`, an HMAC of the business ID under the ID secret, so no code is stored; the Lob mailing that prints it is the composition's and is not wired in this task. With no record contact at all the sign-up is flagged `no_record_contact` and waits in needs review; after the letter nothing more is sent and no flag is added. Code-entry attempt limits are the sign-up route's (SEC rate limits), not this module's. Reason: BIZ-002, D-059, D-281, R11.
- **D-1700** Question (T081, BIZ-022): the About us line must be "checked like a quote (PICK-007)", but `businesses` (layer 4) may not call `quotes` or `ai`. Choice: `about_us.rs` keeps its own short lists: seven or more digits in a row (spaces, dashes, dots and brackets ignored) or a link or email shape is a contact; "call me"-style wording is a contact; "find us on", "search", Google, Facebook and Yelp are channel directions; the WORD-003 claims ("best", "#1", "vetted", "top rated" and their Spanish forms) and `catalog`'s CARD-010 restricted list are claims; "licensed" on a no-license card is refused. The public business name (PICK-041, D-336) is checked for contacts, links and channel directions. Each refusal returns a plain reason line. Reason: the layer rule (`kit/layers.json`), D-491.
- **D-1701** Question (T081): what of the goal is left to the composition or later tasks? Choice: this task builds the records, the rules and their tests; not wired here: the BIZ-020 status email itself (`review_due` and `review_told` give the worker task its list; the text path is TD-BIZ-14's), the Lob letter, the BIZ-021 "<Trade> is open" notice, the BIZ-016 activation list for the owner portal and digest, the LIC-012 limit on who may tick pest control (the sign-up list shows pest like any trade, TD-LIC-17), and TD-BIZ-12's confirmed-handyman-breach case (LIC-025), which is left to the task that records Casey's breach decision. The BIZ-040 verified-email check is T196's (D-491). Reason: the size budget; each piece needs the messaging, letters or portal wiring of a later task.
- **D-1702** Question (T081, size budget): the budget is 7 files and 450 changed lines; the change is about 1,100 lines in the owned files (three new modules, the queries, the migration and a 450-line integration test) plus the shared `lib.rs`, `api.rs`, `Cargo.toml` (`askhava-adapters`, `askhava-catalog`, `askhava-licensing`, `askhava-payments`, `sha2`, all already workspace crates on the allowed list and inside `businesses`' layer calls), `Cargo.lock`, ten `.sqlx/` files, `CLAUDE.md`, `docs/architecture.md` and this file. Choice: kept as one pull request, as D-1692 and D-1698 did; the goal names eleven requirements and six test entries, which do not fit 450 lines.
- **D-1703** Question (T081 review): how strict are the About us screen and the identity code checks? Choice: `about_us.rs` matches its word lists (contact wording, channel directions, the WORD-003 claims, "licensed") as whole words, like `catalog::restricted_match`, so "Asbestos" is not "best", "research" is not "search" and "unlicensed" is not "licensed"; `@`, `.com` and `#1` stay substring checks, and a domain is a word ending in `.com`, `.net`, `.org`, `.biz` or `.us` after a letter or digit, so "1998.Usually" passes. A phone number is also three number words in a row or seven or more digits and number words mixed, as `quotes::gate::number_run` reads them (the number-word list is copied, since `businesses` cannot call `quotes`). The claims list adds "top", "mejor", "mejores" and "verificado" in its four forms. `send_code` and `check_code` refuse (`BusinessesError::Refused`) a business whose status is not `Pending` or `NeedsReview` (`AccountStatus::takes_identity_code`), so an active, paused, waitlisted or removed account never gets or checks a code. The letter code is compared in constant time with `subtle` (already a workspace crate on `kit/allowed_crates.txt`, used by `portals`; no new library, so no new cargo-audit entry). Neither function counts attempts: the sign-up route that calls `check_code` MUST limit code attempts per business (SEC rate limits), since the six-digit letter code is stable for the business's lifetime and the Verify codes rely on Verify's own limits. A repeated sign-up category is listed and counted once. Reason: the T081 review; BIZ-002, BIZ-022, PICK-007, WORD-003.
- **D-1704** Question (T080, CALL-013, CALL-023): how do the PIN prompt's 10-second wait and one repeat, and "calling side only", show in code? Choice: `calls::routing::PinWait` reads `ASKHAVA_PIN_WAIT_SECONDS` (added to `core`'s `KEYS`; 10 to 60, default 10, the upper bound Twilio's longest `Gather` timeout) the way `picks::ConfirmSettings` reads its key; `pin_prompt_twiml` is two identical spoken `Gather`s with that timeout, then a spoken goodbye and `Hangup`, so the repeat and the end need no server state; the pure `pin_heard` states the rule for tests (a digit at 9 seconds is taken, none by 10 repeats, none after the repeat ends). The prompt and the read-back are replies to the calling leg's own webhook, and `dial_twiml` keeps no `url` on `Number`, so nothing plays to the dialed homeowner. Reason: CALL-013 names a setting; TwiML's fall-through after a silent `Gather` gives exactly one repeat.
- **D-1705** Question (T080, CALL-019, CALL-022, D-491): what does the safety call event carry and how is each call logged without a new table? Choice: `intake::emergency::enqueue_safety_call` queues `calls.safety_call` with the contact, inbox message, arrival time and Casey's critical alert, only while the switch is on and `safety_call_trigger` matches (gas, CO, smoke, fire, burning, spark, shock words; a going-off alarm only with CO, smoke or fire words), deduped on the alert so a second message about the same emergency queues nothing. `calls::place_safety_call` re-checks the switch, the 30 minutes and that the calling pool number is not the main number, then the suppression list, dials once with a key derived from the alert, and writes one `calls.safety_call_placed` audit row (subject the inbox message, field `safety_script_v1`, the row's time); "press 9" writes `calls.safety_call_press_9`, and refusals are returned to the caller. The switch is the pure `SafetySwitch` (private field, on only through `turn_on` with an approval that has a reference and every CALL-022 item true); its store, page and the handler's registration wait for T108 and T096, so at launch nothing places a call (D-384). Reason: the audit log already holds time, message and action; a call log table would be a migration this task does not own. Review fix (T080 review, CALL-019, CALL-022, JOB-006): `safety_call_trigger` is now true only on a 911-list match (`check` gives `Match`), so the voice call never fires where no INT-004 text and no critical alert exist and `enqueue_safety_call` no longer rests on the caller's alert alone; within a match it calls for gas, smoke, fire and electrical matches, a CO, smoke or fire alarm going off, and otherwise (a power line or a bare going-off alarm) only for whole spark, burning or electrocution words or a shock or "descarga" word beside an electric word or part, so "sparkling", "shocked by the price", "el quemador", "quemadura" and "la descarga del inodoro" never call. Consequence: "I got a shock from the switch" or "me dio una descarga" alone, which INT-002's list does not match, places no call; a shock-only 911 entry would be an INT-002 change for Casey (raised in `docs/for-casey-review.md`). T096 must still call `enqueue_safety_call` only on its suspension path with the alert raised for that match. `place_safety_call` now commits a `calls.safety_call_dialing` claim (subject the alert, field `safety_script_v1`) through the new `ops::api::audit_once` (one transaction, an advisory lock on action and subject, then an existence check on the subject index) before dialling, and returns `AlreadyPlaced` when the claim exists, so a retried or doubled task dials once; a provider refusal after the claim writes `calls.safety_call_failed` about the message and is not retried (at most one call per emergency beats a second call). CALL-022's log is now complete in `calls`: the trigger message is every row's subject, the script version the claim's and placed row's field, the time the row's, the result `calls.safety_call_result` (`to_status` `person`, `machine`, `unknown` or `nobody`, from `safety_call_answered` for every answer) and every key press (`calls.safety_call_press_9` with field `key_9`, any other key `calls.safety_call_key` with `key_0` to `key_8`, `key_star`, `key_hash` or `key_other`, never the raw input). `Conditions::logged` may be set only once T096's voice route calls `safety_call_answered` and `safety_call_key` for every call; nothing sets it today. `ops::api::audit_once` adds two `.sqlx/` files, written by an online build against a migrated scratch database.
- **D-1706** Question (T080, OPS-028): how does `calls` acknowledge a critical alert "through `ops::api`" when `ops` had no acknowledge function? Choice: `ops::api::acknowledge_alert(db, alert, at)` (a new public function in the shared `api.rs`) sets `resolved_at` on an open critical alert and writes one `ops.alert_acknowledged` system audit row in one transaction, false on a repeat; the weekly digest (a later task) lists those rows. `calls::safety_call_answered` calls it only for `AnsweredBy::Person`. Its `.sqlx/` file was written by an online build against a migrated scratch database and matches byte for byte.
- **D-1707** Question (T080, OPS-028, CON-035): from which number does Casey's bridge ring, and on which channel does "press 9" list a number? Choice: `ring_owner` dials Casey from an Ask Hava pool number (the voice adapter dials only from a `PoolNumber`, CALL-021), keyed on the alert and the press, and `owner_bridge_twiml` says the INT-004 words to him, then dials her with that number shown, never recorded; his number is never sent to her. "Press 9" lists through `messaging::api::suppress` with channel `owner` and detected `voice:press_9`, since `RevokeChannel` has no voice channel; a `voice` channel is a proposal for `messaging`'s owner. `voice.rs` has its own `VoiceError` (`Calls` or `Provider`) for the two functions that dial, since `models.rs` is not this task's. Review notes (T080 review): (1) CALL-022 and OPS-028 say the call shows "the Ask Hava number", but CALL-021 lets the voice adapter dial only from a `PoolNumber`, and CALL-022 forbids the main number for the safety call; so Casey's bridge shows a pool number, not the main number. This is a plan conflict, raised in `docs/for-casey-review.md`; if he wants the main number shown on his bridge, a harness or adapters task must let the adapter dial from it. (2) Who hears the INT-004 words is a choice: only Casey's leg, read before the dial, so he knows why he is calling; she hears nothing played (CALL-023), and he says what he needs himself. (3) "Press 9" is stored on the suppression list with channel `owner` and detected `voice:press_9`, so the list row reads as an owner-entered listing; the `voice:press_9` tag and the `calls.safety_call_press_9` audit row (field `key_9`, subject the message) are what mark it as her key press. A `voice` `RevokeChannel` stays a proposal for `messaging`'s owner.
- **D-1708** Question (T080, size budget and plan gaps): the budget is 4 files and 400 changed lines. Choice: one pull request of about 900 lines: the four owned files plus `calls`' `lib.rs` and `api.rs`, `intake`'s and `ops`' `api.rs`, `core`'s `settings.rs` key, one `.sqlx/` file, the `CLAUDE.md` files, `docs/architecture.md` and this file. Gaps for the runner: the voice adapter's `open_call` sends no `Url` or `Twiml`, so a placed call has no script until a harness or adapters task adds one; no inbound-voice route serves the TwiML yet; T096 must call `enqueue_safety_call` and register `place_safety_call`, T108 the switch store and the "Call from the Ask Hava number" button. Copy (WORD-028, WORD-029): the cold read and copy panel rewrote the PIN prompt ("Please enter the 4 digit PIN you were given. Take your time."), its goodbye (adds "You can call back to try again"), the callback ("To call us back, dial 9 2 8, 5 5 5, 0 1 0 0", grouped as people say numbers) and the safety script's order (leave and call 911 before "Ask Hava is not an emergency service"; "You sent us a message about a danger"); not taken: "L L C" in the code call, since CALL-014 writes "LLC" and CALL-022 "L L C" (how the live voice says "LLC" is to be heard before Gate C). Review notes (T080 review): (1) the code call wraps its words in SSML `<prosody rate="slow">` inside a plain `<Say>` with no `voice` attribute; Twilio applies SSML only to Polly or Google voices, so with the default voice the slow rate may be ignored (the comma-separated digits still give pauses); the voice is to be set and heard before Gate C. (2) The code-call and safety-call scripts are English only: CALL-014, CALL-015 and CALL-022 give English words and no Spanish script exists in the spec; a Spanish version needs Casey's words (TXT-039 covers texts, not calls). (3) `code_call_twiml` now takes only 4 to 8 ASCII digits as the code, so "+1234" is refused (the `+` was stripped by the number reader).
- **D-1709** Question (T193, BIZ-026, BIZ-031, CARD-019, D-491): what do the sign-up screens rest on, and what is left for later? Choice: `portals::business_signup` renders every screen from facts (as `receipts_page` does) and `done_facts` reads them; the routes that serve and post the screens wait on the business portal's sign-in and form handling, the daily-list hook that calls `businesses::api::resume_on_new_record` and sends `signup_record_updated` waits on the daily list worker, and the launch email that `claim_launch_notice` guards waits on the trade-opened notice (BIZ-021). The done screen's <n> counts the active businesses with a job type in the trade (the businesses a card in that trade goes to) plus the business itself, which is not active yet; a waitlist screen counts waitlisted businesses whose sign-up chose the trade (`businesses.signup.trades`, new, since sign-up stored no categories). The hard-bounce exclusion of CARD-019 is not applied, since the provider-accepted count is T147's. Jobs store no trade, so the open jobs are every carded job still in Open or No quotes yet (`quotes::api::open_card_jobs`, using `JobStatus::takes_late_cards`), shown under the trade the route passes; each links to `/b/jobs/<job ID>` until the business job page's route exists. Source: `docs/spec/businesses.md:30`, `docs/spec/businesses.md:35`, `docs/spec/job-cards.md:23`.
- **D-1710** Question (T193, BIZ-031): BIZ-031's sentences read "You're one of <n> businesses" and "one of <n> businesses waiting"; what does the first business see? Choice: "You're the first <trade> business so far." and "the first business waiting", the rest of each sentence unchanged; "one of 1 businesses" is not plain English (WORD-028). Every <n> of 2 or more uses the spec's words exactly. Source: `docs/spec/businesses.md:35`.
- **D-1711** Question (T193, BIZ-026, BIZ-027, D-223): which settings, defaults and date form? Choice: `ASKHAVA_BIZ_REVIEW_TARGET_DAYS` (default 4, calendar days) and `ASKHAVA_BIZ_LIST_DELAY_DAYS` (the typical delay before the daily list shows a record change, default 3, a guess until the first lists are read), each a whole number from 1 to 30, parsed by `businesses::api::SignupSettings::from_pairs` and listed in `core`'s known keys. The review target is the waiting time plus 24 hours a day, shown as a month and day in Arizona time (UTC-7, no daylight time): "Decide by <date>, 4 calendar days after this came in. Nothing is held up in the meantime."; the owner-portal view that shows it is T108's. Source: `docs/spec/businesses.md:30`, `docs/spec/businesses.md:31`.
- **D-1712** Question (T193, BIZ-026, PRIV-001, D-178): how does the sign-up know the next daily list shows a new record contact without storing the contact, and where does the chain restart? Choice: "That number is old" stores three SHA-256 digests, one each for the record's texting phone, email and mailing address, each over the ID secret, the business ID, the contact kind and the value, length-prefixed (`old_text_key`, `old_mail_key`, `old_letter_key`, named by chain step since contact words in a column name belong to the vault, TD-PRIV-01; `businesses` has `sha2` but no HMAC crate, and the digests are only compared). `RecordContacts` holds only a has-address flag, so the caller passes the full record address beside it (`RecordSeen`). `resume_on_new_record` ends the wait when a contact present on the new list differs from the one saved, and sets `identity_step` to the step before the first changed contact in chain order (none for the phone, text for the email, email for the address), so the next `send_code` goes to the changed record contact (an email-only change resumes at the email, an address-only change at the letter), never to the old one or a typed one; a contact that only disappeared does not resume. Only a sign-up whose code is not yet done can wait. Known gap, outside T193's files: `identity::send_code`'s idempotency key is the business and the step only (T081's `identity.rs`), so a resumed send on a step already used (a new phone after a text, a new email after an email) reuses the earlier key, and Verify could treat it as a repeat; the key should add the contact's digest or an attempt count, which needs a change to `identity.rs` by its owner or a fix task. Source: `docs/spec/businesses.md:30`.
- **D-1713** Question (T193, size budget): the budget is 5 files and 350 changed lines. Choice: one pull request of about 1,400 lines (about 470 of them tests): the five owned files, plus `businesses`' and `portals`' `api.rs` and `CLAUDE.md`, `portals`' `lib.rs` and `Cargo.toml` (the allowed path dependency on `businesses`, layer 4, D-491), `quotes`' `api.rs` and `CLAUDE.md` (`open_card_jobs`), `core`'s `settings.rs` keys, the `signup_record_updated` English and Spanish templates (Spanish marked draft), seven `.sqlx/` files, `docs/architecture.md` and this file. The letter screen links to the Registrar of Contractors' site (`https://roc.az.gov`) as the ROC update guide until an Ask Hava guide page exists. The cold read (WORD-028) and copy panel (WORD-029) rewrites were applied (the code lines now say text or email and name the ROC or city license record; the fix-record lines are shorter; the button says "Next: get your code"), except the panel's title "Get Lake Havasu City job requests by email", which would be wrong once business texting is on (WEB-024). Both readers note that WEB-024's "We don't text or call businesses." sits beside a sign-up code sent by text (BIZ-002, BIZ-024's "forward the text"); the spec line is kept word for word and the conflict is left for a spec change. AI-smell list: add "the list we check" and "goes by email to the email". Review fixes: the pest fields carry no `required` (the server checks them only when pest control is ticked, LIC-047); a Spanish notice line is marked `lang="es"` on its element, and the Spanish notice lines are drafts for native review, as `es.json`'s are; the fee box writes a Confirm window that is not whole hours as hours and minutes ("4 business hours and 30 minutes") instead of cutting it down; the catalog has no display names, so a category shows as its code in sentence case ("Plumbing repair"). Source: `kit/prompts/T193.md:44`.
- **D-1714** Question (T082; CON-019, CON-020, BIZ-017, BIZ-032, BIZ-048): where do the consent, welcome, business STOP, auto-reply and recruiting rules live, given that the task owns only `consent.rs`, its test and one migration? Choice: all in `app/businesses/src/consent.rs`, exported through `businesses::api`. The E-SIGN box is a value (`consent_box`, `ticked: false`) whose wording names each channel; `record_consent` refuses an unticked box or one with no channel and stores one append-only `businesses.esign_consent` row per channel with `CONSENT_VERSION` (`con019-v1`) and the time, plus an audit row; the table's channel check allows only `email` and `text`, so no call consent can be stored (D-344). `may_text` is true only for a current member who ticked its own text box (D-191), so the owner's box never covers a member's phone and an email-only box covers no phone. The welcome and the BIZ-017 owner email are recorded as `core.task` requests (`businesses.welcome`, deduped per business; `businesses.phone_stopped`, deduped per inbox row), since `messaging`'s email request for modules above does not exist yet (D-1380) and its `Notice` enum is not this task's; `phone_stopped` never changes the account status (D-311 superseding D-062). `may_get_cards` is false until `welcome_sent` marks the welcome gone (CON-020). `auto_reply_due` is false for a text the caller expected (a quote or a reply it asked for, which only `picks` and `quotes` can read, layer rules), HELP, INFO, AYUDA, an opt-out and a command word (CONFIRM, YES, HOLD, PAUSE, RESUME, BUSY, START, LINK and their Spanish), and true for anything else; the charge details and the help request are T148's and T151's (D-492). Recruiting has no text or call path at all; `recruiting_email` opens with "This email is an advertisement for Ask Hava.", refuses a subject that is empty or starts like a reply, a forward or a notice, and needs an askhava.com stop link and a checked P.O. box or PMB; `businesses.recruit_stop` keeps the keyed digest of each address that stopped, honored at once by `may_recruit`. Source: `kit/prompts/T082.md:11`.
- **D-1715** Question (T082, wiring outside the owned files): the sign-up form template, `quotes`' card sender, the inbound text route and the email handlers are other tasks' files. Choice: this task stores and gates; wiring follows with the owners: the sign-up form shows `consent_box` and posts it to `record_consent` (BIZ-001's form, with the portal routes, D-1709); activation (`identity::settle`, `approve`) is followed by `request_welcome`; `quotes`' card sender must check `may_get_cards` next to `receives_cards` before any card; every business text send must check `may_text` for the phone's member before `send_checked`; the inbound route calls `phone_stopped` after `messaging`'s `Outcome::OptedOut` for a number `sender_business` knows, and sends `business_auto_reply` when `auto_reply_due`; the email handlers for `businesses.welcome` (lines from `welcome_lines`, the contact card file, `welcome_sent` after the send) and `businesses.phone_stopped` (`stopped_email_line` with the last 4 read from the vault, to the owner's account address) come with the email request (D-1380). Known gaps until then: a card is not yet held for the welcome, and a member's phone is not yet checked for its text box at send time; the text-only business's move to email on an owner STOP is T147's channel preference (D-491). Source: `kit/prompts/T082.md:11`.
- **D-1716** Question (T082 cold read and copy panel): which rewrites were taken? Choice: the email box reads "I agree to get job and account notices from Ask Hava by email at the address above, not on paper."; the text box adds "Message frequency varies."; the welcome email puts the sender address and the spam steps first, says "If we land in spam or junk:" before the provider steps, drops "Ask Hava never calls you with a recording." (the fixed BIZ-046 line "Ask Hava never calls you." already says it, more strongly) and says "If you choose texts, text STOP from a phone to stop texts to that phone."; the auto-reply says "We couldn't read that as a quote or a reply word." and the Spanish uses "mensaje" and "Escriba AYUDA", all GSM-7 in one segment. Not taken: the panel's "texts about job cards, picks and reminders" for the text box, since CON-019 names "job-card texts"; both readers note that BIZ-036 also texts picks and reminders, so the CON-019 wording should be widened by a spec change. The panel's optional fee line in the welcome is left out (CON-020 does not list it). AI-smell list: add "We can't read this text". Source: `kit/prompts/T082.md:230`.
- **D-1717** Question (T082 review fixes; CON-019, CON-020, BIZ-017, BIZ-032, BIZ-042, D-191): what changed after the fresh-eyes review? Choice: (1) text consent is per phone: `businesses.esign_consent` gains `line_id`, the `businesses.staff_phone` ID (named for the line, since a column named for a contact kind belongs to the vault, TD-PRIV-01; required on a text row, absent on an email row, by a check; no foreign key, since an unlinked `staff_phone` row is deleted while its consent stays as history, and a relinked phone gets a new ID and needs a new box); `record_consent` takes `(business, member, phone)` and refuses a text box with no phone or another business's phone (`UnknownPhone`); `may_text(business, phone)` is true only while the phone is linked to that business and a current member ticked the text box for it, so D-1715's "check `may_text` for the phone's member" now reads "for the phone's `staff_phone` ID". (2) The welcome's spam steps add BIZ-042's Gmail filter with "Never send it to Spam" and "In any other email app, add us to your contacts." (4) `auto_reply_due` treats a text as a command only when the whole text is a command word (CONFIRM, YES, SÍ, HOLD, ESPERA, AWAY, AUSENTE, PAUSE, RESUME, BUSY, START, UNSTOP, LINK and their Spanish) alone or with one whole number, trailing periods and exclamation marks dropped, as `picks`' `read_business_word` and `read_time_word` accept them; "Yes, why was I charged?" and "Hold on, what is this $75?" get the reply. An empty text (a photo alone, or blank) is not a keyword, a quote or an expected reply, so under BIZ-032 it gets the reply pointing to the portal; a photo the app expects (a quote) is the caller's `expected`. (5) Each audit row names its true subject: `businesses.team_member` for a consent, `businesses.business` for the welcome, `messaging.inbox` for a STOP. (8) The welcome's first line says "Your business is active and can now get job cards.", true for an email or text choice (BIZ-036); a repeated box (the same member, channel, phone and version, also twice in one call) stores no second row and no second audit row (a unique index with NULLS NOT DISTINCT, `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING`). Not changed here (review items 3 and 6, wiring in other tasks' files, D-1715): the sign-up form and its post are the portal sign-up routes' (T193's screens, wired by the portal routes task); the card sender's `may_get_cards` check is `quotes`' card sending (T044's code, by a fix task or the next task that touches it); the inbound route's `phone_stopped` and auto-reply calls and the text-only move to email are T147's and T148's; the two email handlers come with `messaging`'s email request (D-1380). Source: `kit/prompts/T082.md:11`.
- **D-1718** Question (T082, size budget): the budget is 3 files and 500 changed lines. Choice: one pull request of about 1,050 changed lines (about 340 of them tests): the three owned files, plus `businesses`' `api.rs`, `lib.rs` and `CLAUDE.md`, the `business_auto_reply` English and Spanish templates (Spanish a draft for native review), the `.sqlx/` query files, `docs/architecture.md` and this file; splitting the five requirements across pull requests would leave the consent, welcome and STOP rules half-built in one task. Source: `kit/prompts/T082.md:44`.
- **D-1719** Question (T083; BIZ-012, BIZ-029, OPS-005, OPS-001, D-222, D-280): which `ops.alert` rows does a complaint write, and how is "3 in 90 days" counted? Choice: a safety-word complaint writes one `businesses.complaint_safety` row at once and every complaint writes one `businesses.complaint` row when its 5-day reply box closes (the `businesses.complaint_box_closed` task, retried while the box is still open; `listed_at` makes a repeat write nothing). Both are severity `normal`, as `intake`'s urgent call-back alert is: OPS-032's push picks safety complaints by kind (T204), and a `high` severity would let an unacknowledged complaint start OPS-001's safe mode, which only High alerts may. The count covers complaints received from exactly 90 days (2,160 hours, inclusive) before the new one up to it; the third pauses through `pause_for_rule` (`complaints` reason); a business not active (or already paused by a rule) stays as it is. The business row is locked (`FOR UPDATE`) before the count, so two complaints recorded at once cannot both miss the third; a business that moved on meanwhile stays as it is and the complaint stays recorded. The `businesses.complaint_recorded` audit row names the system as actor (the homeowner, not the business, filed it). The safety words are unsafe, threat(s), threatened, threatening, steal, stealing, stole(n), hurt, injured, injury, injuries, police, fire(s) and inseguro/a, peligroso, amenaza(s), amenazó, amenazo, robó, robo, robaron, herido/a, lastimado/a, policía, policia, incendio, fuego, whole words in any case (unaccented Spanish forms included, as texts often drop accents; amended in T083's review round); the homeowner's words are read for this check and never stored (PRIV-001). - **D-1739** Question (plan change, November 6, 2026; numbered under the interim rule of D-1144 because this builder session does not write `claude/kit-state`: max(`next_decision` 1729, re-read after T084 claimed D-1724 to D-1728, main's highest D-1723 + 1, no open `claude/` plan PR) + 10 = 1739, re-read right before committing; an external review of the release path, verified by the overseer against `main` bb6d771; D-1480, D-1563, D-1564, D-1565, D-1688; PICK-022, PICK-023, PICK-024, PRIV-003, PRIV-004, PRIV-005, PRIV-007, SEC-046, BIZ-037, BIZ-043, INT-029, CALL-001; new TD-PICK-48, TD-PICK-49, TD-PICK-50, TD-INT-39; new tasks T253, T254, T255): `picks::api::release` claims the once-only `picks.release` row before it reads the vault (D-1564, kept on purpose so racing proofs cannot both read), so a vault read that fails after the claim commits, a lost response or a reload leaves the business with no way to see the details again; D-1565 (1) gives the fix (a `privacy` capability for the signed-in business session of a released pick, no stored copy, PRIV-002) to "the business-portal release view task", but that task, T085, owns only `app/portals/src/job_release.rs` and its template, no `privacy` or `picks` file, and no recovery case; nothing calls `release` in production, because the `ReleaseSink` was handed to T224 (DONE) by D-1480 (b) and D-1563 (1) and no queued task owns it, nothing moves a pick to `paid` or `free` (D-1564 (1)), and the webhook route is not merged in `server::build_router` (`app/server/src/lib.rs:72`); the `picks.address_needed` event and the re-release once an emergency address arrives (D-1563 (2)) have no owner; D-1688's masked-line retry names T079 (DONE) or the release caller; and no test runs claim-then-vault-failure against the database, because only `privacy`, `payments` and `server` may name the release mint (`tests/integration/tests/architecture.rs:30`) and no test crate may depend on `askhava-server` (D-1563 (4)). Viewing is not an introduction: it writes no release row, notice, charge, fee or masked line and may repeat while the pick stays paid or free and the vault holds the fields; after the PRIV-007 purge or "Delete my data" (T092) it answers that the details were removed. (B) Tests: T253 owns TD-PICK-48 (the access rules, in `app/server/tests/released_view.rs`, since `server` is the one test home allowed the session mint); T254 owns TD-PICK-49 (claim commits, vault fails, vault recovers, reload, restart: the portal path shows the details, one release row, one notice, no second fee) and TD-PICK-50 (status move, duplicate and simultaneous deliveries, line retry) in `app/server/tests/release_recovery.rs`, minting through `server::release_minter()` with real proofs (a seeded $0 decision through `no_fee_release`, and a signed fake event through the webhook route); no test-only route and no public proof constructor, so production authorization is unchanged. T255 (build, stage 4, deps T254 and T162; T103 now depends on T255, the next owner of `app/intake/src/conversation.rs`, and so does T100, the stage-4 cleanup over `app/`) owns the `picks.address_needed` handler (ask the name-and-address question again at once, INT-029), the `intake.address_in` event after an address is taken, `payments::api::reclear_release` (a `Releasable` only from the pick's stored charge success or recorded $0 decision, never a redirect, SEC-030) and its handler in the sink, with TD-INT-39. (D) D-1688's retry belongs to T254: `line_failed` also queues one `picks.line_retry` task whose handler opens the line from the release row's bound contact only if the job never had one, under the worker's retries; the High alert stays. - **D-1751** Question (plan change, November 6, 2026; numbered under the interim rule of D-1144 because this builder session does not write `claude/kit-state`: max(`next_decision` 1729, main's highest D-1723 + 1, the release plan change `claude/plan-release-portal-read` (ae86813) at D-1740 + 1) + 10 = 1751, re-read right before committing; an external repository audit of November 6, 2026 (ChatGPT, pinned main bb6d771), finding A01, verified by this session against main 5aac33d; TXT-012, PRIV-001, CON-008, CON-019, CON-020; new TD-TXT-32, TD-BIZ-39; new task T256): two first texts from one unknown phone race in `app/server/src/inbound_text.rs`: both record their inbox row and find no contact, the loser's `store_contact` answers `VaultError::PhoneTaken` (`app/privacy/src/vault.rs:264`, `:289`, D-752), `vault_halt` makes it `Halt::Failed` (`app/server/src/inbound_text.rs:356`), and `in_transaction` commits the inbox row and answers 200 (D-1311), so the second text never reaches intake and its resend stops as a repeat. - **D-1752** Question (plan change, November 6, 2026; the next number after D-1751 under the same interim rule; audit finding A02; AI-003, AI-020, PRIV-001, PRIV-002, PRIV-003, PRIV-007, PRIV-024; D-752; new TD-AI-19; new task T257): the served SMS route scrubs with `vault_name: None` and a fresh `NameMemory` for every webhook (`app/server/src/inbound_text.rs:297`, `:299`), so neither the vault name (AI-003) nor a name stated in an earlier text (AI-020) is removed from a later one; the scrubber supports both (`app/privacy/src/scrub.rs` `NameMemory`, `mark_known`) but nothing supplies them, and no queued task owns conversation-aware scrubbing (T023, the scrubber's owner, is DONE). Kind: plan, with a narrow rule on in-transaction reads. - **D-1753** Question (plan change, November 6, 2026; the next number after D-1752 under the same interim rule; audit finding A03; FEE-026, FEE-028, FEE-029, FEE-030; D-1543, D-1545; new TD-FEE-42; new task T258): `PaymentsAdapter::create_refund` parses only the refund's ID (`app/adapters/src/payments.rs:176`), `refunds::finish` turns any answer into `RefundOutcome::Refunded`, marks the row `succeeded` and appends the ledger `refund` (`app/payments/src/refunds.rs:279`), and `reconcile::own_refund` counts any answer as refunded (`app/payments/src/reconcile.rs:370`), though Stripe's refund can be `pending`, `requires_action`, `failed` or `canceled`; D-1545 (2) recorded that after `refund.failed` the ledger keeps the `refund` entry because FEE-028 has no reversal kind. How are refunds recorded truthfully? Choice: new task T258 (harness, Opus review, stage 4, deps T066, T067, T176, T075, T064, T071): the typed refund is additive for production callers, and the four test fakes that reach a refund (`tests/integration/tests/disputes.rs`, `late_success.rs`, `reconcile.rs`, `ledger_1000_jobs.rs`, DONE tasks' tests that T258 takes over) each gain one `impl RefundStripe` answering `Succeeded` with the ID their `create_refund` returns, no expected value changing; the other five `PaymentsAdapter` fakes are untouched: a payments-owned trait `RefundStripe: PaymentsAdapter` (the `IntentStripe` and `ReconcileStripe` pattern) in `app/payments/src/refund_stripe.rs` answers a typed refund (ID, state, amount, currency, PaymentIntent; an unknown state is an error) from `refund` and `fetch_refund`, implemented for `StripeHttp` over two new inherent HTTP calls, while `PaymentsAdapter::create_refund` stays unchanged until T132 retires it; `refunds::finish`, the retry and `reconcile::own_refund` take `&impl RefundStripe`; `EntryKind::RefundReversal` needs `app/payments/src/models.rs` (its exhaustive match), which T258 now owns; the `refund` ledger entry is appended only on `succeeded`; `pending`/`requires_action` are stored and asked again; `failed`/`canceled` take FEE-026's failure path; a `failed` or `canceled` after `succeeded` appends one compensating `refund-reversal` entry of the same amount keyed by the `re_…`, and the retry's success appends a new `refund` entry keyed by its own `re_…`, so the ledger stays append-only and nets to Stripe. FEE-028 now lists `refund-reversal` (changed in place in `docs/spec/fees.md`, same source line); this changes D-1545 (2)'s keep-until-retry choice for refunds T258 records. The webhook events that carry these states are dispatched by T259 (D-1754). T258 and T260 both own `app/adapters/src/payments.rs` before T132 (T132 now depends on T260). This is an adapter change (governance section 3, item 4), made here in a plan change with an independent Opus review; `docs/architecture.md` section 7 now says `payments` reads refunds through `RefundStripe`'s typed answer. Review: an independent Fable review of 04637b9 found the first version (changing `create_refund`'s return) would break nine test files T258 does not own and miss `models.rs`; this additive design is its fix; its re-review of 2943cc9 found that the public functions reaching a refund (`request_refund`, `run_refund_retry`, `early_fraud_warning`, `reconcile`, `run_reconcile` and T064's `run_late_refund` in `app/payments/src/late.rs`) must take `&impl RefundStripe` too, so T258 owns `late.rs` and those four test files and is a harness task. `EntryKind` is in `app/payments/src/ledger.rs:14`; the exhaustive match is in `app/payments/src/models.rs:782`. Kind: plan and spec (FEE-028). Owner approval: delegated to the overseer. Reason: a money record must say what Stripe holds; compensating entries keep the ledger append-only. Source: app/adapters/src/payments.rs:176, app/payments/src/refunds.rs:279, docs/spec/fees.md:32

- **D-1773** Question (T194, SEC-004): where does a known device live? T194 owns only `app/portals/src/business_auth.rs` and its test, so it can add no migration, and a device must be remembered server-side (a cookie alone could be forged; the used sign-in link can't serve, since its token sits in the person's email). Choice: a known device is a `portals.login_link` row of that member born used (`used_at = created_at`) with a life of `DEVICE_LIFE` (180 days), holding the SHA256 of a 256-bit token whose only copy is the `__Host-askhava-device` cookie (`Secure`, `HttpOnly`, `SameSite=Lax`, `Path=/`); `known_device` accepts only such a row of the same member whose life is over a day, so a 15-minute link (used or not) is never a device and no link query (`link_open`, `use_link`, both `used_at IS NULL`) ever matches a device row. A correct code stores the device in the sign-in's own transaction. Costs accepted: a device row counts toward `LINKS_PER_LIFE` (one per new-device sign-in), and a removed member's device rows stay but name a member who is no longer current, so they sign no one in. 180 days is a choice (the spec names no device life); it is a constant. Plan gap reported: a `portals.known_device` table would be cleaner; a later task that owns a portals migration may move the rows. Source: `kit/prompts/T194.md:25`, `docs/spec/security.md:8`.
- **D-1774** Question (T194, SEC-004, TXT-038, D-366): how is the code sent and checked? Choice: `DeviceCodes::new(verify, code_address, key)` wraps any `VerifyAdapter` and the composition's `CodeAddress` (which returns `CodeTo::Phone` for the person's own phone that gets texts, else `CodeTo::Email` for their own sign-in address; `portals` never stores or logs either); `CodeTo::channel` gives only `Sms` or `Email`, so a voice code cannot be asked for. On a browser that is not a known device of the link's member, the link's button sends one code and shows the code field (corrected by D-1776: the idempotency key derived from the link's row ID alone does not stop a second code, since Twilio ignores it; a server-side marker does); a new code needs a new link, already capped at 5 per 15 minutes; only a correct 6-digit code uses the link, signs in and remembers the device; a wrong code is an `auth_failed` event, capped per link by D-1777. Nothing goes through the outbox (TXT-038). Without `with_device_codes` the link alone signs in, as T084 built it, so `tests/security/tests/business_signin.rs` (not T194's) keeps passing; the composition must set it when it serves the routes. Source: `kit/prompts/T194.md:50`.
- **D-1775** Question (T194, A11Y-013, A11Y-030): T194 does not own `templates/business_signin.html`.
