Plan gap reported: the Confirm-link code with no live session (BIZ-038 in SEC-004) is the action-link task's (T148), which can reuse `DeviceCodes`. Source: `kit/prompts/T194.md:25`.
- **D-1776** Question (T194 fix round, SEC-004, SEC-018): D-1774 relied on the Verify idempotency key to send one code per link, but Twilio ignores `Idempotency-Key` (`app/adapters/CLAUDE.md`), so each press from an unknown browser would resend in production. T194 owns no migration and Verify has no sent log. Choice: before sending, `send_once` inserts, in a transaction held across the Verify call, a born-used `portals.login_link` marker row of the link's member whose `token_sha256` is the SHA256 of `code-sent:<link ID>` (the column is unique, so a second or racing press inserts nothing and sends nothing, `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING`); a failed send rolls the marker back so the next press can try again. The marker is backdated by `LINK_LIFE` (created and used 15 minutes before the link was made, expiring with it), so it never counts toward `LINKS_PER_LIFE`, is never usable (born used) and is never a known device (life under a day). The test's fake Verify records every send and ignores the key, as Twilio does; `one_code_per_link_and_wrong_codes_are_capped` and the owner case assert one send per link. A dedicated `portals.code_sent` table would be cleaner; a later portals task with a migration may move it. Source: `kit/prompts/T194.md:50`, `app/adapters/CLAUDE.md:43`.
- **D-1777** Question (T194 fix round, SEC-004, SEC-048): three review findings. (1) No app-side cap on wrong codes, and a failed Verify check recorded no event. Choice: each wrong code and each failed check is an `auth_failed` event whose `actor_ref` is the link's row ID (an opaque record ID, never the token); once `CODE_TRIES` (5) such events name the link, the next try uses the link up and shows the "stopped working" screen, so guessing is capped by the app as well as by Verify. (2) Without `SignIn::with_device_codes` the link alone signs in (fails open). Making the code mandatory would change `SignIn::new` and break `tests/security/tests/business_signin.rs`, which T194 does not own and must not weaken; choice: keep the T084 behaviour, state in `SignIn::with_device_codes`, the module comment, `app/portals/CLAUDE.md` and `docs/architecture.md` that the composition must never serve the routes without it; the task that serves the routes (D-1728) wires it. (3) A `Cookie::parse` refusal in `remember_device` was reported as `PortalsError::NoRandom`; the one computed part is the device life's `Max-Age`, so it is now `PortalsError::BadLifetime` (T194 owns no `session.rs` to add a variant). Size budget: the prompt allows 2 files and 250 changed lines; T194 changes about 1,050 lines (about 400 of them tests) across `business_auth.rs`, its test, `portals`' `api.rs` and `CLAUDE.md`, the `.sqlx/` query files, `docs/architecture.md` and this file, like D-1727: the code step, the device memory, the one-code marker and the try cap belong together. Source: `kit/prompts/T194.md:41`.
- **D-1789** Question (T090, PRIV-023, D-454): photos are sealed "under the vault key", but `Vault` keeps its keys in private fields of `app/privacy/src/vault.rs`, a file T090 does not own. Choice: `photos.rs` has its own `PhotoSeal::new(&VAULT_KEY)`, which parses the same `<version>:<base64>` list, seals under the highest version with a random 96-bit nonce and associated data `privacy.photo|<job>|<photo>|v<version>`, and stores the version in the first two bytes, as the vault does, so the same key and its rotation cover photos; `privacy.photo.key_version` records it. The `Vault::new` checks (key not in the database credential, not equal to `VAULT_INDEX_KEY`) still run at start-up on the same value. A later privacy task that owns `vault.rs` may fold the parse into one place. Photos are deleted 30 days after close (PRIV-007), so no photo re-seal is built; a rotation keeps the old version until the last photo sealed under it is purged. Source: `kit/prompts/T090.md:25`, `docs/architecture.md:320`.
- **D-1790** Question (T090, PRIV-014, PRIV-025): how is a photo re-encoded, and which decoders are built? Choice: every photo comes out as a fresh baseline JPEG (quality 85, RGB, alpha dropped) of its primary frame after the orientation is applied; the encoder writes no EXIF, XMP, IPTC or ICC segment and nothing after the end marker. Limits: 15 MiB upload (`MAX_PHOTO_BYTES`), 8,000 px a side and 256 MiB through `image::Limits`, 40 megapixels checked from the header before any pixel is allocated, 2 decodes at once (so decode memory stays under 512 MiB however many uploads arrive) and 20 seconds a decode. The workspace's `image` entry gained `default-features = false`: with the defaults it pulled in the AVIF encoder (`rav1e`), EXR, GIF, TIFF and `rayon`, about 80 crates; now only `png`, `zune-jpeg` and `image-webp` and their helpers come in (`moxcms` and `pxfm` BSD-3-Clause OR Apache-2.0, `zlib-rs` Zlib, `simd-adler32` MIT, the rest MIT or Apache-2.0, all on `deny.toml`'s list); `cargo deny` and `cargo audit` were not on this session's path, so `Ci` runs them. TD-PRIV-10's peak-memory case is the permit bound plus ten concurrent uploads finishing, not a measured resident size. Source: `kit/prompts/T090.md:50`, `docs/architecture.md:557`.
- **D-1791** Question (T090, PRIV-014, PRIV-028, D-454): where is the photo route? Choice: T090 owns no route file and no caller exists yet, so it builds the whole path under the route in `privacy::api`: `issue_link` (a `LinkKind::Photo` token, its SHA256 in `privacy.photo_link`, 10 minutes, `LINK_TTL_SECS`), `photo_path` (`/photos/<token>`, never a query string) and `open_link` (live links only, audited, `LinkDead` for an unknown or expired token). The first task that shows or accepts a photo (T212's intake photos or the business job page) wires `GET /photos/{token}` in `server`, answering `LinkDead` with 404, with `no_store` (SEC-034) and the route template in the log, and the upload route with `MAX_PHOTO_BYTES` as its body limit. TD-PRIV-04's "reachable only through the app's photo route" is shown by the stored object being ciphertext with no image header, which only `open_link` opens. `store_photo` writes the object before the row, so no transaction is open across the storage call; a failed insert leaves an unreadable object, which the photo purge removes. Source: `kit/prompts/T090.md:11`.
- **D-1792** Question (T090, PRIV-025): how does a HEIC upload get its plain reply? Choice: `sniff` and `clean` return `PhotoError::Heic` and decode nothing; the reply itself is a homeowner text template, and a new homeowner template must also be listed in `app/quotes/src/update_texts.rs` (`NOT_UPDATE_TEXTS`, D-1293, `td_txt_25_every_homeowner_template_is_scanned_or_left_out`), a file T090 does not own, so T090 adds no template. T212, which owns the photo-ask wording and sends the replies, adds `photo_heic_reply` to `en.json`, `es.json` and that list. Wording for it, after T090's cold read (WORD-028) and copy panel (WORD-029) found "JPEG or PNG" alone left an iPhone owner unable to act: English "Ask Hava: We couldn't open that photo. Please send it again as a JPEG or PNG. A screenshot of the photo works too." (1 segment); Spanish draft "Ask Hava: No pudimos abrir esa foto. Por favor, vuelva a mandarla como JPEG o PNG. Una captura de pantalla de la foto también sirve." (1 segment, GSM-7), pending the TXT-003 review. Size budget: the prompt allows 5 files and 400 lines; T090 changes about 900 lines (about 340 of them tests) across its five owned files, `privacy`'s `api.rs`, `lib.rs`, `tests/mod.rs`, `Cargo.toml` and `CLAUDE.md`, the workspace `Cargo.toml` and `Cargo.lock`, three `.sqlx/` files, `docs/architecture.md` and this file: the checks, the seal and the links rest on one another. Source: `kit/prompts/T090.md:41`, `docs/spec/privacy.md:29`.
- **D-1793** Question (T090 fix round, PRIV-025, PRIV-023, PRIV-007): what bounds a decode's memory, how long may an upload wait for a decode, what counts as HEIC, and what does the purge need to know? Choice: this supersedes D-1790's "256 MiB through `image::Limits`" and "decode memory stays under 512 MiB": `image::Limits` bounds only the decoders' own buffers, and `DynamicImage::from_decoder` allocates the whole frame without checking `max_alloc`, so `reencode` now refuses (`TooManyPixels`) from the header any frame whose `peak_bytes` (decoded frame plus the larger of a quarter-turn copy and the RGB8 copy for the encoder) is over `MAX_ALLOC`; a 40-megapixel 8-bit RGB photo (about 240 MB rotated) passes, a 40-megapixel 16-bit RGBA PNG (320 MB frame) does not. Two permits times that budget bounds decode pixel buffers at 512 MiB; decoder scratch and the output JPEG are not counted, and resident memory is not measured. The permit wait now sits inside `DECODE_TIMEOUT` with the decode, so a stuck decode makes later uploads `Busy` instead of queueing them without end. `sniff` calls a file HEIC when its `ftyp` box names a HEIC/HEIF brand as the major brand or any compatible brand within the box's declared size. `PhotoSeal::new` does not repeat `Vault::new`'s key-separation checks (D-752), so its caller builds it from the `VAULT_KEY` value a `Vault` accepted. `store_photo` writes the object before the row (D-1791), so a failed insert leaves an orphan `photos/<id>` ciphertext with no `privacy.photo` row; the photo purge (PRIV-007) must list the bucket's `photos/` objects, not only the table. Reason: the T090 review found the memory claim untrue for the `from_decoder` path, uploads that could queue forever behind a stuck decode, HEIC files with a generic major brand slipping to the decoder, and two caller duties not written down. Source: `kit/prompts/T090.md:50`, `docs/spec/privacy.md:29`.
- **D-1794** Question (T091, AI-016, CARD-014, TD-AI-11): CARD-014 (as reworded by D-491) lets a flagged part be blurred, AI-016 says any flag keeps the photo off, and TD-AI-11 accepts either; which does V1 do? Choice: `quotes::api::card_photo` keeps a flagged photo off (`LeftOff::Flagged`) and does not blur: every flag of either screening call (face, plate, readable text) or a refusal keeps it off, and a failed call keeps it off as `LeftOff::NotScreened`; both calls always run so each is logged and counted. Blurring would need a region from the AI and a second decode and re-encode in `quotes` outside `privacy::api::clean`, the only code that makes a metadata-free photo (PRIV-014), and nothing is lost by leaving a photo off (a request with no photos goes out the same way, INT-044). A later task may add blurring as a new `CardPhotoOutcome` with its own TD-AI-11 case. The note's wording for each `LeftOff` is the caller's (T212's photo wording); `photos.rs` holds no customer copy.
- **D-1795** Question (T091, AI-016, CARD-013): who decides that photo screening may call the AI, given `ai::api::ai_mode` lets intake's text AI run without zero retention (the AI-008 switch, outside live) and its `Readiness` is crate-private? Choice: `quotes::api::PhotoAiGate::from_records(zero_retention_signed_on, today, photo_sentence_live)` is AI only when the zero-retention signed date is on or before today and the photo sentence is live, in every environment (the build and `Ci` included), never from `ai_mode` or the AI switch's `live_ok` (true under the AI-008 switch without zero retention); `PhotoAiGate::ON_SERVER_ONLY` is the default. `quotes` must not read `ai`'s tables (R8), so the caller passes the two facts; the task that wires photo screening (with `ai`'s photo job implementing `quotes::api::PhotoScreener`) must add an `ai::api` read of the zero-retention signed date and the AI-018 photo sentence, which `ai` does not expose today. `card_photo` takes only a `privacy::api::CleanPhoto`, so the format and size checks, metadata stripping and re-encoding (PRIV-013, PRIV-014) come first by type, and the homeowner's `HomeownerAnswer::Confirmed` comes before any AI call, so a removed or unconfirmed photo never reaches the AI.
- **D-1799** Question (T092, PRIV-007 to PRIV-009, D-491): `privacy` calls only `adapters` and `ops` and `jobs` may not call `privacy`, so how does a job's close date reach the purge, and how are the 180-day contact purge and its holds ordered? Choice: `jobs` owns a daily sweep (`jobs.purge_sweep`, queued by the worker at start and by itself each day) that queues three `jobs.purge_due` tasks per job in a final status (`JobStatus::is_final`), due at `status_at` plus 30, 180 and 1,096 days (three years never short by a leap day), deduped by job and stage, so `service.rs`'s close path is untouched; the sweep has no look-back limit (every final job, every day; `core.task` keeps each dedupe key, so a stage is queued once), so a worker outage of any length is caught on the next sweep. The composition (`register_purge_handlers`) runs `businesses`' complaint step and `payments`' dispute step before `privacy::api::run_purge_due` on every stage task and re-check. The contact stage waits one hour on its first sight (`privacy.purge_recheck`) so the complaint hold events just queued are applied, then re-checks daily while any `privacy.retention_hold` is unreleased. A release that arrives before its hold is stored released, so the late hold does nothing. Once free, `privacy` queues `privacy.purge` and `intake` (which knows the job's homeowner) calls `privacy::api::purge_contact`; a homeowner with another request open or closed under 180 days ago keeps her contact until that request's own purge. Fix round (review findings): the contact is the homeowner's but holds are per job, so `intake` also keeps the contact while any job of hers has an unreleased hold (that job's own purge clears it once released); a request that never got a job (refused or abandoned) has no `jobs` task, so `intake::api::sweep_requests`, run on the same daily sweep task, queues `intake.request_purge` 180 days after it ended (closed, or for an open request with no job its last answer), and such an open request idle 180 days no longer blocks; a re-check on which `businesses`' complaint step queued new hold events waits another hour (`privacy::api::run_purge_due_after`) so a complaint filed after the first hour is applied before the decision; a purge task (`jobs.purge_due`, `privacy.purge_recheck`, `privacy.purge`, `intake.request_purge`) that fails its last attempt is dead-lettered and never re-queued, so the composition raises one High `privacy.purge_failed` alert naming the job or request (`alert_if_last`). Reason: keeps every layer rule of `kit/layers.json` and every handler safe to run twice (JOB-006).
- **D-1800** Question (T092, PRIV-007): T066's `payments.dispute` records no outcome, so when is a dispute no longer "open"? Choice: a dispute holds the contact purge until 90 days after its evidence due date (`payments::api::DISPUTE_OPEN_AFTER_DUE`), the time card networks take to decide after evidence; after that the hold is released. A complaint (T083) is open until its 5-day box closes and it is listed (`listed_at`); T083 records no resolution, so a complaint still unresolved after its box closes no longer holds the purge (a product choice, listed in `docs/for-casey-review.md`). Reason: no outcome column exists to read, and holding forever would break the 180-day promise; the task that records Stripe's `charge.dispute.closed` should release the hold at once and may drop the window.
- **D-1801** Question (T092, PRIV-008): no table stores scrubbed job text yet, so what does the 3-year text stage delete? Choice: the job's `intake.intake_answer` rows (the answers that describe the job), through `intake::api::purge_answers`; the conversation row, its consent records and terms acceptances stay. A later task that stores scrubbed job text adds its delete to `intake`'s (or its own module's) `privacy.purge` handler for stage `text`. `messaging.inbox` holds only the Twilio SID and time (no body, no phone, no job), so `messaging` needs no purge handler today. Reason: nothing else holds job text; the goal's messaging handler has no rows to act on.
- **D-1802** Question (T092, PRIV-010, D-492): ledger, payment, audit and terms-acceptance rows are append-only for the app role (TD-SEC-33, TD-SEC-34), so how are they "kept 7 years"? Choice: the purge deletes none of them and holds no contact field in them (IDs only), so they are kept at least 7 years; deleting them after 7 years (or 7 years after the last pick or charge under a terms version) needs a migration-role job and is left to a later operations task, since the first such row cannot reach that age before 2033. "Delete my data" leaves ledger rows untouched; they already carry no names, so PRIV-011's "replaces names with deleted" is met by the cleared vault name.
- **D-1803** Question (T092, PRIV-009, PRIV-027, D-1793): the photo purge must remove the sealed objects (and any orphan `photos/` object) and the purge must call Twilio's body-delete at day 31, but `StorageAdapter` has no delete or list and `SmsAdapter` no message delete, and `adapters` and `stand_ins/` are not this task's files. Choice: the photo purge deletes the `privacy.photo` rows and their links (no link can ever open the photo again; the object is AES-GCM ciphertext under `VAULT_KEY` bound to the deleted row's IDs); the object delete, the orphan sweep and the TD-PRIV-12 Twilio day-31 body delete are left to a task that adds `delete_object`/`list_objects` and `delete_message_body` to `adapters` and the stand-ins, which then extends `purge_photos` and adds `messaging`'s day-31 handler. No task in `kit/tasks.json` owns that work today: TD-PRIV-12's day-31 Twilio body-delete case and PRIV-009's delete of the sealed photo objects have no owning task, a plan gap for the runner. Nothing is weakened meanwhile: `tests/integration/tests/retention_purge.rs` carries a marked pending note and no test claims either is done. Reason: no adapter call exists to make, and protected paths change only in a harness task.
- **D-1804** Question (T096, TXT-021, TXT-023, BIZ-046): TXT-023 puts homeowners with no email on Casey's call list "during a texting suspension", while TXT-021's web-and-email switch says only that updates go by email and the quote page; a homeowner who began by text with no email, once Casey switches homeowner texting off, would have no way to learn an update exists. Choice: `messaging::mode::update_route` gives `CallList` to a homeowner with no email whenever her line is paused (switched off or suspended), `Email` with one, and for a business with no address `PortalOnly`, never a call (BIZ-046, D-366; sign-up requires an email, D-144, so this is a fallback only). Reason: TXT-023's purpose (nobody stranded) holds equally for the switch; Casey's list only grows.
- **D-1805** Question (T096, TXT-024, CALL-019, CALL-022, D-206, D-210, D-275, D-491): which paused states allow the safety voice call, and how does a layer-3 crate ask for it when the event is intake's? Choice: `messaging::mode::emergency_plan` is `None` while the homeowner line is open or with no 911-list match (the normal INT-004 path); while paused it always asks for a critical alert and the web-chat INT-004 text, the email when on file, the banner only when the number is suspended (a switch Casey chose needs no banner), and `voice_call` only in `NumberState::Suspended` for a message that arrived at or after the suspension began, with the safety switch on, intake's `safety_call_trigger` true and the number not opted out; a restored number waiting for Casey, or the switch alone, never calls. The composition passes `voice_call` as the `switch_on` of `intake::api::enqueue_safety_call` (deduped on the alert, so a second message about the same emergency queues no second call), with the alert `messaging::api::raise_emergency_alert` raised. Reason: TXT-024 scopes the call to "the homeowner's own message sent during the suspension"; `messaging` may not call `intake` (`kit/layers.json`).
- **D-1806** Question (T096, CON-033, TXT-022, D-315): what does "refused for a suspended number" cover? Choice: `messaging::mode::TollFree::configure` refuses with no recorded refusal (or a blank reference), without Casey's go, and while the homeowner number is `Suspended` or `Restored` but not yet switched on by Casey; `may_carry` refuses every business template (TXT-035's written approval is a separate business line, never this number); `launch_channel` is web-and-email until `verified`. Reason: a restored number waiting for Casey is still inside the suspension D-144 describes; the fallback exists only for a campaign refused before launch.
- **D-1807** Question (T096 scope, two owned files): TXT-021 to TXT-024 also need stored state and wiring this task owns no file for. Choice: `mode.rs` takes the lines, suspension state, launch channel and safety switch as inputs; not built here, and with no owning task in `kit/tasks.json` that the runner should confirm: the stored homeowner switch, suspension state and launch-channel setting with their owner-portal controls (T108 owns the safety switch's), the provider's suspension and restore events feeding `NumberState`, the INT-004 email `Notice` (customer copy, which this task may not write), the automatic status-banner write (no `ops.status_banner` table exists yet), and the composition that runs `emergency_plan` on an inbound message, raises the alert and queues the email and intake's event. Reason: a plan gap reported, not filled with unowned files; nothing claims these are done.
- **D-1808** Question (T096 review, TXT-024, CALL-019, CON-017, OPS-003, D-144, D-206): D-1805 let a restored number waiting for Casey never call and turned the banner on only for a suspension, while D-1806 treats that state as still inside the suspension and TXT-024 turns the banner on while texting is "off or suspended"; intake's `enqueue_safety_call` dedupes on the alert, but every message raised a new alert, so a second emergency message queued a second call; a retried message raised a second alert; an opted-out number's emergency got optout's `messaging.opted_out_emergency` and this module's alert both; and `Line.texting_on` had no stated tie to the `ops` texting pause. Choice (corrects D-1805): `emergency_plan` turns the banner on whenever the homeowner line is paused (TXT-024's words); `voice_call` covers `Suspended` and `Restored`-waiting-for-Casey alike, for a message sent since the suspension began (D-1806: texting is still off then, so a homeowner with no email is not left with no safety message); `critical_alert` is false for an opted-out number, whose one alert is optout's on the same inbox row (CON-017). `raise_emergency` (replacing `raise_emergency_alert`) claims each inbox message once with `ops::api::audit_once` (`messaging.paused_emergency_handled`), so a retry raises nothing more, and keeps the call only for the first message per homeowner and suspension, claimed with `audit_once` (`messaging.paused_safety_call` on a key of her contact ID XOR the suspension's start in milliseconds); every later message still raises its own critical alert ("any message ... raises a critical alert"). `messaging` may not read `ops.alert` (architecture section 2, rule 3), so the claim lives in the audit log, the pattern `audit_once` exists for (D-1705). `Line.texting_on` is the audience's own switch (TXT-021, TXT-035); `ops::Switch::Texting` and `Switch::All` (OPS-003) pause both audiences on top of it, and `send_on_line`, the send that takes its `From` from `Line::sender`, refuses while either is on. The texting switch off on a working number still gets no call (TXT-024 scopes the call to a suspension). Reason: one safety call per emergency (CALL-019) and one alert per message without reading another module's schema; the spec wins on the banner.
- **D-1809** Question (T097, JOB-015, JOB-028, D-240, D-874): `jobs` owns the check-in moves, but nothing schedules the check-ins, reads the reply words or says what LATER, ONGOING and OTHER do to the job. Choice: `app/jobs/src/followups.rs`: `schedule_check_ins` queues a `jobs.check_in` task for day 3 (from the later of the release and the earliest visit) and day 14 (from the release, as JOB-026's 21-day backstop counts), dropping a day 3 that would not come before day 14; `run_check_in` (registered in `app/server/src/lib.rs`) queues the check-in text only while the job is Connected (`JobStatus::takes_check_ins`, added in `status.rs`), so ONGOING, OTHER, DONE or a close stops every later check-in without cancelling tasks; `parse_answer` is a pure reader of the reply words that `intake` can call (D-874 gave parsing to `intake`, but no task owns it and the words are the rule; one reader avoids two lists); `after_answer`: DONE and ONGOING go to Done with the feedback request, OTHER to Closed with no no-show (it never returns the job to Quotes ready, even under email contact, unlike a day-3 NO), LATER moves nothing (at day 3 the already-queued day-14 check-in asks again; at day 14 JOB-026's backstop closes it 7 days on). The one feedback request is the `feedback_request` text event queued in the Done move's transaction, so it goes only after Done and once (Done is final; the event is deduped per job and template); `connected_reply` stays the bare move and sends no request. Reason: smallest change on the existing arrows and timers, each move fenced on Connected (JOB-004). Source: `docs/spec/lifecycle.md:19`, `docs/spec/lifecycle.md:21`, `docs/spec/lifecycle.md:30`, `docs/spec/lifecycle.md:32`.
- **D-1810** Question (T097, JOB-016, TXT-029, OPS-005, D-071, D-222, D-277): how is a PROBLEM reply "listed for Casey with its text" when `ops.alert` holds IDs only (PRIV-006), and where are the safety words? Choice: `answer_check_in` closes the job with the TXT-029 `problem_reply` text and, in the same transaction, raises one `ops.alert` whose subject is the reply's `messaging.inbox` row (the digest reads its scrubbed words from there; the job is found through the request): kind `jobs.problem_report` for the weekly digest, or `jobs.problem_report_safety` for the OPS-032 push when the words hold a safety word, severity normal for both, as `businesses`' complaint alerts are. The safety-word list stays `businesses::api::has_safety_word` (the one list, D-222); `jobs` may not call `businesses` (`kit/layers.json`), so the caller passes `Inbound { inbox, safety }`. A PROBLEM on a job no longer Connected writes nothing, so a repeated reply is never listed twice. No fee, ledger or refund code is called (D-071). Reason: no homeowner words outside the inbox, one safety list, R11. Source: `docs/spec/lifecycle.md:20`, `docs/spec/messaging.md:33`.
- **D-1811** Question (T097): what of the goal can T097 not finish inside the files it owns? Choice, each a gap for the runner: (1) the `check_in_day3`, `check_in_day14` and `feedback_request` templates are not added, and `problem_reply` (TXT-029, whose English and Spanish template exists) is not in the sender's list: a new homeowner template must be listed in `quotes`' `UPDATE_TEXTS` or `NOT_UPDATE_TEXTS` (`app/quotes/src/update_texts.rs`, T213's; `td_txt_25_every_homeowner_template_is_scanned_or_left_out` fails otherwise) and every one of the four must be in `intake`'s `JOB_TEXT_TEMPLATES` (`app/intake/src/job_texts.rs`, T240's) for the sender to send it, and the feedback link is T230's page; until a task owning those files adds them (with the JOB-015 first line, MORE's full list and the T230 link), these events, the TXT-029 reply included, are queued but the sender refuses them as a bad payload, so no PROBLEM reply reaches the homeowner yet. (2) Nothing calls `schedule_check_ins` yet: the release (`picks`, T069's) should call it when the job connects, with the picked quote's earliest visit. (3) Nothing calls `answer_check_in` yet: the inbound route (T241's `intake::api::receive_reply`) should, for a Connected job's reply, call `parse_answer`, `businesses::api::has_safety_word` and then `answer_check_in`, and record the no-show for a day-3 NO under email (`picks`, FEE-035). (4) The size budget: the two owned files are about 510 lines against 400 after the review round merged the pure tests and helpers (D-1812), mostly documentation and the seven test cases; no assertion was dropped. Kind: gap. Owner approval: Casey's standing approval for plan improvements through the normal review gate. Source: `kit/prompts/T097.md` (Scope).
- **D-1812** Question (T097 review, JOB-015, JOB-016, JOB-026, JOB-028, D-240, D-806): a job can connect twice (a day-3 NO under email contact returns it to Quotes ready, PICK-045), so how are the second connection's check-ins kept apart from the first's, and how are ONGOING, a day-14 PROBLEM and LATER read? Choice: (1) `schedule_check_ins` loads the job and puts its version in the `jobs.check_in` payload and dedupe key (`jobs.check_in.<job>.<version>.<day>`); `run_check_in` does nothing unless the job is still Connected at that version, and queues its text itself with the dedupe key `jobs.homeowner_text.<job>.<template>.<version>` (the shared `handlers::queue_text` key, one per job and template, is T032's and stays for TXT-042), so a second connection gets its own day-3 and day-14 texts and the first connection's pending day 14 does nothing; a check-in for a job that no longer exists does nothing instead of retrying. (2) ONGOING (or CONTINUO) is treated exactly as DONE: the job moves to Done with the one feedback request (JOB-028 "moves the job to Done"). (3) A PROBLEM at day 14 is flagged to Casey exactly as at day 3 (JOB-016 names day 3; flagging a later one too is the safer reading of D-071 and D-222, and no fee changes either way). (4) LATER calls no `restart_timer`: the day-14 check-in counts from the release, and Connected's JOB-026 backstop (`CONNECTED_DAYS` = 14 + 7 from the connection, D-806) already closes it 7 days after that check-in, so LATER at day 3 simply waits for day 14 and LATER at day 14 leaves the backstop to close it; the day-3 move to a later visit date never moves day 14. Reason: a check-in must never go for a connection that is over (JOB-015), and the smallest reading that keeps JOB-026's timer untouched. Kind: build choice. Owner approval: Casey's standing approval for plan improvements through the normal review gate. Source: `kit/prompts/T097.md` (Goal), `docs/spec/lifecycle.md:19`, `docs/spec/lifecycle.md:30`, `docs/spec/lifecycle.md:32`.

The caller (the worker, not wired yet) gathers the facts: `call_record` turns `calls::api::LoggedCall` into the rule's `CallRecord` (a machine, nobody or unknown answer is never talking); `missed_call_text` queues the one `caller_missed` text (TXT-030, an important text already in `IMPORTANT_TEMPLATES`, quiet hours as a `Kind::PickStep`, so any hour on an emergency job and 08:00 otherwise) when the first business attempt after the release was not answered by a person, and its `true` is FEE-022's `notice_attempted` (D-286: queued counts, a failed delivery still counts); `queue_reminders` queues each TXT-026 reminder still owed at release + 24 h and + 48 h (`business_no_call_reminder`, or `business_no_call_reminder_email` with the D-049 email line), cancelled by any business attempt before its time, keyed per pick and time; `decide_at_96_hours` calls `payments::api::decide_unreachable`, refunds through `request_refund` with `RefundTrigger::Rule`, moves Connected to Closed (which stops the check-ins: `takes_check_ins` is false) and closes the line in one transaction, so a second run (the job moved on) changes nothing (the homeowner's close text and the 72-hour question wait, D-1818); `no_call_at_72_hours` returns a call-contact job with no business call to Quotes ready with its line closed and its pick `no_show` (never refunded, FEE-035) and leaves an email-contact job Connected for `jobs`' day-3 answer (D-143); `dispute_auto_submit` calls `mark_auto_submit` only with a recorded release and a call attempt or 3DS (FEE-050); `fraud_warning` calls `early_fraud_warning` and, for an unreleased charge, ends the paid pick `fraud_refunded` and moves Payment pending to Quotes ready (FEE-052, JOB-014). `PickStatus` gains `NoShow` and `FraudRefunded` (codes already in the table's check). - **D-1819** Question (T191 review, FEE-022, FEE-052, JOB-013, JOB-027, TXT-030, D-1814): the first build closed the job, marked the pick fraud-refunded and emailed "your fee is refunded" whatever `payments` answered; a run that refunded but stopped before the close never finished (the rule then reads `AlreadyRefunded`); an email-contact day-3 NO had no entry point; the missed-call text counted as sent even for a number that can never be texted, and was queued with no due time. Choice: (1) `decide_at_96_hours` returns `AtNinetySix`: only `RefundOutcome::Refunded` or `Unchanged` (already refunded, or a try in flight that `payments`' hourly retry finishes) goes on to the close and the email; `Blocked` (a dispute) or `Failed` returns `RefundWaiting { blocked }` with nothing closed or emailed, so the caller runs the step again. (2) The rule is judged with `refunded_before` cleared first; when it still refunds, `request_refund` (which never sends twice) answers `Unchanged` and the close and the decision email (deduped per pick) happen once, so a half-finished run completes. (3) `fraud_warning` likewise acts only on a refunded fee, and moves Payment pending to Quotes ready before ending the pick, rolling back when the job moved on, so a pick is never `fraud_refunded` while its job stays elsewhere. (4) `no_call_at_72_hours` takes the day-3 answer (`EmailCheck`) and returns an email-contact job on a NO with its pick a no-show and its line closed (TD-JOB-07, `payments::no_show`), the entry point `jobs`' check-in answer calls. (5) `missed_call_text` takes the caller's `messaging::api::send_window` answer (`picks` never reads her phone): `OptedOut` or `NotTextable` queues nothing and answers `false`, so FEE-022's `notice_attempted` is not met; a failed delivery still counts and TXT-014's retries email an important text. Two gaps stay, both for the worker task that wires the 24 to 96-hour steps: TXT-030's email copy for a number that can't be texted (it needs `messaging`'s email queue with the homeowner's address, postal address and manage link, outside T191's files), and the send time: the outbox row has no due time, so the sender must hold it by `send_at` (a `Kind::PickStep`, any hour on an emergency job). Kind: fix. Owner approval: Casey's standing approval for plan improvements through the normal review gate. Source: `kit/prompts/T191.md` (Scope), `docs/spec/fees.md` (FEE-022), `docs/spec/messaging.md` (TXT-030), `docs/spec/lifecycle.md` (JOB-013, JOB-027).
- **D-1820** Question (T230): how does the private feedback page reach its job, where do its queries live, and how does its share box pass the A11Y-007 edge check? Choice: (1) The page is `/f/{token}` keyed by the job's existing quote-page link token (`jobs::api::quote_token::resolve`), so no new token table is needed; it opens only while the job is Done (`JobStatus::takes_feedback`) and within PICK-011's 30 days after the close, anything else a bare 404 (SEC-037). (2) `jobs.feedback` is `jobs`' table (architecture section 3), and section 4 rule 3 lets only `jobs` name it, so its queries (`jobs::api::feedback`: `store`, `given`, `remove`, `mark_author`, `shown`) are written in `app/jobs/src/api.rs`, the one `jobs` file this task may change, as T247's `first_quote` is. (3) The table has no rating or tone column, so no code can leave ticked feedback out for being negative; a removal is one of the four JOB-017 reasons in a `CHECK`, set once, only on ticked feedback, with an audit row naming the reason in the same transaction; an author mark (owner, owner's relative, business) keeps feedback off whatever the tick. The words and tick are never updated or deleted by the app role. No column holds a name, phone or address, and the first name and town are read from the vault when a page shows the feedback; but the body is the homeowner's own free text, stored unscrubbed, so it may hold whatever they typed, contact details included (see D-1821 (4)). (4) Chromium's native checkbox reports a 0px border and a transparent fill, so `targets_contrast.spec.ts` flags its edge although it is drawn at about 4.5:1; the site has no stylesheet yet (T101), so the feedback router serves `/static/portals/feedback.css` (same origin, allowed by the CSP) that draws the box with a 2px `#1f1d1b` edge and a filled centre when ticked, listed in `NOT_PAGES` as a stylesheet. T101 may fold it into the site stylesheet. Kind: fix. Owner approval: Casey's standing approval for plan improvements through the normal review gate. Source: `kit/prompts/T230.md` (Goal, Scope), `docs/spec/lifecycle.md` (JOB-017), `docs/architecture.md` sections 3 and 4.

(5) The size budget: 21 files and about 1,120 inserted lines on the first hand-in (most in `.sqlx/`, `app/jobs/src/api.rs`, `app/portals/src/feedback.rs` and the tests), well over the 400-line budget; the review fixes (D-1823) add about 150 more. Kind: gap. Owner approval: Casey's standing approval for plan improvements through the normal review gate. Source: `kit/prompts/T230.md` (Goal, Scope).

- **D-1823** Question (T230, review fixes): can the app role quietly put removed or author-marked feedback back on askhava.com, and what does a send show when the job leaves Done between the page opening and the store? Choice: (1) migration 0139 adds a `BEFORE UPDATE` trigger, `jobs.feedback_marks_stay`: a removal (reason and time), once set, never changes or clears, and an author mark may be corrected to another kind (`mark_author` audits it) but never cleared, so the column grant on `removed_reason`, `removed_at` and `author_kind` cannot undo either without an audit row (JOB-017); the trigger is created by the migration owner, so the app role still holds no TRIGGER privilege (TD-SEC-34). - **D-1825** Question (T147, design): how do business notices go by the chosen channel when `messaging` (layer 3) may not call `businesses` (layer 4), and how are night holds, text consent and the signed `{link}` done? Choice: (1) `businesses.notice_channel` (`migrations/0141_business_notices.sql`, one row per business that chose; none means email) with `businesses::api::set_notice_channel` (text or both refused while the business-texting switch is off, BIZ-036, TXT-035), `notice_channel` and `notice_recipients(business, purpose, business_texting_on)`, which extends T220's `notice_addresses` with each person's channels: their mailbox ID, whether the email goes (false only for "text" with a linked phone) and their linked phone line IDs (none while texting is off). (2) `messaging::api::business_notice` handles `messaging.business_notice` (payload: `template`, optional `text_template`, `business`, `pick`/`job`, `to`, `texts` `[{mailbox, phone}]`, `values`, and for a card `card`, `statement`, `page`); it reads no recipient itself. (3) Text consent is read when the notice runs through a `TextGate` trait the composition implements with `businesses::api::may_text` (D-1715, D-1760); a refused phone or a closed business line sends that person the email instead (BIZ-019). (4) Quiet hours: outside 8:00 to 19:59:59 Arizona time the whole notice is queued again for 8 a.m. under the dedupe key `messaging.business_notice.held.<task id>` and nothing is stored, so email and text share one clock start (QH-005); the zone is Arizona only, because `messaging` never sees a business phone number. (5) `{link}` is `sign_in_link`: `core::link_token(secret, LinkKind::Action, person, LinkSalt(job number BE ‖ expiry BE))` with `p`, `j`, `e`, `t` in `https://askhava.com/b/sign-in`, person = the recipient's mailbox ID, expiry 7 days on (D-1761); the email shows it as its own link under the words. (6) `quotes::api::queue_card_notice` checks `may_get_cards` (D-1715) and queues one card notice per job and business; `quotes::api::sent_count` counts card holders whose card email was sent with no `email.bounced` event, or whose card text was sent (CARD-019, TD-TXT-22) through `messaging::api::card_notice_accepted`. - **D-1851** Question (T093; TXT-019): the message log must hold each text's language, but `messaging::api::NewText` (in `service.rs`, which T093 does not own) carries no language, and every caller already renders the body in the person's language before queuing. Choice: the outbox writer (`models::insert_text`) sets the new `messaging.outbox.language` from the body itself: `retention::language_of` checks the body against the template's English and Spanish texts (each `{name}` matching any text, the fixed parts in order, the first at the start and the last at the end) and stores `en` or `es` when exactly one fits, NULL when neither or both do (a test body, a hand-built text) and for rows queued before migration 0128. A HELP reply is rendered from one of `help_reply`, `help_reply_ca`, `help_reply_away` or `help_reply_away_ca` (`keywords::help_text`) but always stored under `help_reply` (so `rules::may_send_to` lets it reach a listed number, D-887); for a `help_reply` row `language_of` checks the body against all four variants in each language, so every HELP reply, English or Spanish, logs its language (test `td_txt_07_every_help_reply_variant_logs_its_language`). No caller changes. Reason: the language is a fact of the rendered body, so reading it there cannot disagree with what was sent; a typed field on `NewText` would touch every caller in other tasks' files. A later task that owns `service.rs` may pass the language explicitly. Source: `docs/spec/messaging.md:23`, `app/messaging/src/service.rs:53`.

- **D-1853** Question (T093; TXT-020, CON-036, CON-022): what does the 30-day cut act on, and how does the opt-out evidence survive it? Choice: (1) a sent, blocked or failed outbox row already holds no body (SEC-037, D-850), so `retention::cut_bodies` cuts only rows still `queued` or `sending` 30 days after they were queued (`created_at`), ending them `failed` (a text that old is never sent) and keeping the row and its template ID; no log row is ever deleted by it. Limitation (D-1855): this is not the TXT-014/TXT-015 give-up path. `cut_bodies` sets `failed` directly and does not call `retries::give_up`, so a row it ends gets no portal listing, no email and no call-back alert. (2) `messaging.inbox` stores only the message ID and time, and no raw or scrubbed inbound text is stored in `messaging` (the raw body waits for `privacy.message_body`, D-801), so the inbound half of TXT-020 has nothing to cut here; TD-TXT-07 checks the inbox has no other column. (3) `messaging.optout_event` gains `inbox_id` (migration 0128, an ID, not a foreign key, so an event never depends on the inbox row's lifetime and existing callers that pass a stand-in ID keep working): `optout::on_inbound_text` stores the inbox row of the text that opted out or restarted, other channels NULL; `detected` already holds `word:<word>`, `phrase:<pattern ID>` or `provider` (0044), and the table stays append-only for the app, so the evidence outlives the body for the CON-022 period. The pattern-ID label stays `phrase:<id>` (CON-036's "natural language" with the pattern ID): renaming it would change T029's test, which T093 does not own. Source: `docs/spec/messaging.md:24`, `docs/spec/consent.md:40`, `migrations/0044_messaging_optout.sql:17`.
- **D-1854** Question (T093; TXT-020): who runs the cut? Choice: a daily `core.task` of kind `messaging.cut_bodies` (`messaging::api::run_cut`), registered with the retention purge handlers in `app/server/src/lib.rs` and first queued by the worker at start (`schedule_cut`), each run queuing the next day's under a per-day dedupe key, as `jobs`' purge sweep does (D-491). - **D-1855** Question (T093; TXT-014, TXT-015, TXT-020; review of D-1853): should the 30-day cut end an unsent text through `retries::give_up`, so the person still gets the portal listing, the email or Casey's call-back? Choice: not in T093; the cut keeps setting `failed` directly and the gap is recorded here. Why not feasible: `give_up` needs, per row, a `Reach` (for a homeowner the vault and the job's `Urgency`, which lives in `jobs`, above `messaging`, and is not stored on the outbox row), the email secret and the checked `PostalAddress`; nothing in the code calls `give_up` yet (the retry runner that would supply them is not built), and the daily `run_cut` task has none of these inputs. Passing them would mean new composition code reading job urgency, outside T093's files. In practice a row reaches the cut only if the retry runner never gave it up within the hour TXT-015 allows, so the cut is a backstop for a runner fault, not the normal path; but such a row's person is then not told. Follow-up: the task that builds the retry runner (the `give_up` caller) should either give up every row older than its last retry before day 30, or have `run_cut` hand rows still `queued`/`sending` to `give_up` instead of failing them. Kind: gap. Owner approval: Casey's standing delegation. Reason: honest record of a reviewer finding T093 cannot close inside its scope. Source: `app/messaging/src/retention.rs` (`cut_bodies`), `app/messaging/src/retries.rs:148`.
- **D-1846** Question (T196; BIZ-040, TD-BIZ-13; D-1701): how does activation wait for the verified sign-up email when `tests/integration/tests/identity_chain.rs` (T081's, not T196's) activates sign-ups that never had an email check? Choice: `businesses.mailbox_check` (migration 0142) holds one row per mailbox to verify; `email_verification::start_signup_check` opens the sign-up email's row and returns a 6-digit code keyed from the row ID and send time (never stored, 30 minutes, 5 wrong tries, a resend voids the earlier code); `identity::settle` holds activation (a flag still moves to needs review) and `approve` refuses while that row is unverified; `confirm` verifies it and settles. A hard bounce, a complaint, or a second soft bounce 14 or more days after the first (BIZ-055) marks it returned and queues one `businesses.notice_address_returned` task (the owner's other verified addresses, the digest line; no call, BIZ-039), whose handler is the email sender's. - **D-1847** Question (T196; SEC-024, SEC-038, TD-SEC-07, TD-SEC-17): where does "a Verify code in the last 5 minutes" live, and how does a change reach the old address? - **D-1849** Question (T196; D-1712, D-1756, TD-BIZ-40): how is the identity episode kept? Choice: `businesses.signup` gains `identity_attempt`, `sent_text_key`, `sent_mail_key`, `sent_letter_key` (HMAC digests of each step's last destination under the ID secret) and `code_tries`; one guarded `UPDATE` in `identity::send_code_seen` stores the step's digest and raises the attempt (and resets `code_tries`) only when it differs, so identical retries and concurrent sends keep one key. The Verify key and the letter code add the attempt only from episode 1, so episode 0 is unchanged (`letter_code`); `check_code` fails every code after 5 wrong ones in an episode (`IDENTITY_CODE_TRIES`). `send_code` keeps its signature and passes no address, so only `send_code_seen` with the record address starts a new letter episode; the daily-list resume must call it. The episode is one counter for all three steps, as D-1756 says ("the letter and code checks and their rate limits use the same episode"): a changed record phone or email raises it, so the code of a letter already mailed stops working and the chain mails a new one when it reaches the letter step again; a per-step episode would need a spec change (D-1850, review finding). Reason: D-1756. Source: app/businesses/src/identity.rs:156
- **D-1850** Question (T196 fix round; SEC-024, SEC-038, BIZ-040, TD-SEC-07, D-1703): how do the notice-address checks hold up under the review's findings? Choice: (1) `portals::change_channel` writes `businesses.notice_channel_changed` (or `businesses.notice_channel_refused` for a non-owner) with the preference write in one transaction; (2) `identity::check_code` takes one of the 5 tries in a guarded `UPDATE ... WHERE code_tries < 5` before checking and gives it back on a right code, so parallel guesses cannot pass the cap (a Verify error keeps the try); (3, 4) `mailbox_check` gains `change_for`, `requested_by`, `open` and `window_at`: a change may reopen a verified row (A to B to A asks for a code again and moves), the member's own mailbox re-verifies (`replaces` null) only when unverified or returned, and a right code clears `returned_at` and `soft_at`; a request that opens nothing logs nothing; (5) a newer change for a member closes its older open rows, and `confirm` moves the address only with the member current and still on the old mailbox (rows affected checked), else closes the row unverified and returns false, queuing and logging nothing; (7) every notice audit row (requested, refused, changed, reverified, channel) is on the member whose address changes, plus one `businesses.notice_change_by` row (`ACTED_BY_ACTION`) on the member who acted, through `log_notice_change`; (9) wrong mailbox codes carry over resends within 30 minutes of the window's first send; (10) a `step_up_at` in the future is no fresh code. Reason: SEC-024 "every change is audit-logged", SEC-048's try caps, BIZ-040 "Add or fix an email address". Source: docs/spec/security.md:28, docs/spec/businesses.md:44 Retry (T196 attempt 2): Ci went red on `a_refused_or_stale_move_changes_nothing` (`app/jobs/src/tests/transitions.rs`, unchanged by T196 and not owned by it) with no error event counted. Cause: the test sets a scoped subscriber (`set_default`), which leaves tracing-core 0.1.36 with exactly one registered dispatcher (`has_just_one`), so when another test thread first hits the same `tracing::error!` callsite in `app/jobs/src/service.rs` (`every_applied_move_writes_one_audit_row` logs the same refusal) its interest is built from that thread's empty default and cached as never, and the refusal on the listening thread is skipped. A flaky shared-state race, not a T196 effect. Choice: T196 leaves the file alone (the change rules refuse a path the task does not own, `scripts/check_pr_change.py`); the fix for the file's owner or a harness task is the D-1034 one: count errors through one process-wide subscriber installed once whose layer counts only on the listening thread, keeping the assertion of exactly one error event. Reason: never weaken a test (`BUILD_BRIEF.md:69`) and touch only owned files (`BUILD_BRIEF.md:485`); the runner should queue the fix.
- **D-1890** Question (harness fix, November 7, 2026; numbered max(`next_decision` 1880, `main`'s highest 1855 + 1, open plan branch `claude/plan-audit3`'s highest 1874 + 1) + 10 = 1890; first drafted as D-1884 before `next_decision` moved): the runner's smoke of `main` at 6ea04a3a timed out twice running (`runner_log` 17:27Z and 17:38Z, "exit 124; smoke timed out after 540 seconds"; once before at 15:02Z), and while the smoke is red no task is claimed, so the single lane stalled. Why, and how does the smoke get back under SMOKE_TIMEOUT (540 s, D-1178)? Finding: every smoke compiled all 17 workspace members three times (clippy, build, test). Two causes: D-1451's `cargo clean --workspace` after each smoke (needed because the smoke built into the worker's `target` from a random temporary worktree, whose path `env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR")` compiled into artifacts Cargo then served to the worker as fresh, T057); and, even without the clean, Cargo's freshness check for path packages is by mtime, and a fresh worktree makes every file, and every folder a build script watches (`askhava-core`'s `rerun-if-changed=../../migrations`), newer than any cached build. Measured locally on 6ea04a3a (2 cores, own target dir, worktree removed and re-added between runs): with `cargo build -p askhava-server`, a stable path alone still recompiled all 17 members; pinning files alone still did (the `migrations` folder's mtime); with files and folders pinned, the same commit compiled 0 units, a one-file change in `askhava-portals` 2 units, a new migration all 17 (correct: everything depends on `core`). With the smoke's three cargo runs (clippy, build, `test --no-run`, `CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0`, dependencies warm): all members rebuilt 66 + 42 + 142 = 250 s (what every smoke paid), the same commit again 1 s, the `askhava-portals` change 15 + 8 + 92 = 115 s. Choice (`runner/github_env.py`): the smoke worktree sits at a fixed path (`smoke_tree_dir`: `askhava-smoke` under `RUNNER_TEMP`, removed before and after each run); the smoke builds into its own `target/smoke` (`smoke_target_dir`; under an explicit `CARGO_TARGET_DIR`, its `smoke` folder), inside the `target` the D-514 cache already saves, so no workflow change; `pin_smoke_mtimes` sets each tracked file's and folder's mtime from `target/smoke/smoke-mtimes.json` (unchanged blob or entry names: the recorded time; new or changed: now), the manifest written before Cargo runs, so a red or timed-out run cannot leave it wrong and a missing one only means a full build; the smoke runs with `CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0`, as `Ci` does, because the cache keeps its dir and rustc's incremental data was 4.7 of 15 GB; D-1451's clean and `CARGO_CLEAN_MEMBERS` are removed, since the worker's `target` no longer receives smoke artifacts. After the independent Opus review (changes required): (a) the record is deleted before the first mtime change and written back only when every path is pinned; a failed `git ls-files` or `os.utime` stamps the whole tree with the current time (`stamp_tree_now`), so a later revert to earlier content can never get its old time back over an artifact built from other content; (b) any change under `.sqlx/` (offline query data no dep-info lists) gives every path the run's time; (c) the run's time is at least one past every recorded time, against a clock that steps back; (d) cold start: existing cache entries have no `target/smoke`, and the first smoke would build dependencies and members from scratch (well over 540 s) while the per-commit key cannot save progress until `main` moves; so when `target/smoke/debug/deps` is empty, `_seed_smoke_target` copies the worker build's dependency artifacts (`seed_files`: entries of `deps`, `build` and `.fingerprint` whose unit is not a workspace package or target from `cargo metadata --no-deps`) into it, as real copies, never hard links, because Cargo rewrites fingerprint and dep-info files in place and a shared inode would carry the smoke's writes into the worker's build (the T057 failure); it logs the size and free disk first and skips with less than the copy plus 5 GB free; (e) the cache is split now: `backup-runner.yml` has a "Smoke build cache (D-1890)" entry for `target/smoke` (key `rust-smoke-…-<sha>`, its own restore keys) and the main entry excludes `!target/smoke`, so neither entry carries both builds. Cost: the smoke entry holds the smoke's whole build, member test binaries included (the clean used to drop them): about 11 GB uncompressed locally, about 8 GB of it the 80-odd test binaries; compressed (gzip -1; the cache uses zstd) the rebuilt 8.7 GB part came to 2.2 GB, so roughly 2.5 to 3 GB per smoke entry beside the worker's; GitHub's 10 GB per-repository cache then keeps fewer per-commit snapshots and evicts the oldest. Measured locally (2 cores) after a worker-style build of 6ea04a3a (clippy, build, `test --no-run`, incremental on: 527 s cold): seeding copied 3,072 entries, 2.3 GB, in 7 s, and the smoke trio with `CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0` then compiled no dependency unit (incremental does not change dependency fingerprints) and only the members: 33 + 26 + 139 = 198 s. Not done: the checkout's own `target` still rebuilds every member once per job. Tests: `tests/test_runner_keeper.py` (smoke target, fixed tree, pinning, unreadable manifest, failed pin then revert, failed index read, `.sqlx/` and clock rules, seeding, the cache split, `smoke_main` order), `tests/test_runner_live.py`. Owner approval: Casey's standing delegation. Source: `runner/github_env.py` (`smoke_main`, `pin_smoke_mtimes`, `_seed_smoke_target`), `.github/workflows/backup-runner.yml`, D-1178, D-1451, D-514.
- **D-1875** Question (T252; TD-SEC-36, SEC-029, D-1677): how does `tests/integration/tests/architecture_migrations.rs` find dynamic SQL, and what does the allow list cover? Choice: `dynamic_sql` reads the same lexed tokens as `schema_refs` (comments gone, `'...'` strings one token, dollar-quoted bodies lexed as SQL) and returns the first construct: `DO` when `do` is the first token of a statement (file start or after `;`), `EXECUTE` when `execute` is not followed by `function`, `procedure`, `on` or `,`, and in migrations only `format()`/`quote_ident()`/`quote_literal()`/`quote_nullable()` when the name is followed by `(`; a query macro's SQL under `app/` (inline or its `query_file*` file) is checked for `DO` and `EXECUTE` only. One finding per file path, naming its first construct. `DYNAMIC_SQL_ALLOWED` is keyed by the same path as the finding, so it may list a migration or an `app/` SQL file; it starts with `migrations/0019_core_db_migrations.sql` (its `DO $guard$` role guard, T012), the only migration on `main` holding dynamic SQL when T252 started (checked by the real-repository test, since an entry with no dynamic SQL would be a stale finding). `check_repo` takes the allow list; the real test passes the constant, the plants pass their own, and the two TD-SEC-35 cases holding a `DO` block (`revoke_and_do_block`, `revoke_inside_do`) list their planted file so they still give only the REVOKE finding. Beyond the planted cases the goal names, a missing allow-listed file, the words in comments and strings, `REVOKE SELECT, EXECUTE ON FUNCTION`, and `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` and `format(` inside a query macro are planted too. Reason: the goal of T252 and TD-SEC-36. Source: docs/spec/security.md:33

- **D-1871** Question (T287, T261, third audit; FEE-005, FEE-007): `confirm_and_pay` charges whatever `Press::amount_cents` its caller passes (`app/payments/src/models.rs:325`; nothing stores the fee fixed at the pick, `app/picks/src/service.rs:340`), and the fee-mode check runs only after Stripe has charged (`record_fee_at_confirm`, `app/payments/src/service.rs:344`), so an owner's switch between a pick and its Confirm leaves a succeeded charge with no ledger entry until the reconcile. What is fixed where, and what happens to a pick made before a switch? Choice: (0) nothing stored the fee terms in force (`switch_fee_mode` only returns them, `app/payments/src/service.rs:207`), so `payments` keeps them in a one-row `payments.fee_terms` (mode and authorization version, seeded with tiers and `AUTHORIZATION_VERSION`), written by `switch_fee_mode` in its own transaction with its audit row and read through `payments::api::fee_terms_in_force`; `picks`, T261 and T108's owner switch use only those. (1) `payments` stores the fee fixed at the pick (`payments.pick_fee`, written once in the pick's transaction by `picks` through `payments::api::fix_fee_at_pick`; `payments` reads nothing of `picks` or `jobs`); `open_intent` and `confirm_and_pay` refuse, before any Stripe call, a press whose amount, business or job differs from it (`ChargeError::FeeMismatch`). (2) The fee fixed at the pick stands and is the only amount ever charged for that pick (FEE-005); it is never re-derived under the new mode. (3) A press on a pick whose stored mode differs from the mode in force is refused by `may_confirm` before any PaymentIntent is opened or confirmed (`ConfirmError::FeeModeChanged`); nothing is charged; the Confirm page says the fee terms changed after this pick, and the pick ends at once with no fee through T232's "Can't take it" path with its own reason, never counted against the business (PICK-050, OPS-034), so the homeowner gets the other quotes as after any ended pick. Re-pricing would break FEE-005, and charging the old-mode fee under the new authorization would charge under terms D-072 says the business must accept first; the sources do not cover a switch in this window, so this is decided and listed for Casey. (4) `record_fee_at_confirm` writes the stored fee, so after the gate it cannot fail for a switch. D-072 still applies to every pick made after a switch. (5) T287 is a harness task: the existing fee, charge and confirm tests of T060, T062, T189 and T263 gain only the stored terms and pick fee their fixtures now need, with no expected value changed. Reason: the server fixes the fee and nothing changes it afterwards; a check in `payments` is an invariant, a single call site only a convention. Source: `docs/spec/fees.md:9`, `docs/spec/fees.md:11`, `docs/spec/quotes-pick.md:54`, `app/payments/src/charge.rs:91`, `app/payments/src/rules.rs:496`.

Each charge a run reads but cannot settle is stored in `payments.reconcile_open` with the facts it read and retried every night from them, whatever its age, under the live writers' keys (so a retry never doubles an entry or a refund), after reading the charge's current refund and dispute state again, until it settles; one still open 7 days after it was first seen raises one High alert with its row ID only, marked with `alerted_at` in the same transaction so no later run raises it again. `LOOKBACK` stays 7 days; T067's append-only `payments.reconcile_charge` is unchanged. Reason: a charge the reconcile met must stay visible until it is settled. Source: `app/payments/src/reconcile.rs:51`, `docs/spec/fees.md:33`.

- **D-1874** Question (T290, third audit review fix round): how does D-033 apply to a recurring price range whose midpoint is a half cent, and should a worked example pin it? The third audit read D-033 as "floor the midpoint, then apply the 4-month rule". Choice: D-033 stands as written and as built: the 4-month basis of a recurring range is computed exactly from the sum of its two ends (times the period's monthly factor, times 4, divided once) and rounded down to the whole cent once, before the tier is chosen (`app/payments/src/rules.rs:290`); flooring the midpoint first would round twice and is rejected. Example: every two weeks, $57.69 to $57.70 gives (5,769 + 5,770) × 26 × 4 ÷ 24 = 50,002.33 cents, basis $500.02, fee $75 (the midpoint-first reading would give $499.98 and $25). T290 adds worked examples for one-cent-wide recurring ranges a cent below, at and above the $500 and $1,500 edges for each period, wherever whole-cent amounts can reach them, so `scripts/check_catalog.py` and `tests::worked_examples` pin the rule; their logic is not changed. Reason: an example that pins the rule stops the next reader from "fixing" it. Source: `docs/decisions.md:44`, `docs/catalog/worked_examples.yaml:44`, `app/payments/src/rules.rs:290`.

- **D-1895** Question (T253; TD-PICK-48, TD-SEC-10, D-1739): D-1739 puts TD-PICK-48's database cases in `app/server/tests/released_view.rs`, the one test home allowed the session mint, but the architecture test (`tests/integration/tests/architecture_migrations.rs`, TD-SEC-10) fails any file under `app/server/` that uses non-macro SQL or names a module's schema, and no module API yet moves a pick to `paid` or `free` or writes a `picks.release` row (D-1564); a test crate under `tests/` may seed any schema but may not name the mint (`tests/integration/tests/architecture.rs:30`). Where do the cases go? Choice: split by where the data can be made, without weakening either rule: `picks::api::released_view` checks through a crate-private `viewable(conn, (person, business), pick)` that never touches the vault, and `app/picks/src/tests/released_view.rs` runs it on the database (its own `picks` rows, teams through `businesses::api`, demotion with `set_roles`, removal with `remove_member`): owner and "Confirm and billing" member get the bound contact and email choice; a "Cards and quotes"-only member, another business's person, no release row, a status that left paid or free, an awaiting pick and an unknown pick get nothing. `privacy`'s `realm_tests` runs `read_released` with a `BusinessSessionProof` (fields, phone refused, per-field and pick rows with the person as actor, in-transaction refusal, nothing after the purge). `app/server/tests/released_view.rs` keeps what `server` can make: one session mint per process through `session_minter()`, and an unknown pick answered not-found with no vault read. Not covered by any test: a shown view end to end with the real mint, and that a view writes no release row, notice, charge, fee or masked line (true by construction: `released_view` has no write but the vault's audited read rows). Recorded for the runner's plan review and in `docs/for-casey-review.md`: either a paid-release API (the `payments` release sink of D-1563 (1)) or a server-test exemption in TD-SEC-10 would let the end-to-end case be written. Reason: a test must never break another test's rule to pass. Source: `tests/integration/tests/architecture_migrations.rs:731`, `app/picks/src/released_view.rs`.
- **D-1896** Question (T085; TD-BIZ-04, TD-PICK-39 E2E layers, D-1728): the business portal routes are not served (business sign-in waits on the composition's mail and code adapters), so no browser can hold a business session; how is the E2E layer met? Choice: `tests/e2e/business_portal.spec.ts` checks what a request can reach now: a signed-out request for the portal home and a released job's page gets a 4xx with no tip line, no contact-choice line and no phone-shaped number. The page words (the first name exactly once, the details line ending in PICK-024's tip, the D-295 email line, BIZ-013's contact choice, BIZ-035's call log, BIZ-025's panel) are checked on the rendered templates in `app/portals/src/job_release.rs` and `app/portals/src/business_portal.rs`. When the portal is served, that task signs in in this spec and moves the page checks into the browser. Reason: a browser test of an unserved page would test a copy, not the page. Source: `tests/e2e/business_portal.spec.ts`, D-1728.
- **D-1897** Question (T085; BIZ-025, TD-PICK-17 "the panel equals the ledger", TD-BIZ-11): where do the "Your numbers" counts come from? Choice: `portals::api::YourNumbers` is filled by the composition and the page only shows it (fee per job won is fees over confirms, "None yet" before the first; the typical quotes per trade in tenths). No reader of `payments`' ledger or `jobs`' replies for a business's month exists yet, so the "equals the ledger" case of TD-PICK-17 and TD-BIZ-11's picked-to-finished count on the database wait for the task that serves the portal home and writes that reader; the page cases are T085's. Reason: `portals` reads money only through `payments::api`, and that read is not built. Source: `app/portals/src/business_portal.rs`.
- **D-1898** Question (T085; BIZ-035, TD-BIZ-12 call-log case, D-286): the call log needs each attempt's time, the PICK-018 window flag, the answer and the missed-call text's state; `calls::api::call_log` has the first three by line, and the text's state lives in `picks`' unreachable-refund records.
