- **D-1899** Question (T085; SEC-038, TD-SEC-17, D-480): T196 checks the 5-minute step-up inside `request_notice_change` only; the other guarded changes (backup address, phone link and approval, team role, saved card, monthly limit, auto-confirm) are built by later tasks. Choice: one gate, `portals::api::require_step_up(db, principal, (SensitiveChange, route), now)`, which every guarded change calls first, over `businesses::api::has_fresh_step_up` (the same rule as T196: `team_member.step_up_at` at most `STEP_UP_LIFE` before now, exactly 5:00 still fresh, a future time never, a removed member never). A refusal is one `authz_denied` security event (SEC-048, with the member as actor and the route template) and one log line naming the change; no new `SecurityEventKind` was added, so `status.rs` and the stored kinds are unchanged. Reason: one rule in one place, so a later change cannot forget the 5 minutes. Source: `app/portals/src/business_portal.rs`, `app/businesses/src/api.rs`.
- **D-1900** Question (T085; CARD-022, D-491, D-492): how are each person's open-cards email times stored? Choice: `businesses.open_cards_time`, one row per team member who changed the default, three booleans (8 a.m., noon, 5 p.m.) with a check of at most two; no row is 5 p.m. only, all three false is off; set only by the person for themselves while a current member, read by T198's composer through `businesses::api::open_cards_times`. The migration keeps the number the plan gave it, 0133, below main's 0142 (it rests only on 0056; sqlx applies an unapplied lower version). A released job whose homeowner did not choose email says "Homeowner chose calls." for BIZ-013. The change is about 560 lines over 9 owned files plus the shared ones, above the 350-line budget, because the three pages and two test files had no earlier home. Reason: CARD-022 says "up to two times a day they choose", "5 p.m. by default" and "can switch it off". Source: `migrations/0133_businesses_open_cards_times.sql`, `app/businesses/src/open_cards_times.rs`.
- **D-1911** Question (harness fix, November 7, 2026; numbered max(`next_decision` 1901, `main`'s highest 1900 + 1) + 10 = 1911): after D-1890 merged, the runner's smoke still rebuilt every member and timed out again (`runner_log`: 21:16Z on bd7921a "smoke mtimes: 1858 new or changed paths"; 22:08Z on 00daffc8 "1870 new or changed paths", exit 124); why? Finding: the manifest did survive the cache. Job 128506807986 (smoke on d88789f1 at about 19:50Z) logged "42 new or changed paths" and saved it under `rust-smoke-…-7225ed30`, and job 128528133812 restored that entry for the bd7921a smoke. The cause was D-1890's review rule that any `.sqlx/` change makes every path new: d88789f1..bd7921a added 5 query files and bd7921a..00daffc8 added 3, and each was an addition or a rename. Every task that adds a query does that, so every smoke after one was a full rebuild (1,721 or 1,733 tracked files plus folders). None of the 73 commits on `main` that touched `.sqlx/` modified an existing file. Two cache faults made it worse. First, every backup job (`pull_request`, `workflow_run` and `workflow_dispatch` alike) saved `target/smoke` under `…-<sha>`, so a job that never ran the smoke could take a commit's key first: run 42418119257's backup job logged "Unable to reserve cache with key rust-smoke-…-00daffc8…" and job 128528165482 lost `…-bd7921a4…` the same way. Second, the main entry's `!target/smoke` does not reach inside the listed `target`: the main entry grew from 2.2 GB (`…-c4468d67`) to 5.6 to 6.1 GB once smoke entries existed. Choice: (1) `pin_smoke_mtimes` makes every path new only for a changed existing `.sqlx/` file. An added query file comes with the source change that names its hash, which rebuilds that crate; a removed one is read by no build. A changed one (same SQL, new metadata) still rebuilds everything. (2) `backup-runner.yml` splits the smoke cache into `actions/cache/restore@v4`, keyed `…-<sha>-<run_id>-<run_attempt>` with restore keys for the same commit, then the same lock, then any, and `actions/cache/save@v4`. The save runs with `if: always()` only when `target/smoke-ran` exists, which `smoke_main` writes after every smoke run, beside the smoke target and outside both entries, so it never collides and never comes from a job without a smoke. (3) The main entry lists `target/debug` instead of `target` and `!target/smoke`. (4) `_pin_smoke_tree` logs "smoke mtimes: manifest <path>, <n> entries loaded". Tests: `tests/test_runner_keeper.py` (query-file rules, the split cache steps, the marker and the log line). Supersedes the `.sqlx/` clause of D-1890. Owner approval: Casey's standing delegation. Source: `runner/github_env.py` (`pin_smoke_mtimes`, `smoke_main`, `_mark_smoke_ran`), `.github/workflows/backup-runner.yml`, D-1890, D-1178, D-514.
- **D-1912** Question (T195; BIZ-015, TD-BIZ-04, D-491): `payments::api::business_statement` returns every ledger entry carrying the business's ID, which can include Ask Hava's own Stripe costs, and a `dispute` entry holds the disputed amount plus Ask Hava's $15 dispute fee (`DISPUTE_FEE_CENTS`); what do the billing page and the CSV show? Choice: the business's money only: charges ("Introduction fee by job size"), refunds, credits, free first wins, repeat-customer and fee-free $0 entries, and disputes at the disputed amount without the dispute fee, the same split `MoneyView::from_entries` makes; processing fees, countering fees and their returns, and payouts are left out. Totals are the `Statement`'s `MoneyView` (charges, refunds, credits) plus the count of free-first-win rows. The CSV has four columns (Arizona date, entry words, job ID, dollars), no quoting needed because every entry word is fixed and comma-free; no PDF is offered (D-491). The page takes the saved cards (`PaymentMethod`: brand and last four) and the limit from the composition, because `payments::api` has no reader for either yet. Copy panel and cold read (WORD-028, WORD-029): applied "Free first win", "No fee for this job type", "You disputed this charge with your bank", capitalised brand, "You haven't set a monthly limit.", the code line naming text or email; kept "free first win" (the spec's term) over "First job free", and did not name Excel or Google Sheets. Source: `app/portals/src/business_portal.rs`, `templates/business_billing.html`.
- **D-1913** Question (T195; SEC-038, TD-SEC-17, FEE-041, D-480, D-492): who may change the saved card or the monthly fee limit, and in what order are the checks? Choice: `change_fee_limit` and `change_saved_card` refuse anyone but the owner or a "Confirm and billing" member first (no security event, the page never offers them the change), then call `require_step_up` (T085's gate: a Verify code within 5 minutes, 5:00 included, else one `authz_denied` event), then `payments::api::set_fee_limit` or `save_card`. A refusal stores nothing. The code-entry step before a billing change is wired with the routes (D-1728). Source: `app/portals/src/business_portal.rs`.
- **D-1914** Question (T195; BIZ-029, TD-BIZ-09, D-200, D-492, D-1896): who may reply to a complaint, and how are the E2E layers met while the business routes are not served? Choice: any current member of the business may send the one reply (`reply_to_complaint` passes only the principal's own business to `businesses::api::reply`, so a member can never reply for another business); BIZ-029 names no role and the reply goes to Casey, not the homeowner. The page shows kind and date (Arizona time) and never the job ID; the box shows while `now` is before exactly 5 days. As in D-1896, `tests/e2e/business_billing.spec.ts` checks the signed-out edge (no ledger line, card, complaint or PDF from the billing, CSV and complaints paths, and refused POSTs), and the page and database cases run in `business_portal::tests`; Casey's view of the reply and the third-complaint pause stay T083's cases (`tests/integration/tests/complaints.rs`). The change is about 590 lines (business_portal.rs 473, about half of it tests) over the 350-line budget, because three pages, two guarded changes and their database cases had no earlier home. Source: `app/portals/src/business_portal.rs`, `templates/business_complaints.html`, `tests/e2e/business_billing.spec.ts`.
- **D-1915** Question (T195 review; BIZ-015, TD-BIZ-04, D-1912): the ledger stores refunds, credits and disputes as positive amounts, so the billing rows and the CSV showed them like charges and the CSV's amount column did not sum to what the business paid; how is money back to the business shown? Choice: a sign, not a direction column: rows and CSV show charges (and the $0 free-first-win, repeat-customer and fee-free entries) as they are and refunds, credits and disputes (without the dispute fee) negative, so the amount column sums to the net the business paid; the table caption says "A minus sign means money back to you." The totals keep their labelled positive amounts ("Refunds to you", "Credits to you"). The CSV keeps its four columns. Reason: one signed column is what a spreadsheet sums; a direction column would make every sum need a formula. Source: `app/portals/src/business_portal.rs` (`entry_label`, `statement_rows`), `templates/business_billing.html`.
- **D-1916** Question (T195 review; BIZ-029, A11Y-030, TD-BIZ-09, D-1914): the complaints page's error summary always linked to the reply box and told the business to send before the box closed, even when the refusal was `ComplaintError::Closed` (5 days passed, a reply already sent, or not this business's) and no box was shown; what does a refused reply show? Choice: `complaints_page` takes a `RefusedReply` (complaint, `ComplaintError`, the typed words). `BadReply` says "Write a reply of up to 1,000 characters, then send it."; `Closed`, `BoxOpen` and `Unknown` say "Your reply was not sent because the reply box for this complaint is closed."; `Database`, `Audit` and `BadKind` say "Your reply was not sent. Please send it again." The summary links to the box only while that box shows (else plain text); the same words show by the box as "Error: ..." in its `aria-describedby` with `aria-invalid`, and the typed words stay in it. The form's action comes from `COMPLAINT_REPLY_ROUTE`, the CSV link from `STATEMENT_ROUTE`. Source: `app/portals/src/business_portal.rs`, `templates/business_complaints.html`.
- **D-1917** Question (T086; SEC-005, SEC-007, SEC-043, D-098): how are the owner's password, factors, sessions and recovery codes stored and checked? Choice: migration `0135_portals_owner_auth.sql`: `portals.owner` (one row by a `singleton` unique check; the argon2id PHC string, made with argon2's default argon2id parameters and a 16-byte OS-random salt), `portals.owner_factor` (a passkey as webauthn-rs credential JSON, or a TOTP authenticator's 20-byte secret with the last 30-second step accepted, so one code works once, RFC 6238 section 5.2), `portals.owner_recovery_code` (the SHA256 of each 80-bit code, used once), `portals.owner_session` (each owner session's last request and last second-factor time) and `portals.owner_challenge`. A sign-in needs the password and a good factor; either failing is one `auth_failed` event and the same refusal. The session lives 12 hours from sign-in; `owner_principal` deletes it when more than 30 minutes passed since its last request (29:59 and 30:00 live, 30:01 gone) and otherwise restarts the idle clock. `require_owner_step_up` passes only with a factor at most 5 minutes old (5:00 included, never a future one) for each SEC-043 action (`OwnerAction::ALL`); `owner_step_up` records a fresh factor. A recovery code stands in for a factor only while at least two factors are registered (SEC-007's "needs at least two registered"), so a recovery path never exists with one factor; no function takes an email. Sign-in, "Sign out everywhere", a password change and a new factor each write an audit row (SEC-006). Known gaps, for review: the TOTP secret is stored as is (readable to anyone who can read the table, like the vault's ciphertext neighbours but without its key); the argon2 hash runs on the request's async thread (R10), accepted for one owner signing in a few times a day. Reason: SEC-005, SEC-007, SEC-043, D-098; the TOTP secret must be readable to check a code, and encrypting it with the vault key belongs to `privacy`, which has no general-purpose seal yet. Source: `app/portals/src/owner_auth.rs`, `app/portals/src/models.rs`. Review fixes (T086 fix round): (1) An owner session's `portals.session.expires_at` now follows the idle limit: the sign-in and every `owner_principal` read set it to 30 minutes (plus one microsecond, so 30:00 stays live as `idle_ended` says) after the request, never past 12 hours from sign-in; so T051's `current_session` (unchanged: `session.rs` is not T086's file and the change check refuses it) no longer returns an owner session idle for more than 30 minutes, and `Session::owner_proof` cannot mint a vault-read proof for one (tested: 30:00 a session, 31:00 none). Remaining gap, logged: `current_session` still does not check that an owner-realm row came from `owner_sign_in` (a bare `start_session(Realm::Owner, ..)` would pass it); only `owner_sign_in` calls `start_session` with `Realm::Owner`, and `owner_principal` refuses such a row (tested). Proposal for the task that serves owner vault reads: mint the owner proof from `OwnerPrincipal` only, or make `owner_proof` require the `owner_session` row, in `session.rs` under that task's ownership. (2) A recovery code is not a fresh factor (SEC-043 asks for a passkey or TOTP): a recovery-code sign-in starts with `factor_at` at the Unix epoch (stale), and `owner_step_up` refuses any recovery code as `auth_failed` without using it. (3) `change_owner_password` deletes every other owner session in the same transaction, keeping the current one. (4) The migration also takes `INSERT` on `owner_recovery_code` from `askhava_app` (only the bootstrap, as the migration role, makes codes) and limits `UPDATE` on `owner_factor` to `totp_last_step` and `passkey`, so the app role cannot swap a TOTP secret; both tested under `SET ROLE askhava_app`. (5) Known gap: no throttle or lockout on owner sign-in or step-up yet; SEC-040's per-IP limits and brute-force stops belong to T089, so the owner routes must not be served before T089's limits cover `OWNER_SIGNIN_ROUTE`, `OWNER_PASSKEY_ROUTE` and the step-up POST (see D-1921). (6) Size overrun: the task's budget was 7 files and 550 changed lines; the owned files came to about 1,930 changed lines before this fix round (`owner_auth.rs` about 850, `models.rs` about 390, the test about 460), because password, three factor kinds, sessions, step-up, bootstrap and passkey registration landed in one task; splitting would have left unguarded halves. Logged, not hidden.
- **D-1918** Question (T086; SEC-044, TD-SEC-23): how does the one-time bootstrap get the first owner credential without a route? Choice: `server bootstrap-owner` reads the token from `ASKHAVA_OWNER_BOOTSTRAP_TOKEN` (refused when missing or under 32 characters), the password as one line on standard input (refused by the SEC-043 rules), connects as the migration role and calls `portals::api::bootstrap_owner`, which in one transaction inserts the owner (a second run gets `AlreadyBootstrapped`), one TOTP authenticator and 10 recovery codes, with a system audit row; it prints the authenticator secret and the codes once to standard output. The migration takes `INSERT` and `DELETE` on `portals.owner` from `askhava_app`, so no route can create an owner even by mistake (tested with `SET ROLE askhava_app`). Conflict: SEC-044 says the command runs "in the release step", but the release step takes no input and its output stays in the host's deploy logs, which would keep the secrets; so the command is run once as a one-off command in Casey's own terminal against the release environment, and the host token variable is deleted afterwards by hand (the binary cannot delete a host variable); listed in `docs/for-casey-review.md`. The "every owner-creation route returns 404" case holds today because no owner route is served; the task that serves the owner portal adds the route-table check. Reason: SEC-044, D-480; the brief wins on how, and printing secrets into kept logs breaks `BUILD_BRIEF.md:62`. Source: `app/server/src/main.rs`, `app/portals/src/owner_auth.rs`. Review fixes (T086 fix round): the token check is honest about its limits: it only refuses a missing or short value, it is not compared with anything stored, and it proves nothing about who runs the command; what actually guards the bootstrap is the migration role's URL (only that role may insert an owner) and the one-owner rule (a second run fails). No test checks that the host token variable was deleted afterwards (the binary cannot see or delete host variables); that stays a hand step in `docs/for-casey-review.md`. On a terminal the password prompt no longer echoes: `stty -echo` before the read and `stty echo` after, through `std::process::Command` (no new crate; no no-echo crate is on `kit/allowed_crates.txt`); piped input is read as before.
- **D-1919** Question (T086; D-098): how do passkeys work? Choice: webauthn-rs 0.5.5 (already approved, section 11) with its `danger-allow-state-serialisation` feature, so a ceremony's server state can wait in `portals.owner_challenge` between the options and the answer: each row is for one purpose (`sign_in` or `register`), deleted when used and good for 5 minutes. `passkey_sign_in_options` gives the request options for the registered passkeys; `static/passkey.ts` (tsc, WebAuthn in the browser) turns the base64url fields into bytes, asks for the passkey and posts the answer as JSON in the sign-in form's hidden `passkey` field with the password; the server checks it with `finish_passkey_authentication` and stores the updated counter. Registering a passkey (`passkey_registration_options`, `finish_passkey_registration`) needs a fresh factor; its browser page comes with the owner settings page, so `passkey.ts` runs only the sign-in ceremony for now. A real passkey round trip has no Rust test (it needs an authenticator); the tests prove a fake answer, an unknown challenge and a reused challenge are refused. Reason: D-098, D-491; WebAuthn in the browser cannot be avoided, and keeping the state server-side means the browser never holds it. Review fix (T086 fix round): the sign-in page's `GET` stores nothing. `owner_signin_page(csrf, passkey, failed)` takes only whether a passkey exists (`passkey_registered`, a read); `passkey.ts` asks for a challenge by `POST` to `OWNER_PASSKEY_ROUTE` (`/owner/sign-in/passkey`, with the form's CSRF token; the route answers `{"challenge", "options"}`) and puts the row ID in the hidden `challenge` field. `passkey_sign_in_options` first deletes every expired challenge and refuses once `MAX_LIVE_SIGN_IN_CHALLENGES` (20) sign-in challenges are live (one conditional insert), so the table stays small; tested that an expired one is swept.
- **D-1920** Question (T086; SEC-043, D-491): which offline breached-password list? Choice: `app/portals/data/breached_passwords.txt`, compiled in with `include_str!`: one password per line, compared without case, `#` lines are notes; only passwords of 15 characters or more are listed, since shorter ones are refused anyway. It holds 40 long passwords common in public breach lists (number runs, keyboard walks, doubled words). Proposal (not done): swap in a larger offline list cut to 15 characters and up, after checking its license. Reason: SEC-043 asks for an offline check; a network call to a breach service would send a password hash prefix out.
- **D-1921** Question (T086; SEC-005, SEC-006, SEC-019, A11Y-013): what is served now, and how does the owner-only gate work? Choice: no owner route is served yet (like the business pages, D-1728): `owner_signin_page` renders `templates/owner_signin.html` (one form: password with `autocomplete="current-password"`, one code field with `autocomplete="one-time-code"` that takes the app code or a recovery code, paste allowed, an error summary that does not say which part failed, "Use a passkey instead of a code" only when a passkey is registered, with its `role="status"` line and the failure words in `data-failed`). `owner_sign_out` deletes the server session, so the old cookie is refused; `sign_out_everywhere` deletes every owner session. `owner_power` is the SEC-006 gate for pause, refund and release: only a live owner principal passes (a business or homeowner session never), a refund also needs the fresh factor, and a refusal is one `authz_denied` event. The task that serves the owner portal wires the routes (CSRF, cross-site refusal, `no-store`), its `PAGE_STATES` rows, and calls `owner_power` from each pause, refund and release handler. Reason: the composition owns routes; the gate and rules are proven now at the function level (TD-SEC-01, TD-SEC-22). Review fix (T086 fix round): the task that serves the owner routes also serves `POST OWNER_PASSKEY_ROUTE` (CSRF, cross-site refusal, `no-store`; JSON `{"challenge": id, "options": options}`), and must not serve any owner route before T089's rate limits and brute-force stops cover owner sign-in and step-up (SEC-040; D-1917).
- **D-1932** Question (Casey, November 8, 2026, through the overseer session; WORD-001, WORD-008, WORD-021, FEE-049, TERMS-016): the brand may change from "Ask Hava" (most likely to "Laftly") before launch, and today it is written as a literal in about 40 app files, the SMS templates, four of the build's checks and the legal drafts. How does a rename become a data change instead of hundreds of edits? Choice: the brand is configuration. (1) One file, `app/core/data/brand.json`, compiled into `core` and read by Python through `scripts/brand.py`, holds the display name, the "for Business" name, the short name every text opens with (`<short_name>:`), the legal and spoken legal name, the public domain, the email sender name and address, the card-statement prefix, the words never used alone (WORD-021) and the Spanish forms; `core::api::brand()` serves it, a binary checks and installs it at start-up, and a test may install a fake one. It is not an `ASKHAVA_*` setting: it is the same in every environment and ships with the build. (2) Customer-visible code, pages, emails, calls and text templates take the name from it (text templates and data through the tokens `{brand}`, `{brand_business}`, `{brand_short}`, `{brand_legal}` and `{domain}`, filled once at load); internal identifiers (`askhava_*` crates, `ASKHAVA_*` keys, schema and database names) stay. (3) The build's checks (`check_legal_docs.py`, `check_catalog.py`, `pii_scan.py`, the template scan) read the name from the same file, so each still requires the brand, now the configured one, and accepts and refuses exactly what it does today under "Ask Hava". (4) Legal records stay plain text naming the brand: the drafts in `docs/legal/` (the compiled-in homeowner Terms among them), the card authorization `AUTHORIZATION_TEXT` stored under its version, and the WORD-022 phrase list that mirrors the spec's patterns. A name change re-issues them under a new version (TERMS-016), and the checks fail after a switch until it has: `check_legal_docs.py` through (3), and T295's test for the Terms, the authorization and the list. (5) The value stays "Ask Hava" until Casey decides; the spec in `docs/spec/` and `sources/` keep the name, and this entry records how it is applied. The rewritten copy for a new name (wording that reads well with it, the legal drafts, the Spanish forms) comes after the build. A rename also needs outside steps no file covers: the domain and DNS, the Resend sending domain, the Stripe account's statement prefix, the Twilio Verify service's friendly name and the texting registration. Reason: Casey's instruction; one source of truth turns the rename into a reviewed data change, and the legal records are the one part a lawyer must reword, so they are made to fail loudly rather than change silently. Source: Casey, November 8, 2026 (overseer session), `sources/01_spec/Changes_Since_v9.3_AUTHORITATIVE.md:24`, `docs/spec/wording.md:5`.
- **D-1933** Question (plan change for D-1932): how is the work split and ordered, and how do tasks still to run learn the rule? Choice: five harness tasks with Opus reviews, because the work touches about 55 files (39 app files with customer-visible brand words, the checks, tests of DONE tasks) and a harness task may own at most 14: T291 (the brand file, `core::api::brand()`, `scripts/brand.py`, the four checks, and the guard `tests/docs/test_brand_literals.py`, a pytest test so `Ci` and the smoke run it with no protected workflow edit), T292 (messaging texts and emails, calls), T293 (businesses and quotes copy), T294 (pages, through an Askama call on the brand, and `app/portals/src/owner_auth.rs`, where T086 adds the passkey `rp_name` and "Ask Hava owner" wording), T295 (payments, ai, intake and picks, the switch test with a fake "Testbrand", a pinned hash of `AUTHORIZATION_TEXT` per `AUTHORIZATION_VERSION`, and the guard made strict). The guard fails on any brand word, in any letter case, in a customer-visible line of any text file under `app/` outside the brand file; until T295 a baseline written by T291 lets each listed file keep at most its count, and it only shrinks: T292, T293 and T294 (in that order, since each edits it) remove their own files' entries. If the baseline still lists a file no brand task owns when T295 starts, T295 stops and reports it and a plan change gives the file an owner. `app/core/data/brand.json` joins `protected_paths` in `kit/tasks.json`, so after T291 creates it only a harness task with an Opus review (a plan change with its decision) can rename the brand; it is not added to the plan lock's `LOCKED_FILES`, because the runner then treats every task owning `app/` as owning a locked file (`tests/test_runner_two_lanes.py`). Every prompt's wording rule says the brand is data and names the guard (`kit/prompts/TEMPLATE.md`). Order: the runner claims eligible tasks in state order and appends new tasks, so T291 would have come after about 35 others; instead T291 depends only on DONE tasks and every task that was eligible when this was written (T148, T254, T256, T258, T262, T263, T264, T265, T267, T269, T283, T289, T290) depends on T291, and so does every task waiting only on T087 (T088), so T291 is the next claim after T087, which the runner claimed first and which is not edited (it was IN_PROGRESS); a simulated serial run shows no cycle and the same gate-held tasks as on `main`. T292 to T294 follow T291; T294 also follows T086, T095 and T253; T295 follows them and T258 and T287 (it changes `payments/src/models.rs` and `picks/src/service.rs`). Queued tasks that own a file one of these owns wait for it: T199 and T133 (T293), T164 (T293, T294), T155, T157, T232, T200, T101, T269 and T272 (T294), T278 (T293, T295), T236 (T295); T100 waits for all five. A test of a DONE task changes only in how it reaches a text whose constant became a function, every expected literal unchanged. `scripts/trace_spec.py` (it scans the spec, which keeps the name) and the vendor-shape fixtures in `tests/contract/` are not changed. D-1932 and D-1933 were numbered by the interim rule of the November 8 hand-off (the highest of `next_decision` 1922, `main`'s D-1916 + 1 and the open plan branches' + 1, plus 10), not by `--reserve-decision`, which this session cannot run. Reason: the budget rules (D-485) make one or two tasks impossible; a guard that holds from the next claim keeps the queue from adding literals with no long dependency chains. Source: `scripts/validate_tasks.py:218`, `docs/governance.md:17`, `docs/governance.md:64`, `runner/state.py:429`, `docs/handoff/2026-11-08-early.md:32`.
- **D-1934** Question (T087; SEC-008, PICK-055, D-493, D-1728): what of the homeowner portal is served now? Choice: nothing yet, like the business and owner pages (D-1728, D-1921): `app/portals/src/homeowner_portal.rs` and `data_download.rs` give the sign-in by texted code (`send_sign_in_code`, `finish_sign_in`, a 30-day homeowner session started only after Verify says the code is right, a wrong code an `auth_failed` event with the contact ID), the realm-checked read of her number (`OnFile::read` over `privacy::api::read_own_contact`), the texts-off switch and the code-checked delete or copy request, and `homeowner_page` renders every screen of `templates/homeowner_home.html`. The task that serves `/h` (after T089's Verify send caps, PICK-055) wires the routes with CSRF, the cross-site refusal and `no_store`, adds the `PAGE_STATES` rows, and extends `tests/e2e/homeowner_portal.spec.ts` to sign in. Reason: a sign-in route that texts codes must not be served before its send caps exist; the rules are proven now at the function level, and the e2e spec checks the signed-out edge.
- **D-1935** Question (T087; PRIV-021, TD-PRIV-05): the goal says the portal lets her change her properties and language, and TD-PRIV-05 wants an address edit's audit row; how, when `privacy` has no update of a stored contact and no module stores a homeowner's language (only `intake.conversation.language` per conversation)? Choice: the home shows her number's last four digits, the address on her own record and the language she is texted in, read only; the texts-off switch is the one change built. Changing an address needs a `privacy::api` update of her own contact under her `HomeownerSessionProof` (writing `ops` `Change::Field("address")`, no value), and changing the language needs a stored per-homeowner language in `intake`; neither file is T087's, so both are left for the plan (reported). Reason: T087 owns only its four files; a form that stores nothing would mislead her.
- **D-1936** Question (T087; PRIV-031, D-492): where is a delete or copy request recorded, and when is it acted on? Choice: `open_request` writes one `ops` audit row (`portals.data_copy_requested` or `portals.data_delete_requested`, actor and subject her vault contact; the row's time is the received time) and then texts a Verify code to the number on file; `confirm_request` checks the code (`picks::api::rules::parse_code`, then Verify) and acts only on a correct one: a copy is handed over by the caller with `download_file`, a delete runs `privacy::api::delete_my_data`; then `portals.data_<kind>_confirmed`. A wrong, short or unreadable code writes and deletes nothing. `DataRequest::due_at` is the received time plus `ANSWER_WITHIN` (30 days). Reason: T087 has no migration of its own, and the audit log already holds who asked for what and when; a due-date list for Casey reads these rows (T200 or the owner portal).
- **D-1937** Question (T087; PRIV-031): what does "Download my data" hold, and how is no other person's data in it? Choice: `download_file` takes the held records the composition read (`HeldItem`: contact, section, time, words) and writes JSON with four arrays, `requests`, `quotes`, `messages`, `consent`, keeping only items whose contact is the one her `OnFile` names. A quote item carries the business name, the quote and its time only, never a business phone, email or address. Reason: the records live in `intake`, `quotes`, `messaging` and `picks`; the filter on her contact is the last guard whatever the caller passes.
- **D-1938** Question (T087; CON-035, CON-015, TD-CON-28): can the portal switch turn texts back on? Choice: no; the switch only turns texts off (`messaging::api::suppress`, channel `portal`, detected `portal:switch`, listed at once), and with texts off the home shows `TEXTS_OFF_LINE` ("text START"), because only the provider's START lifts a listing so the app's list and the carrier's block agree (CON-015, D-870). AI-smell list: add "on file" and "we still hold" (the cold read flagged both as office talk).
- **D-1939** Question (T087 fix round; PRIV-031, PRIV-011, SEC-008, A11Y-030, R5, R6, R11, R13; the fresh-eyes review): the first cut acted on any correct Verify code with or without a request, trusted the caller's job list, deleted and audited in two transactions, could not finish sign-in (the code form lost the number), said "within 30 days" while deleting at once, did not mask business contact details, printed contact values in `Debug`, hid vault errors as "not on file" and keyed Verify sends on the current time. What changes? Choice: (1) a request is the `portals.data_<kind>_requested` audit row `open_request` writes; its row ID is the request ID the code form carries to `DATA_CODE_ROUTE`, and `confirm_request` acts only on a row made by and about her contact, of a received kind, not past `due_at` (the row's stored time plus 30 days), then a correct code; a separate Verify code per purpose is not possible (Verify checks by number), but the sign-in code is spent by the sign-in and a code alone now acts on nothing; (2) one `portals.data_<kind>_confirmed` row per request (subject `portals.data_request`, the request ID), claimed with `ops::api::audit_once` in the same transaction as `privacy::api::delete_my_data` (its own transaction nests as a savepoint), so the delete and its audit row commit together and a repeat acts on nothing; (3) the jobs come from the new `intake::api::jobs_of_contact`, never the browser; (4) `download_file` masks runs of 7 or more digits, words with `@` and web addresses in the quotes and messages (her requests and consent records are hers and stay whole); (5) `HeldItem`, `HomeFacts` and `PortalScreen` print no contact value in `Debug` (the screen's typed number is a `SecretString`); (6) a vault error other than a bad number is logged once without the number and is `HomeownerError::Database`; (7) Verify send keys are the contact (and kind) with the ten-minute window of `now`, so a double submit reuses the key; (8) the sign-in code page posts the typed number to `HOMEOWNER_CODE_ROUTE`; the sign-in page keeps the typed number, marks it `aria-invalid` with the summary's words by the field, and every error summary follows the h1 (as `pick_code.html`); the delete page says "right away" and the copy button "Download my copy". Not done: the due date is not its own column (no T087 migration; it is the stored received time plus 30 days), and a double submit of the delete button stores two requests (each answered at most once). Reason: the review's findings, fixed inside T087's files and the shared `intake` and `portals` API files.
- **D-1940** Question (T291; WORD-001, WORD-008, WORD-021, TXT-006, TERMS-016; D-1932): the legal-draft check requires each key phrase to be word for word in its spec requirement and in its document, and D-1932 says the check builds every phrase that names the brand from the brand file; but the spec keeps the name (`scripts/trace_spec.py` is not changed), so a phrase filled from a new brand could never match the spec. How are the two compared? Choice: each phrase in `scripts/check_legal_docs.py` is a template over `scripts/brand.py`'s tokens (`{brand}`, `{brand_legal}`, `{domain}`); the document must hold it filled from `app/core/data/brand.json`, and the spec match fills it from `SPEC_TOKENS`, the names the spec's own wording uses, which change only with the spec. The WORD-021 rule is one pattern per `forbidden_alone` word, allowed only where the display name's text before it precedes it and the text after it follows it, so a word that starts or ends the display name is handled (today `(?<!Ask )\bHava\b`, the same as before; a word that is the whole display name gets no pattern). `run` keeps reading the brand file beside the scripts, not under `--root`: the existing cases copy only `docs/legal` and `docs/spec` into a temporary root, so reading it from there needs a fallback that would hide a missing file. `check_catalog.py`'s safety-prompt rule fills a prompt's tokens and requires `<short_name>:` (the Spanish short name for `es`); `pii_scan.py` allows the brand file's domain through `own_domains()`, which puts its own folder on `sys.path` only for the import (because `runner/github_env.py` loads it by path) and takes it off again, and gives no extra domain when `brand.py` or the brand file fails (a `BrandError` is a `ValueError`, which the runner's load does not catch), so a bad brand file makes the scan stricter, never crashes the runner; `check_catalog.py` reads the brand once per question bank; `scripts/brand.py` matches its host-label and prefix patterns with `fullmatch`, so a trailing newline is refused as in Rust; `Brand::fill` and `brand.fill` read a token as `{`, no brace, `}`, the leftmost first (`{{brand}}` fills to `{<name>}`, `{ {brand_x}` is an unknown token in both), and the `FILL_CASES` raw string in `app/core/src/tests/brand.rs` is the one table both languages' tests run (`tests/docs/test_brand_literals.py` reads it from there); the template scan fills each template in its own language before its checks. Under "Ask Hava" every check accepts and refuses what it did, and the existing cases in `tests/test_check_legal_docs.py`, `tests/test_check_catalog.py`, `tests/test_pii_scan.py` and the template scan's planted cases pass unedited. Reason: the spec is the record of what was decided and keeps the name (D-1932 (5)); after a switch the check then fails only on the drafts, which must be re-issued (TERMS-016). Source: `scripts/check_legal_docs.py`, `runner/github_env.py:147`.
- **D-1941** Question (T291; D-1932, D-1933): what exactly does the brand-literal guard count, and how is the Rust API named? Choice: (1) `tests/docs/test_brand_literals.py` counts lines, not matches: a visible line of a file under `app/` holding any brand word (display, short, legal and spoken legal name, domain, a `forbidden_alone` word, the statement prefix) as a whole word in any letter case counts once, and `tests/brand_literal_baseline.json` holds those line counts (39 files, 295 lines at T291, matching D-1933's 39 files). (2) An internal identifier is only the lower-case match `askhava` followed by `-`, `_` or `.` and a lower-case letter (`askhava-core`, the `askhava.vault_probe` database setting, the `askhava.csrf.*` cookie names), or `Askhava` in an `X-Askhava-<Name>` header (the stand-ins' `X-Askhava-Message-Key`); any other brand word joined by a hyphen or dot (`Hava-approved`, `pro-Hava`, `Askhava-branded`) counts; `askhava_*` and `ASKHAVA_*` never match because `_` is a word character; a line opening `"$id"` is skipped; a match holding a space or a dot (`Ask Hava-branded`, `askhava.com`) is never an identifier. (3) Comment lines are those opening `//`, `{#` or `<!--` (with their block to `#}` or `-->`); a `#[cfg(test)]` item is skipped to its closing brace or `;`, starting on the attribute's own line when the item follows it there (`#[cfg(test)] mod tests;`); `AUTHORIZATION_TEXT` is skipped from its `const` line to its `;`, under `app/payments/` only. (4) Main's baseline is read with `git show main:` then `origin/main:`; when neither has it the shrink rule is skipped. (5) `core::api` re-exports `brand::install` as `install_brand`, beside `init as init_logging`, since a bare `install` says nothing at a call site; `askhava_server::start_up` calls `Brand::embedded` and `install_brand` before reading settings, so both binaries stop with the bad field's name. `brand()` falls back to an empty `Brand` (never a panic, `missing_panics_doc`) only if the embedded file failed its check, which `start_up` and `src/tests/brand.rs` refuse first. `Brand` and `BrandEs` derive neither `Default` nor `Deserialize`: the file is read into the private `RawBrand`, so only `Brand::parse`, `Brand::embedded` and that private fallback build one. Reason: the rules D-1933 states, made precise enough to test; a line count is stable under rewording within a line. Source: `docs/decisions.md` D-1933, `app/core/src/api.rs`.
- **D-1945** Question (T088; SEC-019, SEC-048, D-1726, D-1868): what is "the route table" the authorization matrix is generated from while `docs/architecture.md` section 13 does not exist yet and most portal routes are declared but not served, and is a link route's bare 404 a denial to log? Choice: the table is read from the source: every one-line `.route(` call in `app/*/src` (constants resolved; top-level `#[cfg(test)] mod` blocks, `src/tests/` and the `/__test/` routes left out, the latter being TD-SEC-15's) with its methods, plus every `const *_ROUTE` or `*_PATH` naming a path, so a declared route is in the matrix before it is served. Each path gets a door by its prefix (`/webhooks` webhook, `/static` asset, `/sign-in` or `/b/signup` sign-in, `/q/{token}` and `/f/{token}` link, `/h` homeowner, `/b` business); a path with no door fails the run. Served link routes are tried over HTTP through the portals routers merged as `server::build_router` merges them (a test crate may not depend on `server`); unserved homeowner and business routes through the guard their handler must call first (the homeowner realm, the only one `Session::homeowner_proof` mints for, since a test may not take the session mint; `business_principal` and `may`). A link route's token is the key, so an actor without it sends a well-formed token no job has and gets the bare 404 of SEC-037; that 404 is "nothing here", not an authorization denial of a known actor's request, and is not a security event (logging every unknown token would let anyone fill the table and trip the burst alert; token guessing is T089's rate limit). Reason: one generated list that a new route cannot escape, testable today. Fix round (review findings): the realm probe calls the guard only and never reaches a handler, so `td_sec_01_route_table_is_generated_and_every_path_has_a_door` now fails when any `/h` or `/b` path (other than sign-in) is served, that is has a `.route(` method. The task that first serves one (the `/h` routes after T089's caps, D-1934; the `/b` portal routes) therefore turns `Ci` red until the matrix probes that route over HTTP with the six actors; since `tests/security/tests/auth_matrix.rs` is a protected test once merged, that change is made in a `harness` task with an Opus review (`BUILD_BRIEF.md:70`), which the serving task asks for in its report rather than editing the file, and the serving task's PR waits for it. Known limit: homeowner A versus B isolation is proven only for the `/q/{token}` and `/f/{token}` link tokens; `/h` is checked only as "the homeowner realm passes, every other actor fails", not as "A's session never reads B's request or contact", which waits for the `/h` routes to be served and the matrix extension above (`OnFile::read` and `data_download` keep their own per-contact tests, D-1934 to D-1939). Line budget: the file is about 630 lines against the task's 400-line budget, one file being allowed; the extra is the generated route table reader (source walk, test-module stripping, constant resolution, method reading) and the six-actor world with its fake jobs, tokens and sessions, which no shared test helper offers yet; splitting it into a helper crate would add a protected path and a second file for no reader's gain, so it stays one file. Source: `kit/prompts/T088.md`, `docs/decisions.md` D-1726, D-1868.
- **D-1946** Question (T088; SEC-048): which refusals does the matrix prove are security events, and which are not logged as SEC-048 asks? Choice: for every served POST route and every actor, a cross-site post and a wrong CSRF token are each a 403 and exactly one `csrf_rejected` row with the route template, the request ID and the actor's session ID (none for anonymous). Two gaps are reported, not patched, since the code is not T088's: a webhook signature failure is one `adapters::api::refuse` log line (vendor and reason) with no `portals.security_event` row, request ID or route (`app/server/src/inbound_text.rs`, `app/payments/src/routes.rs`); and the realm guards (`business_principal`, `homeowner_proof`) return `None` without an event, so each route wiring task must record the `authz_denied` event when it refuses. Reason: SEC-048 names webhook signature failures and authorization denials; the matrix states what holds now. Source: `docs/spec/security.md:52`, `app/adapters/src/signatures.rs:159`.
- **D-1947** Question (T088; BIZ-041, TD-BIZ-31, TD-BIZ-13, D-491): how is "no push web app in the pilot" checked? Choice: no route path in the generated table holds a push, subscription, manifest or service-worker word; no file under any module's `templates/` or `static/` is named for a manifest or service worker or contains `serviceWorker`, `manifest`, `PushManager`, a push-subscription path or "Turn on job alerts" (case-insensitive); and `channel_choices` offers no push channel with business texting off or on. Reason: the later app phase adds these deliberately, and this check then changes with the spec. Source: `docs/spec/businesses.md:45`.
- **D-1948** Question (T088 fix round; SEC-048, D-1946): who closes the SEC-048 gaps D-1946 reports, and is "every denial is logged as a security event" (T088's goal) met? Choice: only partly. Met: every refused request to a served link route (cross-site post, wrong CSRF token) is one `csrf_rejected` row with route template, request ID and session ID, and the owner and business step-up refusals are `authz_denied` rows (`owner_auth.rs`, `business_portal.rs`). Not met: (1) a webhook signature failure is only an `adapters::api::refuse` log line, never a `webhook_signature_failed` row (`SecurityEventKind::WebhookSignatureFailed` exists in `app/portals/src/security.rs` unused); (2) the realm guards `business_principal` and `homeowner_proof` return `None` without an `authz_denied` row. Owners, by the files `kit/tasks.json` gives them (not edited here): the Twilio inbound route's row is T256's, the next pending task owning `app/server/src/inbound_text.rs` (T257 and T279 after it); the Stripe webhook's row is T259's, the next pending task owning `app/payments/src/routes.rs`; the realm-guard refusals are each route-serving task's when it wires the guard (whichever task serves the `/h` routes once T089's caps land, D-1934, and the `/b` portal routes), and T204, which owns "security events are logged" (SEC-048, SEC-047) and their alerts, checks the whole set is recorded before it is done. These owners are named here and in `docs/for-casey-review.md`; their task prompts do not yet say so, so the runner's next plan change adds the line to T256, T259 and T204, or a fix task is cut if one of them is done first. Reason: T088 owns only the test file; the matrix states what holds and the gap stays visible instead of a test being weakened to pass. Source: `docs/spec/security.md:52`, `kit/tasks.json` (T204, T256, T259 `owns`), `docs/decisions.md` D-1946.
- **D-1950** Question (T089; SEC-014, SEC-015, SEC-020, SEC-040, PICK-055, D-491, D-1837): what are the rate limits, where do they live and how is a burst alerted? Choice: one shared check, `intake::api::admit` (`app/intake/src/limits.rs`): a `Limit` is a code-name scope, a ceiling and a window (a clock hour, or an Arizona day: the UTC day of the time moved back 7 hours); `admit` counts one request per `(Limit, Key)` pair through `core`'s atomic `rate_limit_hit` (one `INSERT … ON CONFLICT … DO UPDATE … RETURNING`, SEC-040), narrowest first, and stops at the first full one, so a refused request never spends a wider bucket; the first refusal of a scope in its window raises one High `ops` alert whose kind is the scope (a `<scope>:alerted` bucket of ceiling 1 admits only the first), so a burst gives one alert, not one per request. Keys are an IP (from `ClientIpPolicy::client_ip`, never `X-Forwarded-For`), a record ID (a vault contact, a business) or everyone; never a phone or email (PRIV-002). Values: intake 5 new requests per phone (vault contact) per hour (SEC-014), 10 per web IP per hour, 40 for all numbers together per hour (SEC-015: a burst of 100 fake requests in an hour has 60 refused and one `intake.requests_all` alert; a normal Lake Havasu hour is far below 40); portals (`app/portals/src/limits.rs`) 10 sign-in link requests per IP and 10 per business per hour, 20 code tries per IP and 20 per business per hour (both in front of T272's per-member link cap and per-link try cap, counting requests, never links or tries, D-1837), 10 code-send requests per IP per hour, 5 portal Verify sends per number on file per Arizona day and the configured global daily Verify threshold (`verify_all`, High alert `portals.verify_daily_cap`, PICK-055), 5 owner password tries per IP and 20 on the account per hour (the passkey path calls no limit, so it is never hard-locked, D-492), 5 business sign-ups per IP and 50 for everyone per Arizona day (SEC-014), 30 quote submissions per business and 60 per IP per hour. No new table: `core.rate_limit` (migration 0020) holds every counter. Reason: one check keeps every limit atomic and alerting the same way; intake owns the per-phone request limit and portals the sign-in and code limits (D-491). Source: `docs/spec/security.md:18`, `:19`, `:24`, `:44`; `docs/spec/quotes-pick.md:59`.
- **D-1951** Question (T089; SEC-014, PICK-055, D-1934): T089 owns only the two `limits.rs` files and its test, so who calls the limits at the routes? Choice: each route's owner calls the matching `admit_*` first and, on `Admission::Refused` or an error, answers as for any failure and does nothing else. The served Twilio inbound route (`app/server/src/inbound_text.rs`, T241's) does not call `intake::api::admit_new_request` yet: the next pending task owning that file, T256, calls it with the sender's vault contact (no IP: the request comes from Twilio) before `receive_reply` for a sender with no open request, and a refused text opens nothing and is answered by nothing. The unserved routes call theirs when served: the `/h` sign-in and data-code sends `admit_code_send` (IP first, then her contact when on file, so an unknown number still spends the IP limit and sends nothing) and their code tries `admit_code_try`; business sign-in `admit_sign_in_link` and `admit_code_try` (with T272's caps after them); owner sign-in `admit_owner_password` on the password POST only; business sign-up `admit_sign_up`; the quote form and quote texts `admit_quote` (quotes by text pass no IP). The page pick's codes keep `picks`' own PICK-055 caps (`picks::api::send_page_code`); `verify_all` counts only portal sends, so the PICK-055 global threshold applies to each counter separately (a plan gap for the runner: one shared global Verify count needs a `picks` change). Reason: changing those files is outside T089's scope; naming the callers keeps the gap visible. Source: `kit/tasks.json` (T256 `owns`), `app/portals/CLAUDE.md` ("never serve an owner route before T089's limits cover it").
- **D-1952** Question (T089; TD-SEC-19, TD-PICK-36): which cases of the shared test entries fall to T089, and which are proven elsewhere? Choice: `tests/security/tests/rate_limits.rs` proves at the function level: 5 per phone then refused, a new hour admits; 100 fake requests over distinct numbers and IPs give 40 admitted and one High alert, and 100 from one IP give 10; code tries, sign-in links (IP hopping on one business) and owner passwords (per IP, then the account across IPs) stop at their limits; 20 concurrent requests over two connection pools (two processes' worth) admit exactly 5; the client IP is the header the setting names, a changing `X-Forwarded-For` never resets the limit, `CF-Connecting-IP` is ignored on a DNS-only hostname and honoured on a proxied one only from Cloudflare's ranges; with password tries throttled the passkey options still answer; portal sends stop at 5 per number, a new Arizona day admits, and the global threshold refuses and alerts once; 50 sign-ups a day, 30 quotes per business per hour. A full passkey sign-in needs a real WebAuthn authenticator, so "a passkey sign-in succeeds while passwords are throttled" is proven only as "the passkey path calls no limit and still answers"; the end-to-end case falls to the task that serves owner sign-in. TD-PICK-36's voice, per-job, 9 p.m. and pick-code cases are `picks`' (`app/picks/src/tests/pick_code_rules.rs`); its unknown-number same-answer case is T087's `send_sign_in_code`. Reason: each entry's cases are completed by the task that owns the code they test. Source: `docs/test-design.md` TD-SEC-02, TD-SEC-19, TD-PICK-36.
- **D-1953** Question (T089 review; SEC-014, SEC-015, SEC-040, D-1950): what do the shared limits cost a real homeowner and Casey, and what happens when a limit's alert cannot be written? Choice: four trade-offs, kept and named. (a) `REQUESTS_ALL` (40 new requests an hour for all numbers together) can refuse real homeowners during a burst of fake ones until the hour ends; kept, because SEC-015 needs the burst blocked and a per-number limit alone cannot stop 100 numbers; the alert tells Casey at once, and the ceiling moves with a decision if real traffic nears it. (b) `REQUESTS_PER_PHONE` now alerts Normal (`Limit::quiet`, the weekly digest), not High: one homeowner over 5 an hour is not a burst, and SEC-015 asks a High alert only for the burst, so Casey's phone is not woken for it; every other limit, the burst (`REQUESTS_ALL`) and the PICK-055 global Verify cap alert High as before, still once per scope and window. (c) A request refused by a wider limit keeps the hits it already put on the narrower keys (her phone, her IP): `core::api::rate_limit_hit` only adds and `intake` may not write `core.rate_limit` itself, so no clean undo exists; checking widest first instead would let one phone's refused requests spend the all-numbers bucket and lock everyone out, which is worse; the cost is at most one hit per refused try on her own keys, gone at the window's end. (d) `alert_once` takes the `<scope>:alerted` marker before writing the alert, so a failed write cannot be followed by a second alert in that window; writing the alert in a transaction held open until the marker answers was tried and starved the pool (each refusal holds two connections; the 20-concurrent test timed out), and the marker cannot be taken back, so the refusal that takes it tries the alert `ALERT_TRIES` (3) times on fresh connections and, if all fail, returns `LimitError::Alert` for the caller to refuse and log. Reason: each is the least harmful choice the increment-only counter allows. Source: T089 fresh-eyes review items 4a, 4b, 4c and 5; `app/intake/src/limits.rs`.
- **D-1954** Question (T089 review; PICK-055, SEC-008, TD-PICK-36): `admit_code_send` did one counter write for an unknown number and three for a known one, so the answer's timing could tell whether a number is on file; how are they made the same? Choice: an unknown number counts against the same per-IP limit, then spends two writes on `CODE_SENDS_UNKNOWN` (`portals.code_sends_unknown`, an Arizona-day limit with an unreachable ceiling, so it never refuses or alerts), one keyed by the nil record ID and one for everyone, in the places the per-number and global counts take for a known number: three upserts either way, on a record row and a shared row alike. A known number refused by its own per-number or global limit still stops early, as an unknown one never does; that difference shows only once the number's 5 sends for the day or the global cap are spent. `tests/security/tests/rate_limits.rs` `td_pick_36_unknown_and_known_numbers_spend_the_same_counter_writes` checks the equal count. Reason: SEC-008 and TD-PICK-36 need identical work and timing for unknown and known numbers. Source: T089 fresh-eyes review item 1.
- **D-1955** Question (T148; BIZ-038, SEC-025, SEC-026, D-333): where are email action links stored, and how is each bound to one person and one object, used once and voided with its member, when T148's only migration is on `quotes`? Choice: in T084's `portals.login_link`: the token is 256 OS-random bits (hex), and the row stores the SHA256 of `action:<kind>:<object>:<token>` with the member, business and the window end as `expires_at`; a token presented for another action or object hashes differently and is refused, and a sign-in link hashes the bare token, so an action token never signs in. `created_at` is set `LINK_LIFE` back (as D-1776's markers), so action links never count toward `LINKS_PER_LIFE`. `run_member_removed` already uses up a removed member's unused rows, and `use_action_link` also re-reads the member's current roles after its one guarded update, in the caller's transaction (roll back on a refused action, so a Quote link is used up only by the submitted quote). Opening a link only reads. Reason: no new table or cross-schema migration; the binding is in the hash, single use and member voiding come from the existing guarded update.
- **D-1956** Question (T148; BIZ-038, BIZ-028, BIZ-033, CALL-011, PICK-043, BIZ-034): which role and what else does each action need? Choice: Quote needs "Cards and quotes" (or the owner); Approve is the owner's alone; every other action needs "Confirm and billing" (or the owner), so a "Cards and quotes" member gets no Hold, Confirm or Pause link and `use_action_link` refuses one. Quote and Hold act through the link alone; Confirm through the link plus a Verify code to that person (T194's `DeviceCodes` when the route is served); Away, Pause, Resume, Busy, Link this phone, Approve and Ask about a charge need a signed-in session (`session_may`). A Hold link is made only when `picks::api::hold_allowed` passes (never on an emergency job, a held pick or an Away-delayed one) and ends with the Confirm window. Reason: the keywords' role rules (BIZ-028, PICK-043, CALL-011 "the owner and a Confirm and billing member can link staff phones") and SEC-004. Fix round: `use_action_link` takes the pick's current facts for a Hold and re-checks `hold_allowed` before the guarded update, so a pick held (or made an emergency or Away-delayed) after the email gets no second hold and the link stays unused; `ActionGrant` keeps its fields private behind `member()` and `business()` and is neither `Clone` nor `Copy` (rust-production R7). SEC-004: a Confirm link opened with no live session asks for a code, so only that page says "We'll send you a code"; a signed-in person's page does not (`does_line(kind, signed_in)`).
- **D-1957** Question (T148; PICK-040, OPS-047, TD-PICK-37, D-491): the quote form needs the PICK-040 facts, "Same as last time" and "minutes this quote took", but `quotes.quote` has no fact columns and T148's migration is named for the minutes. Choice: migration 0143 adds only `quotes.quote.quote_minutes` (1 to 600 or NULL) with `quotes::api::record_quote_minutes`; `portals` owns the form side: `parse_facts` (every fact required, the earliest visit needs a date and a part of day, minutes optional), `prefill` (every fact but the earliest visit from the business's last facts for the job type, empty for a new job type) and the form's "Same as last time" button. Storing the facts on the quote (and reading the last ones per job type) waits for the task that serves the quote form route; until then the caller passes the last facts. The fee lines come from `payments::api::fee_for` and `period_fee_for` (`quotes` keeps no fee code). Reason: the size budget and file ownership; the form rules are testable now. Fix round: a per-visit recurring price gets no fee line (`FeeError::NeedsPeriod`): `payments` takes a per-visit price as `Weekly` only with weekly visits, otherwise converted to monthly by the caller (D-1407), and the form has no visit schedule, so a weekly guess could charge the wrong tier. The form asks for the schedule when the quote form route is served. Deferred to the task that serves the quote form (not built here, size budget): the price field itself (PICK-002 formats, its read-back), the handyman certification box on the same screen as the price (LIC-025, LIC-036) and the $1,000 handyman refusal (LIC-019); `fee_lines` already takes the parsed `Price`. A failed submit shows each summary message again by its field (`QuoteFormFacts::error_for`), and the Busy page keeps a refused value (0, 61) with an "Error: " title, a focused summary and the field's message (`BUSY_DAYS_ERROR`, A11Y-030).
- **D-1958** Question (T148; BIZ-038, BIZ-028, BIZ-032, OPS-036, D-492): which parts are built here and which wait? Choice: built: the links, the pages (rendered, not yet served, like T085's and T195's), the fee lines, the facts, "Ask about a charge" enqueuing `help_request_opened` (business, charge and job IDs only; T151 registers the handler) and its answer (job number, amount, tier, "Why was I charged?" link, the 2-day line with the brand name from `core::api::brand()`), `email_reply` (never a command) and the "Open in browser" email line. - **D-1959** Question (T148; FEE-043, PICK-039): how does the form word a fee whose basis was capped or set by the category? Choice: "If picked, this quote's fee is $<fee> (<how> $<basis>)." with <how> "price", "range midpoint", "your rate times the hours, midpoint" or "4 months of the price", adding ", capped at $<fee>" when the recurring cap set a lower tier than the basis; a diagnostic-visit quote says "(the set fee for a diagnostic visit in this category)"; a tiers quote gives one line per tier, "If the homeowner picks <tier>, this quote's fee is …"; a fee-free job type says "No introduction fee for this job."; an hourly quote with no hours outside a diagnostic-visit category shows no fee (`FeeError::NeedsHours`, FEE-043) and the form asks for hours. Reason: PICK-039's example wording, D-262's basis shown, D-185 per tier. The cold read and copy panel (WORD-028, WORD-029) reworded the action lines, the hourly, capped and tier fee lines, the charge answer ("the introduction fee for a <size> job") and the hints; "Same as last time", the fact names and "Tonight" stay as PICK-040 words them.
- **D-1970** Question (harness fix, November 8, 2026; number given by the overseer, above `main`'s highest D-1959): after a task merges, the runner's start-routine smoke on the new head sometimes outruns `SMOKE_TIMEOUT` (540 s, `runner/github_env.py:76`, exit 124) with few changed paths, the cycle returns `smoke_timeout` and claims nothing (`runner/cycle.py`, `_next_step`), and the chain step of `backup-runner.yml` ("Start the next cycle at once when this one cleared the way", D-500) chains only on `false_red_cleared`, `main_cleared` or a `main_red` that moved a task, so the lane idles until the keeper wakes (20 minutes, D-1451). Should a timeout chain? Measured (`kit/runner_log.jsonl` on `claude/kit-state`): three such timeouts in about 8 hours, at 23:49Z November 7 on ba0b00db, 05:45Z on 9f6ba104 and 07:19Z on 95d2435b, with 15 to 21 changed paths; each retry on the same head passed with 0 changed paths, because "Smoke build cache, save (D-1911)" had kept the partial build; each timeout cost about 20 to 25 minutes of idle lane. Earlier heads (6ea04a3a, 00daffc8) show a second timeout on the same head does happen. Choice: the chain step's `again` snippet also says yes for this job's own `smoke_timeout` row when it is the first timeout on that head: the row's `changed.keys.smoke_runs` (the state's last 20 smoke runs after the cycle) ends with a `timed_out` run, and exactly one `timed_out` run in that list carries its SHA (the same count as `_smoke_timeouts`). A second timeout on the same head falls back to the keeper as before, so the chain starts at most one extra run per commit of `main`, and a new head needs a merge, which is progress. The chain step runs after the save step (both `if: always()`, in file order), so the dispatched run restores the saved entry (`rust-smoke-…-<sha>-` restore key). The dispatch is the existing one with no lane (the gate picks the lane; the lane's concurrency group and the lease keep a second start from doing anything twice), and the keeper armed by the same job is replaced by the newer one the chained run arms (its concurrency group) or re-arms when it sees that run live. Reason: the retry passes every time on a warm cache, so waiting 20 minutes for it is idle time with no information gained; bounding by the timeout count on the head keeps D-500's rule that the chain never spins without progress. Tests: `tests/test_runner_two_lanes.py` (`test_the_chain_retries_a_smoke_timeout_once_per_head`). Owner approval: Casey's standing delegation; harness change with an independent Opus review by the overseer. Source: `.github/workflows/backup-runner.yml` (chain step), `runner/cycle.py` (`_smoke`, `_smoke_timeouts`, `_next_step`), D-500, D-1178, D-1451, D-1911.

- **D-1973** Question (T197; PICK-037, QH-001, D-380): when exactly do the reminders go? Choice: at k times `WindowRules::reminder_minutes` (60, a setting) business minutes after the window's start, for k = 1, 2, ..., while strictly before the window's current end (after any HOLD or grace), so a 4-hour window has 3 and the last is 1 business hour before the end (TD-PICK-31); the list is recomputed from the new end after a HOLD (10:00 pick, HOLD at 12:30: reminders at 11 to 15, the last at 15:00, no Hold line); a time that lands at exactly 8 p.m. (possible because a business-minute sum may end there) waits for 8 a.m.; the last reminder's "<time left>" is the business minutes to the end as "1 hour", "<n> hours" or "<n> minutes"; a reminder is due from its second on (11:00:00, not 10:59:59). Source: `docs/spec/quotes-pick.md:41`.

Choice: (a) `owner_told(confirmed_by, owner)` now compares the person who confirmed with the owner (both opaque person IDs from `businesses`), not the confirming person with the owner's linked phone: BIZ-033 tells the owner "whenever a phone other than the owner's confirms", so the owner's own Confirm never tells the owner, also when the owner has no linked phone (the old `owner_told(member, None)` returned true for any ID, the owner's own included); the test's `owner_told(member, None)` case became `owner_told(member, owner)` (still told) and `owner_told(owner, owner)` (not told), the same rule over the new identity, not a weaker check. (d) `bounce_grace` takes `(now, due)` and refuses at or after `due`, as `hold` does (PICK-035: an ended window is not reopened), tested at 13:59:59, 14:00:00 and 15:00. Two TD-PICK-31/TD-PICK-27 cases need the senders and stay untested until then: "a Confirm stops the rest" of the reminders, and the lapsed business's quote refused on a re-pick (the list already leaves it out, `lapse_plan`). - **D-1986** Question (harness fix, November 8, 2026; number given by the overseer): every release-asset download in `.github/workflows/backup-runner.yml` and `.github/workflows/ci.yml` was a single `curl -sSfL`, so one HTTP 504 from GitHub's release CDN failed the step. Measured: from 08:33Z November 8 every `backup` job failed in "Smoke-test prerequisites (what Ci installs for itself)": the runs at 08:33Z, 08:39Z and 09:09Z on the gitleaks download, the 09:33Z run (gitleaks fine) on the cargo-llvm-cov download (`LLVM_COV_URL`); GitHub's status page showed no incident, so the 504s are intermittent. No cycle could run, so T197, merged, could not be marked DONE and the lane stalled over an hour. `Ci`'s gitleaks, cargo-audit/cargo-deny and Coverage downloads used the same single-shot curl. How should these downloads behave? Choice: (1) every release download in both workflows (gitleaks in both, cargo-audit and cargo-deny and cargo-llvm-cov in `Ci`, cargo-llvm-cov in the backup job) adds `--retry 5 --retry-all-errors --retry-delay 15 --connect-timeout 20`, keeping `-sSfL` and every SHA-256 check as it was; (2) in the backup job's prerequisites step only, the pinned nightly and cargo-llvm-cov are best effort: when the toolchain install, the download after its retries, the SHA-256 check or the extract fails, the step prints `cargo-llvm-cov not installed: <reason>; prehandin coverage will report skipped (D-1986)`, does not add it to `GITHUB_PATH` and goes on. gitleaks stays required there (the secret scan), and `Ci`'s Coverage job and every other `Ci` download stay strict. (3) (follow-up, 09:55Z and 10:02Z `Ci` runs and every backup run since 08:33Z: the gitleaks asset `gitleaks_8.28.0_linux_x64.tar.gz` answered 504 on all 6 tries, so retries alone could not pass) gitleaks gets a verified second source in both workflows, one identical block: when the release download or its SHA-256 check fails (the tarball is extracted only after the check passes), the step builds the same pinned version with the runner image's own `go`: `GOBIN="$RUNNER_TEMP/gitleaks" GOFLAGS=-mod=readonly GOTOOLCHAIN=local GOPROXY=https://proxy.golang.org GOSUMDB=sum.golang.org go install -ldflags "-X=github.com/zricethezav/gitleaks/v8/cmd.Version=${GITLEAKS_VERSION}" github.com/zricethezav/gitleaks/v8@v${GITLEAKS_VERSION}` (the module proxy is not GitHub's release CDN, and the Go checksum database verifies every module it builds; the `-X` flag is the one upstream's `.goreleaser.yml` sets, without which `gitleaks version` prints "version is set by build process"), then requires `go version -m` to show the module at `v${GITLEAKS_VERSION}` with the module hash pinned beside `GITLEAKS_SHA256` as `GITLEAKS_MOD_H1` (`h1:XXeibrt4XbdrYm3FnzXR3uUPs9HbgGduroICjBl6PMw=`, the value sum.golang.org's lookup records for v8.28.0 and a real build's `go version -m` showed; added after the overseer's independent security review, which also asked for `-mod=readonly` and `GOTOOLCHAIN=local`); on either path the binary's `gitleaks version` must contain `GITLEAKS_VERSION`, the step prints which source it used, and with both sources failing the step fails, so gitleaks stays mandatory; nothing turns the checksum database off (no `GONOSUMDB`, `GOINSECURE` or `GOSUMDB=off`), and no `actions/setup-go` is added because `ubuntu-latest` ships Go; with `GOTOOLCHAIN=local` no other toolchain is fetched, so a runner Go older than gitleaks' `go 1.23.8` fails the fallback (and so the step) rather than downloading one. Actions runs these `run:` steps with `bash -e` (no `shell:`, so no pipefail), and the block is written and tested for that. Verified by hand in the builder's sandbox: the release URL answered 504 six times there too, and the fallback built `github.com/zricethezav/gitleaks/v8@v8.28.0`, which reported `8.28.0`. (4) (follow-up, `Ci` run 42470387604 on 40c8f92b: the gitleaks fallback worked there and "Secret scan" passed, then "Prebuilt tools (cargo-audit, cargo-deny) from pinned musl release tarballs (D-693)" failed on the same release 504 after 76 s of retries) that step gets the same design per tool: `AUDIT_VERSION: 0.22.2` and `DENY_VERSION: 0.20.2` sit beside the URLs they match; the release tarball is retried, SHA-256 checked and extracted only after the check; on a failed download or check, `cargo install --locked --root "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools" --version "=<pin>" <crate>` from crates.io (the index checksum verifies the crate, `--locked` builds with the crate's own `Cargo.lock`, the toolchain is the pinned release the earlier "Rust toolchain" step installed) into the same `bin`; either way `<tool> --version` must end in ` <pin>`, the step prints which source it used, `bin` goes on `GITHUB_PATH` as before, and with both sources failing the step fails (no `||` in it). (5) (follow-up, `Ci` run 42471210559 on 5823fdde: the Coverage job's "Measuring toolchain and cargo-llvm-cov 0.9.1" step failed on `LLVM_COV_URL`, 504 on all 6 tries) that step gets the same fallback: `LLVM_COV_VERSION: 0.9.1` (matching the URL's `v0.9.1`) in the Coverage job's env; the tarball is retried, SHA-256 checked and extracted only after the check; otherwise `cargo install --locked --root "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools" --version "=${LLVM_COV_VERSION}" cargo-llvm-cov` from crates.io, built on the pinned stable that `rust-toolchain.toml` selects in the repository (installed by the job's "Rust toolchain" step), not the nightly; into `$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/bin`, never `~/.cargo/bin`, which rust-cache restores, so no cached binary can pass the check; then `cargo-llvm-cov llvm-cov --version` (the form cargo uses; a bare `cargo-llvm-cov --version` errors) must end in ` ${LLVM_COV_VERSION}`; the step prints its source, keeps the same `GITHUB_PATH` line and stays strict. The backup job's best-effort cargo-llvm-cov block is left as it is (no fallback): a crates.io build there would add minutes to every backup job during an outage for a check the gate already reports as skipped. Verified by hand here with curl stubbed to fail: the fallback built `cargo-llvm-cov 0.9.1` with cargo 1.99.0. Reason: retries cover a passing CDN fault at a cost of at most about 75 s of waiting; the backup job's coverage tools only serve the pre-hand-in gate's optional coverage check, which already says skipped without them (`scripts/prehandin.sh:161`–`scripts/prehandin.sh:162`: `if ! command -v cargo-llvm-cov … || [ -z "${DATABASE_URL:-}" ]; then echo "skipped: needs cargo-llvm-cov, the ${NIGHTLY} toolchain and DATABASE_URL (Ci measures it)"; return 0`, documented at `scripts/prehandin.sh:18`–`scripts/prehandin.sh:19`), and `Ci`'s strict Coverage job still judges the floors, so a missing download there must not stop the whole lane. A checksum mismatch is treated the same way in the backup job (nothing unverified is put on the path) and stays fatal in `Ci`. Tests: `tests/test_prehandin.py` (`test_every_release_download_retries_and_only_the_gates_coverage_tools_are_best_effort`, `test_the_backup_jobs_coverage_install_is_skipped_not_fatal`, which runs the step's coverage part under `bash -e` with stub tools; `test_gitleaks_falls_back_to_the_go_module_proxy_and_stays_required`, `test_the_gitleaks_install_runs_under_actions_bash_e`, which runs both workflows' gitleaks block under `bash -e` with stub curl, sha256sum, tar and go: release fine, download failed, checksum failed, both sources failed, wrong version reported, wrong module version built, wrong module hash; `test_cargo_audit_and_deny_fall_back_to_crates_io_and_stay_required`, `test_the_prebuilt_tools_install_runs_under_actions_bash_e`, which runs the Prebuilt tools step under `bash -e` with stub curl, sha256sum, tar and cargo: releases fine, download failed, checksum failed, both sources failed, wrong version reported twice; `test_cargo_llvm_cov_falls_back_to_crates_io_and_coverage_stays_strict`, `test_the_measuring_tool_install_runs_under_actions_bash_e`, the same six cases for the Coverage step). Owner approval: Casey's standing delegation; harness change for an independent Opus review by the overseer.
