- **D-2303** Question (T333, T334, sixth audit U-05; FEE-026, FEE-028, FEE-053; D-1753; new TD-FEE-59): a refund Stripe reports `succeeded` is booked at the charged amount (`succeeded` and `append`, `app/payments/src/refunds.rs:376`, `:474`; `own_refund`, `app/payments/src/reconcile.rs:357`) although `Refund` carries the reported amount and currency (`app/payments/src/refund_stripe.rs:53`), and no spec line says refunds are full. A missing amount is re-read once with `fetch_refund`; still missing, it is booked at the charged amount (the request was full) with the same unconfirmed alert, and its notice goes. The overseer's judgement under Casey's standing "final say" (listed in `docs/for-casey-review.md`): new harness task T336, after T325, queues one `messaging.inbound_retry` task per failed inbox row (3 tries: 5 minutes, 30 minutes, 2 hours; the last failure leaves T325's alert); the retry reads the body back through a new `SmsBodyRead::fetch_message_body(sid)` adapter read, scrubs it with the same reader, runs the route's steps once in the same order (opt-out and HELP first), never stores or logs it (D-801), and closes on `Gone` (redacted or unknown). Permanent classes are not retried: `BadWebhook`, a suppressed sender and a known refusal (`Halt::Ends`). Three rules (review fix round): opt-out and HELP always run; if a newer inbox row from the same sender has already been processed the retry does only that and closes, T325's alert staying as the record; anything it sends goes through the normal outbound path under quiet hours (QH-001), never as an immediate reply outside them. Before building, T336 states how a `Halt::Failed` delivery commits the steps that ran before the failure and makes each step safe to repeat (keyed once per inbox row or MessageSid) or resumes after the last committed one; a step that cannot be made safe stops the task for a report. Privacy and security: the overseer runs an independent review when T336 hands in. Reason: a homeowner's text that failed for a transient reason should be handled without asking her to write again, and Twilio already holds it for 31 days. Source: `app/messaging/src/purge.rs:3`, `app/server/src/inbound_text.rs:174`.

- **D-2269** Question (T284, D-1868, TD-SEC-41): how does the route table say what is served and how does the test tell a served route from an absent one without a database? Choice: `docs/architecture.md` section 13 is one row per method and path, `| Method | Path | Module | Wired |`, `Wired` `yes` or the queued task's ID, `{name}` for a path parameter, `Module` the crate that owns the handler or page; the test-control routes (`/__test/...`, feature-only, SEC-035) are not listed. `app/server/tests/route_wiring.rs` compiles the section in with `include_str!`, builds the router as `main` does (`TestControl::from_settings`, `webhooks`, `voice_hooks`, `pick_code_keys`, `release_sink::stripe_webhook`, every optional part asserted `Some`, fake dev settings over `PgPoolOptions::connect_lazy`) and probes each row with the extension method `PROBE` and same-origin `Host`, `Origin` and `Sec-Fetch-Site` headers: a matched path answers 405 with an `Allow` header, the fallback 404, so a row reaches its route only on 405 with its own method in `Allow`. No handler runs, so no database, signature or connect info is needed, but the route's layers (the cross-site refusal, `no_store`, `noindex`, the request log, any session check) do run before the 405, so a route layer must let a same-origin method the route does not take through to the 405; a task row therefore counts as reached on any answer other than the fallback 404 or a 405 whose `Allow` lacks its method, so a wired route whose layer answers 4xx still fails its row that still names a task. Removing any one `.merge(...)` of `quote_page`, `pick_flow`, `feedback`, `twilio`, `voice` or `stripe` fails the test naming each of that router's rows (run in T284's hand-in, not committed). Reason: a method no route takes reaches the method router of a matched path and nothing else, and `Allow` also checks the row's method, not only its path. Source: `docs/architecture.md` section 13, `app/server/tests/route_wiring.rs`, `app/server/src/lib.rs` `build_router`, `app/server/src/main.rs`. Kind: design.

- **D-2347** Question (T345, T121, pentest PT-01; SEC-045; D-480; TD-SEC-24): 15 external `uses:` lines are pinned to mutable tags (`actions/checkout@v4` in seven workflows, `setup-python@v5`, `cache@v4`, `cache/restore@v4`, `cache/save@v4`, `upload-artifact@v4`, and `anthropics/claude-code-action@v1` on the backup runner's job that holds the Claude OAuth token, the conditional push token and write permissions), no decision allows a tag, and nothing checks any workflow but `ci.yml`. - **D-2348** Question (T346, T307, pentest PT-03 and the PT-02 gap beyond the report; SEC-055 new, SEC-008, PRIV-031; D-1837, D-1934; TD-SEC-60): one Verify service serves every purpose and `check_code(to, code)` carries no purpose (`app/adapters/src/verify.rs:50`), so `confirm_request` acts on any of her open requests, up to 30 days old, after any passing code for her phone, the sign-in code included (`app/portals/src/data_download.rs:222`); homeowner sign-in keeps no local challenge; neither path has an app-side try cap. Choice: new T346 adds `portals.code_challenge` (purpose, subject, sent at, used at, tries) for homeowner sign-in and the copy and delete requests. The rule (amended in the PR #407 review): a challenge lives as long as the code (10 minutes from its first send); a send while an unused challenge of that purpose and subject is alive reuses it and does not reset its tries, because Twilio keeps one pending code per number for its life, so the cap is truly 5 per code; a send after expiry or use opens a new one. A check is refused before Verify unless the newest unused, unexpired challenge of that purpose and subject exists; the try is reserved against it atomically before the Verify call, capped by the same `CODE_TRIES` (5) as T272; a right code uses the challenge with a conditional update (`used_at IS NULL`) in the transaction of the action it confirms, which rolls back when no row changed, so two right checks act once; no pooled connection, transaction or reservation is held across the Verify await (D-2349). Accepted residual: someone who knows her number can spend the 5 tries on her open sign-in challenge and lock her sign-in for the rest of the code's life, as Twilio's own check limit already allows today; in front of it stand the per-IP limits `portals.code_tries_per_ip` (20 an hour) and `portals.code_sends_per_ip` (10 an hour) and the per-number `portals.code_sends_per_number` (5 a day), through `admit_code_try` and `admit_code_send` (D-1951, `app/portals/src/limits.rs:26`). A new `resend_request_code` lets her get a fresh code for an open request (T307 serves it), because the request stays open 30 days. Picks' codes and business sign-in keep their own rows. No separate Verify Service for delete confirmation now: the local purpose-bound challenge closes the hole without a Twilio account step; it is listed for Casey as an option he may choose later. Because Twilio Verify keys a pending code by number, a code sent for one purpose while another purpose's challenge is also open can still satisfy both; each action still needs its own open challenge, made only by its own send. New spec line SEC-055 states the rule. Reason: a code must confirm only the action it was sent for. Source: `app/adapters/src/verify.rs:86`, `app/portals/src/data_download.rs:210`, `app/portals/src/homeowner_portal.rs:164`, `stand_ins/twilio.py:286`.
- **D-2349** Question (T272, pentest PT-04 and PT-03's business half; SEC-004, SEC-018; D-1776, D-1837; TD-SEC-38): `send_once` holds a transaction across the Verify send (`app/portals/src/business_auth.rs:630`), so a slow vendor holds database connections, and `check_once` (:664) never requires that a code was sent for its link. Choice: this sets aside only D-1776's held transaction (its one-send-per-link rule stands). T272's migration also adds `portals.code_send` (link, reserved at, outcome pending, sent or failed): a press reserves the link's one send in a short committed transaction (a new row, a failed one, or a pending one older than the adapter's 15-second timeout plus a minute, left by a crash), calls Verify with no transaction open, then records sent or failed; it replaces the `code-sent:<link>` marker row. Duplicate-send policy: one send per link, except that a press after a crash left a reservation pending may send once more. `check_once` refuses a link with no sent code before any try or Verify call. PT-02 itself stays T272's reserve-then-check, unchanged. Availability (amended in the PR #407 review): no pooled connection is held across a Verify call either. T272's `device_step`, `send_once` and `check_once` take the handler's `&PgPool` and acquire a connection per short database step; T346's homeowner sign-in and data-request functions take `&PgPool` in place of `&mut PgConnection` the same way, and T307's routes pass the pool. Each task tests that, with a fake Verify that hangs, 30 concurrent sends and checks leave a pool of 5 connections able to serve another request (the matrix's AVAIL-01; TD-SEC-38, TD-SEC-60). T242 only confirms each site closed on `main`. Reason: no vendor call inside a database transaction, and a code check needs its own sent challenge. Source: `app/portals/src/business_auth.rs:630`, `app/portals/src/business_auth.rs:664`, `app/adapters/src/base.rs:207`.

- **D-2351** Question (T285, D-1869): the goal puts the owned-files check "in `_mark_done`", whose callers (`_merged`, `_resolve_empty`) have no `Env`, and the fake `Env` of the existing drills has no way to read a file at a commit; where does the check sit and how does it read git? Choice: `_resolve_one` runs `mark_owned_gap` right after `_merged`, which acts only on an entry `_merged` made DONE (so a cleanup task's merge held BLOCKED for its stage proof, an empty hand-in and FIX-MAIN are not checked), and the reads are two optional `Env` methods, `text_at(sha, path)` and `files_at(sha, path)` (`git cat-file -e`, `git show`, `git ls-tree -r --name-only` in `GitHubEnv`), each raising when git cannot read the commit; an `Env` without them, like the drills' `FakeEnv`, skips the check, so every existing runner test runs unchanged. A problem line names the task and the path or route but not the commit, so the per-cycle re-check against a moving `main` head rewrites the mark only when what is missing changes. A git error at the close sets no mark and writes no outbox item (no evidence, D-1350). Reason: the same behaviour as the goal's wording without widening `_mark_done`'s signature across its callers, and no new duty on test doubles the task does not own. Source: `kit/prompts/T285.md` goal; `runner/cycle.py` `_resolve_one`, `_merged`, `_mark_done`. Kind: design.

- **D-2357** Question (T286, D-1870, D-2208): where do the time limit and the panic layer sit, what do their answers carry, and how does TD-SEC-42's Confirm case show the attempt stays `sent` when TD-SEC-10 forbids SQL outside the query macros and any module schema in `server`'s tests? Choice: innermost first, `catch_panic`, then `limit_request` (a `from_fn_with_state` middleware over `tokio::time::timeout`, not `tower-http`'s `TimeoutLayer`, whose answer is a bare status), then the existing request-log, trace, request-ID and security-headers layers, so the 503 and 500 are logged with their status and carry the request ID and SEC-012 headers; both answers have `Cache-Control: no-store` and an empty body, so no customer copy and no panic text (the payload is dropped unread; one warn or error line names no value). The Confirm case seeds through `payments::api::ensure_customer` and `fix_fee_at_pick` only, cuts the press with the paused clock once the fake Stripe confirm is in flight, and shows `sent` by behaviour: the next press asks Stripe first, gets `Pending` and sends no confirm; only after Stripe says `requires_payment_method` does try 2 confirm. A blank `ASKHAVA_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_SECS` counts as unset (60), as for every key the settings parser reads. - **D-2361** Question (T288, D-1872; FEE-029, FEE-030, FEE-051): when is a charge the reconcile read "settled", and what does `payments.reconcile_open` store? Choice: a charge is open when its writes failed (`write-failed`), the refund it is owed was refused, failed or canceled (`refund-refused`), is pending at Stripe or in flight in T066 (`refund-pending`), its own ledger `charge` and `refund` differ from Stripe's (`mismatch`), or, on a retry, Stripe could not be read or answered a malformed charge (`stripe-unreadable`) or has no such charge (`not-found`); anything else is settled, including a charge T066 blocks as disputed and one refunded or disputed at Stripe since it was stored. The per-charge mismatch compares charges and refunds only: a dispute's ledger entry is the webhook's `record_dispute`, and the run-wide FEE-030 match (`payments.ledger_mismatch`) still compares disputes. The row keeps the IDs and amounts the run first read (charge, PaymentIntent, metadata pick, amount, refunded, processing fee, balance transaction), so a retry rebuilds the charge from them and takes only the refunded amount and dispute from Stripe's fresh read. A row of a charge that settled and later fails again (it can, while still in the 7-day list) is reopened with one more try and keeps its `first_seen` and `alerted_at`, since `first_seen` is not an updatable column. Reason: the goal's four causes, and a dispute cannot be closed by the reconcile. Source: `kit/prompts/T288.md` goal (2); `app/payments/src/reconcile.rs` `OpenWhy`. Kind: design.
- **D-2362** Question (T288, D-1872): how does a retry read a charge's current refund and dispute state when `ReconcileStripe` has only `list_charges`, and every TD-FEE-16 and `reconcile.rs` case must pass unchanged with its fake? Choice: a provided trait method `ReconcileStripe::fetch_charge(id) -> Option<StripeCharge>` whose default body searches `list_charges(Timestamp::MIN)`, so the existing fakes (`reconcile.rs`, `refund_lifecycle.rs`, `ledger_1000_jobs.rs`) compile and behave as before; T132's Stripe client must override it with Stripe's retrieve-a-charge call (the event list keeps 30 days only). Each stored row not in the night's list is retried once per run; a listed one is planned with the list. Reason: no test file another task owns changes; the real read is T132's. Source: `app/payments/src/reconcile.rs` `ReconcileStripe`; `docs/brains/payments-stripe.md` section 6. Kind: design.
- **D-2363** Question (T288, D-1872; OPS-004, OPS-029): which alert does a row open 7 days raise, and what does the report add? Choice: one High `payments.reconcile_open` alert per row, subject kind `payments.reconcile_open` and the row's ID (no amount, pick or Stripe ID), raised by `alert_open` in the transaction whose `UPDATE ... SET alerted_at ... WHERE alerted_at IS NULL ... RETURNING id` picks the rows (`first_seen` at or before now less `OPEN_ALERT_AFTER`, 7 days), so a later run never raises it again; which High alerts push to Casey's phone stays `ops`' OPS-029 rule. `ReconcileReport` gains `retried` (stored rows retried this run) and `open` (rows still unsettled at the end, counted in that transaction). The migration grants the app role `UPDATE` of `last_tried`, `tries`, `last_code`, `alerted_at` and `settled_at` only and revokes `DELETE` and `TRUNCATE`. Reason: the goal's step (3), and P5's narrow grants. Source: `kit/prompts/T288.md` goal (1) and (3); `migrations/0173_payments_reconcile_open.sql`. Kind: design.
- **D-2364** Question (T288 review, D-1872, D-2361; FEE-029, OPS-004): a stored row retried every night re-raised `payments.reconcile_charge_failed` or `payments.refund_failed` on each retry with no end (`ops`' `raise_alert` has no dedupe), against D-1872's one High alert; and T066's `request_refund` answers `RefundOutcome::Failed` both for a refused refund and for one Stripe holds `pending` (D-2067), so the row stored `refund-refused` for a pending refund. Choice: a retry of a stored row (one not in the night's 7-day list) raises neither per-charge alert; a listed charge keeps T067's alert each night it is listed (at most 8 nights, `reconcile.rs` unchanged), and the one `payments.reconcile_open` alert after 7 days covers the row from then on. On T066's `Failed` the run reads the pick's `refund_state`: `InFlight` is stored `refund-pending`, anything else `refund-refused`; `ReconcileReport::refund_failed` still counts it, as before, so every `reconcile.rs` case passes unchanged. Reason: one alert per stuck row past the window; the stored code says what Stripe holds. Source: `app/payments/src/reconcile.rs` `settle`, `own_refund`, `failed_why`; `tests/integration/tests/reconcile_open.rs`. Kind: design.
- **D-2366** Question (T289, D-1873; JOB-002, TD-JOB-15): how does `a_refused_or_stale_move_changes_nothing` count its one ERROR event the same way however the crate's tests are scheduled? - **D-2407** Question (plan change, November 10, 2026; owner ruling; numbered under the interim rule of D-1144 because this builder session does not write `claude/kit-state`: `next_decision` read 2397 on `claude/kit-state`, main's highest D-2389 + 1 = 2390, no open `claude/` plan PR, so max(2397, 2390) + 10 = 2407, re-read before committing; LIC-023, LIC-019, LIC-025; D-027, D-081, D-154; the seventh audit's note N7-D1, D-2329): should the handyman split-job check stay? Today LIC-023 blocks a handyman's quote when the same business has another handyman job at the same address within 30 days and the two share a job type or together reach $1,000 (`app/licensing/src/handyman.rs:227`), checked pairwise. Casey, November 10, 2026, about 12:15Z, in chat with the overseer: "I only care about individual jobs being under the 1000 mark" and "I dont want the 30 day rule". Choice: an owner ruling, logged under the decide-and-log rule (`BUILD_BRIEF.md:539`) against the changes file's "no job splitting" and its split-job check (`sources/01_spec/Changes_Since_v9.3_AUTHORITATIVE.md:41`, `sources/01_spec/Changes_Since_v9.3_AUTHORITATIVE.md:208`, `sources/01_spec/Changes_Since_v9.3_AUTHORITATIVE.md:241`), which stay unedited as sources: there is no split-job check. A handyman job is judged only by its own price under LIC-019's limit ($1,000.00 or more, top of any range, refused; $999.99 accepted), and no other job of the same business at the same address, at any time, blocks or changes a quote. This sets aside D-027 and D-154 entirely (both now marked superseded by D-2407 in `kit/superseded_decisions.json`, amended in the PR #416 review) and D-081's overlapping-scope half (its certification box stands; D-081 is left unmarked because only part of it goes). Kept: the handyman's certification on every quote that it is the full-job price under $1,000 with no permit (LIC-025, LIC-036), the card line (LIC-024), the gas, smoke-alarm, sprinkler and permit blocks, and the paid-pilot terms' "A project is never split up to fit under the limit", which is the business's own promise under the statute, not a platform check. Changed now: LIC-023 restates the rule; TD-LIC-10 tests it; `BUILD_BRIEF.md:459` and `docs/constitution.md:131` name it; new T347 removes the code (D-2408). Legal note, recorded as Casey's informed choice: the overseer told him that Arizona's handyman exemption (A.R.S. 32-1121(A)(14)) is strict about a project split to stay under the limit, the exemption covering one project "not part of a larger operation or split to evade" (`docs/brains/legal-terms-privacy.md:28`), and suggested a word with his lawyer; he decided anyway. The trade expert briefs' statute summaries ("is not part of a larger or split job") stay, because they describe the law. Reason: Casey's ruling; it answers N7-D1. Source: Casey's chat of November 10, 2026 (relayed by the overseer), `docs/spec/licensing.md:27`, `app/licensing/src/handyman.rs:227`.
- **D-2408** Question (T347; LIC-023, LIC-019; D-2407; TD-LIC-10, TD-LIC-08): who removes the split-job check and its tests? Choice: new harness task T347 (it deletes and edits DONE tasks' tests, so it is a harness task with an Opus review, amended in the PR #416 review) removes `split_job`, `HandymanJob`, `SPLIT_JOB_WINDOW_DAYS` and `QuoteRefusal::SplitJob` from `app/licensing/src/handyman.rs` and their exports from `app/licensing/src/api.rs`, and the doc lines naming them (`handyman.rs`, `api.rs`, `app/licensing/src/rules.rs:7`); no production code calls `split_job` (only tests do), the quote form's refusal line matches `Bounce::Handyman(_)` (`app/quotes/src/intake.rs:298`, unchanged), and no table, migration or setting holds state for the rule, so nothing else is removed. Tests: `split_job_check_window_and_totals` (`app/licensing/src/tests/handyman.rs:270`) and the property `split_job_blocks_near_jobs_reaching_the_limit` (`app/licensing/src/tests/prop_handyman_never_gas.rs:125`) are removed, and `Bounce::Handyman(QuoteRefusal::SplitJob)` leaves `app/quotes/src/tests/quote_bounce.rs:95`'s list of every bounce. Removing a test is allowed here only because the spec changed and the change is logged (D-2407, `BUILD_BRIEF.md:69`); it is not a weakened test. In their place TD-LIC-10 tests the new rule: two handyman jobs of one business at one address on the same day, sharing a job type, $600 and $500, are each accepted by `check_quote`, and the single-job edges stay ($999.99 accepted, $1,000.00 refused, TD-LIC-08's existing tests kept unchanged). T347 takes over files of DONE tasks T034, T035 and T046; no queued task owns any of them, and no queued task's goal builds on the split rule. TD-FEE-09 (a second handyman job at one address is a free repeat) still holds and is unchanged. Reason: the rule is gone, so its code and tests go. Source: `app/licensing/src/handyman.rs:220`, `app/licensing/src/tests/handyman.rs:270`, `app/licensing/src/tests/prop_handyman_never_gas.rs:125`, `app/quotes/src/tests/quote_bounce.rs:95`.
- **D-2409** Question (T199; BIZ-046, CALL-017, D-344, D-359, D-491): where does the "Ask Hava homeowner calls" card come from and how does it stay current? Choice: `portals::api::contact_card` fills `app/portals/templates/contact_card.vcf` (vCard 3.0, CRLF, values escaped per RFC 6350; a plain-text file with `{name}`, `{numbers}` and `{note}` slots read by `include_str!`, since an Askama template would need its escaping turned off, which SEC-011's check refuses) from the `adapters::api::MaskedPool` numbers it is given, so the card at `CONTACT_CARD_ROUTE` (`/b/contact-card.vcf`) and the portal home's list are rebuilt from the pool on every load and an added pool number shows at once; the card's name and line come from `core::api::brand()` (`contact_card_name`, `contact_card_note`). The sign-up done screen offers the download through Askama path calls in `business_signup.html` (`crate::business_portal::contact_card_note()`), shown when the title is the done screen's, because `business_signup.rs` is not this task's file. Reason: one source for the numbers, no stored copy to go stale; brand as data (D-1932). Source: `kit/prompts/T199.md:10`, `docs/spec/businesses.md:50`.
- **D-2410** Question (T199; SEC-027, SEC-038, D-333, D-478): how is "This inbox is shared" kept and guarded? Choice: `migrations/0148_portals_shared_inbox.sql` adds `portals.shared_inbox` (member, business, `shared`, `changed_at`; app role SELECT, INSERT and UPDATE of the two changing columns, no DELETE); `business_portal::set_inbox_shared` refuses to turn it on unless the composition's `CodeTo` for that person is a phone (`NeedsTextPhone`), then calls `require_step_up` with the new `SensitiveChange::SharedInbox` for both on and off (`NeedsCode`, logged as `authz_denied`), then upserts; `inbox_shared` reads it (false with no row). `action_links::fresh_code_needed(kind, signed_in, shared)` states the rule for T232: Confirm needs a fresh code without a session or while shared; Quote, Hold and session actions never do. The portal home shows the state and a one-button form posting to `SHARED_INBOX_ROUTE` (not served yet, D-1728). Reason: SEC-027's switch with SEC-038's fresh code; an email code would land in the shared inbox. Source: `docs/spec/security.md:31`.

- **D-2412** Question (T199; SEC-026, OPS-037, D-347, D-1992): how does the quote form record its first opening without a scanner using up the link? Choice: `business_actions::open_quote_form(db, (job, token), notice, now)` is the form's `GET`: `open_action_link` (reads only) and then, for the notice the link came in, `messaging::api::record_first_open` (once; a later open changes nothing); a link that would not work stamps nothing. The notice row's ID reaches the route with the link when the senders log notices (D-1992); `None` stamps nothing. - **D-2429** Question (plan change, November 10, 2026; numbered under the interim rule of D-1144 because this builder session does not write `claude/kit-state`: `next_decision` read 2419 on `claude/kit-state`, main's highest D-2413 + 1 = 2414, no open `claude/` plan PR, so max(2419, 2414) + 10 = 2429, re-read before committing; T231 attempt 1, 15:29Z to 15:58Z, returned to QUEUED; TD-SEC-01, TD-TXT-31; SEC-019, SEC-048; D-1945, D-736, D-2128): T231 serves the check-in answer page at the new route `/c/{token}/{answer}`, but T088's authorization matrix (`tests/security/tests/auth_matrix.rs`, DONE, protected) classifies every route through `door`, which panics on a path it does not name (`:107`, "a path no door names fails the run"), so its three tests that call `door` (`td_sec_01_route_table_is_generated_and_every_path_has_a_door`, `td_sec_01_every_route_by_every_actor`, `sec_048_every_refusal_is_a_security_event`) fail, and T231 owns no part of it. Choice: T231 becomes a harness task that also owns the matrix, for exactly its extension: a `Door::Link` arm for `/c/{token}`, the check-in router merged into the matrix's test app, `probe_link` filling `{answer}` with a valid answer code, a CSRF-only `POST` body for `/c/` paths, and `sec_048`'s target filling `{answer}` the same way (amended in the PR #420 review; T231 also adds the two `/c/{token}/{answer}` rows to `docs/architecture.md` section 13 as `yes`, for `route_wiring.rs`); the route meets the same link-door checks as `/q` and `/f` and the same SEC-048 refusal events, and nothing in the matrix is removed or loosened (coverage, never an exemption). A test crate may not depend on `askhava-server` (D-736), so the matrix cannot merge a router defined in `app/server/src/checkin.rs`; the check-in router is built in `portals` and exported as `portals::api::checkin_routes`, as `feedback_routes` is, and `app/server/src/checkin.rs` merges it (this refines how D-2128's serving is split, not what is served). One task rather than a separate harness task first: the matrix extension needs the router T231 builds, so it cannot land before T231, and a combined task lets the runner's next attempt pass in one pull request. The attempt-1 note's "D-2418" is a number the runner allocated to that attempt (kit-state `decision_ids` 2414 to 2418), on a branch that was not pushed; it is not on `main`, and the retry logs its own. Reason: the matrix exists so a new route cannot go untested; the fix is to test it. Source: `tests/security/tests/auth_matrix.rs:107`, `tests/security/tests/auth_matrix.rs:326`, `tests/security/tests/auth_matrix.rs:604`, `tests/security/tests/control_router_absent.rs:11`.
- **D-2440** Question (plan change, November 10, 2026; numbered under the interim rule of D-1144 because this builder session does not write `claude/kit-state`: `next_decision` read 2419 on `claude/kit-state`, main's highest D-2429 + 1 = 2430, no open `claude/` plan PR, so max(2419, 2430) + 10 = 2440, re-read before committing; T348 new; T106, T201, T221, T261, T300, T301, T306, T307, T304, T305, T310, T309, T103; SEC-019, SEC-048, SEC-034, SEC-026; D-1945, D-736, D-2429; new TD-SEC-61): T231's first attempt showed that T088's authorization matrix fails any route it cannot classify (`tests/security/tests/auth_matrix.rs:107`) and any served `/h` or `/b` route (`:527` to `:531`, probed only through the guard function "since those routes are not served yet"), and thirteen queued serving tasks would hit the same wall with no matrix ownership: no door names `/healthz`, `/help`, the legal pages, the web chat or the owner pages, `/b/a/` action links fall under the business door, and every served `/b` or `/h` page fails. Choice: one new harness task, T348, ordered after T231 (the other owner of the matrix) and before every serving task, extends the matrix: a `Public` door (`/healthz`, `/help` and below, the five legal pages, and any route the `site` module serves), an `ActionLink` door (`/b/a/`, T148's signed links), and an `Owner` door (`/owner` and below except sign-in); the served-realm failure becomes a demand that every served path of the five doors has a `yes` row in `docs/architecture.md` section 13, and the new `app/server/tests/door_matrix.rs` probes every such row over HTTP through `server::build_router` with the six actors, because a test crate may not depend on `askhava-server` (D-736). Each door's checks come from the spec and the serving tasks' own goals, not invented: homeowner pages admit only their homeowner and never show the other's job (SEC-008, SEC-019); business pages admit only their business, another business's pick or complaint being the one not-found answer (SEC-004, D-1726); owner pages admit only the owner (SEC-005, SEC-006; the owner tasks' "4xx with a link to `/owner/sign-in`"); action links open only for the minted kind, object and member and a `GET` changes nothing (SEC-026, D-1955); public pages need no session and show no personal data; every realm, owner and action-link response is `no_store` (SEC-034); every refused `POST` is a 403 and one `csrf_rejected` event (SEC-048). Step-up for owner changes (SEC-043) stays with `owner_auth.rs` and the owner tasks' own route tests; the probe checks only who reaches each page, so the owner fixture has no fresh step-up and a step-up challenge counts as admitted. Amended in the PR #421 review: an admitted `GET` is a 200 on the actor's own record and an admitted `POST` (CSRF field only) is anything but the door's refusal or a 5xx; the probe's router uses fake vendor settings as `route_wiring.rs:238` does, so nothing reaches a vendor; planted correct and leaking routes per door on a test-local router prove the judging code; and one shared path-to-door list (`tests/security/door_cases.txt`) is asserted by both files so their prefix rules cannot drift. Declared routes with no row and no owner (`/b/contact-card.vcf`, `/b/shared-inbox`) are risk R-38. Path parameters the probe fills: `{pick}`, `{complaint}`, `{kind}`, `{object}`, `{token}`; a new one fails naming it, and the task that adds it gets the fill by plan change, so no serving task owns the matrix now. Each serving task depends on T348 and its goal says its routes pass the doors unchanged; T304, T305, T310, T309 and T103 also add their section 13 rows (owner pages under `/owner/`, the help forms under `/b/` and `/help`, the web chat as `site` rows), which they lacked. Already passing and unchanged: T280 and T302 (sign-in and `/b/signup`), T303 (`/owner/sign-in`), T308 (`/q/{token}/close`), T271 (a webhook), and T231 (its own `/c` link door). Nothing in the matrix is exempted, loosened or removed. Reason: SEC-019 wants every route tested; the doors must exist before the routes do. Source: `tests/security/tests/auth_matrix.rs:107`, `tests/security/tests/auth_matrix.rs:527`, `tests/security/tests/control_router_absent.rs:11`, `app/server/tests/route_wiring.rs:4`.
- **D-2414** Question (T231; TXT-034, SEC-026, SEC-037, D-493, D-2128): what does the emailed check-in carry and how does a button's link name the job and the answer? Choice: `messaging::api` (`app/messaging/src/checkin_email.rs`) renders the day-3 and day-14 check-in in the SEC-028 layout (English and draft Spanish) with one link-styled button per answer to `https://<domain>/c/<token>/<day>-<answer>`; the token is the job's quote-page link token (`jobs::api::quote_token::issue`, so the page reuses PICK-011's 30-day life and SEC-037's 404s), issued by the caller in the transaction that stores the email (`queue_check_in_email`, one `email.send` row per contact, job number and day), never in a payload or a log; the code is `<day>-<answer>` (`check_in_code`, `parse_check_in_code`), the same constants the page reads, so the two cannot drift. `GET /c/{token}/{answer}` (`portals::api::checkin_routes`, served by `app/server/src/checkin.rs`) shows the answer and changes nothing; only its `POST` with the pre-session CSRF token records it; `no_store` is the router's outermost layer, so a cross-site or CSRF refusal is `no-store` too (TD-TXT-31 asks it of every response).
- **D-2415** Question (T231; TXT-034, JOB-015, JOB-016, D-071, D-222): the goal asks for one button per answer, but a PROBLEM answer goes through `jobs::api::answer_check_in` with the inbound text row it came in (`Inbound`), whose alert names that row so the digest can show her words; a button has no words and no row. Choice: PROBLEM gets no button. The email's last line asks her to reply to the email and say what went wrong, which reaches the help inbox with her words (CON-035's email path); DONE, ONGOING, LATER, NO and OTHER each get a button (`CHECK_IN_ANSWERS`), and `parse_check_in_code` refuses `problem`, so a typed `/c/<token>/3-problem` is a 404. The page passes an `Inbound` with the nil row only because the signature needs one; it is read only for PROBLEM, which the page never sends.
- **D-2416** Question (T231; JOB-015, D-143): `answer_check_in` needs the homeowner's contact choice (a day-3 NO under email contact returns the job to quotes with a no-show, under call contact closes it), but no module stores that choice yet. Choice: the page passes `Contact::Call` (a NO closes the job, never reopens it to quotes) and the system actor (the link names no person), until the pick's contact choice is stored; the task that stores it changes this one argument. LATER is recorded as nothing moving (the day-14 check-in asks again); a job no longer Connected records nothing and shows the closed line, so a second POST records nothing.

- **D-2418** Question (T231; TD-SEC-01, SEC-019, SEC-048, D-736, D-2429): how is `/c/{token}/{answer}` held to the authorization matrix? Choice: `tests/security/tests/auth_matrix.rs` only adds: `/c/{token}` joins `/q/{token}` and `/f/{token}` in the `Door::Link` arm; `world` merges `portals::api::checkin_routes(pool, clock)` as `build_router` merges it through `server::checkin::routes`; `probe_link` and `sec_048`'s target fill `{answer}` with `3-done` and use the quote-page link token the check-in email carries for the job (the token `done_job` issues); `send` posts only the CSRF field to a `/c/` path (the page's `ButtonForm` refuses unknown fields); the table check names `/c/{token}/{answer}` as served on `get` and `post`. The holder of a Done job's token gets the closed line naming her own request (200), everyone else the bare 404 for the unissued token, and every cross-site or wrong-token POST a 403 with one `csrf_rejected` event naming the route template (the `/c` handler's `CsrfForm` runs before it reads the link or the answer). `docs/architecture.md` section 13 lists `GET` and `POST /c/{token}/{answer}` as `yes` (TD-SEC-41).
- **D-2462** Question (plan change, November 10, 2026; numbered under the interim rule of D-1144 because this builder session does not write `claude/kit-state`: `next_decision` read 2419 on `claude/kit-state`, main's highest D-2440 + 1 = 2441, open plan PR #422's highest D-2451 + 1 = 2452, so max(2419, 2441, 2452) + 10 = 2462, re-read before committing; `kit/runner.json`; D-646, D-1128, D-1189, D-891, D-620, D-630): Casey, in chat about 17:00Z on November 10, 2026: "Can we go to a two-lane approach and have each task briefly reviewed to see what the lowest level agent can successfully complete it is, and have that agent do it before it's checked?" Should the runner work two tasks at once again? Choice: `kit/runner.json` `lanes` 1 → 2, as D-646 did and as `BUILD_BRIEF.md:209` allows only through a logged plan change; this sets aside only D-1128's lanes 2 → 1. D-1128's reasons are answered: its spend line, which one lane paced exactly, was removed by D-1189 (the pacer now claims whenever a task fits the five-hour and week budgets); the update-merge conflicts that cost T024, T028 and T034 attempts were pure insertions in shared files, which `runner/update_merge.py` now resolves without an attempt (D-891); the stage-2 chain that made a second lane idle is long past (147 tasks queued, most of stage 4 parallel). The runner's two-lane machinery is unchanged and current: one lease per lane, no two tasks in flight owning one file or in different stages, a stage's cleanup alone, nothing claimed on a lane while its task is MERGE_PENDING (D-620), FIX-MAIN's reserved lane (D-630), and the automatic fall back to one lane after two harness-type strikes in a row (`lanes_fallback` is unset on `claude/kit-state`). Remaining risks, accepted: a conflict that is not a pure insertion (two edits to the same lines of `Cargo.toml`, or two migrations racing for the next number, which V9 orders but a branch made before the other merged can still collide) costs that task an attempt; and two lanes use the five-hour window about twice as fast, so the pacer holds more often (the week's ~97% stop and the Fable window from Thursday November 12 17:00Z, D-2225, are unchanged). Rollback: the same one-line change back to 1; tasks in flight finish normally. `BUILD_BRIEF.md:209` and `:224` already describe both settings and are unchanged; `docs/handoff/2026-11-10-early.md` instruction 9 notes the change; `tests/test_runner_model_window.py:82`, which pins the repository's locked switches, now expects 2 lanes (the one value this decision changes; its other checks are unchanged). Reason: Casey asked for it, and the reasons for one lane no longer hold. Source: Casey's chat of November 10, 2026 (relayed by the overseer), `kit/runner.json:1`, `BUILD_BRIEF.md:209`, `runner/lanes.py:24`.

- **D-2486** Question (T294; WORD-001, WEB-001, D-1932, D-1933): how do the Askama pages reach the brand without each handler passing it, a template call on `askhava_core::api::brand()` or one filter per crate? Askama 0.16 (the pinned version, not 0.13 as the goal says) compiles a path call such as `{{ askhava_core::api::brand().display_name() }}` and method calls on its result with no new dependency and no filter module, and the value is escaped as every value is (SEC-011); `base.html` is compiled only by `portals` (the one crate whose `askama.toml` reads `../site/templates`), which already depends on `core`, so `site` gains no dependency. `pick_review.html` binds it once (`{% let brand = ... %}`) for the contact card, whose `data:` link encodes the display name, legal name and domain with Askama's built-in `urlencode_strict` (the `urlencode` feature is on by default; `percent-encoding` is already in `Cargo.lock`) and whose file name is the display name lower-cased with spaces as hyphens (`ask-hava.vcf` today). - **D-2451** Question (plan change, November 10, 2026; amended the same day when T311 was claimed before this merged: the fix moved to new task T349; numbered under the interim rule of D-1144 because this builder session does not write `claude/kit-state`: `next_decision` read 2419 on `claude/kit-state`, main's highest D-2440 + 1 = 2441, no open `claude/` plan PR, so max(2419, 2441) + 10 = 2451, re-read before committing; T349, T311; CALL-003, CALL-017; D-1755; new TD-CALL-20; risk R-39): why does `tests/integration/tests/call_pins.rs` go red now and then (the smoke reds of November 10, `smoke_env` strike on `c0640d1b`)? Read-only root cause: `os_number` (`app/calls/src/pins.rs:53` to `:60`) rejects two-byte values of 60,000 or more (5,536 of 65,536, 8.45%) and gives up after 4 tries, returning `None` with probability about 5.1e-5 although the OS source works; `draw_pin` (`:46` to `:50`) uses `map_while`, so one `None` ends all 8 draws; `allocate_pin` gives none, and `assign_number` (`app/calls/src/service.rs:137`) calls `refuse_line` (`:162` to `:174`), which raises a false High `calls.pool_exhausted` alert and refuses the line with `NoFreePin`. In production about 1 masked-line assignment in 19,600 is refused that way (`app/picks/src/release.rs:236`, `app/picks/src/settle.rs:148`), mostly hidden by T254's one `picks.line_retry`; TD-CALL-13's 500-line test hits it about once in 39 runs. Choice: the fix goes into new task T349 (Opus), which owns `pins.rs` after T311 (the runner claimed T311, the first owner of the file, before this plan change merged, so its goal stays as on `main` and T349 depends on it): `os_number` returns `None` only when the OS source fails (rejection sampling with a cap so large it is never the reason, bytes from an injectable fill function), `draw_pin` uses `filter_map` so a failed draw costs one draw, and deterministic unit tests cover a failed draw followed by a free PIN, the rejection step through the injected bytes, and a failing source; the existing unit tests and the 500-line integration test stay unchanged. T349's budget is one file and 150 lines; T311 is unchanged. Reason: an alert and a refused line must mean the pool is full, never a dice roll. Source: `app/calls/src/pins.rs:46`, `app/calls/src/pins.rs:53`, `app/calls/src/service.rs:137`, `app/calls/src/service.rs:162`.

- **D-2507** Question (T155, BIZ-049, BIZ-004, CARD-001, D-393, D-492): how is the capability checklist built and stored, and how do the largest-job and recurring answers skip a card? Choice: `businesses::api::checklist_offer(map, catalog, classes)` lists, per enabled catalog category (the trade), the job types `ClassMap::job_types` gives the classes (licensed, pre-ticked) and every job type of an enabled category whose license kind is `none` (a no-license extra, unticked); licensed trades come first. A recurring job type is one in a `recurring` category that is not in its `one_time_job_types` (REC-002). `save_capability` stores the ticks through `set_job_types` with only the offer allowed (so a licensed job type outside the license is `NotCovered` and nothing is stored), drops the recurring ticks on a recurring "no", and in the same transaction stores the towns, the after-hours tick and the new `businesses.capability` row (largest job in cents, NULL for no limit; recurring; migration 0150, no app-role DELETE) with a `capability` audit row. `quotes::api::capability_skip` skips when the homeowner's band floor is strictly above the largest job (a floor equal to it is not "entirely above") or when the job is recurring and the business said no; a business with no capability row is skipped by neither, so businesses signed up before this step keep their cards. `capable_pool` removes skipped businesses before `rules::match_job`, so the skips hold for overflow cards too. Reason: the license map is the only source of ROC cover (LIC-043, D-954), and filtering the pool keeps `rules.rs` and its tests unchanged. Source: `docs/spec/businesses.md:53`, `docs/spec/job-cards.md:5`.
- **D-2508** Question (T155): what of BIZ-049 does this task leave wired to callers that are not its files? Choice: known gaps, logged here: (1) the card send (`quotes::service::send_job_cards` and `send_late_cards`, owned elsewhere) does not yet call `businesses::api::capabilities` and `quotes::api::capable_pool`, and `CardJob` has no band floor; the task that next owns `service.rs` reads the job's size-band answer (`band_floor` of the question bank, through `quotes::api::band_floor_cents`) and the recurring flag (`businesses::api::is_recurring` over the candidates) and filters the pool before matching; (2) the capability route (`portals::api::CAPABILITY_ROUTE`) waits with the rest of sign-up (D-1709), so `tests/e2e/capability_setup.spec.ts` checks the signed-out edge and scans the rendered screens, which `td_biz_29_write_pages_for_axe` writes; (3) the quote form's price field waits (D-1957), so the largest-job warning is `largest_job_warning` plus `quote_form_page_warned`, and the quote POST must call it before `submit_quote` and let the send through only when the posted `over_largest` equals the warned cents (D-2510); (4) BIZ-058's service radius and base ZIP and the portal page that changes the answers later are not built here. Reason: the task owns none of those files. Source: `kit/prompts/T155.md` Scope. Review note (plan gaps, the plan files are locked and unchanged here): the CARD-001 skips (`capable_pool`, `capability_skip`) have no production caller, and no queued task owns wiring `quotes::service` to them while T249 assumes it is done; nor does any task own serving `CAPABILITY_ROUTE`, the quote POST's largest-job check or BIZ-058's radius; until a plan change gives one of them that work, the matching does not yet skip by the largest-job and recurring answers in production.
- **D-2509** Question (T155, BIZ-049, A11Y-012): how do the one-page form and the guided screens give the same result, and what quote size is checked against the largest job? Choice: every guided screen posts its own answer plus every other answer as hidden fields (`CapabilityValues::carried`), so both forms post the same `(name, value)` pairs and `CapabilityValues::from_pairs` reads them alike; the check screen reads the answers back (BIZ-030) before "Save and continue". The quote size is the firm price, the top of a range, the highest tier, the visit fee, or the hourly rate times the most hours; a monthly price and an hourly rate with no hours have no job size and never warn. Reason: one server-rendered question per page with nothing asked twice (accessibility-forms section 3, WCAG 3.3.7). Source: `docs/brains/accessibility-forms.md`, `docs/spec/businesses.md:53`.
- **D-2510** Question (T155 review, BIZ-049, D-393): how is the quote form's largest-job confirmation tied to the price warned about? Choice: `largest_job_warning(price, largest, confirmed: Option<u64>)` returns a `LargestWarning` (its text and the quote's top amount in cents); the form's hidden `over_largest` field carries those cents, and the warning is skipped only when the posted cents equal the quote's top amount now, so a price raised (or changed) after the warning is warned again. Reason: a bare `over_largest=yes` stayed valid after a later price change, so a much larger quote could go out unwarned. Source: `docs/spec/businesses.md:53`.
- **D-2511** Question (T155 review, BIZ-030, A11Y-030): what does the check screen show when answers are missing (a hand-typed or stale `step=check`)? Choice: `capability_page` renders the one-page form instead, with the missing answers added to the problems (an "Error: " title and the focused summary) and the "Check your answers" button, never an empty read-back with "Save and continue". Also: the job-types fieldset is described by its hint, the typed amount by the largest-job error when shown, and "(no license needed)" sits on a trade's legend only when no row needs a license, else on each no-license row. Reason: a Save offered over an empty summary would save nothing the business read back. Source: `docs/brains/accessibility-forms.md`.
- **D-2512** Question (T338, D-2318): how does the refused-connection test stop racing the stand-ins? Choice: `unreachable_vendor_is_not_sent` holds its port with a bound, never-listening `tokio::net::TcpSocket` for the whole test, so the connect is refused and no other process can take the port; the assertion stays exactly `Err(AdapterError::NotSent)`. A second case, `closed_without_answer_is_outcome_unknown`, pins the other branch: a listener that accepts and closes without answering gives `Err(AdapterError::OutcomeUnknown)`. `send_error`'s mapping is unchanged. Reason: a request that may have reached the vendor must not be resent blind (SEC-018), and a flaky test costs attempts. Source: `app/adapters/src/tests/adapter_config.rs`, `app/adapters/src/base.rs:114`, TD-SEC-59.

Don't weaken the red-main protection."): every backup job runs a full `scripts/smoke.sh` before the session (D-2028, 326 to 573 s on November 10) even when `kit/state.json` already records a green smoke on the same head (`0cac801c` was smoked green three times between 19:53Z and 20:20Z, `ec13297f` twice), and three in-session smokes timed out at 541 s that day (`c0640d1b` 08:11Z, `77805472` 12:51Z, `d145202d` 15:04Z). Why did they time out, and how can a green be reused without weakening red-main protection? Finding: each timeout is the same chain, read from the jobs' logs (runs 42771164378, 42809623302, 42835728296): the pre-session smoke ran on the checkout's head (`e5b1fbdb`, `f973fd92`, `3ddb3a44`, green in 534, 450 and 538 s), main moved while it ran (the other lane's merge), so the session logged "the pre-session smoke ran on …, main is now …: the smoke runs here" and ran smoke.sh inside its Bash call under `SMOKE_TIMEOUT` 540 s, which is at the median of a warm smoke (no hanging test and no cache miss: the build was warm, 0 to 14 changed paths; the 534 s run spent 195 s in pytest, 1,873 tests, and 304 s in about 180 `cargo test` binaries, the slowest 22 s, the rest checks). The 300 s red of 08:32Z was not a timeout but the `call_pins` PIN flake (D-2451). Choice: (1) Reuse. `state.reusable_smoke(state, head, now)`: a start routine on main's head may reuse the LAST `smoke_runs` entry for that head when it is green and not timed out, no finished run on that head was red and no D-498 strike (`smoke_env_problems`) names it, `main_red` is unset, the head is in no `main_red_history` entry and the green run it stands on (`reused`, else `at`) is at most `SMOKE_REUSE_MAX_AGE` 6 hours old (same commit, same verdict; the cap bounds drift of the job image and the `postgres:16` service). `cycle._start_smoke` never reuses while this job has its own smoke for the head (`GitHubEnv.own_smoke_for`: a pre-session or background result of this job for the head, or a background smoke of this job still running): that result is judged through `_smoke`, so this job's own red always counts (D-498 strike or `set_main_red`), also after a lost race re-read; it also refuses a reuse when kit/nightly.json is for the head and not a success or `main_checks_green(head)` is False (`_head_doubted`), records the reuse as its own entry (`why` "start routine (reused <at>)", `reused`, no `seconds`), and otherwise calls `_smoke` as before. `clear_main_red` keeps calling `_smoke`, so `main_red` still clears only on the runner's own new green run (governance 5.3); `set_main_red`, FIX-MAIN, D-498 strikes and D-1178 timeouts are unchanged, and a reuse can only ever say green on a head the runner smoked green with no red since the green. Two lanes on one head: a green recorded by either lane is reusable by the other only when the reusing job has no smoke of its own for the head. (2) The step skip. A new `backup-runner.yml` step "Read the recorded smoke runs for the pre-session smoke (D-2560)" saves kit/state.json from `claude/kit-state` read-only with the job token (as "Pick the session's model" does); `--pre-smoke` reads it (`RUNNER_PRE_SMOKE_STATE`, `GitHubEnv._reusable_line`) and, when `reusable_smoke` allows a reuse on the checkout's head, runs nothing and writes no result; the session's start routine then reuses, or smokes itself if something changed meanwhile. (3) The timeouts. With `RUNNER_SMOKE_BACKGROUND=1` on the session step, `smoke_main` without a usable pre-session result starts `python3 -m runner --pre-smoke` for the fetched head (`RUNNER_PRE_SMOKE_HEAD`) detached in its own session (`start_background_smoke`, `target/smoke-bg.json` {sha, job, pid, at}, output `target/smoke-bg.log`, `target/smoke-ran` marked), within `PRE_SMOKE_TIMEOUT` 1,500 s (2.6 times the slowest smoke recorded), and waits for its result until `SMOKE_WAIT` 450 s after the runner call began (`wait_from`, so a lost-race retry in the same call never waits again; room for the cycle's own work inside the 600-second Bash call); still running, the cycle returns `smoke_pending` (not recorded, nothing claimed, no strike, `main` untouched; from `clear_main_red` too) and the session prompt's step 2 says to run step 1 again; the result is used like a pre-session one (`source` "background", `why` "<why> (background)"); a background smoke of an older head still running is stopped first, before the start routine judges a reuse (`settle_background_smoke`; `stop_background_smoke`: SIGTERM to its process group and its smoke.sh's, recorded in `target/smoke-bg-child`, which is removed before every start, up to 30 s for both, then SIGKILL to every recorded group whatever the wait saw), so a green another lane recorded on the new head can stand and otherwise one is started for the new head, never two in the one smoke tree and database; since `own_smoke_for` covers a smoke of the head still running (it asks whether the smoke runs before it reads the result, and `_background_smoke` reads the result again before calling an ended smoke lost, so a smoke that writes its result and ends in between is judged), nothing is reused or claimed beside it; a zombie counts as ended (`process_alive`); a new step "Stop a background smoke before the cache save (D-2560)" stops one still running when the session ended and then the save of `target/smoke` is skipped for that job; one that ended without a result is a timeout as before (D-1178, D-1970's chain). Outside Actions or without the switch the smoke runs in the call as before. `BUILD_BRIEF.md:240` says a recorded green on the same head stands for the start routine's smoke (same line). Saving: a job on an unchanged head skips the ~9-minute pre-session smoke (3 of the 20 runs recorded on November 10); a moved head no longer loses a 540 s timeout plus a chained job (about 25 minutes each, 3 times that day) but finishes its smoke within one or two more runner calls. Not done: running pytest and the Rust tests in parallel inside smoke.sh, or pytest-xdist (a new dependency), which would cut the smoke itself. Tests: `tests/test_runner_smoke_reuse.py`; the red-main drills of `tests/test_failure_drills.py` and `tests/test_runner_pre_smoke.py` pass unchanged. Source: Casey in chat, November 10, 2026; `runner/cycle.py`, `runner/state.py`, `runner/github_env.py`, `.github/workflows/backup-runner.yml`; job logs 129679528643, 129807557322, 129906632445, 129714336738.
- **D-2550** Question (harness change, November 10, 2026; numbered under the interim rule of D-1144 because this builder session does not write `claude/kit-state`: `next_decision` read 2517 on `claude/kit-state`, main's highest D-2511 + 1 = 2512 (D-2506 when first drafted; T155's merge added D-2510 and D-2511), open plan PR #431's highest D-2540 + 1 = 2541, so max(2517, 2512, 2541) = 2541; the interim rule's + 10 would give 2551, and the overseer assigned D-2550 instead, with D-2551 reserved for the follow-up, both above every number in use, re-read before committing; T290, T231; D-2386, D-2429, D-2440, D-1350): two attempts today failed on the same kind of plan gap: a task added to a list that an existing test pins by exact list or count, and the task could not edit that test. T290 added rows W41 to W62 to `docs/catalog/worked_examples.yaml`, which `RECURRING`'s 13 ids (`app/payments/src/tests/worked_examples.rs:18`, T058's) and `assert_eq!(checked, 14)` (`app/payments/src/tests/recurring.rs:130`, T188's and T244's) pinned (D-2386); T231 served a new route, `/c/{token}/{answer}`, which T088's `door` (`tests/security/tests/auth_matrix.rs:107`) does not name and so panics on (D-2429). Casey, in chat on November 10 at about 20:20Z: "Add a pre-claim plan-gap check that flags a queued task whose goal adds rows, routes or fixtures that existing tests pin by exact list or count, when the task doesn't own those tests (the T290 and T231 cases from today). Report-only first, then make it fail the plan check." Choice: plan-health check (d), in the new `scripts/plan_pins.py`, imported by `scripts/plan_health.py`. It finds two kinds of pin from the test files alone: a data pin (a test that reads a repository data file and asserts an exact count, `assert_eq!(x.len(), N)`, `assert_eq!(counter, N)` for a counter it increments, `assert len(x) == N`, `toHaveLength(N)`, with N at least 2, or holds a `const NAME: [&str; N]` of ids all found in that file; a path the test writes itself, `docs/decisions.md` and `kit/` are no data) and a route pin (a Rust test that reads the route table from `.route(` calls and classifies each path in a function that panics on a path no branch names, with the branches it fails once served). A task trips a data pin when it may write the data file and a goal sentence names the file with an adding verb; it trips a route pin when it owns `app/` source and a goal sentence has the task itself serve something ("This task also serves", "it serves", "a new route") and either quotes a path no branch takes or takes one the test fails once served, or quotes no path at all. No warning when the task may edit the test (`runner/verify.py` `check_paths`, the hand-in rule), when a task that owns the test by name is a dependency not yet DONE (planned to extend it, as T348 is for the matrix, D-2440), or when a decision the task pastes names the test in a sentence that lets it edit it (D-2386's form: "also owns", "may update"). Report-only: `check_task`, the runner's hook (`runner/cycle.py` `plan_health_pass`), returns nothing from (d), so it holds no task, and the exit code ignores it; `python3 scripts/plan_health.py --all` (and any run with `--pinned`) prints each as a `WARN` line naming the task, the pinning `path:line`, the symbol, the test's owners and the reason (in `--json`, under the key `pinned lists (report-only, D-2550)` when there are any); `python3 scripts/plan_pins.py --pins` lists the pins found. Shown on the plan just before each fix: at `01ba88c7~1` with that morning's state, T290 is warned for both tests (`recurring.rs:130 checked == 14`; `worked_examples.rs:18 RECURRING`, 13 ids) and T231 and T304 for the matrix; at `261a13b1~1`, T231 and T304; after D-2386 and D-2429 neither T290 nor T231 is warned. On today's plan (156 tasks not DONE) it warns none: T304, T305, T309 and T310 name owner, help or `/b/` paths the matrix does not take yet, and each waits on T348, which owns it. Known limits: a goal that serves pages without saying the task serves them is not seen (D-2440 found thirteen such tasks by reading; this check, on the plan of `261a13b1~1`, found two), and a count reached through crate code in a test that reads several data files is not tied to them. D-2551 (reserved) makes (d) a holding problem once it has shown no false positives. Amended in this pull request's review: `plan_health.py` imports `plan_pins` only inside the check, so a fault in it can never stop the runner, which imports `plan_health` (D-1350), and any error in (d) prints one `check (d) unavailable` line after the (a) to (c) report, leaving the exit code as it was; `plan_pins.py` exits 2 when a test file cannot be read; `tests/test_plan_pins.py` records the known false positives (a count in a function that names two data files, an "add a field" goal, an id list that is not the file's whole set, a serving goal that names no path) and the too-loose "owns the" decision excuse as current behaviour. The reviewer's recommendations for D-2551: a crash in (d) is kept apart from (a) to (c) inside `check_task`; only the precise subset holds a task (a quoted route path no branch takes or one under a door the test fails once served; a count pin whose function names exactly one data file, with a goal sentence that adds rows or ids; a list pin compared with the file's full set of ids); the decision excuse must name the task's own ID; a not-yet-DONE owner excuses only when its goal names the path or its prefix; and `plan_health.py --all` runs on every plan pull request for an evidence period before the switch. Reason: a plan gap found before the claim costs no attempt. Source: `app/payments/src/tests/recurring.rs:130` and `app/payments/src/tests/worked_examples.rs:18` at `01ba88c7~1`, `tests/security/tests/auth_matrix.rs:107` at `261a13b1~1`, `scripts/plan_pins.py`, `scripts/plan_health.py`, `tests/test_plan_pins.py`.

Reason: D-2201, with every edge failing closed (no bridge, no words) rather than falling back to another line. - **D-2592** Question (T207, BIZ-050, LIC-043, D-393): when a daily license list changes a business's classes, which job types are removed, which are offered, and when is the business paused? Choice: `businesses::api::reapply_license(conn, id, (map, catalog), (old, new), now)` removes, in one transaction with a `job_types` audit row, every ticked job type of a licensed category (license kind not `none`) that `ClassMap::job_types(new)` does not cover; a no-license job type is kept, because it needs no license. It offers the job types `new` covers that `old` did not and that are not ticked, and never ticks them. "No covered job type left" is read as nothing left ticked at all: a business still holding a no-license job type keeps getting those cards and is not paused; one left with nothing is paused through `pause_for_rule` with `no_covered_job_type` when active or self-paused, and left as it is in any other status. One `businesses.license_change` task per change carries the business ID, the removed and offered `[category, job type]` pairs, the dropped classes (the reason) and the pause; `license_change_words` renders the owner's email in English and Spanish. Reason: BIZ-050 says removed job types go at once and new ones are offered, never ticked; pausing a business that can still take no-license work would stop cards it may receive. Source: `docs/spec/businesses.md:54`.

- **D-2623** Question (T352, T359, T261; FEE-013, FEE-028, FEE-030, FEE-031, FEE-042, FEE-045; D-1414, D-1419, D-1557, D-1561, D-2302): a successful charge writes no `charge` ledger entry (`record_fee_at_confirm` has no caller and no `ch_` ID reaches the success path), so a repeat customer is charged again, the statement shows refunds with no charges, and the reconcile would raise an unknown-charge alert for every charge; the evidence record lacks the charge ID; `queue_receipt` has no caller; and a fee-free job-type pick is never released, since `waive_at_confirm` writes nothing for a $0 pick. Choice, as amended by the plan review (H1, H2, M2): two tasks. T352 (harness) adds `latest_charge` to the adapter's `PaymentIntent` and the stand-in, and adopts the eight done tests that build it by name, `late_success.rs` included (each literal gains a fake `ch_` ID; no assertion changes). T359 (build, Opus, money review) makes the release proof's fresh fetch require the `ch_` ID; the success transaction stores it in `payments.charge_evidence` (new nullable column), appends one `charge` entry at the pick's stored fee under a key derived from the pick, not from (job, business), with the reconcile's own-intent charge key changed to match, and queues the receipt when the evidence row is new (D-1557's caller). The per-pick key is the safer reading of the spec: a business whose first paid pick on a job was refunded and that is picked and charged again on the same job has two real charges, and a (job, business) key would hide the second from the ledger, the statement and the reconcile; FEE-013's repeat waiver is about another job of the same customer and is unchanged, and D-2302's accepted overlap concerns $0 decisions only. For FEE-045, `waive_at_confirm` writes the `fee-free-job-type` $0 entry when the pick's stored fee row says it is fee-free, needing no card and no `may_confirm` proof (FEE-036, BIZ-001), instead of T261 calling `record_fee_at_confirm`, which needs a card authorization; T261's goal is unchanged from `main` and it now runs after T359. The re-review adds: `is_repeat` counts a charge as an introduction (FEE-013) only when its pick was not refunded before any release (a late success auto-refunded with nothing released, T332's trigger, or an unreleased `fraud-warning` refund do not count; refunds after a release do); and `record_fee_at_confirm` stays as it is and unused in production, because four done tests call it and the success path and `waive_at_confirm` write every ledger kind it wrote; T359 owns `service.rs` only to say so in its doc comment. T352 also adopts T328's `payment_jobs.rs` when it builds `PaymentIntent`, and runs after T328. This sets aside only D-1414's premise that the charge is made before `record_fee_at_confirm` is called at Confirm. Reason: FEE-028 and FEE-030 build the statement and money view from the ledger only. Source: `app/payments/src/service.rs:340`, `:401`, `:426`, `app/payments/src/charge.rs:656`, `app/payments/src/handlers.rs:144`, `app/payments/src/release_proof.rs:193`, `app/payments/src/free_wins.rs:139`, `:160`, `app/payments/src/reconcile.rs:381`, `app/payments/src/receipts.rs:56`, `app/adapters/src/payments.rs:32`.

- **D-2627** Question (T355; PICK-022, PRIV-005, FEE-052): the release claim reads its target unlocked and inserts its row on the pick ID alone, while the fraud path sends the refund (`payments::api::early_fraud_warning`, `app/payments/src/refunds.rs:140`) on the caller's `released` snapshot before any lock, so a racing release can open the details of a pick being refunded. Choice, as amended by the plan review (H3) and its re-review: the fraud path first takes `SELECT … FOR UPDATE` on the pick, reads in a separate statement whether a release row exists, and, when none does, commits a durable marker (one `picks.fraud_hold` row, a new table in T355's migration, INSERT and SELECT only) before calling `early_fraud_warning` with `released` read under that lock; a released pick only alerts and goes to Casey. The claim takes the same pick lock first and then, in a separate statement, requires the wanted status, no end and no `picks.fraud_hold` row, answering `MovedOn` before any vault read. `end_pick` keeps its status-only guard, since `no_call_at_72_hours` ends released picks through it. A marker table rather than a new pick status leaves `PickStatus` and its exhaustive matches alone, and the refund row is not written in the lock transaction, so T355 does not own `refunds.rs`. This is a clarification consistent with FEE-052's order, not a change of meaning: "not yet released" is decided under the pick's lock and the release is then refused. Reason: a business must never get both the refund and the details. Source: `app/picks/src/release.rs:282`, `:394`, `app/picks/src/unreachable_refund.rs:432`, `:439`, `:490`, `app/payments/src/refunds.rs:140`.

- **D-2597** Question (T349, D-2451; CALL-003, CALL-017, D-1755; TD-CALL-20): how does a PIN draw fail only when the OS random source fails, and how is the rejection step tested without the OS? Choice: `pins.rs`'s `os_number` passes `SysRng`'s fill to the crate-private `number_from(fill)`, which draws two bytes and draws again while the value is 60,000 (`UNBIASED_BELOW`, the largest multiple of 10,000 two bytes hold) or more, returning the value modulo 10,000; it returns `None` at once when `fill` fails, and after `NUMBER_TRIES` (64) rejections, whose odds (5,536/65,536)^64 ≈ 2e-69 make the cap never the reason. `draw_pin` uses `filter_map` instead of `map_while`, so a failed or invalid draw costs that one of the 8 draws, not the rest; the existing TD-CALL-13 cases keep their meaning (8 colliding draws, an always-failing source and an always-invalid value still give `None`). Unit tests beside TD-CALL-13's: a failed draw then a free PIN gives the PIN; injected values 65,535, 60,000, 61,234, then 59,999 give 9,999 after four fills; a failing fill gives `None` after one call; 64 rejected values give `None` (covering the cap). T311's read-back code is untouched.

The background smoke's child process also carries `RUNNER_PRE_SMOKE_HEAD` (`runner/github_env.py:332`), which makes `pre_smoke()` smoke that pinned SHA in the tests (34 red with all four set, matching the live 33), and the pre-smoke step sets `RUNNER_PRE_SMOKE_STATE`. Choice: `tests/conftest.py` gains an autouse fixture that removes `RUNNER_SMOKE_BACKGROUND`, `RUNNER_PRE_SMOKE_HEAD`, `RUNNER_PRE_SMOKE_STATE`, `GITHUB_RUN_ID` and `GITHUB_RUN_ATTEMPT` before every test, as `_no_live_runner_tokens` already does for the job's tokens (D-510); tests that need them set them with `monkeypatch`, as they do today. Reason: a smoke that is red for its own environment spends D-498 strikes and claims nothing; three on one head would be believed as a red `main`. Source: `claude/kit-state` `runner_log` (2026-11-11T00:26:17Z, lane 2), `.github/workflows/backup-runner.yml:431`, `runner/github_env.py:93`, `tests/conftest.py`.

- **D-2661** Question (T157; PICK-047, PICK-017, D-400): where does the backup chosen on the pick review step live, given the pick is stored only after the code step and T157 does not own `pick_code.html`, so a field cannot ride through the code form? Choice: the review step's final Pick form carries `backup` (empty is "No backup"); `final_pick` stores it with `picks::api::choose_backup` before the code is sent, as a new append-only `picks.backup_choice` row (job, the quote she is picking, the backup or NULL, time). When a pick ends, the job's latest row made before the end counts only if it was made for that pick's quote, so a later review of another quote, or a text pick of another quote, never inherits it; pressing Pick again on the waiting quote shows the result (no code) and stores the new choice, which is how she changes or removes it until the pick ends; a row after the end never counts. A backup that is the same quote or not an available quote is stored as "No backup". Ask Hava never writes a row of its own. Source: PICK-047 (`docs/spec/quotes-pick.md:51`), `app/portals/src/pick_flow.rs` `final_pick`. Fix round (review finding 1, privacy): a choice asked for with the final Pick counted without the 6-digit code, so a forwarded link could set or change the backup of a waiting pick, and a pick later made by text inherited an abandoned page choice. Now each `picks.backup_choice` row carries `browser` (SHA256 of the page's CSRF token, never the token) and an optional `pick_id`: `choose_backup` writes an unbound row only; `bind_backup` binds this browser's latest choice for the pick's quote in the transaction that stores the pick after `check_page_code` passed (`store`, for a new pick and for `PagePick::Same`); only the pick's latest bound row made at or before its end counts. Pressing Pick again on the waiting quote with a different backup (`backup_changed`) sends a code instead of the result, and the change counts after it passes; the same backup again still needs no code (TD-PICK-47). The hint now says to type the new code. A text pick binds nothing, so it has no backup. Superseded in this entry: "the job's latest row made before the end counts" and "pressing Pick again ... shows the result (no code) and stores the new choice". Fix round (CI, E2e and Ally): the code step's `CodeForm` refuses unknown fields, so the review form posted straight to `/code` (as `tests/e2e/j1_reduced.spec.ts`, `tests/a11y/pick_forms.spec.ts` and `tests/a11y/j1_keyboard.spec.ts` do, D-1264) was refused once it carried `backup`; `CodeForm` now accepts `backup` and never reads it, so only the final Pick stores a backup and the other fields stay strict.
- **D-2662** Question (T157; PICK-047, PICK-037, PICK-035, D-446): how does an ended pick move to the backup? Choice: `picks::api::backup_choice(tx, pick, paused, (actor, at))` acts once per pick (`picks.backup_move`, append-only; a rerun is `Backup::Done`), only on a pick that ended without an acceptance (status `expired`, or `cancelled` other than `replaced` or `paused`, which are her own acts) and only while no other pick waits on the job (she picked again herself: `Done`). The backup must still be available and never the ended quote or business (`backup_target`); it is placed through `page_pick` with channel `page`, so the new pick fixes its own introduction fee by job size, writes its audit row and queues its pick notice (PICK-037), whose real send starts its own Confirm window (`notice_sent`). The homeowner pause is the caller's input because `picks` cannot read `intake` (layering); a paused job takes no backup and the answer is `NoBackup`. With no backup or an unavailable one the answer is `NoBackup` and the caller sends PICK-046's `lapse_text`; a moved pick's homeowner text is `backup_text` (en, es, built from the brand file like T197's lapse text, D-1971). Source: PICK-047, `app/picks/src/service.rs` `page_pick`. Fix round (review findings 2, 3, 6): `backup_choice` also takes `payments`' end states `payment_failed` and `needs_card` (codes of `migrations/0079_picks_code.sql`, not yet `PickStatus` variants) when `ended_at` is set; the caller contract (FEE-041, FEE-018, FEE-020, T062) is: end the pick with `ended_at`, move the job from Payment pending back to Quotes ready (JOB-001's arrow), then call it in the same transaction; a job still in Payment pending is `PicksError::Job` and nothing is recorded, so the caller can never turn the move into a permanent `NoBackup`. On an emergency job still in Awaiting confirm the move restarts `jobs`' 60 clock minutes from the move (`restart_timer`), since `notice_sent` starts no window for an emergency (PICK-044); a job moved from Quotes ready already counts from the move. A paused job (CON-029) is now `Done`, recorded once, so no PICK-046 text goes to a homeowner who paused; superseded: "a paused job takes no backup and the answer is `NoBackup`".
- **D-2663** Question (T157; D-491, D-492, D-493): who calls it? Choice: T157 builds the calls and leaves the callers to their owners, as T197 did with the lapse text (D-1972): `confirm_reminders::lapse` (expire a waiting pick, then move) for `run_confirm_ends` (`handlers.rs`, not owned here) and `confirm::refused_at_confirm` for the Confirm press; "Can't take it" (T214), leaving Ask Hava (T228) and the payments paths (FEE-041, FEE-018, FEE-020 through T062's handler on the payments event) end the pick their own way and then call `backup_choice` in the same transaction. The senders of `backup_text` and `lapse_text` are still to be built (quiet hours except an emergency, PICK-046). Source: the task's goal line, D-1972. Fix round: review findings 4 and 7 of the T157 review are follow-ups, not fixed in this task (their wording was not passed to this fix round, so they are recorded here by number only, for the reviewer's record to name).
- **D-2664** Question (T157; PICK-020, PICK-047): how does a Confirm refused by the re-check end the pick? A pick no longer waiting is `Done`. Source: PICK-020, `app/picks/src/confirm.rs` `check_at_confirm`.

- **D-2782** Question (harness change, November 11, 2026; numbered max(`next_decision` 2746, `main`'s highest 2740 + 1, open plan PR #446's highest 2771 + 1) + 10 = 2782): Casey asked for a faster build without hurting the product. Where does `Ci`'s time go? Measured by the overseer's CI audit (ten recent `ci` runs and their job logs, a local pytest profile): `Ci` takes about 16 minutes and `Checks` is always its longest job (warm about 800 s, a cold cache adds about 400 s); the build caches hit in 5 of 10 runs because GitHub's 10 GB repository cache evicts least-recently-used entries and every branch run saves its own (about 1.5 GB each for the branch's `rust-cache` entries, about 6.8 GB per backup-runner claim), while a branch-scoped entry can be restored only by that branch; pytest runs serially inside `Checks` for 249 s before any Rust step; and PyYAML's pure-Python `SafeLoader` parses `docs/catalog` in 1.31 s against 0.12 s for libyaml's `CSafeLoader`, with identical results. Choice: (1) Every `Swatinem/rust-cache` step in `ci.yml` (Checks, Coverage, E2e), `twin.yml` and `a11y.yml` gets `save-if: ${{ github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' }}`, and the sqlx-cli cache is split into `actions/cache/restore` (every run) and `actions/cache/save` (only on `main`, only on a miss), both pinned to the same commit as before. Branch runs still restore `main`'s entries; `main`'s are refreshed by nightly-main, which calls all three workflows on `main` every night (scheduled workflows run on the default branch, so `github.ref` there is `refs/heads/main`). A cache only saves time: Cargo's fingerprints decide what rebuilds, so no result changes. `backup-runner.yml` is unchanged: its `target/debug` entry is keyed per commit of `main` on purpose (D-1178, so the workers' builds never freeze at the last lock change), its smoke entry is already saved only by a job whose smoke or warm-up actually compiled for at least 60 s (D-1911, D-2007), and `CARGO_INCREMENTAL` is 0 in the smoke environment, so `target/*/incremental` holds nothing worth excluding; any further throttle (say, one save per lock hash per N hours) would re-open the stale-target timeouts D-1178 and D-2007 closed, which needs its own measurement first. (2) pytest moves out of `Checks` into a new parallel job `Python` in `ci.yml` (same checkout depth 200, the same read-only fetch of `main` that the brand-literal guard needs, Python 3.12, `pytest==9.1.1 PyYAML==6.0.1`, the same command). The `Ci` aggregate job now `needs: [checks, python, coverage, e2e]` and is green only when all four results are `success`, so the required check `Ci` still requires every test it required before; its name, and the names `Twin` and `Ally`, are unchanged. `Checks` keeps `setup-python` (the Rust tests start `stand_ins/server.py` with `python3`) and installs PyYAML for `scripts/check_include_paths.py`; nothing else in `Checks` read what pytest left behind. (3) `scripts/check_catalog.py`, `scripts/check_ai_smell.py` and `scripts/check_include_paths.py` load YAML with `yaml.load(text, Loader=SAFE_LOADER)`, where `SAFE_LOADER = getattr(yaml, "CSafeLoader", yaml.SafeLoader)`: the same safe constructors, libyaml's parser when PyYAML has it (the PyYAML 6.0.1 cp312 manylinux wheel `Ci` installs ships `yaml/_yaml.cpython-312-x86_64-linux-gnu.so`). Proof: every tracked `*.yaml` and `*.yml` (56 files, 45 under `docs/catalog`) parsed with both loaders gives equal and identically typed results (`==` and `repr`), with PyYAML 6.0.1 on Python 3.12 (8.8 times faster) and 6.0.3 on Python 3.13 (10.1 times faster). No gate weakens: no check, test or step is removed or skipped, every test still runs under `Ci`, and the required check names stay. Kind: harness change (protected `.github/`, locked `scripts/`), plan lock rewritten. Owner approval: Casey's request for a faster build; independent Opus review arranged by the overseer. Source: the CI audit's run and job logs, `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, `.github/workflows/twin.yml`, `.github/workflows/a11y.yml`, `.github/workflows/nightly-main.yml`, `.github/workflows/backup-runner.yml`, `runner/verify.py:11`, `scripts/validate_tasks.py:68`, D-693, D-1178, D-1911, D-2007.
