- **D-2798** Question (harness, the CI audit of November 11, 2026; Casey: speed up the build without hurting the product): in 6 of the last 7 task pull requests (T155, T294, T231, T199, T349, T338) `main` had already moved before the hand-in push, so the reviewed head's full round of `Ci`/`Twin`/`Ally` (about 16 minutes) could never be the one that merges; the runner then pushed its update merge (`runner/update_merge.py`, D-620) and a second full round ran, starting 3 to 19 minutes (about 11 on average) after the first. Can the hand-in carry that merge? Choice: yes. At hand-in, when the reviewed head does not contain `main`'s head, `finish` builds the same deterministic update merge stage C would build later (`GitHubEnv._built_update`, now shared by `update_branch` and the new `hand_in_merge`: `UpdateMerge.commit`, then `is_update_merge` against exactly the reviewed head and `main`'s head, the same commit, same SHA) and the review record adopts it in the same state write as stage C adopts its own (`_adopt_update`, `update_merges` entry with `how: "hand-in"` and `from` the reviewed head), so `reviewed_sha` is the merged head before the single push of the reviewed head plus the merge; auto-pr, auto-merge, `_head_reviewed`, `_finished_by` and the resync gate then see one reviewed head, and the merge is accepted by the same rule as any update merge (`update_merge_of` and `reviewed_plus_main` accept it; one with an extra change is refused). Unchanged: the review binds to the reviewed head, which is recorded as the merge's `from`; the pre-hand-in gate runs on the reviewed head; the insert-only resolution rules; a red `main` (for any task but FIX-MAIN, checked before the build and again inside the review record's write, as stage C refuses an update merge while `main` is red), a conflict, a failed tree check, a git error, a dry run or an `Env` without the method push the reviewed head unmerged and stage C's conflict and resync path handles it; `main` moving again during the checks is stage C's as before; a rejected push is the same failed attempt. Expected saving: one full round of checks (about 16 minutes of runner time) per task whose head is behind at hand-in (6 of 7 lately), and the merge waits about 11 minutes less on average. Cost: a check that fails on the merged head has no earlier round on the reviewed head, so `_broken_by_main` cannot tell main's change from the task's; `_lane_outcome` then neither strikes the lane nor clears its strikes (`_unjudged_hand_in`), so such a failure never wipes a run of strikes (the attempt fails either way, as today). - **D-2810** Question (plan change, November 11, 2026; numbered under the interim rule of D-1144 because this builder session does not write `claude/kit-state`: `next_decision` read 2788 on `claude/kit-state`, main's highest D-2740 + 1 = 2741, the open `claude/` branches' highest D-2798 (`claude/harness-premerge-handin`; #446 D-2771, #449 D-2782) + 1 = 2799, so max(2788, 2741, 2799) + 10 = 2809, rounded to 2810; `kit/runner.json`; D-2462, D-620, D-630, D-723, D-1128, D-1155): Casey, in chat about 03:30Z on November 11, 2026, after a lane simulation showed stages 4 and 5 bound by capacity with two lanes and about 25% sooner with three: "We can go to a third lane now." Should the runner work three tasks at once? Choice: `kit/runner.json` `lanes` 2 → 3, through a logged plan change as `BUILD_BRIEF.md:209` requires. Audit of every place that could assume two lanes: none does in code. `runner/lanes.py` (`effective_lanes`, `free_lanes`, `claim_lane`, `compatible_ids`, which checks a candidate against every task in flight, strikes on any lane above 1), `runner/state.py` (`in_flight`, `run_lane`, `free_lanes`, `_claim_refusal`), `runner/cycle.py` (`refill_lanes`, `_requeue_blockers`, which checks each leased task, `_ours_onto`, which merges `usage` and `lane_strikes` per key whatever the number of writers), `runner/__main__.py` (lost-race retries and refill at `lanes >= 2`), `runner/github_env.py` and `runner/status.py` (every lane's lease listed), `scripts/check_state.py` (at most `lanes` live leases), `scripts/pacing.py` (`in_flight_tokens` sums every other IN_PROGRESS task) and `backup-runner.yml` (the gate's `range(1, lanes + 1)`, a concurrency group per lane, the hourly tick and the chain dispatching one run per free or refill lane, the keeper per lane) all take the count from the setting. Only wording said "1 unless Casey sets 2": `BUILD_BRIEF.md:209`, `docs/governance.md:53`, `docs/architecture.md` (runner logic) and `runner/state.py:12` now say 1 unless a logged plan change sets more, 3 since this decision; `docs/ai-operating-manual.md:102` says a fall back follows two strikes on any lane above 1 (line counts unchanged). Tests (a spec change to tests under CLAUDE.md rule 6; the covered set grows, nothing is weakened): new `tests/test_runner_three_lanes.py` runs the two-lane drills over three lanes (three claims on non-overlapping tasks and a fourth run claiming nothing; a lane-3 candidate refused for overlapping or a different stage against either of two tasks in flight, a compatible one claimed; `refill_lanes` naming up to three lanes; two harness-type strikes on lane 3 falling back to one lane, and one strike each on lanes 2 and 3 not; MERGE_PENDING in two lanes leaving only lane 3 to claim, with `check_state` clean at 3 and flagging 3 live leases at 2; pacing reserving the estimates of two other running attempts; the gate's lane pick with three lanes and while fallen back); `tests/test_runner_lanes.py:206` now allows (1, 2, 3), the lane counts the drills cover; `tests/test_runner_model_window.py:82`, which pins the repository's locked switches, now expects 3 (the one value this decision changes). Pacing, unchanged: the latest session reading holds only the week (58% at 03:17Z, resets 2026-11-12T17:00Z), so the five-hour window is judged from the ledger (11.1M of the 29.1M effective `budget_tokens_five_hour` at 03:10Z) plus the recorded estimates of the other two lanes' attempts (median 1.75M, recent ~3M each); a third claim waits whenever ledger + both reservations + its own estimate pass 29.1M, so with three lanes handing in about 9M weighted per hour the five-hour hold will bind within about two hours of a window's start, and the week's 80M left will be spent well before its reset. The ledger counts about 2.3 times what the reading does over this week (266M ledger against 58% of 200M), so the five-hour hold is likely stricter than the real limit; the 30M figure stays a placeholder until a five-hour reading exists, and is not raised blindly here. Rollback: the same one-line change back to 2 (or 1); tasks in flight finish normally, and two strikes on lane 2 or 3 fall back to one lane by themselves (`lanes_fallback` is unset on `claude/kit-state`). Reason: Casey asked for it, and the lane machinery has no two-lane limit; the drills now prove three. - **D-2743** Question (T374 review; LIC-006, LIC-007, CARD-001, CARD-015; D-906, D-2712): `holder_for` took every class `read_back` returns for the number, whatever its status, so a number whose only class is Suspended read as holding it and `HolderParts::for_job` set `roc_covers` for its job types. Should a holder report an Inactive class? Choice: no. `holder_for` reads only the classes the latest ROC list shows Active for the number (`licensing.agency_record.status = 'active'` on the latest `roc` import, the same latest-by-date list `read_back` uses), so an Inactive-only number holds no class and a mixed number only its Active ones. `read_back` itself is unchanged (it is the sign-up display of what the record shows, LIC-027), and `check_license` stays per number as D-906 chose; this is stricter than D-906's lenient per-number read only for cover, which is per class by nature (LIC-043), and it is the per-class direction D-906 names for a mixed number. - **D-2744** Question (T374 review; CARD-015, LIC-006; D-2741): `holder_for` trusted the caller's ROC number over the business's own daily checks, so a caller passing another number could read classes for a license the card gate (`roc_check_allows_card`, keyed by the checked number) never sees. Prefer the checked number, or refuse a mismatch? Choice: prefer. When the business has a `licensing.license_check` row, `holder_for` reads the classes of its latest check's number and ignores a different caller number; the caller's number (normalised) is used only before any check, the sign-up case (T302) where no check exists yet. Not refusing keeps sign-up and the card pool on one path with no new error variant, and a changed license reaches the holder through the next daily check, the same moment the card gate sees it. Kind: build. Owner approval: not needed. Reason: classes and the card gate then speak of the same license. Source: `app/licensing/src/holder.rs`, `tests/integration/tests/holder_read.rs::the_daily_checked_number_wins_over_the_callers`.

- **D-2783** Question (T209; PICK-048, FEE-014, D-401, D-491): the goal says Stripe's written answer is a `catalog` setting read through `catalog::api` by `payments::off_session` and the portals route, but T209 owns one migration, `migrations/0156_quotes_auto_confirm.sql`, which may name only the `quotes` schema (`tests/integration/tests/architecture_migrations.rs`, TD-SEC-10), and a second, `catalog`-headed migration is outside the task's paths (`scripts/check_pr_change.py` refuses it). Choice: the record is `quotes.stripe_written_answer` (date, reference, `allows`, `filed_at`; the latest row in force; insert and select only) in 0156, read by `quotes::api::stripe_answer_filed`; the portals route and `picks::auto_confirm` read it there (both may call `quotes`); `payments`, which may not call `quotes`, takes the caller's reading as `OffSessionCharge::answer_filed` and charges nothing when it is false, and `prop_no_other_off_session_charge` keeps `picks::auto_confirm` the only caller. Plan gap for the runner: moving the record to `catalog` (its own migration and `catalog::api` reader, as D-491 and the goal say) needs a task that owns a `catalog` migration; the table and its reader then move, and `payments` reads it itself instead of trusting `answer_filed`. The charge reuses `confirm_and_pay` unchanged through a crate-private `OffSession` wrapper whose `confirm_intent` calls `OffSessionStripe::confirm_off_session`; so the fee fixed at the pick, the FEE-017 state, the pause, an earlier undecided try and `begin_attempt`'s hard limit reservation (D-1758) all apply, and the press ID is the pick's own ID, so a pick gets one off-session attempt ever (FEE-016). Source: the task's goal line, `app/payments/CLAUDE.md` (FEE-041, D-2081).
- **D-2784** Question (T209; PICK-048, PICK-019, FEE-020): `confirm_and_pay` opens the FEE-020 card-fix window on a decline or a bank approval, but PICK-048 says an off-session decline or `authentication_required` falls back to the normal Confirm step and window. Choice: `charge_off_session` ends the card-fix `pay_timer` row its decline opened (`ended_at`), so `card_fix_window` reads `Closed`, the card-fix notice sends nothing, the timer handler does nothing, and a `needs_action` attempt no longer reserves its fee against the monthly limit; the pick stays `awaiting_confirm` and the business's later press is a new attempt (try 2, its own key). Stripe's `authentication_required` on an off-session confirm arrives as a 402 decline or a `requires_action` intent and is treated the same. Residual risk (review fix round): `confirm_and_pay` records the decline and queues the `CARD_FIX_KIND` notice task in one transaction in `charge.rs`/`handlers.rs`, which T209 does not own, and `stop_card_fix` runs just after that commit, so a worker that runs the notice task in that gap can still send one card-fix notice for an off-session decline, and a failed stop leaves the window open; closing the window in the decline's own transaction needs a task that owns `handlers.rs` (a flag on `Press` that skips the card-fix window). A failed stop heals on rerun: `charge_off_session` again answers from the recorded attempt (press ID = pick ID, no Stripe call) and ends the window (`tests/integration/tests/auto_confirm.rs::td_fee_30_a_rerun_ends_a_card_fix_window_left_open`); `stop_card_fix` ends it only while the pick's latest attempt is the off-session one, so a rerun after the business's own press never ends that press's window. Source: PICK-048, `app/payments/src/handlers.rs` `effects` and `card_fix_window`.
- **D-2785** Question (T209; PICK-056, TD-FEE-31): when is a tick void, and how is "the business is told" met? Choice: at the pick, `picks::auto_confirm` voids (unticks with reason `void`) a tick whose member is no longer the owner or a current "Confirm and billing" member, whose card is not the saved card now (latest `payments.payment_method` not removed), whose fee differs from the fee fixed at the pick, or whose authorization version differs from `AUTO_CONFIRM_VERSION`; it then queues one `picks.auto_confirm_voided` event (pick, job, business and the reason code; deduped per pick) in the void's transaction, and the pick takes the normal Confirm step. A text pick and an unfiled answer leave the tick as it is and charge nothing; a pick stored with channel `text` is read as `PickProof::Text` whatever proof the caller passes (PICK-056, FEE-014). Only a tick placed at or before the pick's `picked_at` counts (`quotes::api::auto_confirm_of` takes the pick time): the authorization reads "if the homeowner picks it", so a tick placed after the pick never fires for that pick and stays live on the quote form; `quotes` cannot read `picks.pick`, so ticking is not refused while a pick waits. Plan gap: no new text template can be added to `app/messaging/templates/en.json` or `es.json` today (a `{brand_short}` token fails `tests/integration/tests/voice_calls.rs::td_call_06_*`, a literal brand raises the files above `tests/brand_literal_baseline.json`'s 96 lines; the same conflict as D-2387 and D-2411), so the business notice itself (the `messaging.business_notice` to the money recipients, wording in D-2787) is left to the task that moves the files to the brand tokens; TD-FEE-31's "the business is told" is met only up to the stored event. The void is found at the pick rather than at the card change itself, because the card change (`portals::change_saved_card`) is not T209's file; telling the business at the change is a follow-up. An untick needs no Verify code (it can only stop a charge); a tick does (SEC-038). Source: PICK-056, SEC-038, D-480.

- **D-2859** Question (harness, November 11, 2026; the overseer's review of T337 and T295): when a worker reports that only a plan change can unblock its task, why does the runner retry it on the same prompt? Finding (`claude/kit-state` `kit/state.json` and `kit/runner_log.jsonl`): T337's attempt 1 ended "smoke/prehandin red on tests T337 does not own ... needs a harness task (D-2714)" and T295's "A plan change must give these an owner before the guard is made strict. No code changed."; both went through `record_failure` as an ordinary `tests_failed`, back to QUEUED, and were claimed again on the unchanged prompt; each burned attempt 2 (T337 also attempt 3) on the same gap, about 8M tokens, before going BLOCKED at the cap, and came back only through `--requeue --plan-fix` (D-2832, D-2843). D-1058's `plan_gap_failure` covers only verify's path problems ("<path>: not owned by T###"), never the worker's own report. Choice: (a) block at once for a plan fix, not (b) a QUEUED hold until the task's plan fingerprint changes on `main`. (a) reuses D-677's whole `--plan-fix` path and D-583's plain `--requeue` (decision new on `main` and in the task's `decisions` list, the task's entry or prompt changed since the attempt started, once per decision, lease checks) and STATUS.md's existing BLOCKED line and D-1869's outbox pattern, adds no state key and no claim-time read of `main`; (b) would need a new held mark, a fingerprint read before every claim and a new STATUS line, and would free the task on any prompt change, such as a prompt-wide regeneration, which D-677 already learned to refuse. How: a structured signal, never free-text matching of stored text. `kit/prompts/TEMPLATE.md` tells the worker that if, and only if, the task cannot pass without a change the plan forbids it to make (a file or test it must change is owned by another task, naming the file and that task; a test or spec line it must satisfy contradicts another, citing both as file:line; or the work cannot fit the task's budget), it stops, commits nothing more and opens its report with one line `PLAN GAP: <file:line> <owner or contradiction> <the smallest plan change>`, followed by the command and output that show it; a hard or large change, a failing test or bug in its own files, or running short of time is an ordinary failure, and a plan-gap report still uses up the attempt. The session's step 5 (`.github/workflows/backup-runner.yml`, `BUILD_BRIEF.md:581` edited in place, line count kept) hands in with `--outcome plan_gap` only when the reviewer subagent, asked to check it, confirms the cited ownership or contradiction (else `tests_failed`), and passes every `--log` text through a quoted heredoc (`--log "$(cat <<'EOF'` ... `EOF` `)"`), never inside double quotes, since a report's backticks or `$` would otherwise run as commands. `cycle.session_outcome` (called only by `--after`, on the session's own `--log`, before a held pre-hand-in gate's output is appended, D-1300) also turns a `tests_failed` into `plan_gap` when the log opens with `PLAN GAP:` (any case), or, as a narrow documented fallback for a session that forgot the outcome, when its first sentence (up to the first ". " or line end) matches `PLAN_GAP_PHRASES`: "a/the plan change must", or "needs a plan/harness change/task/fix" or "needs plan/harness fix" with the plural "needs" right after a task id, "it", "this task", "the task" or a ";", ":" or "," (so a gerund clause such as a task goal's "adding one needs a harness task" does not match), and the sentence has none of `PLAN_GAP_HEDGES` (not, no, never, n't, but, thought, think(s), if, whether, maybe, might, goal, says, said, a quotation mark or backtick), so a denial ("does not need a plan change"), a doubt ("thought it needs a plan change but ...") or a quoted goal stays an ordinary failure. Both reports above put the phrase after their first sentence, so the fallback would not have caught them: the marker is the channel, the fallback only a net. "not owned by T###" alone is not read, since that is verify's path problem (D-1058). The cycle acts only on the outcome, so a stored `last_failure` carried into a later log (a resync's lost result, D-891) never blocks a task. A RUNNER_WORKER_CMD result file does not pass through `session_outcome` (its command reports `plan_gap` itself); that is harmless, since no session writes it. `cycle.record_plan_gap` counts the attempt (the 3-attempt cap still holds: a worker that keeps reporting gaps still runs out) and sets the task BLOCKED with `reason` "plan gap reported: <first 600 characters>; fix the plan ..., then run `python3 -m runner --requeue T### --plan-fix D-### --reason ...` (D-2859)" and the whole report as `last_failure`, so the attempt after the fix reads it; a `resync` mark goes as in `record_failure`; `_plan_gap_outbox` writes the outbox item `T###-plan-gap` (kind `blocked`, the report and both ways back), so the overseer hears of it in the same cycle as an owned gap (D-1869). FIX-MAIN is not in the plan, so its `plan_gap` stays an ordinary failure with no outbox item. `plan_fix_precheck` accepts such a task with attempts left (`_plan_gap_blocked`), and `requeue_plan_fix` brings it back with the attempts it has left (on Opus from the second attempt, D-2474). A plain `--requeue T### --reason` also lifts it while attempts remain, the cheap way back from a mistaken report: the attempt stays counted and the re-queue is kept in `requeues`; at the cap only D-677's `--plan-fix` applies, unchanged. STATUS.md's "Needs attention" lists every BLOCKED task with its reason. The TEMPLATE change regenerates every prompt (`scripts/gen_prompts.py`, one added sentence each); the generator refreshes the stored `budget.context_pct` of the tasks whose measurement moved more than its drift allowance: T012 16 to 20, T016 22 to 26, T061 21 to 25, T100 41 to 45 (QUEUED) and T191 20 to 24 (this change), T081 25 to 29, T244 35 to 39 and T374 10 to 14 (already drifted on `main`), all within their limits (`gen_prompts.py --check --strict` names only T246); DONE T246's stored 48 is kept (it measures 57, the known `--strict` failure, D-2821), its prompt rendered with it. The regeneration also touches the prompt files of the tasks in flight when it was made (T327, T209, T383 at 05:39Z) by the one template passage only; their kit/tasks.json entries are untouched, which is what the no-edit-in-flight rule protects, and a worker already holds its prompt, so this is allowed. Kind: harness change. Source: `runner/cycle.py` `session_outcome`, `record_plan_gap`, `_plan_gap_outbox`, `_after_worker`, `requeue_refusal`, `requeue`, `plan_fix_precheck`; `runner/__main__.py` `after`; `kit/prompts/TEMPLATE.md`; `.github/workflows/backup-runner.yml` step 5; `BUILD_BRIEF.md:581`; tests in `tests/test_failure_drills.py`.

Choice: a deliberate, logged exception: only this one test file compiles `lib.rs`; it never calls `mint` (the registry is built and its kinds read, and the no-handler check never touches a pick), its process is a test binary with fake settings and no live key, and the once-per-process `OnceLock` holds there as in the worker. The alternative, moving `worker_registry` out of `lib.rs` into a file without the minters, would still need `register_handlers`, which takes the release mint first by design (SEC-030). A new test file that compiles `lib.rs` needs its own entry. Kind: build. Source: `tests/integration/tests/architecture.rs` `MINTS`, `app/server/src/lib.rs` `release_minter`, `session_minter`.
- **D-2943** Question (plan change outside the runner, November 11, 2026; number set by the overseer; T316, T165, T302, T251; independent review fixes A to D applied; D-2206, D-2741, D-336, D-1111, D-1687, D-1310; PICK-041, BIZ-022; TD-BIZ-43, TD-BIZ-32): T316's attempt 1 stopped with a reviewer-confirmed `PLAN GAP:` report: nothing links a business to a stored record that holds a name. Checked on `main` (`015e158f`): `businesses.business` and `businesses.signup` hold no name or license number (`migrations/0055_businesses_records.sql`, `0119`, `0120`); `licensing.agency_record` keeps only number, class, status and issue date (`migrations/0050_licensing_imports.sql:22`, `ROC_HEADER` at `app/licensing/src/imports.rs:18`); `licensing.city_license_entry` has names but no business ID, and `city_standing` matches names the caller passes and stores no match (`app/licensing/src/service.rs:375`); `licensing.license_check` links a business to its ROC number only after a daily check; `businesses::api::holding` takes the names from the caller because no table holds them (D-2741, `app/businesses/src/holding.rs:8`); and nothing in `main` or the plan reads names from the state record at sign-up (the sign-up form, `app/portals/templates/business_signup.html`, has no name field). D-2206 (2) assumed a license-record name that is not stored, and T316's own goal forbade storing one, so T316 could never pass as planned. What T316 needs the name for: the public business name shown to the homeowner in the LIST reply (T317, TXT-031) and the who's-calling text (T318, TXT-027), and later on the quote cards (PICK-041, IC-71), screened against phone numbers, links and channel directions (BIZ-022, D-336). Options weighed: (a) callers pass the name in: not viable, since T317 (an inbound text) and T318 (a release) hold only business IDs and have nowhere to get a name; (b) keep the license-record source: extend the ROC import to keep each record's business name and DBA and store the business's matched record at sign-up; rejected: it changes the done `licensing` import (T036) and its list fixtures, keeps the names of every licensee on the daily list when only the signed-up businesses' names are shown, against the import's verification-only minimum (LIC-010; `migrations/0050_licensing_imports.sql:6`), and still leaves the no-license case on a name match nobody stores; (c) store the name the business gives at sign-up: chosen. The spec settles that this is allowed: the business record holds the business name and ROC number (`sources/01_spec/Havasu_Home_Quotes_Technical_Blueprint_v9.3.md:90`); the contact vault and PRIV-001 cover homeowner details only (`sources/01_spec/Havasu_Home_Quotes_Technical_Blueprint_v9.3.md:81`, `docs/spec/privacy.md:5`), so the "no name stored (PRIV-001)" comments in `migrations/0055_businesses_records.sql` and `app/businesses/src/holding.rs` over-read it; BIZ-022 already treats the public name as something checked and "returned to the business with the reason", which is a name the business gives; and T316's "nothing is stored" rule came from D-2206, not the spec. No third party's personal name is stored: the city list's owner name is never copied, and the business stores only the names it goes by. Choice: T165 (QUEUED; owns the sign-up form, `app/portals/templates/business_signup.html` and `app/portals/src/business_signup.rs`, both on `main` from T193, T155 and T199, and `app/businesses/src/links.rs`, `tests/integration/tests/business_links.rs` and `migrations/0160_businesses_links.sql`, not yet on `main`) also asks the business name (required) and trade name or DBA (optional), each at most 200 characters and screened by `screen_public_name`, adds `businesses.business_name` (one row per business, no owner name, phone, email or address) to its own migration, so no migration number or serial order changes, with an explicit `GRANT SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE` (a save replaces the row; migration 0110's default for `businesses` gives only `SELECT, INSERT`), and exports `businesses::api::save_business_name`, which screens again, writes or replaces the row and audits by field name only; it also takes over `app/businesses/src/holding.rs` (T374, DONE, now listed in T165's deps so the file has one owner at a time) only to correct the stale module doc at line 8 ("No business table holds a license number or a name (PRIV-001)"), doc lines only (`budget.files` 6 to 7, `budget.lines` 400 to 480; BIZ-022, D-336 and this decision join its lists; its title names the business name). T302 (QUEUED, already after T165) calls it on the sign-up `POST`, and for a no-license business passes the same stored business name and trade name as the `CityRecord` names (`holding`'s `Known.city_names`) to LIC-011's city-list match (`sources/01_spec/Changes_Since_v9.3_AUTHORITATIVE.md:37`, D-255); no match follows LIC-011, BIZ-003 and BIZ-016 (pending until a later daily list matches; a flagged sign-up waits in needs review). An owner-name-only match (D-255 counts one) cannot be repeated later from what is stored, since the owner name is not kept: the daily re-match after sign-up sees only the business and trade names, so such a business shows `Pending` there; logged, not changed. T251 (QUEUED, already after T165) now says that the `Known.city_names` it passes for a no-license business are these stored names, without which `holding` reads the business as `Pending` and it gets no card (goal sentence only, budget unchanged; this decision joins its `decisions`). T316 becomes a read of that row: the trade name when given, else the business name, screened again, left out with one Low alert (business ID only) on a failing or missing name; it reads nothing through `licensing` and adds nothing; it now depends on T165 (no cycle: T165's deps are T207, T193, T155, T164 and T384; T317 and T318 already wait for T316). TD-BIZ-43 is reworded to the stored names (the record and city-list cases go, since no record name exists); TD-BIZ-32 gains T165's sign-up name case and covers BIZ-022, so that case also appears in the prompts of T215 and T228, which list TD-BIZ-32 and both run after T165 (regenerated; the case is T165's to build). Not changed here: a portal edit of the name (still not built, as D-2206 said); IC-71 (the quote page's cards) can now take its name from `public_names`. Open, and required before T302 can be claimed: for an ROC business, BIZ-016's name-mismatch check waits on a sign-up read of the business's own state record, and that same read is what the identity chain's `RecordContacts` (BIZ-002) need, but no task produces them: `licensing` drops contacts and names at import (`migrations/0050_licensing_imports.sql:6`) and `LicenseSource` has no record-detail call (`app/adapters/src/license_sources.rs:17`, only the daily list and the live status lookup); until that read exists an ROC business could type another business's name and it would be shown. A follow-up plan change for that sign-up record read is required before T302 is claimed (the overseer's next change). This decision joins T316's, T165's, T302's and T251's `decisions`, so `--requeue T316 --plan-fix D-2943` applies (D-677, D-2859). Kind: plan change. Owner approval: not needed (BUILD_BRIEF section 16); the change of source from the license record to the name the business gives is listed for Casey. Reason: T316 could never pass as planned, and the spec puts the business name on the business record. Source: `app/businesses/src/holding.rs:8`, `migrations/0050_licensing_imports.sql:22`, `migrations/0050_licensing_imports.sql:35`, `app/licensing/src/service.rs:375`, `app/licensing/src/imports.rs:18`, `app/adapters/src/license_sources.rs:17`, `app/server/src/lib.rs:277`, `sources/01_spec/Changes_Since_v9.3_AUTHORITATIVE.md:37`, `sources/01_spec/Havasu_Home_Quotes_Technical_Blueprint_v9.3.md:90`, `docs/spec/businesses.md:26`.
- **D-2954** Question (plan change outside the runner, November 11, 2026; number set by the overseer; new T385; T302, T134, T371, T165; independent review fixes 1 to 7 applied; D-2943, D-059, D-366, D-493, D-1699, D-1712, D-255, D-145; BIZ-002, BIZ-016, LIC-006, LIC-008, LIC-010, LIC-011, LIC-048; new TD-LIC-30, TD-BIZ-49): D-2943 left open that no task reads a business's own public record at sign-up, which BIZ-016's "record or name mismatch" flag needs for an ROC business (the name it typed, stored by T165, against the record's names) and which the identity chain's `RecordContacts` need for every business (`app/businesses/src/identity.rs:44`; BIZ-002 sends the code to the phone, then the email, then the address on the state record, or on the city list for a no-license or pest business, D-059, LIC-048). Checked on `main` (`9d873d46`): the daily imports keep no ROC name, phone, email or address and no city-list contact (`migrations/0050_licensing_imports.sql:6`, `app/licensing/src/imports.rs:9`); the live lookup answers only Active, Inactive or Unknown (`app/licensing/src/handlers.rs:203`); `LicenseSource` has only the daily list and that lookup (`app/adapters/src/license_sources.rs:17`); no production code builds a license source; the settings parser refuses an unknown `ASKHAVA_*` key (`app/core/src/settings.rs:4`); and the license-source stand-in is the adapter's `file://` fixture directory, not `stand_ins/server.py`. What the spec settles, so no owner question is open: how a business proves it controls the license is BIZ-002's code to the record contact, never a typed one (`docs/spec/businesses.md:6`, `sources/01_spec/Havasu_Home_Quotes_Technical_Blueprint_v9.3.md:428`, `sources/01_spec/Changes_Since_v9.3_AUTHORITATIVE.md:93`); the blueprint looks the license up at sign-up as well as daily and at each pick (`sources/01_spec/Havasu_Home_Quotes_Technical_Blueprint_v9.3.md:194`); a name or record mismatch only sends the sign-up to Casey's review (`docs/spec/businesses.md:20`, D-145); record contacts are passed in by the caller and never stored (D-1699, D-1712); and the lists are for verification only (LIC-010, `sources/01_spec/Changes_Since_v9.3_AUTHORITATIVE.md:250`). Options weighed: (a) keep names and contacts at the daily import: rejected, as D-2943 rejected it for names: it keeps every licensee's details when only the signing-up business's are needed, and changes T036's done import; (b) one read of the business's own record when sign-up needs it, nothing kept: chosen. Choice: new harness task T385 (harness only because it edits T227's `tests/e2e/webserver.ts`; Opus review; after T165, T176, T036, T081, T227; 8 files, 650 lines): (1) `adapters` gains a second read-only trait, `LicenseRecords::lookup_record(list, number)` on `LicenseLists`, so `LicenseSource` and its test fakes are untouched; (2) `ASKHAVA_LICENSE_BASE_URL` joins the settings parser's keys as an optional typed field (D-493); requiring it in the parser would break the done settings and adapter-config tests that build `test` and `live` settings, so the composition that builds the source requires it in `test` and `live` and, absent in `ci` or `dev`, every read is `Unreadable` (review fix 1, placed at the composition rather than the parser for that reason); (3) `licensing::api::read_own_record` makes one call and reads one row of a fixed record format into `OwnRecord` (no `Debug`, contacts as `SecretString`), `NotFound` only for a 404 and everything else `Unreadable` (fix 5; the fixture reader maps a missing file to 404, which fails safe to review), an `Unreadable` read raising one Normal `licensing.record_unreadable` alert a day with no values (fix 5, as LIC-008 treats an unreadable page); `names_agree` uses LIC-011's existing comparison, which does not drop "LLC" or "Inc", so such a difference goes to review (safe, more reviews; fix 7); the qualifying party and any owner name are never read; `city_match_number` takes the business's entered city license number when given and a matching row agrees (`numbers_agree`, `app/licensing/src/rules.rs:201`), and otherwise gives a number only when the matching rows carry exactly one (fix 3); `bound_roc_number` reads the number `check_license` (`app/licensing/src/service.rs:288`) recorded; (4) one composite, `businesses::api::signup_record(conn, source, business)`, that takes no number from the request: the ROC number bound at the license match, or for a city-list business the stored names and stored city license number, one read, then the name flag, the contacts, the address for `RecordSeen` and the masked contact, or `NoContact`, `Unreadable` or `Unbound` (fixes 2 and 7); (5) fake fixtures: one ROC record, the daily `roc` list with that license Active R-37 and a `city` list, so list and record agree in the e2e (fix 4), and `ASKHAVA_LICENSE_BASE_URL` in the e2e start-up. Nothing from the record is written to any table, audit row or log line (LIC-010, PRIV-016). T302 now depends on T385: it binds the ROC number server-side once, through `check_license` at the license match, and every later read (name flag, license match, identity screens) goes through `signup_record`, so a number posted later changes nothing (fix 2; TD-BIZ-49 gains that case); reads happen only on screens that need the name check or a contact, inside T089's sign-up limits; `NoContact` is `no_record_contact` (needs review); `Unreadable` and `Unbound` change nothing and ask the business to try again; it gains BIZ-002, this decision and the TD-BIZ-49 cases (budget unchanged). T165 also keeps an entered city license number on `businesses.business_name` (`city_license_number`) through `save_business_name`, so `signup_record` reads it by business ID. T371 names the `ASKHAVA_LICENSE_BASE_URL` key and the list names `roc` and `city`, and now follows T385 (fix 4). T134 (the real client) now follows T385 and answers `lookup_record` from that license's row of the ROC posted download list (`sources/01_spec/Changes_Since_v9.3_AUTHORITATIVE.md:250`) or the ROC's public detail page, mapping the six-digit number to the page's own license ID, a field the source does not publish left empty (fix 6). Known limits (fix 6, from public descriptions of the Arizona ROC detail page: business name, six-digit license number, phone, city, state and ZIP, qualifying party; no email, maybe no street address, no DBA): with no record email the chain goes from the phone straight to the letter; with no street address there is no letter step, so a business whose record phone is a landline or can't get texts waits in review; with no DBA on the record, a business that typed only its trade name goes to review; so many ROC sign-ups may land in Casey's review, listed for him plainly. Also: a city-list match with no single number gives no record contact (review); a record phone of unknown kind is tried by text first. Open, no owner: BIZ-026's resume when a later daily list shows a new record contact needs a daily caller of `businesses::api::resume_on_new_record` with the record seen (D-1709 left it for the daily list worker; T371's goal does not include it); with T385 that caller would make one `signup_record` read per waiting sign-up; for the overseer's next plan change. This decision joins T385's, T302's, T134's, T371's and T165's `decisions`. Kind: plan change. Owner approval: not needed (BUILD_BRIEF section 16); listed for Casey. Reason: without this read an ROC business could type another business's name and have it shown, and no identity code has a record contact to go to, so T302 could not be built as planned. Source: `docs/spec/businesses.md:6`, `docs/spec/businesses.md:20`, `app/businesses/src/identity.rs:44`, `app/adapters/src/license_sources.rs:17`, `app/core/src/settings.rs:4`, `app/licensing/src/handlers.rs:203`, `app/licensing/src/imports.rs:9`, `app/licensing/src/rules.rs:201`, `app/licensing/src/rules.rs:211`, `app/licensing/src/service.rs:288`, `migrations/0050_licensing_imports.sql:6`, `sources/01_spec/Havasu_Home_Quotes_Technical_Blueprint_v9.3.md:194`, `sources/01_spec/Havasu_Home_Quotes_Technical_Blueprint_v9.3.md:428`, `sources/01_spec/Changes_Since_v9.3_AUTHORITATIVE.md:93`, `sources/01_spec/Changes_Since_v9.3_AUTHORITATIVE.md:250`.
- **D-2928** Question (T278, D-1842, D-1811 (1), D-1817, D-1818; JOB-015, JOB-016, JOB-017, JOB-027, TXT-029, TXT-040, WORD-028, WORD-029): what do the new homeowner templates say, and where does MORE's full list live? Choice: six keys in `app/messaging/templates/en.json` and `es.json` (Spanish drafts): `check_in_day3` and `check_in_day14` open with JOB-015's first line word for word, then one line naming the business she picked for request `{job}` ("Checking in again" at day 14); `check_in_more` is MORE's (or MÁS's) full list, one line per answer (DONE, PROBLEM with optional words, NO, LATER, ONGOING, OTHER; LISTO, PROBLEMA, NO, MÁS TARDE, CONTINUO, OTRO in Spanish, the words `jobs::api::parse_answer` reads), a separate template because JOB-015 sends the list only on MORE (its sending is T277's reply dispatch); `feedback_request` thanks her for the update, asks how it went, links her private `/f/` page (T230) and says what she writes stays private unless she checks the share box (JOB-017; no reward, nothing about quote order); `unreachable_closed` is JOB-027's sentence exactly; `emailed_question` is D-1817's "Text back YES or NO" ("Responda SÍ o NO" in Spanish, as D-1817 chose; TD-CON-24's guard passes unchanged). All are `Shape::Capped` in `quotes`' `UPDATE_TEXTS`; `problem_reply` stays in `NOT_UPDATE_TEXTS` where T213 put it (a template is in one list only). Cold read and copy panel (WORD-028, WORD-029; a fresh reviewer that saw only the copy): applied "ONGOING: they've started a regular service."; the feedback text's "You can tell Ask Hava here" to "Tell us here" and "tick" to "check" (Arizona usage) with "What you write" for the unclear "It"; Spanish "nunca se comunicaron con usted" for "nunca le contactaron", "¿Todavía no terminan?", "LISTO: ya terminaron el trabajo.", "Cuéntenos aquí" and "correo electrónico" (not postal mail). Not applied: LUEGO for MÁS TARDE (the parser reads MÁS TARDE, D-1809) and a Spanish verb other than "Responda" in the 72-hour question (D-1817 chose it). No new AI-smell pattern: the flagged lines were regional and clarity choices, not machine phrasing. Kind: build. Owner approval: Casey's standing delegation. Reason: the texts must reach her in her words. Source: `kit/prompts/T278.md`, `docs/spec/lifecycle.md:19`, `docs/spec/lifecycle.md:31`.
- **D-2929** Question (T278, D-1811 (1), D-1821; JOB-017, SEC-037): how does `intake`'s sender send the new texts, and where does the feedback link come from? Choice: `JOB_TEXT_TEMPLATES` adds `check_in_day3`, `check_in_day14`, `check_in_more`, `feedback_request`, `problem_reply`, `unreachable_closed` and `emailed_question` (13 in all), so none is refused as a bad payload. `LINKED_TEMPLATES` now names each linked template's page: `/q/` for `first_quote` and `all_quotes_in`, `/f/` for `feedback_request`, on the brand's domain, with the token `jobs::api::quote_token::issue` makes in the send's transaction (the feedback page resolves the quote-page token, T230); issuing revokes the earlier quote-page link, as every linked send already does, so the newest text's link is the live one. `job_text_body` also fills `{business}` from the event's `values.business` (the business's public name; JOB-027's texts), never a homeowner detail. Kind: build. Owner approval: Casey's standing delegation. Source: `app/intake/src/job_texts.rs`.
- **D-2930** Question (T278, D-1811 (2), D-2015 (1), D-1812; JOB-015): when does the release queue the check-ins, given that nothing moves a job to Connected yet? Choice: the release's claim transaction (`record`) calls `picks::api::check_ins_at_release`, which queues `jobs::api::schedule_check_ins` only when the job is Connected, from the release time and `quotes::api::earliest_visit` (new: the picked business's quote's earliest visit date, as the start of that Arizona day; none without a date). A job not Connected gets none: check-ins are tagged with the job's version and `run_check_in` sends only at that version, so ones queued before the move to Connected would never send. The task that builds the move to Connected (D-2015 (1), no owner yet) must move the job before the release's claim, or call `check_ins_at_release` in its own move's transaction; until then no production release queues check-ins. TD-JOB-13's release case calls `check_ins_at_release` directly on the database: a `ReleaseProof` can only be minted in `server`, which the integration crate does not depend on. Kind: build and plan gap. Owner approval: Casey's standing approval for plan improvements through the normal review gate. Source: `app/picks/src/release.rs`, `app/jobs/src/followups.rs`, D-2015.
- **D-2931** Question (T278, D-1818; JOB-027, CON-021, CON-028, QH-001): how does `close_unreachable` tell the homeowner? Choice: in the close's own transaction, after the move to Closed and the line close, one `jobs.homeowner_text` event for `unreachable_closed` at the closed job's version (final, so the sender still sends it, QH-007), values the job number and the business's public name, dedupe key `jobs.homeowner_text.<job>.unreachable_closed`; `intake`'s sender then applies consent, opt-out and quiet hours, as for every job text. A job that moved on, or a refund that is not `Succeeded`, queues nothing. The 72-hour `emailed_question` send stays T281's. Size: about 750 inserted lines over 15 files, the 5 owned and 10 shared (the prompt's budget is 450 lines and 5 files), mostly the integration test's seeding (a carded, quoted job; a paid pick with its charge and line) and the two template files; no case was dropped to fit. Kind: build. Owner approval: Casey's standing delegation. Source: `app/picks/src/unreachable_refund.rs`.
- **D-2944** Question (T331, fifth audit AH-004; SEC-017, PICK-022, FEE-029; D-2289, D-2073): how does a signed `payment_intent.succeeded` whose `metadata.pick_id` is missing, empty or not a UUID stop being dropped before any database read? Choice: `dispatch_of` (`app/payments/src/routes.rs`) maps such a success to the existing `Dispatch::Unreadable`, so it takes the same path as D-2073's unreadable events: one `payments.webhook_event` row and one High `payments.stripe_event_unreadable` alert with no subject in that row's transaction, answered 200, once per event ID (a resend finds the row and changes nothing). Nothing is released: no pick is read from untrusted metadata, and the nightly reconcile (FEE-029) still matches the charge by its PaymentIntent. The route's unit test `an_event_without_a_pick_changes_nothing` pinned the old answer (200 with no database); renamed `an_event_without_a_pick_releases_nothing_and_reaches_the_database`, it now expects 500 from its unreachable database (the event is to be recorded, so Stripe must resend) and still nothing released; its lazy pool fails at the first read, so TD-FEE-53 (`td_fee_53_a_success_naming_no_pick_is_recorded_not_released`) guards the recording itself, including a `pick_id` that is a JSON number or `null`. Reason: a signed money event must leave a record and reach Casey (D-2289). Source: `kit/prompts/T331.md`, `app/payments/src/routes.rs:254`.
- **D-2945** Question (T331, fifth audit AH-005; FEE-052, SEC-017; D-2289, D-2290): which alert does a fraud warning raise when its pick has a `payments.pick_intent` row but no `payments.charge_evidence` row yet, and how is it kept to one across Stripe's resends? Choice: the event row's transaction rolls back, and `no_evidence_alert` raises `payments.fraud_warning` (`refunds::FRAUD_WARNING_ALERT`, the kind FEE-052's own alert already uses), High, subject `payments.pick_intent` and the pick (as `refunds` and `late` raise pick alerts), through `ops::api::raise_alert_once` on a fresh pool connection: its own short transaction, an advisory lock on kind and subject, and the check for an unresolved alert of that kind with that subject in the same transaction, so concurrent or repeated resends raise one. The route answers 500. Reusing the kind means an open FEE-052 alert on the pick (from T281's run of `early_fraud_warning`) also suppresses a new no-evidence alert, which is right: Casey is already looking at a fraud warning on that pick. It holds one way only: `refunds::early_fraud_warning` raises through plain `ops::api::raise_alert` (`app/payments/src/refunds.rs:80`), so once the evidence row appears and a resend runs it, Casey can get a second High `payments.fraud_warning` alert on the same pick while the no-evidence one is still open. That is accepted: the second alert marks a different step (the warning now acted on, a refund requested or Casey's decision awaited), and T331 does not change `refunds`. No new alert kind or constant. Reason: Casey hears of it once even if the evidence row never appears and Stripe's retries run out (D-2289). Source: `kit/prompts/T331.md`, `app/ops/src/api.rs:292`, `app/payments/src/refunds.rs:55`.
- **D-2946** Question (T331; FEE-052, SEC-017; D-2289, D-2073 (3)): what does a fraud warning whose PaymentIntent matches no `payments.pick_intent` write? Choice: `unmatched_warning` commits the event row with one High `payments.fraud_warning` alert with no subject (no record `payments` holds names the charge) in that row's transaction and enqueues nothing; it answers 200, and a resend finds the row and changes nothing. T259's `td_fee_43_an_unknown_object_changes_nothing` pinned the old silent answer for its `evt_FakeU6`; it now expects that event's row (3 rows, not 2) and the one alert, and every other effect unchanged, the only change D-2289 allows to T259's cases. Migration 0157 adds `quotes.quote.visit_schedule` with a `CHECK` that it is set only beside period `visit`; `save_quote` clears it before the upsert and sets it after, in the quote's transaction, so an edit from per visit to monthly never trips the check. - **D-2986** Question (plan change, November 11, 2026; number set by the overseer; `kit/runner.json`; D-2810, D-2462, D-620, D-515, D-723): Casey, in chat about 12:35Z on November 11, 2026: "If we can speed the build up without any issues let's do that. Use tokens effectively but dont worry about running out". Should the runner work four tasks at once? Evidence: since 06:30Z the pacer held a claim only 4 times (the five-hour placeholder ledger rarely binds), so the lanes, not the pacer, limit throughput; the week has about 62M tokens left before the Thursday 17:00Z reset, which four lanes will spend sooner, and Casey accepts that. Choice: `kit/runner.json` `lanes` 3 → 4, through a logged plan change as `BUILD_BRIEF.md:209` requires. Audit, repeated from D-2810 over `runner/`, `.github/workflows/` and `scripts/`: nothing assumes three lanes or caps the count. `runner/lanes.py` (`effective_lanes`, `free_lanes`, `claim_lane`, `refusal` against every task in flight, `strike` on any lane above 1), `runner/state.py` (`in_flight`, `run_lane`, `free_lanes`), `runner/cycle.py` (`refill_lanes`), `runner/__main__.py` (lost-race retries and refill at `lanes >= 2`), `scripts/check_state.py` (at most `lanes` live leases), `scripts/pacing.py` (`in_flight_tokens` sums every other IN_PROGRESS task) and `backup-runner.yml` (the gate's `range(1, lanes + 1)`, the per-lane concurrency group `backup-runner-lane-<n>` built from the lane, the hourly tick and the chain dispatching one run per free or refill lane) all take the count from the setting; no workflow input enumerates lanes. Only wording named the count: `BUILD_BRIEF.md:209`, `docs/governance.md:53`, `docs/architecture.md` (runner logic), `docs/ai-operating-manual.md:102` and `runner/state.py:12` now say 4 since D-2986 (line counts unchanged). Tests (a spec change to tests under CLAUDE.md rule 6; the covered set grows, nothing is weakened): new `tests/test_runner_four_lanes.py` runs the three-lane drills over four lanes (four claims on non-overlapping tasks and a fifth run claiming nothing, `check_state` clean at 4 and flagging 4 live leases at 3; a lane-4 candidate refused for overlapping or a different stage against any of three tasks in flight, a compatible one claimed; `refill_lanes` naming up to four lanes; two harness-type strikes on lane 4 falling back to one lane, one strike each on lanes 2, 3 and 4 not; MERGE_PENDING in three lanes leaving only lane 4 to claim; pacing reserving the estimates of three other running attempts; the gate's lane pick with four lanes and while fallen back); `tests/test_runner_lanes.py:208` now allows 1 to 4, the counts the drills cover; `tests/test_runner_model_window.py:82`, which pins the locked switches, now expects 4 (the one value this decision changes). Kept unchanged: `lanes_fallback` after two harness-type failures in a row on one lane above 1 (`STRIKES_TO_FALL_BACK`, `runner/lanes.py:38`) is the safety net, and it drops the build to one lane by itself until `python3 -m runner --restore-lanes`; the owned-path overlap refusal, the same-stage rule and the lone cleanup task (D-620); FIX-MAIN's reserved fix lane outside the count (D-630). Risks, accepted: merge contention rises with lanes (more update-merge rounds, more conflicts that are not pure insertions, such as `Cargo.toml` and migration numbers, with four branches open; the hand-in merge of D-2798 trims the rounds), and the week's tokens run out sooner, which Casey accepted. Rollback: the same one-line change back to 3 (or fewer) through a logged plan change; tasks in flight finish normally. Reason: Casey asked to speed the build up and the lanes are the limiter; the lane machinery has no count limit and the drills now prove four. - **D-3030** Question (harness change, November 11, 2026; number reserved from the live counter): since about 13:48Z on November 11, GitHub-hosted runners cannot resolve the Ubuntu mirrors (`Temporary failure resolving 'security.ubuntu.com'`, `archive.ubuntu.com`, `azure.archive.ubuntu.com`). The "Chromium and its system libraries" step in `.github/workflows/a11y.yml` (Ally) and in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (E2e) runs `npx playwright install-deps chromium` on a browser-cache hit or `npx playwright install --with-deps chromium` on a miss; apt then waits about 12 minutes and exits 100, so Ally and E2e fail before any test runs. The logs show every library Chromium needs already at "the newest version" on the runner image; only nine optional font packages are new (fonts-ipafont-gothic, fonts-freefont-ttf, fonts-tlwg-loma-otf, fonts-unifont, fonts-wqy-zenhei, xfonts-cyrillic, xfonts-encodings, xfonts-scalable, xfonts-utils). T384's attempt was lost to it (runner log: "Ci: failure; E2e: failure; Ally: failure"), and every hand-in waits on Ally and E2e green. How does the browser setup survive a mirror outage without weakening a test? Choice: the same step body in both workflows (name, the `actions/cache` browser cache and every pinned action unchanged): (1) apt's waits are bounded by `/etc/apt/apt.conf.d/99-askhava-bounded` (`Acquire::Retries "2"`, `Acquire::http::Timeout` and `Acquire::https::Timeout` "20", `DPkg::Lock::Timeout "120"`); (2) on a cache miss the browser alone is downloaded first (`npx playwright install chromium`, Playwright's CDN, not the Ubuntu mirrors), so `--with-deps` becomes browser then libraries, the same result; (3) `npx playwright install-deps chromium` is tried up to three times, each under `timeout --kill-after=15s 150s`, with pauses of 15 and 45 seconds and a `pkill -x apt-get` after a failed try so a stray apt cannot hold the lock; (4) a launch check always runs (`node -e` with `@playwright/test`'s `chromium.launch()`, a new page, `setContent`, close) and fails the step if Chromium cannot start or render; (5) if every install-deps try failed but the launch check passed, the step prints a `::warning::` that the optional fonts were not installed and the suite runs. The step gains `timeout-minutes: 15` (worst case about 10 minutes, inside the jobs' 30). The test commands, configs and axe rules are untouched. Risk, and why the fallback cannot hide a missing required library: Playwright checks the host's shared libraries when it launches Chromium and refuses to start with "Host system is missing dependencies"; any absent library Chromium links against also fails the dynamic loader; either way the launch check exits 1 and the step fails as before. What it can let through is the optional fonts: CJK, Thai, Unifont, FreeFont and X11 Cyrillic and scalable fonts. The pages are English and Spanish, rendered with the image's default Latin fonts, which are installed; axe works on the DOM and computed styles, so a missing CJK or Thai font changes no result; a reflow or spacing test could only differ if a page used one of those scripts, which none does. The warning makes every such run visible. Tested here: actionlint 1.7.7 with shellcheck 0.10.0 over `.github/workflows/*.yml` reports the same 8 pre-existing infos and warnings before and after (none in the changed steps); the step body, run under `bash --noprofile --norc -eo pipefail` with stubbed `npx`, `sudo`, `sleep` and `node`, takes the three paths as meant (install-deps fails three times and the launch passes: warning, exit 0; install-deps passes: no warning, exit 0; install-deps fails and the launch fails: exit 1); the `node -e` launch check against `@playwright/test` 1.64.1 in a `"type": "module"` package exits 0 with Chromium present and 1 with `PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH` pointing at nothing. Ci's E2e path filter already lists `.github/workflows/(ci|a11y)\.yml`, so this change runs E2e and Ally on its own PR. `kit/plan.lock` does not cover `.github/` and is unchanged; `docs/architecture.md` does not describe the step. Changed: `.github/workflows/a11y.yml`, `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, `docs/decisions.md`, `docs/for-casey-review.md`. Numbered by: reserved with --reserve-decision (D-1058). Reason: a mirror outage outside the build should cost no attempt when everything Chromium needs is already on the image; a launch check proves that on every run, so the gate stays as strict as the tests behind it. Source: `BUILD_BRIEF.md:69`; `BUILD_BRIEF.md:261`; `BUILD_BRIEF.md:424`; D-1058; D-1328; D-1986.
- **D-3024** Question (plan change outside the runner, November 11, 2026; T214 BLOCKED on attempt 1 with a `PLAN GAP:` report its reviewer confirmed; PICK-050, PICK-037, TXT-001, TXT-044; D-446, D-493, D-491; TD-PICK-43, TD-PICK-33, TD-BIZ-14, TD-WORD-38, TD-TXT-01, TD-INT-08): T214's goal puts the pick notice's "Can't take it" link in "the pick notice composer `app/picks/src/confirm.rs`", but `confirm.rs` only names the two template IDs (`app/picks/src/confirm.rs:41` to `:44`); the notice's values are built in `run_pick_notice` (`app/picks/src/handlers.rs:73` to `:76`, T063's) and its words are the shared `pick_notice` and `pick_notice_emergency` keys (`app/messaging/templates/en.json:322` and `:327`, `es.json:394` and `:400`), which the shared-path rule lets a task only add to. Each only gains a fake `cant_take` value (`td_pick_33` the appended sentence, still exact); every other line stays byte-identical and no assertion is removed or loosened, so none is a loosening. Not affected: `business_consent.rs:353` lists IDs only; `job_timers.rs`, `pick_aftermath.rs`, `close_cancel.rs`, `emergency.rs`, `prop_consent_first.rs` and the other `render` callers name fixed other IDs; `confirm_window.rs` checks only `template`, `window` and `job`; `auto_confirm.rs` counts notices; `text_retries.rs` queues by ID with nothing filled (`email.rs:349`); `emergency_emails.rs` builds its subject without the registry; the Python scans (`tests/docs/test_template_scan.py`, `test_no_phone_numbers_in_templates.py`, `test_brand_literals.py`, `test_word_022_phrases.py`) fill only brand tokens and leave other `{name}`s (`scripts/brand.py:136`); `twin/` keeps its own templates. TD-PICK-43's pick-notice half: T214 proves the value and the page; T386 proves the rendered line, in one new test in `business_notices.rs` that checks both the plain and the HTML body hold "Can't take it:" and the address. - **D-3018** Question (plan change outside the runner, November 11, 2026; numbered by: max(`next_decision` 2997, main's highest D-3007 + 1, open PR highest (`claude/plan-four-lanes`, D-2986) + 1, in-flight `decision_ids` max 2996 + 1) + 10 = D-3018; T333 BLOCKED on attempt 1 with a `PLAN GAP:` report its reviewer confirmed (D-2859); FEE-026, FEE-028, FEE-053, FEE-022; D-2303, D-1836, D-2072): T333 owns only `refunds.rs`, `refund_stripe.rs`, `refund_lifecycle.rs` and `refund_amounts.rs`, but D-2303's check has two more places to reach. (1) The webhook path: `refund_event` re-reads a `succeeded` refund with `fetch_refund` and keeps only its state (`app/payments/src/routes.rs:398` to `:399`), then calls `refund_succeeded(pool, refund, now)` with the `re_…` alone (`:412`; `app/payments/src/refunds.rs:559`), so a webhook-driven success is booked at the charge whatever Stripe refunded; `refund_succeeded` cannot read the amount itself (it has no Stripe client). (2) The "refunded in full" notice is not `payments`': it is `picks`' `unreachable_refunded` business text, queued by `decide_at_96_hours` whenever `payments::api::refund_state` reads `Succeeded` (`app/picks/src/unreachable_refund.rs:363`, `:369`), so a mismatched or foreign-currency refund still sends it. Both checked on `main` (`6cc6ce4c`); the worker's commit was not pushed, so the check is against `main`'s code. Which `picks` read decides the notice? `refund_state` cannot: D-2303 keeps the refund state machine, a mismatched refund must still close the job, and D-2303 books a foreign-currency refund and a refund whose amount is missing on both reads the same way (at the charge, with the same `payments.refund_amount_unconfirmed` alert) yet sends the notice only for the second, so neither the ledger nor an open alert tells them apart; the tests of T191, T270 and T278 refund through fakes whose provided `send_refund` reports no amount (`app/adapters/src/payments.rs:174`) and whose `read_refund` answers `NotSent` (`:189`), and they expect the notice (`tests/integration/tests/unreachable_refund.rs:305`, `tests/integration/tests/unreachable_refund_states.rs:37`). A migration storing the check's outcome would renumber every queued migration after it (V9). Choice: T333 also owns `app/payments/src/routes.rs` and `app/picks/src/unreachable_refund.rs`, each for one function. In `routes.rs` only `refund_event` changes: `refund_succeeded` takes the re-read `Refund`, and the `Succeeded` arm passes it, so the webhook books and alerts as the request path does (its `use` line and describing `//!`, `///` lines may follow). That `Refund` counts as D-2303's re-read: a missing amount is booked at the charge with the unconfirmed alert and nothing is fetched again. The third caller, `run_refund_check` (`app/payments/src/refunds.rs:661`), passes the `Refund` it fetched; the owned `refund_lifecycle.rs` calls (`:303`, `:305`) change only to pass a `Refund`, no expected value changing. A present amount with a missing currency is unconfirmed, as a missing amount is: booked at the charge with the unconfirmed alert, never at the reported figure, and `refund_in_full` answers `true` for it. A new `payments` read `refund_in_full(pool, stripe, pick)` in `refunds.rs`, exported through `api.rs`, answers `false` only on positive evidence: the ledger holds the pick's refund at an amount other than the charge, or a re-read of its `re_…` with `fetch_refund` reports a currency other than `usd` or a `usd` amount other than the charge; a missing amount or currency, or a re-read failing with `AdapterError::NotSent` (what the provided `read_refund` answers, `app/adapters/src/payments.rs:189`, so the test fakes), answers `true` (the request was for the whole charge, D-2303); any other read error is `Err(MoneyEventError::Stripe)`, never `true`, since a foreign-currency refund must not be announced and nothing stored tells it from a missing amount. In `unreachable_refund.rs` only `decide_at_96_hours` changes (a private helper may join it): it calls `refund_in_full` before `close_unreachable`, so an error returns before anything closes and the next run retries (the existing finish-on-next-run path), and it queues `unreachable_refunded` only when `refund_in_full` answers `true`; the job, the call line and the homeowner's text close and go as today; on `false` no business text is queued and Casey's alert stands. `refund_state`, `PickRefundState`, `refund_waiting`, `fraud_warning` and `refund_state.rs` do not change, and every existing test of these paths passes unchanged. `refund_amounts.rs` adds a webhook-path case through `refund_succeeded`, `refund_in_full` for each TD-FEE-59 case, and two `decide_at_96_hours` cases ($25 of $75; `eur`) that close the job and queue no `unreachable_refunded`. T333 reads `tests/integration/tests/unreachable_refund_states.rs` for its fixture; budget 6 files, 620 lines. Order (`scripts/validate_tasks.py` refuses two unordered owners of one file): T333 gains the dependency T278 (DONE; it orders T333 after T191, T282, T270 and T278, the earlier owners of `unreachable_refund.rs`), and queued T355 gains the dependency T333 (its `deps` only; its prompt does not change); the other order would hold T333, and T334 after it, behind T318. Review areas gain `privacy` (the validator asks it of an owner of `unreachable_refund.rs`). No test-design row or requirement changes, and no queued task but T355's `deps`. Reason: the smallest change that lets D-2303's check reach both the webhook and the notice without a migration, a state change or another task's test; T353 and T381 (`routes.rs`) and T355 (`unreachable_refund.rs`) are queued and build on the merged result. Changed: `kit/tasks.json` (T333: `goal`, `deps`, `review_areas`, `owns`, `reads`, `decisions`, `budget`; T355: `deps`), `kit/prompts/T333.md`, `kit/plan.lock`, `docs/decisions.md`, `docs/for-casey-review.md`. Independent Opus review (changes) folded in: a failed re-read answers `true` only for `NotSent`, any other error retries before the close; the `Refund` given to `refund_succeeded` is the re-read; `run_refund_check` and the `refund_lifecycle.rs` calls named; a present amount with no currency is unconfirmed. - **D-2987** Question (T384; PICK-051, PICK-008, D-084, D-2912; TD-PICK-34): how does the quote page show a withdrawn or edited quote without any pick path changing? Choice: `quotes::api::page_quotes` now reads every confirmed quote (no `withdrawn_at IS NULL` filter) in the same `ORDER BY received_at, business_id`; a withdrawn row is always `unavailable: true` and `withdrawn: true`, and its `original` comes from `CASE WHEN withdrawn_at IS NULL THEN original ELSE '' END`, so its words never leave the database; `updated_at` is `edited_at` only for an unwithdrawn row. Every pick caller already gates on `!unavailable`, so `picks` and `portals` `pick_flow.rs` refuse it unchanged, and numbers stay put. `PageQuote::updated_line` ("Updated Nov 3, 9:15 a.m. Arizona time", `notify::updated_line`, Arizona's fixed UTC-7, so it cannot fail) and `updated_stamp` (the `data-updated` value, empty when never edited) feed `quote_page.html`; `quote_page.ts` also swaps a card whose `data-updated` changed and adds nothing to the status line for it (an edit is not a new quote). A withdrawal flips `data-available` to false, so the live page counts it in the existing "no longer available" status line: it can no longer be picked, which is what that line says. Kind: build. Source: T384 prompt (1), (2).
- **D-2988** Question (T384; TXT-031, PICK-051, D-084, D-1310): how are LIST lines numbered, and what does a withdrawn quote's line say? Choice: `models::list_rows` returns every confirmed quote in page order as `ListRow::Pickable`, `Unavailable` or `Withdrawn` (withdrawn wins when both), reading a price only for a pickable one; `notify::list_texts` numbers each line by its place in that order (the number "<n> YES" picks), skips an unavailable one with its number, and writes "<n>. Withdrawn by the business." / "<n>. Retirada por el negocio." (no name, price or visit) for a withdrawn one, which needs no `names` entry, so a missing name for it never fails the LIST (D-1310). Lines go through the private `Line` enum and `numbered_texts`, 10 lines a text as before; `Listed` and `list_texts_from` keep their signatures and output (T047's `prop_quote_texts.rs` unchanged). No pickable line means no text, so no "2 YES" line goes out with nothing to pick. Kind: fix (the LIST's line 2 could differ from what "2 YES" picks after a failed pick). Source: T384 prompt (3); `app/quotes/src/models.rs` `list_rows` before T384.

- **D-3019** Question (T342; PICK-007, D-2334; TD-PICK-58): folding every whitespace run to one space joins "555\n123\n4567" into a phone number, but a domain cut at its dot ("example-pools\n.com") folds to "example-pools .com", two words the card gate reads as it would on one line, so the split domain still passed. Choice: `intake::text_bounce` gates the text as written and a folded view (`intake::folded`): every whitespace run (line feed, carriage return, tab, no-break space; `char::is_whitespace`) becomes one space, except a run before a dot followed by a letter, which is removed, so "example-pools\n.com" reads "example-pools.com". Either view cut bounces (`Bounce::Contact`, or `Restricted` for a listed phrase split across lines). A run before a dot and a digit or another dot stays a space, and a run after a full stop is never removed, so "Pump replaced.\nParts included" and "2 coats\n3 days" pass. `gate.rs` is unchanged, so a card keeps its lines; `notes::check_note` calls `text_bounce`, so the form's notes check gets the folded view too. Reason: PICK-007 bounces a quote containing a link however it is laid out; joining after every full stop would bounce ordinary sentences. Source: `app/quotes/src/intake.rs`, `app/quotes/src/gate.rs:280`, `tests/integration/tests/quote_whole_field_gate.rs`.
- **D-3020** Question (T342; REC-010, D-2333, D-2898; TD-PICK-58): D-2333 has `quotes`' parse carry a per-visit price's visit schedule on `Price::Monthly` and bounce one with none, but T164 (D-2898) already returns the schedule beside the price from `formats::parse_price` (`(Price, Option<VisitSchedule>)`), bounces a per-visit price with none or an unknown one as `PriceProblem::Schedule` with its reason at the form's submission, stores it in `quotes.quote.visit_schedule` and reads it with `visit_schedule_of` (for T341). A new field on `Price::Monthly` would change every constructor of it: `formats.rs`, `models.rs` (twice), `api.rs` and tests owned by other tasks (`quote_parse.rs`, `prop_quote_texts.rs`, `quote_texts.rs`, `business_actions.rs`, `pick_aftermath.rs`, `quote_formats.rs`), far past T342's 2 files. Choice: `Price::Monthly` keeps its shape; the schedule stays beside it as T164 built it, and T342's TD-PICK-58 case proves the requirement through the form's path: no schedule (or "twice a week") bounces with its reason, each of the five schedules is taken with the price, and "Other" is a monthly price with none. `submit_quote` alone (no form, as tests and a future text quote use) still stores a per-visit price without a schedule; T341 refuses such a quote at the pick (its prompt already says "one from before is refused"). Kind: implementation choice within D-2333; listed for Casey. Reason: the requirement (REC-010: the schedule is stated, carried and convertible) holds without moving it into the enum. Source: `app/quotes/src/formats.rs:195`, `app/quotes/src/formats.rs:292`, `docs/decisions.md` D-2333, D-2898.
- **D-3021** Question (T342 fix round, privacy review; PICK-007, D-3019; TD-PICK-58): D-3019's folded view rejoined only a run before a dot and a letter, so a domain split right after its dot ("examplepools.\ncom"), around a lone dot ("examplepools\n.\ncom") or inside its ending ("examplepools.c\nom", "Visit\nexamplepools\n.c\nom") still passed in notes, original wording and a tier name. Choice: `intake::joins` also removes the run before a lone "." and before a piece of letters (trailing punctuation aside) that, with the up to 2 letters after the last dot of the previous word (2 or more letters or digits before that dot), spells one of `SPLIT_TLDS` (com, net, org, biz, us, io, co, info). This replaces D-3019's "a run after a full stop is never removed". "Pump replaced.\nParts included" stays two words. Cost: a sentence ending in a full stop followed by a line starting "Us" or "Co" alone joins; the card gate still reads "ready.Us" as a domain only when 2 or more letters precede the dot, so such a line can bounce; rare, and privacy wins. Reason: TD-PICK-58 bounces a domain split across lines. Source: `app/quotes/src/intake.rs` (`joins`), `tests/integration/tests/quote_whole_field_gate.rs`.
- **D-3022** Question (T342 fix round, privacy review; PICK-007, D-3019; TD-PICK-58): folding every line break to a space turned "Prices:\n$450\n$300\n$120" and "Sizes\n24\n36\n48\n60" into one run of 9 or 8 digits, which the card gate's number rule (7 or more digits in a row, `app/quotes/src/gate.rs:295`) cuts, so ordinary lists bounced, while "555\n123\n4567" must still bounce. Choice: `intake::kept_breaks` keeps a line break in the folded view only between two pieces of one number run (pieces of only digits, the letter O and price or phone punctuation, or number words the card gate cuts three in a row) and only when the run is not phone-shaped: no unbroken stretch of it adds up to exactly 7, 10 or 11 digits (a number word counting one) and it holds fewer than 3 number words. A phone number's own pieces always add up to its length, so padding it with other lines ("24\n555\n123\n4567\n99") or splitting it into words ("555\n123\n45\nsix\nseven") still bounces. Trade-off: a list whose neighbours add up to 7, 10 or 11 digits ("$1200\n$450", "450\n300\n1200") bounces like a phone number; the business writes it on one line with words ("$1,200 for the pump, $450 for labor") or as tiers. Privacy wins over the convenience of a bare list. Tabs and no-break spaces are not line breaks, so "555\t123\t4567" is still one line to the gate. Reason: PICK-007 bounces a phone number however it is laid out, and REC-010's price lists should not bounce for being lists. Source: `app/quotes/src/intake.rs` (`kept_breaks`, `phone_shaped`), `app/quotes/src/gate.rs:295`, `tests/integration/tests/quote_whole_field_gate.rs`.
- **D-3025** Question (T269; PICK-024, SEC-004, SEC-026, D-1761): what does a valid release-notice link "open", given that a `GET` must change nothing (mail scanners open links) and the link alone must never sign anyone in? Choice: `signin_page` (the composition's `GET /b/sign-in`) checks the link (`core`'s Action token over `p`, salted with `j` and `e` as 8 big-endian bytes each, recomputed and compared in constant time with `subtle`, and `now < e`) and shows the existing "Sign in" button screen of `templates/business_signin.html`; its `POST /b/sign-in/notice?p=&j=&e=&t=` (CSRF, cross-site refusal) checks the link again and emails that person the usual 15-minute one-time link (T084), under the same `LINKS_PER_LIFE` cap, then shows the existing "Check your email" screen; that link and T194's new-device code run unchanged. The link's person is a mailbox ID (the notice's `to` and `texts` are opaque email IDs), so `portals` finds the memberships through a new `businesses::api::businesses_of_mailbox` (one query on `businesses.team_member`, current members only) and emails one link per membership, as the address form does for an address on file twice. - **D-3037** Question (T165 fix round; BIZ-052, SEC-041, BIZ-022, PICK-041, LIC-011; D-3034, D-336, D-2954): the review found that `on_site` took any page on a Google or Yelp domain (a `google.com/search?q=<phone>`, `sites.google.com`, `docs.google.com`, `google.com/url?q=` or `yelp.com/search` link would sit on every quote card), that `share.google` links were refused, that `GuardedOpener`'s result mapping had no test, and that the city license number was not screened. The city license number, after its 64-character check, goes through `screen_public_name` (`NameRefusal::CityLicenseScreened`), so a phone number, link or channel direction there is refused with the same reasons.
