- **D-2971** Question (T333; FEE-026, FEE-028, FEE-053; D-2303, D-3018): D-2303 and D-3018 leave four edges open: what counts as a "present" amount and currency, whether the request path's re-read may change the state it books, whether the alert of a refund the nightly reconcile already booked still goes, and what `refund_in_full` answers for a pick with no succeeded refund. Choice: one pure reading, `Refund::amount_against(charged)` (`app/payments/src/refund_stripe.rs`) giving `RefundAmount`: a currency other than `usd` (compared without case) is `Foreign` whatever the amount; an amount with no currency, no amount, or an amount not above zero is `Missing` (a ledger refund must be above zero, so such a figure is never booked); a `usd` amount equal to the charge is `Full`, any other `Differs`. The request path re-reads only a `succeeded` `Missing` answer, once, outside any transaction (R11), and uses the re-read only when it is still `succeeded` for the same PaymentIntent, so the re-read never moves the state machine. The alert is raised in the `succeeded` transaction before the "ledger already holds a refund" check, so a refund the reconcile booked while `pending` still alerts when its `succeeded` arrives; `raise_alert_once` keeps it to one open alert per kind and pick, so a duplicate event or retry raises nothing new. `refund_succeeded` records nothing for a `Refund` naming another PaymentIntent than the pick's charge. `refund_in_full` answers `true` when the pick has no `succeeded` refund row (no positive evidence; `picks` calls it only after `refund_state` reads `Succeeded`). Reason: each choice books only money Stripe confirmed in `usd`, never a foreign or absent figure, and keeps one alert per pick. Source: app/payments/src/refund_stripe.rs, app/payments/src/refunds.rs, tests/integration/tests/refund_amounts.rs
- **D-2972** Question (T333; FEE-028, FEE-030; D-1753, D-2303): `refund_ended` appended its `refund-reversal` at the charged amount; once a refund can be booked at Stripe's own `usd` amount (D-2303), a `refund.failed` after a $25 refund of a $75 charge would reverse $75 and the ledger would owe Stripe $50. Choice: a reversal is appended at the amount of the pick's latest `refund` ledger entry (`last_refund`, keys `refund.<pick>` and `refund.<pick>.<re>`), falling back to the charge only when none is found (the reversal is appended only when the ledger holds more refunds than reversals, so the fallback is not reached in practice). Known gap, T334's: the nightly reconcile still books its own `refund.<pick>` entry at the charge while the row is `pending`. Reason: the ledger nets to what Stripe holds (FEE-030) and no row is changed. Source: app/payments/src/refunds.rs, tests/integration/tests/refund_amounts.rs (`td_fee_59_the_same_event_twice_records_once`)
- **D-3038** Question (T272; SEC-004, SEC-014, D-1725, D-1837, D-2635): how is the 5-links-per-member cap made atomic, and which rows count? Choice: `models::admit_link` runs the count and the insert of the new `portals.login_link` row in one short transaction after `pg_advisory_xact_lock(hashtextextended('portals.login_link:' || member, 0))`, commits, and only then does `send_one` email the link; a refused request sends nothing and shows the same screen. The count leaves out rows living over a day (a remembered device, born used with a 180-day life), so a new-device sign-in costs no link; action links and old code markers are backdated past any window. Reason: a per-member lock serializes only that member's requests and is never held across the mail call (postgres brain P9, P10). Tests: `tests/security/tests/signin_admission.rs` (20 simultaneous requests with one link left send one; a new-device sign-in then 5 requests all send; removing the lock makes the first fail with 6 emails). Source: app/portals/src/models.rs, app/portals/src/business_auth.rs
- **D-3039** Question (T272; SEC-020, SEC-048, D-1777, D-1837): how are code tries counted so simultaneous checks cannot pass the cap, and what does each outcome mean? Choice: migration `0167_portals_code_tries.sql` adds `portals.code_try` (link, `try_no` 1 to 5 by check constraint, primary key on both, reserved time, outcome `pending`, `right`, `wrong` or `abandoned`; app role SELECT, INSERT and UPDATE of `outcome` only). `check_once` reserves the next number with `INSERT ... SELECT count(*) + 1 ... HAVING count(*) < CODE_TRIES` under the link's advisory lock in its own committed transaction, calls Verify with nothing held, then records `right` (Verify said yes), `wrong` (Verify said no, or the code is not six digits, which reaches no Verify) or `abandoned` (Verify gave no answer: failure or timeout). A try never finished stays `pending` and counts. With no try left the check uses the link up (the existing guarded `UPDATE`) and shows the "stopped working" screen, as T194's test expects after five wrong codes. Every wrong or failed check still writes its `auth_failed` event; the events no longer count tries. A right code signs in only through `start`'s single guarded use of the link, so a concurrent right and wrong code never both sign in. Reason: the reservation is the admission; the unique key and check constraint refuse a sixth even if the lock were skipped. Source: migrations/0167_portals_code_tries.sql, app/portals/src/business_auth.rs
- **D-3040** Question (T272; PT-03, PT-04, D-1776, D-2349): how is the link's one code send recorded without a transaction across Verify, and what may a check ask of it? Choice: `portals.code_send` (link primary key, reserved time, outcome `pending`, `sent` or `failed`; app role SELECT, INSERT and UPDATE of `reserved_at` and `outcome`) replaces the born-used `code-sent:<link>` marker row. A press reserves with one `INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE ... WHERE outcome = 'failed' OR (outcome = 'pending' AND reserved_at < now - 75 s)` (`SEND_STALE`: the adapter's 15-second timeout plus a minute), calls Verify with nothing held, then records `sent` or `failed` fenced on its own reservation time; a press that finds the send reserved or sent sends nothing and shows the code field. `check_once` reads `outcome = 'sent'` first; any other link is one `auth_failed` event and the "didn't work" code screen, with no try reserved and no Verify call. Reason: a failed send can be pressed again, 20 presses at once send once, and a crash costs at most one more send after 75 seconds (D-2349's duplicate-send policy). Source: app/portals/src/models.rs, app/portals/src/business_auth.rs
- **D-3041** Question (T272; PT-04 availability, AVAIL-01, D-2349): which connection does sign-in hold while Verify works? Choice: `device_step`, `send_once`, `check_once`, `auth_failed` and `start` take the handler's `&PgPool`; each database step acquires a connection (or runs a single statement on the pool) and gives it back before Verify is called, and `signin_post` no longer acquires one for the whole request. `signin_request` and `notice_post` still hold one connection across `SignInMail::send_link`, whose trait takes `&mut PgConnection`; only its transaction was removed (D-3038). Tests: with a hanging fake Verify, 30 concurrent presses and checks leave a 5-connection pool serving a link page, and `pg_stat_activity` shows no idle transaction during the wait. Reason: a slow Verify cannot drain the pool. Source: app/portals/src/business_auth.rs, tests/security/tests/signin_admission.rs

- **D-3043** Question (plan change, November 11, 2026; `kit/runner.json`; D-2986, D-2810, D-620, D-723, D-1451, D-515): Casey, in chat about 17:00Z on November 11, 2026, after the overseer explained that tokens were the limiting factor: "Dont worry about the token budget. Just use the tokens efficiently"; earlier that day (D-2986): "If we can speed the build up without any issues let's do that." Should the runner work five tasks at once? Choice: `kit/runner.json` `lanes` 4 → 5, through a logged plan change as `BUILD_BRIEF.md:209` requires. Tokens: Casey's words lift the week's budget as a reason to hold back, not the plan's real limits; the five-hour and weekly usage windows may still cap claims, and the pacer (`scripts/pacing.py`, which already sums the estimates of every other running attempt, `in_flight_tokens`, `scripts/pacing.py:188`) still holds a claim that would cross them, so on a busy window five lanes may run as four or fewer. "Efficiently" is kept by what already stands: one task per session, the plan's model per task, no claim the pacer refuses. Audit, repeated from D-2986 over `runner/`, `.github/workflows/`, `scripts/` and `kit/state_schema.json`: nothing assumes four lanes or caps the count. `runner/lanes.py` (`effective_lanes`, `free_lanes`, `claim_lane`, `refusal` against every task in flight, `strike` on any lane above 1, `restore`), `runner/state.py` (`free_lanes` over `range(1, lanes + 1)`, `in_flight`, `run_lane`), `runner/cycle.py` (`refill_lanes`), `runner/__main__.py` (lost-race retries and refill at `lanes >= 2`, `--restore-lanes`), `scripts/check_state.py` (at most `lanes` live leases), `scripts/pacing.py`, `runner/status.py` (`lane_line` lists every held lane, sorted, so "1" to "5" and "fix" render in order), `runner/keeper.py` (reads the live lane map as the gate does), the smoke reuse (keyed by `main`'s head, `runner/cycle.py:960`, shared by every lane) and `backup-runner.yml` (the gate's `range(1, lanes + 1)` at `.github/workflows/backup-runner.yml:124`, a dispatched lane accepted when `1 <= lane <= lanes`, the per-lane group `backup-runner-lane-<n>` at `:187`, the hourly tick dispatching one run per free lane) all take the count from the setting. `kit/state_schema.json` types `lanes` as an integer and `leases` and `lane_strikes` as open maps (`additionalProperties`), and a task's `lane` matches `^([1-9][0-9]*|fix)$`, so no schema enumerates lanes; `claude/lease`'s `leases` map has the same open shape. Only wording named the count: `BUILD_BRIEF.md:209`, `docs/governance.md:53`, `docs/architecture.md` (runner logic), `docs/ai-operating-manual.md:102` and `runner/state.py:12` now say 5 since D-3043 (line counts unchanged). GitHub Actions' concurrent-job cap (20 on GitHub Free, more on paid plans): one lane's hand-in push to `claude/task/**` starts `ci.yml`'s Checks, Python, Coverage and E2e in parallel (then its Ci gate job), `a11y.yml`, `twin.yml` and `auto-pr.yml`, about 7 jobs at once while that lane's own `backup` job is still running (8); Ci's end then starts `governance.yml` and a `backup-runner.yml` gate that waits up to 15 minutes for the auto-merge, and the merge starts another gate and the lane's next `backup` job; the keeper (one sleeper) holds one more. Five lanes handing in together want about 40 jobs (four already wanted about 32, three about 24, so the cap already binds today). The excess queues: GitHub starts queued jobs as slots free, a job's `timeout-minutes` counts only running time, and a check that has not finished never fails a task (the gate's wait ends in "run anyway", the runner reports `merge_pending`, and the next event or the keeper picks it up). Nothing a lane starts cancels another lane's run: `ci.yml`, `a11y.yml`, `twin.yml` and `governance.yml` have no concurrency group; `auto-pr.yml` groups by its own ref with `cancel-in-progress: false`; `notify.yml` and `nightly-main.yml`'s `record` share `kit-state-writer` with `cancel-in-progress: false`; the backup job's per-lane group has `cancel-in-progress: false` and GitHub replaces only an older pending job of the same lane (D-620); the one `cancel-in-progress: true` is the keeper's `backup-runner-keeper` (D-1451), a sleeper, never a check. So five simultaneous hand-ins cost minutes of queueing, not failures; at the 09:17Z nightly the queue is longest. Tests (a spec change to tests under CLAUDE.md rule 6; the covered set grows, nothing is weakened): new `tests/test_runner_five_lanes.py` runs the four-lane drills over five lanes (five claims on non-overlapping tasks with lease keys "1" to "5" and a sixth run claiming nothing, `check_state` clean at 5 and flagging 5 live leases at 4; a lane-5 candidate refused for overlapping or a different stage against any of four tasks in flight, a compatible one claimed; `refill_lanes` naming up to five lanes; two harness-type strikes on lane 5 falling back to one lane, lanes 2 to 5 then refused, and `restore` (`--restore-lanes`) giving all five back; one strike each on lanes 2 to 5 not falling back; MERGE_PENDING in four lanes leaving only lane 5 to claim; pacing reserving the estimates of four other running attempts; the gate's lane pick with five lanes, lane 5 refused while the setting is 4, and while fallen back; lane 5's own backup concurrency group never cancelling; no workflow a hand-in starts cancelling in progress, the keeper the only one that does); `tests/test_runner_lanes.py:208` and `:209` now allow 1 to 5; `tests/test_runner_model_window.py:82`, which pins the locked switches, now expects 5 (the one value this decision changes). Kept unchanged: `lanes_fallback` after two harness-type failures in a row on one lane above 1 (`STRIKES_TO_FALL_BACK`, `runner/lanes.py:38`) is the safety net, dropping the build to one lane by itself (with an outbox `kind: info` item) until `python3 -m runner --restore-lanes`; the owned-path overlap refusal, the same-stage rule and the lone cleanup task (D-620); FIX-MAIN's reserved fix lane outside the count (D-630). How the overseer watches it: STATUS's lane line (five held lanes) and verdict, the outbox item and `lanes_fallback` in kit-state, the pacer's held-claim lines in the runner log (if it holds claims most cycles, the windows are the limiter and five lanes buy nothing), queued Actions jobs (`gh run list --status queued`) and the time from hand-in to merge, and update-merge rounds and non-insertion conflicts (`Cargo.toml`, migration numbers) across five open branches; a fall back is answered by reading its two reasons before restoring, and lasting contention or queueing is answered by this decision's rollback. Risks, accepted: more merge contention and update-merge rounds with five branches open, longer Actions queues when lanes hand in together, and the week's tokens spent sooner, which Casey accepted. Rollback: the same one-line change back to 4 (or fewer) through a logged plan change; tasks in flight finish normally. Changed: `kit/runner.json`, `BUILD_BRIEF.md`, `docs/governance.md`, `docs/architecture.md`, `docs/ai-operating-manual.md`, `runner/state.py` (docstring), `tests/test_runner_five_lanes.py`, `tests/test_runner_lanes.py`, `tests/test_runner_model_window.py`, `kit/plan.lock`, `docs/decisions.md`, `docs/for-casey-review.md`; `runner/` and `tests/` are protected, so this is a harness-kind change the overseer lands with an Opus review (D-1328, D-2986). Numbered by: reserved with --reserve-decision (D-1058). Kind: plan change. Owner approval: not needed (BUILD_BRIEF section 16); listed for Casey. Reason: Casey asked to speed the build up and not to hold back for the token budget; the lane machinery has no count limit, the drills now prove five, and the cap on Actions jobs queues rather than fails. Source: Casey's chat of November 11, 2026 (relayed by the overseer), `kit/runner.json:1`, `BUILD_BRIEF.md:209`, `runner/lanes.py:38`, `runner/lanes.py:44`, `runner/lanes.py:181`, `scripts/pacing.py:188`, `.github/workflows/backup-runner.yml:124`, `.github/workflows/backup-runner.yml:187`, `.github/workflows/backup-runner.yml:654`.
- **D-2955** Question (T332; FEE-021, FEE-018, FEE-020, FEE-026; D-1547, D-2290, D-2970, D-3007): where does `payments` call `late_success` so that a success on a pick it ended (the four-hour end or the card-fix window) is queued once whether the webhook, the check round, or both store it, and what about a pick that ends after the success is stored? Choice: one call, in `handlers::record`'s success effects right after `write_evidence`, as `late_success(tx, pick, PickNow::Payable, at)` in the transaction that stores the success; `late_success` already answers `Current` and writes nothing for a pick `payments` has not ended, so every success path (`paid_release`'s `store_success`, the `CHECK_KIND` round, the pay timer's ask and a synchronous confirm answer) gets it with no second rule. `paid_release` now reads the pick's intent without refusing an ended pick before the fetch, verifies and stores the success as before, then re-reads the pick: ended means one more `late_success` call in its own short transaction (it writes nothing when `record` queued it, and covers a pick whose end committed after `record` read it, which would otherwise be charged, not released and never refunded), then `PickEnded`; nothing is released and no `Releasable` exists, so no `ReleaseProof` can be minted. A failed queue answers `Database`, so Stripe resends the event. The nightly reconcile's refund of a charge on a pick `payments` ended also uses `LATE_TRIGGER` (`app/payments/src/reconcile.rs:472`), so it is stored `late-success` too, which is what it is; no reconcile test pins the code. Reason: one place covers every way a success is stored, and the dedupe key and new-task-only alert already make repeats one refund and one alert. Source: `app/payments/src/handlers.rs`, `app/payments/src/release_proof.rs`, `app/payments/src/late.rs`.
- **D-2956** Question (T332; FEE-026; D-2290): T332's goal says `RefundTrigger::LateSuccess` is "read back by the same parser", but `RefundTrigger` had no parser (only `code`), and TD-FEE-56 needs the stored code read back; how is it read, and how is the check widened? Choice: `RefundTrigger::ALL` (the five triggers in the check's order) and `RefundTrigger::from_code`, the inverse of `code` over `ALL` (`None` for an unknown code), so a new trigger is read back as soon as it is in `ALL`. Migration 0177 drops `refund_trigger_check` and adds it again with `late-success`, `NOT VALID` then `VALIDATE` (postgres brain P2), so stored rows keep their code; the drop's lock is still held to commit inside the migration's one transaction (D-2957). Reason: the smallest reader that cannot drift from `code`. Source: `app/payments/src/models.rs`, `migrations/0177_payments_late_success_trigger.sql`.
- **D-2957** Question (T332 fix round; FEE-026; D-2956): does migration 0177's `NOT VALID` then `VALIDATE` keep `payments.refund` open to writes while the new check scans it? Choice: no, and the comment and D-2956 now say so: sqlx runs the migration in one transaction and `DROP CONSTRAINT` takes an `ACCESS EXCLUSIVE` lock held to commit, so the table is locked for the whole migration, the `VALIDATE` scan included. The split stays (harmless, and the pattern P2 asks for); the lock is accepted because `payments.refund` holds one row per refunded pick, so the scan is brief. Reason: say what the migration really does. Source: `migrations/0177_payments_late_success_trigger.sql`.
- **D-2958** Question (T332 fix round; FEE-021, FEE-018, FEE-020; D-2290, D-2955): `late_success` read `pick_intent.ended_at` with no lock, and `record` (which locks only the `charge_attempt` row) could race `end_pick` (which locks only the `pick_intent` row): `record` read "not ended" and answered `Current`, then `end_pick` committed, leaving a stored success on an ended pick with no refund task or alert on the check-round path. How is the race closed without a deadlock? Choice: three changes. (1) `late_success`'s select takes `FOR SHARE OF p`, so it waits for a concurrent end and reads the committed `ended_at`. (2) `record`'s success effects take that share lock first (`handlers::hold_pick`), before `end_timers` updates the `pay_timer` rows: `end_pick` locks `pick_intent` then `pay_timer`, so taking the share lock only inside `late_success`, after `end_timers`, would lock in the opposite order and could deadlock; the order is now `charge_attempt`, `pick_intent`, `pay_timer` in `record` and `pick_intent`, `pay_timer` in `end_pick`, and nothing locks `pay_timer` then `pick_intent`. (3) `end_pick` calls `late_success(tx, pick, PickNow::Payable, at)` after ending the pick (`NothingCharged` is not an error), so a success whose `record` committed before the end is queued by the end. Whichever of the two commits second sees the other, so the refund is queued once whichever commits first; the dedupe key and new-task-only alert keep it one task and one alert. `paid_release`'s `ended_late` and the nightly reconcile stay as backstops. Reason: the reviewer's lock alone would wait for an end in progress but miss an end that starts after `record` commits, and its placement would invert `end_pick`'s lock order. Source: `app/payments/src/late.rs`, `app/payments/src/handlers.rs`.
- **D-2923** Question (T316; PICK-041, BIZ-022, TXT-031, TXT-027; D-336, D-1310, D-1687, D-2206, D-2943; TD-BIZ-43): how does T316 give each business's public name to the LIST reply (T317) and the who's-calling text (T318)? Choice: `businesses::api::public_names(conn, &[Uuid]) -> Vec<(Uuid, String)>` (the shape of `server::inbound_text`'s `names`) reads `businesses.business_name` (written by T165's `save_business_name`) joined to `businesses.business`, in the order asked, a repeated ID once: the trade name (DBA) when stored, else the business name, screened again by `screen_public_name` (D-336), since a row may predate a stricter screen. A failing trade name is not replaced by the business name: the business chose to go by its trade name, and a failing row needs a look, not a quiet swap. A known business whose chosen name fails, or with no row, is left out (the caller shows its own fallback) and raises one `businesses.public_name_unusable` alert at `Severity::Normal` (`ops::api::Severity` has no Low level; `Normal` is "everything else, listed in the weekly digest", `app/ops/src/models.rs:199`) about `businesses.business` and the ID only, through `ops::api::raise_alert_once`, so a LIST read every few minutes adds no second open alert; an unknown ID is left out with no alert (nothing to look at). Read only: no table, column or writer, nothing through `licensing`. Not built here: a name the business edits later in the portal (no portal edit exists yet; whoever builds it must call `screen_names` and `save_business_name`, and `public_names` picks the change up at once), and the callers (T317, T318, IC-71). Reason: one read, one screen and one alert rule for every place the name is shown (BIZ-022). Source: app/businesses/src/public_name.rs, tests/integration/tests/business_public_name.rs
- **D-3055** Question (plan change outside the runner, November 11, 2026, before the runner claims them; an independent read-only pre-flight audit of `main` 82e788ae found five queued tasks that cannot finish as written, each re-verified here against the code; PICK-042, PICK-050, PICK-054, TERMS-033, SEC-027, LIC-047, LIC-048, QH-001, QH-008, FEE-029, SEC-004; TD-PICK-42, TD-PICK-43, TD-TERMS-11, TD-SEC-32, TD-PICK-19, TD-LIC-22, TD-BIZ-32, TD-QH-05, TD-FEE-60, TD-SEC-40, TD-SEC-41): how do T232, T280, T356, T215 and T334 become finishable? - **D-3057** Question (harness change, November 11, 2026; number reserved from the live counter; D-2591, D-891, D-498): `tests/test_runner_critical_path.py::test_on_the_real_plan_the_top_claim_heads_the_longest_open_chain` failed in the runner's smoke (runner job 130704663742: `assert 43 == 54`), giving `smoke_env` results on healthy main heads ef7f7fc8, 60a8d50b and b2f1343b and five sessions that ended with no claim; at `SMOKE_ENV_STRIKES` (`runner/cycle.py`) it could raise a false `main_red` and a FIX-MAIN revert. Ci never saw it: the test reads `origin/claude/kit-state:kit/state.json` when that ref exists, which it does only in the runner's job. Its "ready" set was every not-DONE/SKIPPED task whose deps were finished, so it included tasks already in flight (IN_PROGRESS, MERGE_PENDING), which `st.eligible` never offers to `claim_order`. Replaying the last 300 kit-state commits through the old check: 29 fail, all the same way (for example 76da1552, 18:53Z: T332 IN_PROGRESS with a `resync` note went first by D-891's resync-first key with chain 45 while T228, IN_PROGRESS, headed the longest open chain at 54); a QUEUED task with a resync note (16 of the last 400 states) would fail it the same way, by design of D-891. Choice: compute the expectation over what the runner can claim, so it is right for any live state, and keep reading the live state (a fixed fixture alone would stop checking the real plan against real progress). A new helper `check_top_claim(tasks, state)` drops every task in flight and every task downstream of one (`held_by_flight`), then asserts on the rest: every open chain at least 1 (stated in the old docstring, now asserted); the longest open chain starts at a dependency-ready task; `claim_order` puts the resync ids first (D-891), as a group; within that group and within the rest the top id has the longest chain and the chains fall in order (`claim_order` sorts by resync, then `claim_first`, then chain, so the resync group is ordered by chain and state order breaks ties). With nothing in flight and no resync note (Ci, and the fresh-state call the real-plan test now also makes) these are exactly the old assertions. A new test, `test_work_in_flight_at_the_head_of_the_longest_chain_is_not_a_failure`, rebuilds the failure on nine tasks (an in-flight task heading the longest chain, an in-flight task with a resync note, a QUEUED one with a resync note), shows the old expectation fails there and the new check holds. A second, `test_two_claimable_resync_tasks_are_ordered_by_chain`, has two claimable resync tasks, the later one heading the longer chain, and pins that it goes first. Why it is not a weakening (`BUILD_BRIEF.md:69`; a wrong test changes only through a logged decision): the test asserted something the runner never promised (that a task it cannot claim heads its claim order), so it was wrong, not strict; the property it exists for still fails on the bug it names: with `chain_lengths` reading deps instead of dependents, `check_top_claim` fails on the real plan (mutation run here); all 300 replayed live states pass it. Other tests that read the kit-state: none reads the live `origin/claude/kit-state`; `tests/test_runner_live.py`, `tests/test_runner_update_merge.py` and `tests/test_prehandin.py` read `claude/kit-state` in temporary repositories they build, `tests/test_status.py` stubs `git show`, `tests/test_runner_smoke_reuse.py` and `tests/test_gen_prompts.py` only check text. Tested here: the module with and without a local `origin/claude/kit-state` ref (12 passed both ways), the full `python3 -m pytest -q tests`, `scripts/validate_tasks.py`, `scripts/check_plan_lock.py`, `bash scripts/prehandin.sh --quick` and `scripts/check_pr_change.py`. Independent Opus review (changes) folded in: the first draft asserted the resync group in state order (`ordered[:len(resync)] == resync`), which fails with two claimable resync tasks of different chain lengths (probe: T001 and T002 both resync, T002 heading a chain of 2, `claim_order` gives T002, T001); it now asserts the group as a set and chain-descending order within the group and within the rest, with the two-resync test added. A harness change (CLAUDE.md rule 7), landed by the overseer with an Opus review as in D-1328 and D-3030. Changed: `tests/test_runner_critical_path.py`, `docs/decisions.md`, `docs/for-casey-review.md`. Numbered by: reserved with --reserve-decision (D-1058). Reason: a smoke test must judge main, not the moment's lane traffic; a false red on main costs claims and can revert good work. - **D-3056** Question (harness change, November 11, 2026; number reserved from the live counter; D-486, D-1110, D-1155, D-1189, D-2225, D-3043): the pacer budgets two windows, `five_hour` and `week`. The week has a real in-band reading (`usage.session_reading`, 72% at 19:10:58Z), but no reading has ever reported a five-hour window, so that window fell back to the ledger against `budget_tokens_five_hour: 30000000`, a placeholder (kit/pacing.json's note: "the five-hour budget stays as it was for want of a reading"). At 18:36Z the pacer stood at 26.85M of 29.1M in the five-hour window (2.2M left, ledger reset 20:04Z), and at 19:10Z the ledger had about 3.8M left there (room for about four tasks in flight at about 880k each) while the week had 42.6M left; at 19:09Z all five lanes were empty with eligible tasks waiting. Casey, in chat about 19:15Z: "Also, I don't have a 5-hour token window, so don't worry about that"; earlier the same day: "My usage says we will have tokens to spare by the reset time. We need to use them all before then." and "Dont worry about the token budget. Just use the tokens efficiently". Should the pacer keep limiting on a five-hour window the plan does not have? Choice: no. `kit/pacing.json` `budget_tokens_five_hour` is now `null`, and `scripts/pacing.py` reads a null budget as "no such window" (`budgeted(cfg)`): `standing` leaves it out, so the estimate test (`_verdict`), the PROGRESS line ("week has X left (no five-hour budget, D-3056)") and `projected_finish` use the week alone; the ledger still counts five-hour tokens, so a number set back restores the old rule at once. `assess` now also waits on `at_limit` outside the model window: a real reading (the quota command or a fresh session reading) that reports any window, five-hour included, at 100% holds the claim until its reset (no later than the session reading's expiry), so a limit the plan does enforce is never run through (BUILD_BRIEF.md:509); for a budgeted window this changes nothing, because a reading at 100% already left no room. The week budget (200M), headroom (0.03), the keeper's 97% week stop and the model-window rules are unchanged. Raising the placeholder to a number that could not bind was rejected: it would keep printing a made-up five-hour standing in PROGRESS and STATUS and keep a fictitious window in the projected finish. Tests: a new `tests/test_pacing.py` test checks that with no five-hour budget a ledger far past the old figure still claims, the standing holds only the week, the line says so, a five-hour reading at 100% (quota command and session reading) waits until its reset, one at 99% claims, and a full week still waits; the shipped config is checked to budget only the week. Existing tests use their own budgets and are unchanged. Run here: `python3 scripts/pacing.py --state` on a copy of `claude/kit-state`'s `kit/state.json` with four tasks in flight at 880k each (the five-lane picture at 18:36Z) said "waiting until 2026-11-11T20:04:09Z" before and "claimed" after. `runner/status.py` reads only the week's standing and `status_line` prints the windows present, so neither needs a change. Changed: `kit/pacing.json`, `scripts/pacing.py`, `tests/test_pacing.py`, `docs/architecture.md`, `kit/plan.lock`, `docs/decisions.md`, `docs/for-casey-review.md`. Numbered by: reserved with --reserve-decision (D-1058). Reason: the owner says his plan has no five-hour window, the figure was never measured, and it idled the build with the week's tokens to spare; real readings still stop the work at any limit that exists. Source: Casey in chat, November 11, 2026, relayed by the overseer; `BUILD_BRIEF.md:509`; D-486; D-1110; D-1155; D-1189; D-1328; D-2225; D-3030.
- **D-3059** Question (T387, November 11, 2026; D-3049; FEE-011, FEE-026, FEE-028, FEE-029, FEE-051, FEE-053; D-694, D-2303, `BUILD_BRIEF.md:272`, `BUILD_BRIEF.md:481`): which `app/payments/` branch flaps the 95% floor, how is its coverage made deterministic, and how is the margin made real? Evidence: five scoped runs on `main` 53eba4df (pinned `nightly-2026-10-15`, cargo-llvm-cov 0.9.1, `cargo +nightly-2026-10-15 llvm-cov --no-report --locked --branch -p askhava-payments -p askhava-integration` against the test database, then `llvm-cov report --branch --json --ignore-filename-regex '(/tests/|/bin/)'` without `--summary-only`, `llvm-cov clean --profraw-only` between runs) measured 753, 752, 753, 753 and 753 of 792 `app/payments/` branches (792 since T332 merged). The per-branch diff of `app/payments/src/` between the runs has exactly one line: `app/payments/src/models.rs:746` `if charge.fee_cents > 0` in `plan_charge`, its false arm (a charge on a known pick whose balance transaction has no Stripe fee, so no `processing-fee` line), covered in runs 1, 3, 4, 5 and not in run 2. Only `src/tests/prop_ledger_matches_stripe.rs` reaches it: its unseeded strategy draws `fee_cents` from `0..300` with a pick half the time, about one case in 600. The other leads are not the flap: `free_wins.rs` `use_win`'s `won.rows_affected() != 1` true arm (line 267) was uncovered in all five runs and `claims.keys != claims.added` covered in all five (the second Confirm in `td_fee_08_simultaneous_wins_on_a_shared_key` waits on the shared claim and gets `Race` from that arm every run), and T333's `refunds.rs` arms were the same in all five, so `tests/integration/tests/free_wins.rs` is unchanged. Choice: the property test and its random seed are left alone; `app/payments/src/tests/coverage_margin.rs` (registered by one `mod` line in `src/tests/mod.rs`) adds a fixed example, `plan_charge` on a known pick with a $0 fee (one `charge` line, no fee line), so the arm is covered on every run. Margin: measuring showed that llvm-cov 0.9.1's per-file branch summary counts each function from its single best-covered instantiation (each integration binary's own fake Stripe makes a generic `refunds.rs` function a separate instantiation, and the unit-test binary compiles its own copy of the crate), so a test that covers only the arm other binaries miss adds nothing (a first draft covering `reread_missing`'s two false arms alone left the total at 753). Each margin test therefore drives every arm of its function in one binary: `tests/integration/tests/payments_coverage_margin.rs` (own `FakeStripe`, fake IDs, TD-FEE-59) covers `reread_missing` fully (a missing-amount success whose re-read is `pending`, `succeeded` for another PaymentIntent, or `succeeded` for its own at $25; an answer with its amount; a `pending` answer, which is not re-read) and `refund_in_full` fully (no succeeded refund `true`; no ledger refund: `usd` full `true`, `eur` `false`, `OutcomeUnknown` `MoneyEventError::Stripe`; a ledger refund at the charge reads Stripe, `NotSent` `true`; one at $25 `false`), and `coverage_margin.rs` covers every arm of `Refund::checked`, `StripeCharge::is_well_formed`'s dispute check and `vendor_id`'s character check. Nothing pins T380's behaviour (the forgotten-key retry, `charge_already_refunded`, the refusal answer). Five consecutive scoped runs on the hand-in head each measured 759 of 792 (95.83%), with identical per-branch reports; the scoped set is a lower bound of Ci's `--workspace` Coverage job, which stays the gate. Plan notes: the integration package is `askhava-integration`, not `askhava-integration-tests` as the T387 goal writes; and the margin target needed whole-function coverage per binary, which the goal did not foresee. No production code, floor, `scripts/coverage_floor.py` or existing assertion changed. Changed: `app/payments/src/tests/coverage_margin.rs`, `app/payments/src/tests/mod.rs`, `tests/integration/tests/payments_coverage_margin.rs`, `app/payments/CLAUDE.md`, `docs/decisions.md`. Reason: a deterministic example ends the coin flip without touching the randomized suite, and margin counted the way llvm-cov counts it is real. Source: `BUILD_BRIEF.md:272`; `BUILD_BRIEF.md:481`; `tests/coverage_floor.json`; `app/payments/src/models.rs:746`; D-694; D-2303; D-3049.
- **D-3058** Question (harness and plan change, November 11, 2026; number reserved from the live counter; amends `BUILD_BRIEF.md:240` on the same line; D-2560, D-2870, D-3031, D-3043): Casey told the overseer in chat on November 11, 2026 at about 20:05Z: "Any decision that you have for me, use Fable to make the decision and go with that. You don't need to ask me." A Fable agent decided option (C), both changes below, with the conditions listed. The runner log from 12:00Z to 19:29Z that day shows the start-routine smoke as the largest overhead after the work itself: 690 worker minutes over 22 claims against 228 minutes of smoke; 29 smoke runs on 18 heads, 11 of them duplicates on a head already smoked (about 95 minutes); and 9 of 23 sessions ending `smoke_pending` before they claimed. Almost every head between two real smokes is one DONE task's squash merge, which `verify.check_done` already let merge only with `Ci`, `Twin` and `Ally` green on a head whose tree equals that squash commit. Should a recorded green smoke stand across a few such merges, and should a lane stop its own smoke when another lane has already smoked the same head green? Choice: (1) Ancestry reuse. `BUILD_BRIEF.md:240` (same line, so no citation moves) now lets the start routine's smoke be the last real green run on an ancestor of `main`'s head up to N first-parent commits back. N is kit/runner.json `smoke_ancestry_reuse` (shipped 3; 0 turns it off; `runner/__main__.py` `smoke_ancestry` reads it, a missing, unreadable, negative, boolean or non-integer value is 0, into `Config.smoke_ancestry` and `GitHubEnv.smoke_ancestry`). `cycle._start_smoke` tries it only when this job has no smoke of its own for the head and no same-head reuse (D-2560) applies; `cycle._ancestry_reuse` reads the chain (`GitHubEnv.main_first_parents`: `git rev-list --first-parent --max-count=N+1 <head>`, refused unless it starts at the head) and `state.ancestry_smoke` judges the state. Every condition is required: (a) every commit from the head down to the base, the head included, matches by SHA the recorded squash SHA (`merged_sha`) of a DONE task (`state.done_merges`; never FIX-MAIN's revert, never an empty hand-in's, whose `merged_sha` is another task's merge); a plan or harness merge, or anything else, forces a fresh smoke; (b) the base is the nearest ancestor with a real green run (`_real_green`: finished, not timed out, no `reused`, no `base`; a reuse of any kind is never a base), it passes `reusable_smoke` and the real run is at most `SMOKE_REUSE_MAX_AGE` (6 hours) old, so a real smoke runs at least every N+1 merges; (c) every D-2560 refusal applies to the head, every in-between commit and the base: `main_red` set, a `main_red_history` entry, a `smoke_env_problems` strike, any red or timed-out smoke run, a kit/nightly.json for the commit that is not a success, `main_checks_green` False (`_head_doubted` on each); (d) `clear_main_red` is unchanged and still needs the runner's own fresh green on the head (governance 5.3); (e) any error (git fails, a chain not starting at the head, an env without the reader, a malformed state or time) runs a fresh smoke; (f) each ancestry reuse is recorded in `smoke_runs` as its own entry: `why` "start routine (ancestry reuse of <base[:12]>, <at>)", `reused` the base run's time, `base` the base SHA; `kit/state_schema.json` now declares `reused` and `base` (strings, `base` non-empty) and `tests/test_check_state.py` checks each smoke-run kind the runner writes validates and a wrong type is refused (D-2870's lesson); `reusable_smoke` never reuses an entry naming a `base` as is, so the next start routine on that head judges the chain again and sees any doubt that arrived since; (g) the pre-session step honours it: `GitHubEnv._reusable_line` falls back to `_ancestry_line` (the same `st.ancestry_smoke` over the state the step read), so the ~9-minute step can skip; the session's start routine still checks the nightly and `main`'s checks and smokes itself if they doubt anything. (2) Duplicate-smoke fix (D-2560's own-smoke rule narrowed, no `BUILD_BRIEF.md` change): when this job's own background smoke of the head is still running with no result and a green recorded on the same head passes the same-head reuse in full (`reusable_smoke` and not `_head_doubted`), `GitHubEnv.yield_own_smoke` stops it (`bg_stop`), removes its record and the green stands; it refuses, and the own smoke is judged as before, when there is no such running smoke, when its result already exists, or when one was written while it was being stopped; a finished own result, red or green, is always judged, so a red of its own still makes a D-498 strike or `set_main_red`. An ancestry reuse never stops an own smoke. Kept unchanged: `set_main_red`, FIX-MAIN, D-498 strikes, D-1178 timeouts, `clear_main_red`, the same-head reuse and its 6-hour cap. Tests (the covered set grows; nothing is weakened): new drills in `tests/test_runner_smoke_reuse.py` for reuse within N (1 to 3) and the recorded entry, a claim through `run_cycle` with the setting on, N=0 and no N both smoking, a fresh smoke at N+1, a plan merge, FIX-MAIN, an empty hand-in or a not-DONE task in between forcing a smoke, each doubt (red run, timed-out run, strike, `main_red_history`, red nightly, red checks) on the head, an in-between commit or the base forcing a smoke and on an older commit changing nothing, never while `main` is red, a reuse never becoming a base (N=2 over two chained reuses smokes), the base's 6-hour cap measured from its real run, a later red on the base, a head with its own stale real green never bridged around, an ancestry entry judged again with a new doubt seen, six error fallbacks, `clear_main_red` never asking for an ancestry reuse, the pre-session step skipping and five cases where it smokes, `main_first_parents`, the setting's reader and wiring, a running own smoke stopped for a fully reusable green and never for seven not-fully-reusable cases, a finished own red judged, a result written during the stop judged, and `yield_own_smoke` refusing other heads, other jobs, ended smokes and written results. Mutation runs here: dropping the DONE-merge test, the base's `reusable_smoke`, the in-between doubt checks, the nightly/checks walk over the chain, the reuse-entry refusal, the FIX-MAIN and empty-hand-in exclusions, N+1 instead of N, the N=0 switch or either yield guard each fails a test. The red-main drills of `tests/test_failure_drills.py` and `tests/test_runner_pre_smoke.py` and every existing smoke-reuse test pass unchanged; `test_a_smoke_of_the_head_itself_still_running_is_never_claimed_beside` still passes as written because its env offers no `yield_own_smoke`, and its rule ("collected, not stopped") is narrowed by this decision only for a green that passes the same-head reuse in full, which the new tests pin. Tested here: the full `python3 -m pytest -q tests`, `scripts/validate_tasks.py`, `scripts/gen_prompts.py --check`, `scripts/check_plan_lock.py`, `scripts/trace_spec.py`, `bash scripts/prehandin.sh --quick` and `scripts/check_pr_change.py --base origin/main --branch HEAD`; the live `claude/kit-state` state validates with the new schema. - **D-3074** Question (T388; PICK-042, PICK-054, D-244, D-3055): where does the Confirm queue the homeowner's accepted-quote email, and what does its task carry? Choice: `picks::api::settle`'s `SettleStep::Move` branch (the one move from awaiting confirm to `paid` or `free`, under the pick's row lock) queues one `picks.accepted_quote` task (`ACCEPTED_QUOTE_KIND`) after its audit row, in the caller's transaction, payload `{pick, job, business}` only, dedupe `picks.accepted_quote.<pick>`; the settle's SELECT also reads `business_id` (its `.sqlx/` file regenerated), and its signature, `Settled` and the `Was` and `Left` branches are unchanged. `picks::api::accepted_pick(db, job)` (the job's unended pick whose status `shows_release`, newest first) is the one read of "the job's pick is `paid` or `free`" for the handler and the quote page. The handler, `intake::api::run_accepted_quote`, sends nothing (task done) when that read no longer names the task's pick and business, when no open request opened the job, or when the quote no longer reads. Kind: build. Owner approval: Casey's standing delegation. Reason: the move happens once per pick, so the email is queued once and never by a re-settle. Source: `app/picks/src/settle.rs`; `app/intake/src/accepted_quote.rs`.
- **D-3075** Question (T388; PICK-042, WORD-011; D-1957): what are the accepted quote's "type, amount and quote facts", and where are they worded? Choice: `quotes::api::accepted_quote(db, (job, business))` reads the confirmed, unwithdrawn quote through the existing `page_quotes` (page number, the business's words), `quoted_prices` (the stored `Price`) and `earliest_visit` (its day in Arizona), so no new query; `AcceptedQuote::kind` names the format in English and Spanish (the card definitions' leading names, with "Hourly rate" for an hourly price), `amount` writes the price with the LIST text's words and `visit` the day ("Nov 9", "9 nov"). The stored facts are the price and the earliest visit; the other PICK-040 facts are not stored yet (D-1957), so they are not shown. `amount` repeats the private `notify::amount` because `api.rs` is the only quotes file this task may change; the two must change together (said on `amount`'s doc comment and in `app/quotes/CLAUDE.md`). Kind: build. Owner approval: Casey's standing delegation. Reason: one wording for the email and the page, in the crate that owns the quote. Source: `app/quotes/src/api.rs`.

(brand name and domain from `core::api::brand()`), with no link: an email may carry no `data:` card and a home-page link would not add a contact (copy panel). Verified on 53eba4df: `request_link` (`app/calls/src/lifecycle.rs:279`) is exported by `calls::api` and called only by `tests/integration/tests/line_lifecycle.rs`; no code in `app/` handles a "LINK" text (a business phone's text reaches only `phone_stopped` or the auto-reply, `app/server/src/inbound_text.rs:246`); the voice route answers each turn through `voice_turn`/`voice_confirm` and calls nothing after a dial (`app/server/src/inbound_voice.rs:149`). A "blocked call" is read as an unlinked phone made to enter the PIN (D-078); its business is known only once that PIN connects a line (`pins::connect` stores the CallSid's line, `calls.call_start`), so T390's `link_after_dial` queues the notice only then, and a call that connects nothing queues nothing (no business is guessed, so no business is told another's caller's digits). The pending link keeps D-1696's "the full number is never stored": it holds only the caller's keyed `sender-dir` digests, which is all `messaging.sender_directory` keeps for a linked phone (PRIV-002), with an expiry time 24 hours after the request; a pending link is live only while its expiry time is still in the future (TD-CALL-24 refuses one exactly 24 hours old), and is deleted on use or once met no longer live. - **D-3069** Question (T232; SEC-027, SEC-014, SEC-020, TXT-038, A11Y-011, A11Y-012, D-493, D-3055): how does the Confirm page ask for and check SEC-027's fresh code while T261 has not served the route? Choice: `portals::api::confirm_code_needed(db, member, signed_in)` is T199's `fresh_code_needed(Confirm, signed_in, inbox_shared)`. `confirm_page_with_code(facts, Some(CodeStep))` shows "Confirming needs a code sent to your phone" (it said "Only you can confirm this job", which was untrue: anyone with the phone can; changed after review) with why ("This inbox is shared, so others may see this page. Each time you confirm, we text a new code to your own phone."; reworded after the cold read and copy panel), the last send's line (`role="status"`) and a "Text me a code" button in its own small form posting to `/b/picks/{pick}/confirm/code` (T261 serves it with `send_confirm_code`), then the code field inside the Confirm form, so the press script's `FormData` posts it with the press; a failed code gives an "Error: " title, a focused `role="alert"` summary linking to `#code`, the inline error and `aria-invalid` (as the pick code form). `confirm_page(facts)` is unchanged (no code step). `DeviceCodes`' fields are private to `business_auth.rs`, which this task does not own, so `ConfirmCodes::new(verify, code_address, key)` is built from the same three parts. `send_confirm_code` first looks up the person's phone: an email-only person gets `NoPhone`, nothing is sent (an email code would land in the shared inbox) and no send slot is spent; then it passes `admit_code_send(pool, (ip, Some(person)), (now, threshold))` and sends by Verify SMS only to that `CodeTo::Phone`, keyed `verify.confirm_code` over pick, person and time (Twilio ignores the key, D-1776), holding no connection across Verify. `check_confirm_code` refuses a code that is not 6 digits without spending a try, then passes `admit_code_try(pool, (ip, Some(business)), now)`, then asks Verify: true `Right`, false `Wrong`, a 4xx refusal (its 5-check cap, 60202, or an expired or unknown code) `Ended` ("That code has run out"), and no answer, a 5xx or an unreadable answer `Unchecked` ("We couldn't check the code. Type it again, then confirm."), so a network failure never says the code ran out; it writes no `portals.code_try` row. A Confirm code is bound to the phone, not to the pick: Verify keys a pending code by phone number only, so a code still pending for that phone from another flow (a new-device sign-in code, another pick's Confirm code) also passes this check. T261 must therefore accept a code on the Confirm press only after a `send_confirm_code` for this pick and person returned `Sent` within the code's 10 minutes (stored server-side), and refuse the check otherwise. A refused send or try reaches no Verify and charges nothing. Source: `docs/spec/security.md:31`, `app/portals/src/confirm_pay.rs`, `app/portals/templates/confirm_pay.html`.
- **D-3070** Question (T232; TERMS-033, TD-TERMS-11, D-493): how is a Confirm press's business-terms acceptance stored? Choice: migration `0159_businesses_confirm_terms.sql` adds nullable `pick_id` to `businesses.terms_acceptance`, widens the channel check to `business_signup` and `confirm_page` and adds `terms_acceptance_pick_check` (`pick_id` set exactly on `confirm_page` rows), both `NOT VALID` then validated, and the partial unique index `terms_acceptance_pick_idx` on `pick_id`; 0119's append-only revoke stands and T081's insert (channel `business_signup`, no pick) is untouched. `businesses::api::record_confirm_terms(conn, (business, person), pick, ConfirmTerms { version, published_text, language }, now)` inserts document `business_terms`, the version as text, the SHA256 of the published text, the language and `confirm_assent_line(version)` ("You're agreeing to business terms version <n>.", the page's own line) with `ON CONFLICT (pick_id) WHERE pick_id IS NOT NULL DO NOTHING`, so it is safe in the press's transaction and a second press for the pick returns false and stores nothing; the time comes from the caller's clock, so the signature gains `now`. `docs/architecture.md` section 3 lists tables, not columns, and does not list `businesses.terms_acceptance`, so the column is recorded in the "What T232 built" paragraph and the locked section is unchanged. Source: `docs/spec/terms.md:36`, `app/businesses/src/confirm_terms.rs`.
- **D-3071** Question (T232; OPS-037, BIZ-045, D-2412): which notice does opening the Confirm page stamp? Choice: `portals::api::open_confirm_page(db, (business, job, member), now)` finds the member among `businesses::api::members(business)` (not a current member: nothing), then the latest `Pick` row of `messaging::api::notice_log(business, job)` sent to that member's own mailbox, and stamps it through `record_first_open` (once; a reload, a card notice, another person's pick notice and another business's log stay as they were). A pick notice that reached the person only through a backup address is not stamped (the backup's mailbox is not the member's). Source: `app/portals/src/confirm_pay.rs`, `app/portals/src/business_actions.rs` (`open_quote_form`).

- **D-3094** Question (plan change outside the runner, November 11, 2026, before the runner claims them; an independent read-only pre-flight audit of `main` 6a428761, each finding re-verified here against the code; D-3055's and D-3083's precedent; CON-016, CON-030, CON-009, TXT-040, BIZ-049, LIC-002, LIC-046, CON-010, AI-020, CON-018, QH-002, JOB-006, OPS-004, LIC-011, BIZ-016; TD-CON-34, TD-TXT-25, TD-BIZ-30, TD-BIZ-46, TD-CON-32, TD-QH-06, TD-OPS-38, TD-LIC-30): which queued tasks would stop on a plan gap or mislead their worker as written, and what is the smallest fix for each? Choice, per task. **(1) T360.** Evidence: the goal sent the CON-030 confirmation "through `send_email`" and put new homeowner email templates in `en.json` and `es.json`; but queueing is `queue_email` (`app/messaging/src/email.rs:343`, unowned, T094's), which takes `(secret, postal)` and renders only its fixed `Notice` list (`:149`: `TextFailed`, `OptedOut`, `StillOpen`), and a new homeowner template would break the done TD-TXT-25 test (`app/quotes/src/tests/update_texts.rs:133`), which needs every homeowner template in `UPDATE_TEXTS` or `NOT_UPDATE_TEXTS` (`app/quotes/src/update_texts.rs:112`, a fixed `[&str; 43]`, not T360's), and the registry tests' fixed sample values (`app/messaging/src/tests/template_registry.rs:8`, `app/intake/src/tests/intake_timeouts.rs:53`). Fix: the confirmation reuses `Notice::OptedOut` (`email.rs:153`), which already renders the CON-009 text (`opt_out_confirmation`, `:245`), so it needs no template; the wrote-again email is built in Rust in `optout_email.rs` and stored through `models::insert_email` (`app/messaging/src/models.rs:525`), as `queue_check_in_email` does (`app/messaging/src/checkin_email.rs:208`), and sent by `send_email`; nothing is added to `en.json` or `es.json`, which leave T360's owns (owns and budget files 4 to 2), so `update_texts.rs` and the registry tests are untouched and T360 needs no ordering with T318. A first draft of this change instead gave T360 `update_texts.rs` with dependencies on T278 and from T318, which lengthened T360's critical-path chain from 42 to 47 (the review's measure) and made it the next claim after T387 (harmless, but no longer needed); an independent review found the `Notice` limit, and that draft was replaced before merge. **(2) T368.** Evidence: T207's done `tests/integration/tests/license_change_reapply.rs` builds the catalog from the file and never stores it (no `catalog::api::load`), so if `reapply_license` read only the stored switch, `catalog.category` would be empty and `assert!(!change.offered.is_empty())` at `:99` would fail. Fix: a category with no stored row falls back to the file's `enabled` flag, the value `load` gives a new category (`app/catalog/src/service.rs:20`); a stored row, on or off, always wins. Chosen over a second stored-set entry point because it keeps one rule and `reapply_license`'s signature: a switch-off is always a stored row (`set_category_enabled` refuses an unknown category), so LIC-002 holds, and an unstored category is exactly the shipped default, which LIC-003's catalog check already keeps off unless confirmed. **(3) T350.** Evidence: the goal's "\"Bob here\" then \"stop texting me\"" case passes on today's `main`: "here" is no name trigger (`TRIGGERS`, `app/privacy/src/scrub.rs:197`), so nothing is remembered; the failing case is "This is Bob stop texting me" (`mark_stated`, `:657`, cuts "bob" and "stop", and `newly_stated` stores both) then "Stop texting me please" (`mark_known` removes "stop", leaving "[removed] texting me please", which no `OPT_OUT_PHRASES` entry matches). Fix: the goal and TD-CON-32 (`docs/test-design.md:360`) name that case. **(4) T358.** Evidence: `AreaCodes::parse` (`app/messaging/src/rules.rs:70`, not owned) reads only `BTreeMap<String, Vec<String>>` and refuses any key that is not a known time zone (`:74`). Fix: the "or a tag in the same file" option is deleted; the country is read from the zone. **(5) T366.** Evidence: `jobs` and `server` may name no other module's schema in SQL (`tests/integration/tests/architecture_migrations.rs:44`, `:250`), so neither can count dead letters by kind or revive a `core.task` row; T327 put its `dead_without_handler` in the shared `app/core/src/api.rs` (`:46`) for that reason. Fix: the goal puts the per-kind count and the one-row revive there and says `core/src/tasks.rs` is not needed. **(6) T385.** Evidence: `numbers_agree` and `compared` are private (`app/licensing/src/rules.rs:203`, `:211`) in a file T347 (QUEUED) owns; the goal's `:201` was stale. Fix: `own_record.rs` copies the comparison locally or uses the public `city_list_standing`, never editing `rules.rs`. State checked on `claude/kit-state` before any edit: T350, T358, T360, T366, T368 and T385 QUEUED with 0 attempts, none resync-marked. No requirement line changes; TD-CON-32's row names the failing case. Changed: `kit/tasks.json` (T360: `goal`, `owns`, `budget`, `decisions`; T368, T350, T358, T366, T385: `goal`, `decisions`), `kit/prompts/` for those six tasks, `docs/test-design.md` (TD-CON-32), `kit/plan.lock`, `docs/decisions.md`, `docs/for-casey-review.md`. This decision joins the `decisions` of T360, T368, T350, T358, T366 and T385. Numbered by: reserved before this change (D-1058). Kind: plan change. Owner approval: not needed (BUILD_BRIEF section 16); listed for Casey. Reason: each task as written would stop on a plan gap after a claim or mislead its worker; every fix keeps every done test byte-identical, adds no requirement and loosens nothing. Open, not fixed here (found by the review of this change, verified): intake's `catalog::api::is_enabled` (`app/catalog/src/api.rs:72`) reads a category with no stored row as off while T368's fallback reads the file's flag, and nothing in `app/` outside `catalog` calls `catalog::api::load_embedded`, though its doc says to run it at start-up (`api.rs:18`), so a fresh deployment's stored catalog is empty, intake treats every category as off and the checklist would offer the file's set; listed for Casey for the next plan change (a start-up load in the composition, so stored rows always exist). Source: `app/messaging/src/email.rs:149`, `app/messaging/src/checkin_email.rs:208`, `app/quotes/src/tests/update_texts.rs:133`, `app/messaging/src/email.rs:343`, `tests/integration/tests/license_change_reapply.rs:99`, `app/catalog/src/service.rs:20`, `app/privacy/src/scrub.rs:197`, `app/messaging/src/rules.rs:70`, `tests/integration/tests/architecture_migrations.rs:250`, `app/core/src/api.rs:46`, `app/licensing/src/rules.rs:203`.
- **D-3089** Question (T348; TD-SEC-61, SEC-019; D-2440): the goal gives the `Public` door to "any route the `site` module serves", and also says homeowner and business pages need their realm's session; which door does a `site` route under `/h`, `/b` or `/owner` get? Choice: the realm's: in `door` (both `tests/security/tests/auth_matrix.rs` and `app/server/tests/door_matrix.rs`) the named public paths (`/healthz`, `/help` and below, the five legal pages) and the link, sign-in, action-link, owner, homeowner and business prefixes are tried first, and a `site` route is public only when none of them names it (`door_cases.txt`: `Homeowner /h/requests site`). The route table records the module of each `.route(` call (`routes()`, whose `bool` is "a `site` call serves it"). Reason: a public page under a realm prefix would skip the realm's session test; the stricter door fails loudly (the probe demands the realm's refusal), the looser one would not. Source: `kit/prompts/T348.md` goal (1); D-1945. Kind: design.
- **D-3090** Question (T348; TD-SEC-61, SEC-019; D-736, TD-SEC-10): the goal says the six actors are "signed in the way `auth_matrix.rs` signs them in", but that file writes `portals.business_session` with a raw `sqlx::query`, which `tests/integration/tests/architecture_migrations.rs` refuses anywhere under `app/` (the SQL-form and own-schema checks walk every `.rs` of each crate, tests included); and the `{pick}` and `{complaint}` fills need real records. Choice: the same realms and actors, made through module APIs only: homeowners A and B get a homeowner session on their own vault contact (`privacy::store_contact`, fake name, phone and street) whose request names their job (`intake`); the owner a plain `Realm::Owner` session as in `auth_matrix.rs`; businesses X and Y sign in through `portals`' own emailed-link sign-in (`signin_request` then `signin_post` on a test-local `SignIn` router with a one-address fake mail), which writes the business session row; each business's job is carded and quoted by it (`quotes::send_cards`, `submit_quote`), page-picked by its homeowner (`picks::page_pick`), given a quote token (`jobs`) and a complaint (`businesses::record_complaint`), and a Quote action link is minted for its owner (`portals::mint_action_link`). Each actor's realm is asserted after sign-in, so the fixtures are proven even while no row is probed. Reason: the only way to the same sessions that the architecture test allows; the release-recovery test builds its picks the same way (D-2013). Source: `kit/prompts/T348.md` goal (3); `tests/integration/tests/architecture_migrations.rs` `check_sql_forms`, `check_query_schemas`; `app/server/tests/release_recovery.rs`. Kind: design.
- **D-3091** Question (T348; TD-SEC-61, SEC-048; TD-SEC-10): the probe must find "one `csrf_rejected` security event naming the route template" per refused `POST`, but `server` code may not name `portals.security_event` and `portals::api` has no reader. Choice: `door_matrix.rs` installs a capturing `tracing` subscriber (`Events`, `tracing::subscriber::set_default` for the test) and reads the `security event` line `portals::record_security_event` writes once per event (kind, route template, request ID), matched by the request's `x-request-id`; `judge_csrf` demands a 403 and exactly one `[csrf_rejected, <template>]`. No new crate (only `tracing`, already a dependency). A portals reader function was not added: it would be production code serving only a test. Reason: the line and the row come from the same call, so one line is one event. Limit: `record_security_event` writes the log line before it inserts the row, so the probe proves the event was attempted, not that its row was stored; the row itself stays covered by `auth_matrix.rs`' `sec_048_every_refusal_is_a_security_event`, which reads `portals.security_event` for the link routes. Source: `app/portals/src/security.rs` `record_security_event`; `kit/prompts/T348.md` goal (3). Kind: design.
- **D-3092** Question (T348; size budget 3 files, 800 changed lines): the work came to about 1,450 changed lines in the three owned files (`door_matrix.rs` about 1,200 after `cargo fmt`). Choice: hand in over budget rather than drop a demanded case: the fixtures of D-3090 (about 250 lines: carded, quoted and picked jobs, vault contacts and requests, complaints, links, the business sign-in), the router of fake settings copied from `route_wiring.rs` (which the probe may not import), the restated door rules, the judging code, the event capture and the planted cases all are named in the goal. - **D-3093** Question (T348; TD-SEC-61; SEC-019, SEC-026, SEC-037): how does the probe judge what the goal leaves open? Choice: (1) "the one not-found answer" is the reply to the same path with fresh unknown IDs (for an action link: an unissued token): the foreign reply must equal it byte for byte with a 404, `no-store` on the action-link door; (2) a homeowner's admitted `GET` is a 200 that never shows the other homeowner's quote token or `request <number>`; a business's admitted `GET` is a 200; on a homeowner or business route with `{pick}` or `{complaint}`, A (or X) is also sent B's (or Y's) ID on its own session and must get (1); (3) the action-link row is probed for every actor with a fresh Quote link minted for X's owner on A's job (Quote acts by the link alone, BIZ-038), and the wrong ones are a Hold kind, B's job as object, and a token minted for Y's owner on B's job, each on X's path; the path names kind, object and token but no member, so the last case is refused by its object (it differs from the second only in the token), and "another member" on the same kind and object is not separately probed: the link is the key, and the member it acts for is the one recorded at minting; a `GET` must leave `open_action_link` as it was; (4) refusals and public pages are searched for every fixture name, phone, street, quote and action-link token and `request <number>`; (5) a row's `Module` cell `site` marks a `site` route for the door rule. Reason: the goal's wording made concrete, one rule per sentence. Source: `kit/prompts/T348.md` goal (3), the PR #421 amendment. Kind: design.
- **D-3100** Question (plan change outside the runner, November 12, 2026, before the runner claims them; D-3055's, D-3083's and D-3094's pre-flight precedent and D-3079's budget precedent; FEE-012, FEE-014, FEE-045, PICK-022, LIC-001, LIC-002, LIC-003; D-2076, D-2302, D-1754; TD-FEE-25, TD-FEE-45, TD-FEE-58, TD-LIC-27, new TD-LIC-31; new register row IC-96; new task T400): T261's prompt names a `no_fee_release` signature that no longer exists and measures over its context limit, and D-3094 left the catalog's start-up load unowned with two readers disagreeing on a category that has no stored row; what is the smallest fix? Choice. **(1) T261.** Evidence: the goal says `payments::api::no_fee_release(conn, pick)`, but since T337 it is `no_fee_release(conn, pick, (business, job))` (`app/payments/src/release_proof.rs:237`, called so in `app/server/tests/release_recovery.rs:343`); the goal names T260's `StripeHttp`, which does not exist (D-2076: `adapters::api::StripePayments` implements `IntentStripe`, `app/payments/src/intent_http.rs:15`); `python3 scripts/gen_prompts.py --check --strict` measured the prompt at 46% against its 45% limit, 149,099 bytes of it (about 19 points) the whole off-database records section of `docs/architecture.md`, counted only because the goal asked to update that section by number (`gen_prompts.cited_sections`, D-1350). Pre-flight: T224's done `tests/e2e/confirm_pay.spec.ts` (TD-FEE-25, `:118` to `:126`) gives a fake `handleNextAction` that answers success at once and asserts "Your bank wants to check" (`:123`); T261's goal (3) makes success replace that line with the checking line in the same turn of the event loop, so the asserted line is never visible and the case would fail while the goal said the file "stays as it is". Fix: the goal names the three-argument call with the pick's own business and job and `StripePayments`; it adds one line to the off-database notes, found by grep and never loaded whole (D-3079's way), so the section is no longer counted and no read is dropped; T261 owns `tests/e2e/confirm_pay.spec.ts` for that one case only: the case holds the fake's answer until it has asserted the bank line and the `3ds` call, then asserts the checking line while its stand-in holds the answer to the page's state ask, and only then releases that answer, so neither line can race; every other case stays byte-identical, so nothing is loosened (owns and budget files 5 to 6, acceptance updated); T261 becomes a harness task for it (title "(harness)", review area `harness`; only a harness task changes an earlier task's test, `scripts/validate_tasks.py:613`), as T337 did. Checked and not a gap: `tests/security/tests/headers.rs` and `no_third_party.rs` test the self-only constant and other pages, which T261 keeps; `app/server/src/lib.rs` is a shared path; the "Can't take it" link is already in T224's template (`app/portals/templates/confirm_pay.html:57`). **(2) Catalog.** Evidence: nothing in `app/` outside `catalog` calls `catalog::api::load_embedded` (`app/catalog/src/api.rs:25`), whose doc says to run it at start-up; `app/server/src/main.rs` builds the pool and serves with no catalog step, so on a fresh deployment `catalog.category` is empty; `is_enabled` (`:72`) and `enabled_categories` (`ai`'s reader) read a category with no stored row as off, while D-3094 gave T368 a fallback to the file's `enabled` flag. One rule: a stored row, on or off, wins and a category with no stored row is off. Chosen over the fallback because it fails closed (LIC-003: an unconfirmed category stays off), it is what both existing readers and their done tests (`tests/integration/tests/catalog_settings.rs`, `tests/integration/tests/not_covered.rs`) already hold, so no done catalog code changes, and the fallback would have left `ai`'s list and intake on a different rule. So: new build task T400 (stage 4, Sonnet worker with an Opus reviewer, D-2506's tiering for a low-risk task; deps T021, T009 and T075, all done, T075 because the stage-3 cleanup owns `app/`) owns `app/server/src/catalog_start.rs` and `app/server/tests/catalog_start.rs` (new TD-LIC-31) and calls `load_embedded` from the web path of `main.rs` (a shared path) before serving; a failure refuses to start; a repeat load never switches a category on (`app/catalog/src/service.rs:19`), so a restart keeps the owner's switches (LIC-002). T368 drops D-3094's fallback and follows the rule; T207's done `tests/integration/tests/license_change_reapply.rs` never stores the catalog and asserts a non-empty offer at `:99` and `:230`, so T368 owns it for one setup line only (`catalog::api::load(db, &catalog())` in the shared `r11_business` helper, `:40`, which every case uses; every assertion byte-identical), as D-2896 gave T337 a fixture-only fix (owns and budget files 3 to 4), and becomes a harness task for it in the same way. T100 (stage-4 cleanup) gains T400, and T302 (QUEUED, 0 attempts, no resync mark) gains T400, because the served sign-up reads T368's stored switch and before T400 a fresh database offers no category; T400's deps are all done, so no cycle. Register row IC-96 (product) names T400 and T368 with TD-LIC-31 and TD-LIC-27. State checked on `claude/kit-state` before any edit: T261, T368, T100 and T302 QUEUED with 0 attempts, none resync-marked; T400 is new. Changed: `kit/tasks.json` (T261 and T368: `title`, `type`, `review_areas`, `goal`, `owns`, `budget`, `decisions`, and T261's `acceptance`; T100: `deps`; T302: `deps`, `decisions`; new T400), `kit/prompts/` for T261, T368, T302 and T400 (T100's prompt does not change), `docs/test-design.md` (TD-LIC-31), `docs/integration-closure.md` (IC-96), `kit/plan.lock`, `docs/decisions.md`, `docs/for-casey-review.md`. This decision joins the `decisions` of T261, T368, T302 and T400; for T368 it sets aside choice (2) of D-3094 (the fallback), and only that choice. Numbered by: reserved before this change (D-1058). Kind: plan change. Owner approval: not needed (BUILD_BRIEF section 16); listed for Casey. Reason: a worker given a wrong signature, a missing type or an owned-elsewhere test that its own change must break stops on a plan gap after a claim; a budget the runner checks must be met; and a category switch is only a settings change (LIC-002) when every reader reads the same stored switch and the rows exist. - **D-3085** Question (T317; SEC-014, SEC-015, D-1951, D-1953, D-2041 (2), D-2206, D-3083): how does `admit_new_request` count inside the delivery's transaction, and what does the route do with each answer? Choice: `core::api::rate_limit_hit_on` (`rate_limit::hit_on`) runs `hit`'s upsert on a `&mut PgConnection`; `hit` keeps its signature and now acquires one connection and calls it (same statement, so `.sqlx/` is unchanged). `admit_new_request` takes `A: Acquire<'a, Database = Postgres> + Send + 'a` and returns `impl Future + Send + 'a` (an `async fn` over `Acquire` fails axum's `Send` check with "implementation of `Acquire` is not general enough" when handed `&mut PgConnection`); it acquires one connection, opens a transaction on it (a savepoint inside the delivery's), and counts per phone, per IP when given, then `REQUESTS_ALL` last; the first refusal of a scope in its window takes the `<scope>:alerted` marker and writes the alert on the same connection, so marker and alert commit or roll back together and need no retry (`admit` over a pool keeps D-1953's `ALERT_TRIES`). A `&PgPool` caller gets the same counts, each call now one short transaction (`tests/security/tests/rate_limits.rs` unchanged and passing). The route counts only for a homeowner with no open request and not for a START text (narrowed by D-3087 to a START that lifted her listing, and a 911-list text added; HELP and STOP already ended at `screen`), as the last step before `receive_reply`, which makes no network call (INT-021); `Refused` ends the text with 200 (`Halt::Ends("limited")`): the inbox row is kept, so Twilio's resend is a repeat, nothing opens and nothing is queued; a counter or alert error is `Halt::Database` (500, the whole delivery rolls back, so it counted nothing). TD-SEC-52's "Low alert" is `REQUESTS_PER_PHONE`'s Normal alert, the lowest severity `ops.alert` has (`critical`, `high`, `normal`), one per scope and window and with no subject, so it holds no body or phone. Open item, closed by D-3087: a 911-list text is now never counted or refused. Kind: fix. Reason: D-2041 (2)'s double count and D-1951's missing call, closed in the delivery's transaction as D-3083 requires. Source: `app/core/src/rate_limit.rs` `hit_on`; `app/intake/src/limits.rs` `admit_new_request`, `admit_on`; `app/server/src/inbound_text.rs` `admitted`; `migrations/0021_ops_audit.sql:37`.

- **D-3087** Question (T317 fix round, review of e4531830; SEC-014, SEC-015, INT-002, INT-003, CON-015, D-3085): D-3085 refused a 911-list text from a homeowner with no open request when her limit (or `REQUESTS_ALL`) was full, so she got no INT-002 safety text; and its START exemption was word-based, so a number never on the opt-out list could text START and open a request uncounted. What does the route do? Choice: (1) a text whose `intake` 911 screen matched (`msg.emergency`, the same flag `receive_reply` and the T279 paused path read) is never counted and never refused, so `receive_reply` runs and queues `emergency_911` as on every other path; safety beats the limit (INT-002 and INT-003 apply to every inbound message, SEC-014 does not name emergencies). Recorded risk: a flood of texts carrying 911-list words from many phones skips `REQUESTS_ALL`; each still needs its own phone and opens a request Casey sees, and a separate emergency cap would need a spec change, so it is flagged in `docs/for-casey-review.md`, not built. (2) `screen` now returns whether `messaging::api::on_inbound_text` answered `Outcome::Resubscribed` (the provider's START that lifted a current listing, CON-015), and only that START is exempt; a START from a number that was not listed is `Outcome::Open` and counted like any new request. (3) Recorded gap, not changed: `intake::api::open_request_jobs` and `receive_reply`'s own open-conversation read are two reads in one READ COMMITTED transaction, so a request closed or opened by another transaction between them can make one text counted that opens nothing new, or uncounted that opens one; the window is one delivery's few statements, the worst case is one miscount, and closing it needs `receive_reply` to take the decision, which is `intake`'s change. Kind: fix. Reason: the review's finding 1 (safety) and 2 (exemption tied to the list, small); 3 noted. Source: `app/server/src/inbound_text.rs` `intake`, `screen`; `app/messaging/src/optout.rs` `Outcome::Resubscribed`; test `tests/integration/tests/inbound_text_guards.rs` `td_sec_52_an_emergency_at_the_limit_still_gets_the_911_text`.
- **D-3044** Question (T228; BIZ-051, BIZ-054, PICK-047, PICK-051; D-446, D-463, D-491): how does leaving run, and how is "asked once" kept? Choice: `portals::api::leave` is the owner's button, after `require_step_up` as a saved-card change (SEC-038; the refusal event is kept because the check runs before the transaction), and does the rest in one transaction: `businesses::api::record_reason` (the answer or none), `businesses::api::leave` (`removed` through `service::apply`, with its status audit row), `picks::api::waiting_picks_of` and `end_for_leaving` for each waiting pick (ended `cancelled` with `end_reason` `ineligible`, no fee, then `backup_choice`; with no pick waiting the job returns to Quotes ready), `quotes::api::withdraw_for_leaving` (each unwithdrawn quote on a job that still `takes_quotes`, under the job's row lock, even after a pick, since the business's own PICK-051 edit lock does not apply to leaving), `payments::api::remove_saved_cards` (`removed_at` set, rows kept) and the end of every session and unused sign-in link of the business; the cards are detached at Stripe after the commit through the caller's `CardDetach` (R11). The ledger and audit rows are never touched. `ineligible` is used, not a new `business_left` code, because a migration may name only its own schema (`tests/integration/tests/architecture_migrations.rs`) and `picks`' existing code already means "the account can no longer take this pick" (PICK-020's refusal). "Asked once" is one `businesses.leave_reason` row per business (`migrations/0161_businesses_leaving.sql`, append-only), stored when the question's form is posted (a GET changes nothing, SEC-026), whether a choice was made or not; a business that answered at a long pause is not asked again when it leaves, and its first answer stays. The pause question is due only while the business is paused for strictly more than `PAUSE_ASK_AFTER_DAYS` (14) days since its status changed; the spec calls it a setting, and it is a function argument with that constant until an `ASKHAVA_*` key is added (D-3045). The "Something else" box is kept only beside that choice, trimmed and cut to 500 characters, and never shown in `Debug`. Nothing reads `leave_reason` but `leaving.rs` (pinned by a source scan in `tests/integration/tests/business_leaving.rs`), so the answer cannot change routing or fees. Kind: build. Source: `docs/spec/businesses.md:55`, `docs/spec/businesses.md:58`.
