- **D-3081** Question (plan change outside the runner, November 11, 2026; number reserved from the live counter; stacked on D-3079's branch, which opened register row IC-95 with owner `none`; revised after two independent Opus reviews of this change; BIZ-033, CALL-012, BIZ-038, SEC-038; D-078, D-311, D-288, D-480, D-963, D-1695, D-1848, D-1955, D-2128, D-2440, D-2636; new TD-BIZ-52, TD-BIZ-53, TD-CALL-25, TD-SEC-65 and TD-SEC-66, TD-BIZ-34 reworded; new tasks T396, T398, T397 and T399): BIZ-033 (`docs/spec/businesses.md:37`) and CALL-012 (`docs/spec/calls.md:16`) say a phone linked by a member other than the owner works only after the owner approves it. Verified on D-3079's head 09768c35: `team::link_phone` (`app/businesses/src/team.rs:439`) and `team::change_phone` (`:503`) write the number's digests into `messaging.sender_directory` in the same transaction, so `messaging::api::sender_business` (the inbound text route's lookup) and `calls::routing::party_of` (`app/calls/src/routing.rs:419`, the one party lookup of routing and both PIN paths) treat the phone as the business at once; `calls::lifecycle::phone_works` and `gate` (`app/calls/src/lifecycle.rs:241`, `:248`) are called only by `tests/integration/tests/line_lifecycle.rs`; `businesses.staff_phone` (`migrations/0056_businesses_team_members.sql:32`) has no approval column; the email's Approve action link (`ActionKind::Approve`, `app/portals/src/action_links.rs:59`, served by T301) only uses up the link, though SEC-038 already guards the change (`SensitiveChange::ApprovePhone`, `app/portals/src/business_portal.rs:59`, D-480); and D-1695 left the approval to T148 and the gate to T080, both DONE without either. Who owns IC-95, and how is the approval enforced? Choice: **(1) T396** (stage 4, harness, Opus): a phone's standing is `staff_phone.approved_at IS NOT NULL` alone; the owner's link and number change store `approved_at = now` (so the owner's act and the owner's approval are one fact), as does the phone T391's LINK reply adds (the main phone's reply is the owner's act, CALL-012; T396 takes `app/businesses/src/reply_link.rs` after T391 for that line). A link or a number change by any other member (`team_member.is_owner` false, so a "Confirm and billing" member holding both roles too) stores `approved_at` NULL and moves the number's digests into a new `messaging.sender_held` table in the same transaction, whatever the phone's standing was, so no member can put a working number in place by changing an approved or owner-linked phone; every change first drops the phone's held digests, so an approval releases only the current number. The owner's `approve_phone` moves the digests back (a number another phone took meanwhile refuses the approval and changes nothing); `reject_phone` deletes the phone and its held digests; both owner-only, one audit row of IDs each. The hold keeps D-963's shape: `SenderLink` is unchanged (no test's fake directory changes) and `messaging::api::sender_hold` needs no vault. An approval names the number it approves, not only the phone: `staff_phone.number_set_at` and `number_set_by` record when and by whom the current number was set, every link and change writes them, and `approve_phone` and `reject_phone` take the `number_set_at` the owner was shown and refuse a mismatch (`NumberChanged`), since a member's change keeps the phone's ID; T396 also takes `app/businesses/src/tests/team.rs` (T220's) only for the `now` argument `change_phone` gains. `staff_phone.number_end` keeps the last 4 digits so the owner can tell which phone to approve (staff data; the LINK notice already names them, D-078; never the whole number). Migration `0186_businesses_phone_approval.sql`; rows existing when it runs get `approved_at = linked_at` (linked under the earlier rule; no row exists outside a test database before Gate C, so no standing changes and no cross-schema statement is needed). It is a harness task because `tests/integration/tests/sender_directory_sync.rs` and `tests/integration/tests/team_members.rs` (T220, DONE) assert that a member-linked phone, and in `td_biz_34_a_staff_phone_follows_into_the_directory` (`:91`) a member-changed number, is found at once, the opposite of BIZ-033; TD-BIZ-34 now ends "except that a phone a member other than the owner links, or changes to a new number, enters it only when the owner approves it, and never once declined (BIZ-033, D-3081)", and those tests gain only absence checks and the owner's approval before their existing assertions (`BUILD_BRIEF.md:69`: the spec already decides; this entry logs the test-design change). Deps T391, T322, T220. **(2) T398** (stage 4, build): the gate behind the hold in both routes. `party_of` resolves a directory hit through `messaging::api::sender_line`, reads `businesses::api::phone_standing` and applies `gate` (`calls` may call `businesses`, `kit/layers.json`; `businesses` may not call `calls`, so the gate lives in routing); the inbound text route treats a directory-named sender as the business (`phone_stopped`, the auto-reply, the LINK reply) only when the phone is approved, else as an unknown number. So a digest left in the directory by any path still cannot act for the business by call or text; the review asked that the text route not rely on the hold alone. T398 also closes the two other sending paths the second review found: `notice_recipients` (`app/businesses/src/channel_preference.rs:142`, the one list every business notice text reads its phones from, used by `app/quotes/src/card_notices.rs:86` and `emergency_card_notice.rs`) had no approval filter, so a waiting phone would get job card texts; it now lists only approved phones and a member with no approved phone gets the email. A re-grep of every `businesses.staff_phone` reader outside `team.rs` found only that list and `consent.rs` (an existence check and `may_text`, which gate texts already listed and send nothing themselves). And a member's number change sent the owner no new email (the `businesses.phone_linked` task was keyed by phone alone, `app/businesses/src/complaints.rs:521`); the key now adds `number_set_at` and `api::change_phone` queues the email on a member's change, so the owner is told of every number they are asked to approve. Deps T396, T365 (last earlier owner of `routing.rs`), T391 (of `inbound_text.rs`), T147 (of `channel_preference.rs`) and T293 (of `complaints.rs`); T299 gains T398. **(3) T397** (stage 5, build): the owner's `GET /b/phones` lists waiting phones with the linking member's sign-in email address (a member has no stored name; read from the vault in `server` by `mailbox_id`, as notice addresses are, D-1848), the last 4 digits and the linked time, each form carrying the `number_set_at` shown, with Approve and Don't approve (`POST /b/phones/approve`, `/b/phones/reject`, the line in the form body so T348's probe needs no path parameter), behind the business session, owner only, CSRF and cross-site refusal, `no_store` and SEC-038's step-up. **(4) T399** (stage 5, build): the email's Approve link `POST` approves only with its owner's session and a fresh step-up, and only when the link was issued (`portals.login_link.created_at`) at or after the phone's `number_set_at`, so a link from an email about an earlier number approves nothing; otherwise, and for an expired link, nothing is approved and the link stays unused. Ambiguities decided: the spec names no way to decline; a declined phone is deleted, which changes nothing a rule observes (a phone not approved never works either way) and lets the owner clear a phone they don't recognise. The spec does not say whether a member's number change needs approval again; it does, since otherwise a member could make any number work by changing an approved phone, which is what BIZ-033 forbids. - **D-3095** Question (T313; SEC-028, D-1826 (1), D-2203, D-2287, D-493): no setting held the email footer's postal line, so no business-notice or receipt sender could be built; what key, and where is it checked? Choice: `ASKHAVA_POSTAL_ADDRESS` in `core`'s typed settings (`Settings::postal_address`, trimmed; absent or blank is `SettingsError::Missing` naming the key). `core` cannot call `messaging`, so the mailbox check stays `messaging::api::PostalAddress`: `server`'s `notice_senders` takes a line that names a P.O. box as `MailboxKind::PoBox`, else checks it as a private mailbox, and refuses any other line with "setting ASKHAVA_POSTAL_ADDRESS has an invalid value" (never the value). Without the key dev and CI register neither sender (the tasks wait, as with `twilio_config`) and test and live refuse to start naming it. The email idempotency key and the version-1 link key are `ID_SECRET`, as `job_text_keys` already uses them. Source: `app/core/src/settings.rs`, `app/server/src/lib.rs` (`notice_senders`).
- **D-3096** Question (T313; D-2203, D-3083, D-2853, D-736): the prompt says to register `messaging.business_notice` in `server::register_handlers`, which takes no settings, and the postal setting must decide the registration as `twilio_config` does; and TD-CARD-15 and TD-FEE-55 must run "through the worker" from a test crate that may not depend on `askhava-server`. Choice: the two registrations sit in `worker_registry` (the same shared `app/server/src/lib.rs`, which already takes the settings and holds the `twilio_config` precedent the prompt names), through `register_notice_senders`; `register_handlers`' signature is unchanged, so every caller and `tests/integration/tests/task_registry.rs` (no postal key in its stand-in pairs, both kinds still in `tests/task_kinds_deferred.json`) are unchanged. `tests/integration/tests/emergency_notices.rs` compiles `app/server/src/lib.rs` in place exactly as `task_registry.rs` does (a second logged exception under D-2853, with the same `#[allow(dead_code, reason)]`), so its cases run `worker_registry`'s real registry, `NoticeChecks` included, on a manual clock, then hand each stored email to a fake provider through `send_email`. Source: `app/server/src/lib.rs`, `tests/integration/tests/emergency_notices.rs`.
- **D-3097** Question (T313; CARD-021, CARD-020, QH-004, QH-005, BIZ-037; D-2011 (1)): how does `business_notice` treat an EMERGENCY card? Choice: a payload with `emergency: true` must carry `subject` and `first_line` strings (else it is malformed: nothing is stored and the task fails with "business notice is malformed", never an EMERGENCY email under the ordinary subject); it skips `held_until` entirely, since `quotes::queue_emergency_card` chose its at-once recipients under QH-004 and BIZ-037 and queued the rest as a second task due at 8 a.m.; its email's subject is the payload's and its first line precedes the template's words (HTML and plain part); `{time}`, the card, the statement and the job-page link are as for any card. Texts are unchanged (the emergency card is queued email only). Any payload without `emergency: true` is held at night exactly as before (every `business_notices.rs` case passes unchanged). `run_business_notice` loads the stored lines with no configured number, since none is stored yet (D-492), so a business text candidate gets the email; `NoticeChecks::accept_by` maps a `picks::api::notice_sent` error to `None` (the pick notice is then `Dropped`), as `SendChecks` has no error channel. Known gap accepted by the plan: an `emergency: true` notice skips the night hold and the worker does not re-check its recipients at send time, so a daytime emergency card queued for everyone and delayed past 20:00 (a retry or a backlog) could reach members without the "Emergency emails at any hour" switch; a follow-up should have `quotes` put a chosen-at-night flag in the payload or add a send-time `night_people` check. The T313 diff is over the 450-line budget, mainly from `tests/integration/tests/emergency_notices.rs`'s setup helpers. Source: `app/messaging/src/business_notices.rs`.

- **D-3107** Question (T325, fourth audit F25, D-2207; TXT-012, D-801, D-1311, PRIV-016, PRIV-028): how the inbound-text route records a text a non-database module error stopped (`Halt::Failed`, answered 200 so Twilio never resends, body never stored), and where the failed step goes when an `ops.alert` row has no field for it? Choice: `text` runs `receive_inbound` and then the rest of the steps (`handle`); on `Halt::Failed(step, _)` it calls `failure_alert`, which in the delivery's transaction (committed on `Halt::Failed`) raises one High `messaging.inbound_text_failed` alert (`FAILED_ALERT`) with subject (`messaging.inbox`, the inbox row) through `ops::api::raise_alert`, and writes one system audit row through `ops::api::audit` with the same code name as action, subject (`ops.alert`, the alert's ID) and `Change::Field(step)`; the step is a code name written in code, the error's variant name stays on the warn line only, and neither row can hold a body, phone or address (both tables accept code names and IDs only). One per inbox row needs no lock: a resend of the MessageSid stops at `receive_inbound`'s repeat check before `handle`, and the whole delivery is one transaction. A failed alert or audit write maps to `Halt::Database` (500, rollback, Twilio resends), chosen over `ops_halt`'s `Failed("ops")`, so a failure is never committed unseen. No field is added to `Webhooks` (D-2206). Kind: build. Reason: Casey sees the alert in the owner portal and digest and can ask the sender to write again; the step tells him where it stopped without any of the text. Source: `app/server/src/inbound_text.rs` `text`, `failure_alert`; `app/ops/src/service.rs` `raise_alert`; test `tests/integration/tests/inbound_text_failures.rs` `td_txt_34_a_failed_text_raises_one_body_free_alert`.
- **D-3101** Question (T368; BIZ-049, BIZ-004, BIZ-021, LIC-002, LIC-003, LIC-011, LIC-012, LIC-014 to LIC-016, LIC-019, LIC-021, LIC-022, LIC-027, LIC-046, LIC-047; D-2701, D-2711, D-3100): how does T368 build the checklist from the holder and the stored switch without changing the done callers? Choice: new entry points beside the old ones. `businesses::api::holder_offer(map, catalog, parts, enabled)` (pure) and `offer_for(conn, id, known, (map, catalog))` (reads `holding` and `stored_enabled`, the `catalog::api::enabled_categories` set, so a category with no stored row is off, LIC-003) build the checklist; `stored_category_list(map, enabled, codes)` is the sign-up list by the stored switch (a stored-on category keeps the file's `launch_open` label: "Open now" when the file opens it, else "Coming later"); `reapply_license` keeps its signature and offers only categories of its `catalog` that are stored on. `checklist_offer`, `category_list`, `license_change` and `sign_up` keep their signatures and answers (they read the file), so every done test passes unchanged; T302's served sign-up calls the new ones. Per row: a licensed category's job type (kind not `none`) is pre-ticked exactly on `Card` from `eligibility_for_request` with an empty request text and no candidates, so its own gas, smoke-alarm, sprinkler and permit check applies; `HandymanCard` gives an unticked extra; any other answer leaves the row out. A no-license row is read with the city list taken as matched, then left out on `NotHandyman` or `RefusedJobType` and otherwise offered unticked: without that, a business whose city match is still pending would read `CityListPending` for the Handyman category and be offered it (an R-11 business with no city names, against TD-BIZ-46), while one that matched would not. So an ROC-only holder's offer equals `checklist_offer`'s less the Handyman trade, which the test asserts as "unchanged" (the Handyman trade was offered to every business before, against D-2711 (2)). Known gap: `sign_up` and `waitlisted` still read the file's opening, since their done tests (`identity_chain.rs`, `signup_screens.rs`) never store the catalog; the served route must call `stored_category_list` first. - **D-3082** Question (harness change, November 11, 2026; number reserved from the live counter; D-620, D-891, D-2540, D-2591, D-3043; efficiency audit F2, Casey's upload of November 11, 2026): with five lanes (`kit/runner.json` `lanes: 5`, D-3043), the lane check (`runner/lanes.py` `refusal`) keeps two tasks from owning the same file but lets two tasks in one `app/` crate run side by side, and each must update that crate's `CLAUDE.md` (`docs/code-docs.md:24`, a shared path) and append to `docs/decisions.md`; the second to merge then hits "merging main into the reviewed head conflicts in app/<crate>/CLAUDE.md; a resync merges it in on this attempt (D-891)", one more worker session. Evidence, `origin/claude/kit-state` `kit/state.json` at the time of this change: 6 resyncs recorded (`resyncs` on 6 tasks, one each), every one on a crate `CLAUDE.md`: `app/portals/CLAUDE.md` 3 (T269 attempt 2 at 15:51Z, T165 attempt 1 at 16:35Z, T272 attempt 1 at 17:45Z), `app/payments/CLAUDE.md` 2 (T332 attempt 4 at 18:20Z, T228 attempt 1 at 19:15Z), `app/quotes/CLAUDE.md` 1 (T164 attempt 3 at 11:35Z), all on November 11 after the move to five lanes; `git log -G'conflicts in app/[a-z]+/CLAUDE.md'` over the kit-state's `kit/state.json` finds 8 state commits carrying them and none earlier; no attempt failed past `RESYNC_LIMIT` on one; the only other update conflicts in any task history (T024, T028, T034, `update_conflict`) predate D-891 and name no crate `CLAUDE.md`. `kit/runner_log.jsonl` keeps only its last 200 lines and holds none of them. Choice: a soft preference, never an exclusion. `lanes.crates` reads a task's `app/<crate>/` folders from its owned paths; `lanes.crowded` names the claimable ids that share a crate with a task in flight (`state.in_flight`: a live lease on a numbered lane or MERGE_PENDING); `cycle.claim_order` takes them as a fourth sort key, after the resync mark (D-891), the `claim_first` rank (D-2540) and the critical-path chain length (D-2591) and before state order, so it only reorders ids equal on all three and never moves one above a resync, a listed id or a longer chain; FIX-MAIN is alone when `main` is red and is untouched. It drops nothing: when every candidate shares a crate the order, and so the claim, is the one before this change, and every lane still fills (`refill_lanes` is unchanged). On the live snapshot (in flight T232, T228, T387, T388) 14 of the 21 claimable ids share a crate with one of them, and chain lengths tie in groups of 2, 3, 7 and 8 just below the top, which is where the key acts; the top id itself is unchanged there, so the gain comes as the leading ranks are claimed. The new `kit/runner.json` key `prefer_disjoint_crates` turns it on (`true`, read by `runner/__main__.py` `prefer_disjoint_crates`, false when missing, malformed or anything but `true`, and false in `cycle.Config`'s default, so every existing drill keeps the old order); `cycle._claim_ordered` builds the arguments, which also takes two lines out of `_next_step`. Not taken: excluding a crowded task (it could idle a lane when a whole stage sits in two crates, against D-620's fill rule), or the audit's other options (splitting crate `CLAUDE.md` files, a serialized decision append), which are larger and outside the runner. Tests: new `tests/test_runner_crate_preference.py` (9 tests: crates from owned paths; `crowded` with a lease and with MERGE_PENDING, never counting a task against itself; a disjoint crate claimed before an earlier crowded task through a full cycle on lane 2; when all candidates share a crate the claim is as before; flag off keeps the old order and is the Config default; a resync, `claim_first` and a longer chain each still win over a disjoint task; ties on the critical path go to the disjoint crate; the setting reader fails safe; the repository sets it and `build` passes it). No existing test or assertion changed. Rollback: set `"prefer_disjoint_crates": false` in `kit/runner.json` (or remove the key) in a reviewed plan change; nothing else needs undoing. Measure after: resyncs per completed task (`resyncs` in `kit/state.json`), as the audit asks. A harness change (CLAUDE.md rule 7) on protected `runner/`, with an independent Opus review before it lands, as in D-1328 and D-3030. Changed: `runner/lanes.py`, `runner/cycle.py`, `runner/__main__.py`, `kit/runner.json`, `tests/test_runner_crate_preference.py`, `docs/architecture.md`, `kit/plan.lock`, `docs/decisions.md`, `docs/for-casey-review.md`. Numbered by: reserved with --reserve-decision (D-1058). Kind: plan change. Owner approval: not needed (BUILD_BRIEF section 16); listed for Casey. Reason: every one of the day's resyncs was a crate `CLAUDE.md` met by two lanes at once; ordering within an equal rank costs no critical-path progress and no lane, and saves a worker session each time it separates them. - **D-3129** Question (T326, round 24 audit R24-1, D-2247; CALL-011, CALL-003; D-1696, D-2091): `request_link` built the `link_this_phone` notice's `{job}` from `job_pin(line)`, the line ID modulo 10,000, which since T262 no longer connects; how does the notice name the PIN the voice route accepts, and what happens to `job_pin`? Choice: `request_link` reads the line's PIN with `pins::stored_pin` inside its own transaction, after the open-line check, and names exactly those four digits; a line with no stored PIN (opened before migration 0151) queues no notice and answers `false` (a notice naming no working PIN would be worse than none, and the business can still call from its main phone). `job_pin` and `route` are deleted from `app/calls/src/routing.rs` and `calls::api`; `route_with(party, lines, turn, pin_of)` becomes the public pure rule, each line's PIN given by the caller, so no code can derive a PIN from a line ID. Kind: build. Owner approval: not needed. Source: `app/calls/src/lifecycle.rs`, `app/calls/src/routing.rs`, `app/calls/src/api.rs`.
- **D-3130** Question (T326, D-2247; TD-CALL-02, TD-CALL-05, TD-CALL-08, TD-CALL-11, TD-CALL-13): how do the done tests that used `job_pin` or `route` move without weakening any assertion? Choice: `tests/integration/tests/pin_routing.rs`'s pure cases call `route_with` with an explicit PIN per line (`pins_of`), each line given the very digits `job_pin` gave its fixed ID (1234, 1111, 2222, 5555), so every input, expected step and assertion is otherwise the same; the one assertion that pinned the ID-modulo rule itself (`job_pin(l.line).digits() == "1234"`) goes with the rule. Its two database cases picked their wrong PIN as "not the ID-derived PIN", which since T262 could equal the stored PIN by chance (1 in 10,000); they now read the stored PINs (`stored_pin`) and pick a PIN none of them is, which is what the cases meant. `line_lifecycle.rs` asserts TD-CALL-05's notice `job` equals the line's stored PIN, and TD-CALL-08's pure gate case routes with `route_with` on the PIN its fixed line ID gave (4321). `call_pins.rs` keeps TD-CALL-13's "not the ID-derived PIN" count by computing the ID modulo 10,000 in the test. New `tests/integration/tests/link_pin.rs` (TD-CALL-18) picks a line whose stored PIN differs from its ID digits, so building `job` from the ID fails it (checked: the mutation failed the case), connects a `voice_turn` on the named digits and checks a line with no stored PIN queues nothing. TD-CALL-21's cases in `app/server/tests/voice_confirm_line.rs` pass unchanged. Not built here and unowned: `request_link`'s production caller and the LINK reply handler (register row IC-74). Kind: build. Owner approval: not needed. Source: `tests/integration/tests/pin_routing.rs`, `tests/integration/tests/line_lifecycle.rs`, `tests/integration/tests/call_pins.rs`, `tests/integration/tests/link_pin.rs`.
- **D-3064** Question (T334, attempt 2; FEE-029, FEE-051; D-2304, D-1872): once a run reads back to the checkpoint less a day, a charge T288 stored more than 7 days ago comes back in the list, so T288's `tests/integration/tests/reconcile_open.rs:343` (night 0 then night 8 expects `seen`, `retried`, `open` = 0, 2, 0) and `:423` (the unreadable row expects `open` 1 with `stripe-unreadable`) would see it as a listed charge rather than a retry; attempt 1 stopped with a plan gap the reviewer did not confirm. How does a listed charge with an old open row go? Choice: a listed, well-formed charge whose unsettled `payments.reconcile_open` row has `first_seen` before now less `LOOKBACK` is left out of the page and not counted in `seen`; the retry reads it through `fetch_charge` and settles it under the same ledger and refund keys. A charge is created before it is first seen, so such a charge is only in the catch-up range; a charge listed for the first time has no open row and takes the normal path. Because the listed set no longer fits in memory across pages, the retry no longer filters by the listed IDs: it takes every unsettled row whose `last_tried` is not this run's start (`record` sets `last_tried` to it for every listed charge it stores), which is the same set unless a run is repeated at the very same instant. `reconcile_open.rs` is unchanged and passes. Reason: meets D-2304 inside `reconcile.rs` alone, keeps memory bounded by the page, and keeps T288's retry semantics. Source: `tests/integration/tests/reconcile_open.rs:343`, `tests/integration/tests/reconcile_open.rs:423`, `app/payments/src/reconcile.rs` (`one_page`, `carried_over`, `open_rows`).
- **D-3065** Question (T334; FEE-026, FEE-028, FEE-029; D-2303, D-2971): the T334 goal says the reconcile's own refund "uses T333's check: a reported amount that differs or a currency other than `usd` records Stripe's amount and raises the same High alert", while D-2303 books a refund in another currency at the charge, never at the foreign figure, with `payments.refund_amount_unconfirmed`, and books a missing amount at the charge with that alert after one re-read. Choice: `own_refund` books by `Refund::amount_against`: `Differs` (another `usd` amount) at Stripe's amount with one High `payments.refund_amount_mismatch`; `Foreign` at the charge with one High `payments.refund_amount_unconfirmed` (D-2303 wins on the figure: a foreign amount is never written to a `usd` ledger); each through `raise_alert_once` on the pick, or `raise_alert` with no subject for a charge naming no pick (no ledger entry then); `Full` and `Missing` at the charge with no alert. `Missing` gets no alert here because the reconcile's own check follows: the charge it refunded is compared, that night and on every later list or retry, with Stripe's `refunded` amount (`ledger_agrees`, D-1872), so a refund that was not full shows as `mismatch`; and every existing reconcile fake reports no amount, so an alert there would add one to each of their refunds. The row's held charge takes the booked amount, so the night's match compares like with like. Reason: one reading of a refund across the crate, the foreign-figure rule kept, no double signal. Source: `kit/prompts/T334.md` goal (3), D-2303, D-2971, `app/payments/src/reconcile.rs` (`own_refund`, `own_booked`, `flag_refund`).
- **D-3066** Question (T334; FEE-029; D-2304, D-3055, D-479): what else does the build settle? Choice: (1) `payments.reconcile_checkpoint` is one row (`id boolean` primary key, always true) with `run_started_at`; `finish` upserts it to the run's start with `GREATEST`, so a late rerun never moves it back; it is written only after the match and its alert, so any error leaves it. (2) `list_charges_page(since, after, limit)` returns `ChargePage { charges, next }`; the provided body clamps `limit` to 1 to `PAGE_SIZE` (100), orders `list_charges` by charge ID and gives a next cursor only when charges remain, so a page of exactly the last 100 ends the read. A page whose next cursor equals the cursor just sent fails the run with `MoneyEventError::Stripe` rather than loop. Each charge keeps its own short transaction (R11, no Stripe call inside), so a page is committed before the next is read; the FEE-030 totals add page by page and compare once at the end. (3) The gap alert has no subject and is raised once per run that starts more than 2 days after the last finished one; a run that then fails raises it again on its rerun, which is information only. (4) `docs/architecture.md` section 3 is fingerprinted in `kit/plan.lock` and T334 owns no locked file, so the new table is described in section 10 (and the crate `CLAUDE.md`) only; section 3's `payments` row (which still names a `payments.reconcile_run` that no migration makes) should gain `payments.reconcile_checkpoint` in the next plan change. (5) The size budget (500 lines) is exceeded: about 330 changed lines in `reconcile.rs` and 435 in the test file, most of it doc comments and the TD-FEE-60 fakes. Reason: bounded memory and transactions with the smallest surface the done fakes can keep using. Source: `kit/prompts/T334.md`, `docs/governance.md` section 1, `app/payments/src/reconcile.rs`, `migrations/0178_payments_reconcile_checkpoint.sql`.
- **D-3067** Question (T334 review; FEE-026, FEE-028, FEE-029; D-2303, D-3065): since T333, T066's `request_refund` books a succeeded refund at Stripe's own `usd` amount, but the reconcile held a T066 `Refunded` at the full charge, so an evidence-backed partial refund ($75 charge, $25 refunded) set the held refunded amount to 7500 against a 2500 ledger entry, stored the charge as `mismatch` and raised a false `payments.ledger_mismatch`. Choice: after T066 answers `Refunded`, the reconcile reads the pick's latest `refund` entry back with its own query in `reconcile.rs` (`booked_refund`, the same lookup as T066's private `last_refund`, whose file T334 does not own) and holds that amount, falling back to the charge only when none is found; `RefundOutcome`, `refunds.rs` and T066's own tests are unchanged; the one new query has its `.sqlx/` file. TD-FEE-60 gains `td_fee_60_a_partial_t066_refund_found_by_the_reconcile_settles` (pick with charge evidence, Stripe reports $25 `usd`): nothing open, $25 booked, one refund-amount alert, no ledger-mismatch alert. Reason: the reconcile compares what T066 booked, not what it asked for, so like is compared with like as in D-3065. Source: `app/payments/src/reconcile.rs` (`refund`, `booked_refund`), `app/payments/src/refunds.rs` (`last_refund`, `booked`, read only), `tests/integration/tests/reconcile_catch_up.rs`.

- **D-3142** Question (harness change, November 12, 2026; number reserved by the coordinator; Casey's approval at about 00:55Z to make `Ci` faster without harming quality): where does `Ci`'s time go now, and what shortens it with no check lost? Measured with the GitHub Actions API on the twelve most recent successful `ci` runs on `claude/task/*` heads (runs 43140041719 to 43146409600, 02:07Z to 03:10Z): `Ci`'s wall time is 712 to 1105 s (median 1022), always set by `Checks` (703 to 1099 s, median 1017; the spread is the runner's speed, every step scales together); `Coverage` 412 to 619 s (median 580), `E2e` 155 to 255 s, `Python` 117 to 161 s. Every Rust build cache missed: 0 of 36 `rust-cache` restores (Checks, Coverage, E2e) and 0 of 12 sqlx-cli restores found an entry, although the nightly of November 11 (run 43065110252, 17:25Z) saved exactly the keys these runs asked for (`v0-rust-checks-Linux-x64-7543b454-85776c68`, `sqlx-cli-0.9.0-Linux-e5913cae…`); they were gone nine hours later, evicted from the 10 GB repository cache (the cache listing itself is not readable from this session; the backup runner's per-commit target entries of D-1178 are the likely cause and are left for a measured change of their own). So every run is cold, and inside `Checks` (run 43146409600, 1099 s) the time is: setup and scans 60 s, sqlx-cli build 77 s, fmt and clippy 116 s, migrations and `cargo sqlx prepare --check` 32 s, `cargo build -p askhava-server` 100 s, test compile 157 s, and the test run 545 s, of which `release_proof_compile_fail` (the first trybuild driver, which builds the cold trybuild project) 162 s and `prop_prompt_injection` (TD-AI-03) 65 s, all in sequence. Choice: a sixth job, "Lint and slow tests" (`lint`), runs in parallel with `Checks`: the unchanged fmt and clippy commands, `sqlx migrate run` and the unchanged `cargo sqlx prepare --workspace --check -- --all-targets --all-features` (sqlx-cli restored from the cache `Checks` saves on `main`, built on a miss), and the Rust tests named by a new workflow-level `SPLIT_TESTS` list of libtest filters (`_cannot_be_forged_outside_`, the three trybuild drivers, and `td_ai_03_`, the TD-AI-03 tests), run as `cargo test --workspace --locked -- <filters>`. `Checks` runs the same `cargo test --workspace --locked -- --skip <filter>…`; libtest's filter and `--skip` are the same substring match, so the two runs partition every test (doc-tests included; checked on a scratch crate with this toolchain), and using the same `--workspace` command keeps Cargo's feature unification identical (a `-p askhava-security` split was rejected: `cargo tree` shows it would build `tokio` without `test-util` and `regex-syntax` without its unicode features). `Checks` keeps everything else in its order (the scans, the plan checks, the build, its tests, the named mutants, which still find every test binary built in its `target/`, audit, deny, npm) and `sqlx migrate run` before its tests, so its database is as before. The `target/tests/trybuild` cache directory and its exact-hit guard (D-488, D-693) move with the trybuild tests to the new job's own `rust-cache` entry (`shared-key: lint`, saved on `main` only as D-2782). The job decides "Rust changed" with a copy of `Checks`' path rule. `Ci` now `needs: [checks, lint, python, coverage, e2e]` and is green only when all five are `success`; the required names `Ci`, `Twin`, `Ally` and `Governance` are unchanged. New `tests/test_ci_workflow.py` asserts that `Ci` needs every other job and compares each result, that the two test commands are the same command with the filters and the skips read from one `SPLIT_TESTS`, that each filter names an existing test, that the two jobs' path rules are equal, that fmt, clippy and the query check run once and the build, mutants and deny stay in `Checks`, and that the trybuild cache and guard sit in the job that runs the trybuild tests. Expected (from the same twelve runs, cold caches as now): `Checks` median 1017 → about 660 s, the new job about 700 s, `Coverage` unchanged at about 580 s, so `Ci`'s wall time median 1022 → about 710 s (about 5 minutes, 30%, per task head; 1105 → about 760 s on the slowest runners); actual to be measured on the first task runs after the merge. Cost: about 6 more runner-minutes per `Ci` run (the new job compiles the workspace again and builds sqlx-cli again while the caches stay cold); the repository is public, so Linux minutes are not billed (D-1451), but each run holds one more concurrent job. Nothing is removed, skipped or weakened: every step, test and lint that ran on a task head still runs there and gates `Ci`. Kind: harness change (protected `.github/`), plan lock rewritten. Owner approval: Casey's request (November 12, about 00:55Z); independent Opus review arranged by the coordinator. Source: the GitHub Actions jobs API and job logs of the runs named above and of nightly run 43065110252; `.github/workflows/ci.yml`; `tests/test_ci_workflow.py`; `docs/architecture.md` section 11; D-488; D-489; D-693; D-1178; D-2782.
- **D-3143** Question (harness change, November 12, 2026; number reserved from the live counter; D-514, D-693, D-1178, D-1890, D-1911, D-2007, D-2782; Casey's go of November 12, 2026 to speed the build up without lowering its quality): why do `Ci`'s caches miss, and how do they survive? Evidence: in 12 `ci` runs on November 12, 0 of 36 Rust cache restores and 0 of 12 sqlx-cli restores hit (the overseer's count; re-checked on run 43151219026: "No cache found" in Checks, Coverage and E2e, "Cache not found" for `sqlx-cli-0.9.0-Linux-…` and `playwright-Linux-…`); the entries the nightly saved on `main` at 17:10Z to 17:25Z on November 11 (Actions run 43065110252: Checks 1.13 GB, named-mutants 0.62 GB, Twin 0.45 GB, Coverage 0.36 GB, sqlx-cli, Playwright, npm) were gone within 9 hours. Branch runs save nothing shared since D-2782, so the space went to `backup-runner.yml`: its job log for run 43115397861 (November 11, 22:53Z) restores `rust-Linux-<lock>-<sha>` at 3,602,468,211 bytes (`~/.cargo` registry and bin plus the whole `target/debug`), saves `rust-smoke-Linux-<lock>-<sha>-<run>-<attempt>` at 3,893,277,114 bytes, and tries to save `rust-Linux-<lock>-<new sha>` at its end. Every commit of `main` thus gets a new worker entry (the key holds `github.sha`, D-1178) and every job whose smoke compiled a new smoke entry (D-1911): about 7.3 GB per merge against a 10 GB repository limit, so each merge forced GitHub to evict, and `Ci`'s `main` entries, written once a night, could not coexist even with the newest pair. Runs started by a `pull_request` event (9 of the backup runs since 17:00Z on November 11) also saved under `refs/pull/<n>/merge`, which no later run can restore. And a branch run whose Playwright restore missed saved its own branch-scoped entry. Choice, changing no test, no check and nothing a restore reads differently: (1) the worker entry (`Rust build cache (D-514)`, key, paths and restore keys unchanged, per commit as D-1178 wants) becomes `actions/cache/restore`. A fresh checkout gives every workspace file a new mtime, so Cargo rebuilds every member of the worker's build whatever the entry holds; only the dependency artifacts ever carried over, and the smoke build of `main`'s head holds the same ones. So "Give the worker the smoke build's dependencies (D-3143)", after the pre-session smoke and before the session, runs `python3 -m runner.cache seed` (new `runner/cache.py`): when `target/debug` holds no build yet and the disk has `SEED_MARGIN` to spare, it copies the smoke build's dependency artifacts (`github_env.seed_files`, the set the smoke seed of D-1890 copies the other way, by real copies) into it; anything Cargo finds stale it rebuilds. At the job's end, from `main`'s ref and only when the restore missed its exact key, "Empty the worker build before the save (D-3143)" (`python3 -m runner.cache clear`, run from the job's worktree of `main` as the keeper steps are) empties `target/debug`, so the entry holds the registry, git sources and `~/.cargo/bin` alone; it prints `pruned=no` when it cannot, and nothing is saved. (2) "Smoke build cache, save (D-1911)" also requires `main`'s ref. (3) Before either backup save, a "Drop the superseded … entries (D-3143)" step (`python3 -m runner.cache drop`, the job token, which has `actions: write`) deletes the family's entries (key prefix `rust-<os>-`, which never matches `rust-smoke-<os>-`, or `rust-smoke-<os>-`) created before the job started, and answers `save=no`, skipping the save, when another job has saved an entry of the family since this one started, so two lanes never keep two smoke entries; an unreadable list answers `save=yes`, the behaviour before. The restore keys only ever took the newest entry, so the dropped ones were never read again. Only `key=value` lines reach `$GITHUB_OUTPUT`; messages go to standard error (a test checks every standard-output line). (4) `ci.yml` E2e and `a11y.yml` split the Playwright browser cache into `actions/cache/restore` and an `actions/cache/save` on `main` only, after the install, both pinned to the same commit as before, as D-2782 did for sqlx-cli. Budget, from the nightly's save logs (run 43065110252): Checks 1.13 GB, named-mutants 0.62 GB, E2e 0.51 GB, Twin 0.45 GB, Coverage 0.36 GB, Playwright 0.29 GB, npm 0.01 GB, sqlx-cli 0.01 GB, 3.38 GB in all, plus the `lint` Rust entry of sibling change D-3142 (#550, about 1.2 GB): about 4.6 GB for `Ci`'s `main` entries; the backup job's one smoke entry (3.9 GB) and one worker entry holding the registry alone (not yet measured; the registry is part of Checks' 1.13 GB entry, so estimated at 0.3 GB): about 8.8 GB, under the 10 GB limit with a margin; a second concurrent smoke save is refused by `save=no` except when two jobs list the family within the same few seconds. Keeping the worker's dependency artifacts in its entry (about 1.1 GB more) would have left about 9.9 GB, which is why they now come from the smoke build. Expected: the nightly's entries live until the next nightly, and branch runs hit again (a warm Checks saves about 400 s per run, D-2782). Costs: the first job after this change still restores an old full worker entry while one is left (its restore keys match it), and the next commit's job drops it; a job that drops older entries and then fails to save leaves the next job to rebuild once; between the drop and the save, about a minute, a starting job finds no smoke entry and seeds from the worker build as D-1890 does; a job whose head is newer than another lane's concurrent save keeps that save's smoke build rather than its own, so the next warm-up compiles a little more; a worker build the seed skipped (disk short) builds its own dependencies, as before D-514. Not done: `actions/setup-node`'s `cache: npm` (about 13 MB) still saves a branch entry on a miss, which a surviving `main` entry makes rare. Changed: `runner/cache.py` (new), `.github/workflows/backup-runner.yml`, `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, `.github/workflows/a11y.yml`, `tests/test_runner_cache.py` (new), `docs/architecture.md` section 12, `docs/decisions.md`, `docs/for-casey-review.md`; `kit/plan.lock` is unchanged (`scripts/check_plan_lock.py` reports every item matching, since none of these files is in the locked blueprint). No state field is added. Kind: harness change; independent Opus review before merge (its first round found the `$GITHUB_OUTPUT` line, the Changed list and the budget, all fixed here). Owner approval: Casey's go to speed the build up (November 12); listed for Casey. Source: Actions runs 43115397861, 43065110252 and 43151219026 job logs, `.github/workflows/backup-runner.yml` "Rust build cache (D-514)" and "Smoke build cache, save (D-1911)", D-2782.
- **D-3145** Question (T356, D-2628; TXT-011, TXT-014; D-558): how are a definite refusal and an unknown outcome told apart, and where does each row state change? Choice: `service::send` claims only a `queued` row (`status = 'sending'`, `sending_since`, `attempts + 1` in one `UPDATE ... WHERE status = 'queued'`), so a second worker's claim of the same row matches nothing and makes no carrier call. A refusal is `AdapterError::NotSent`, `InvalidId`, `BadConfig` or a vendor 4xx (21610 included): `send` puts the row back to `queued` before it returns `OutboxError::Carrier`, so `text_retries.rs`'s four calls on one row each see `Carrier`, and `optout::send_checked`'s 21610 block now takes a `queued` or `sending` row. Everything else (`OutcomeUnknown`, `Decode`, a vendor 5xx) may hide an accepted send and is the new `OutboxError::OutcomeUnknown`, the row left `sending`; a failed vault read after the claim also puts the row back to `queued`. The sender moves an unknown row, and any row still `sending` 5 minutes after `sending_since` (a row with none, from before 0182, counts as stale), to `unknown` with `models::mark_unknown`, whose one statement drops the body and returns it for the email copy. `sending_since` is the caller's `now` when the send came through `send_checked` (so the sweep counts on the worker's clock) and the database's `now()` for a bare `send`. `delivery_status` still reads `unknown` and `expired` as `Sending`; nothing reads them yet. Kind: build. Owner approval: not needed. Source: `app/messaging/src/service.rs`, `app/messaging/src/models.rs`, `app/messaging/src/optout.rs`, `migrations/0182_messaging_outbox_not_before.sql`.
- **D-3146** Question (T356, D-2628, D-3055, D-3106; QH-001, QH-004, QH-006): the plan says `not_before` is set at enqueue from the row's kind and `rules::decide`, but `enqueue` has neither the phone (`rules::decide` needs its area code) nor a clock, and `NewText` may not change; how is the window kept? Choice: at enqueue only the QH-004 exemption is stored (`quiet_exempt_until`: `infinity` for `service::ANY_HOUR_TEMPLATES`, i.e. `emergency_911`, `help_reply`, `opt_out_confirmation`, `start_reply` and the INT-033 night counts `night_count_many`, `night_count_one`, `night_count_none`; `enqueue_exempt`'s `Exemption::EmergencyJob` is `infinity` and `Exemption::DirectReply { inbound_at }` is `inbound_at` plus 15 minutes); `not_before` stays NULL and the sender, which reads her number from the vault at the send instant, runs `rules::retry` there and writes `not_before` = the hold's `until` (QH-006). The effect is the plan's: a row queued at night waits for 8 a.m. and is never sent early. Pick codes go by Twilio Verify, not the outbox, so no template stands for them. Kind: build. Owner approval: not needed. Source: `app/messaging/src/service.rs`, `app/messaging/src/outbox_sender.rs`.
- **D-3147** Question (T356, D-2628, D-2188, D-2042; TXT-009, TXT-021, CON-013, CON-030, QH-003): what does the sender do with the cases the plan leaves open? Choice: (1) it sends only homeowner rows: a business row's `recipient_id` is a phone record or a business ID whose number `messaging` cannot read (D-2042), so those rows wait for the task that resolves business phones; (2) TXT-009 was checked at enqueue and the sender cannot read the request's state, so it sends as `Relation::OpenRequest`; (3) "queued while the line was paused" is the homeowner line's latest `messaging.mode_state` row at the row's `created_at` (`changed_at`, then `seq`): switched off, suspended or restored-not-on; every such row but the HELP reply (it answers her own text) is `expired` with one `messaging.text_expired` system audit row, whenever the sender first sees it; (4) a row `send_checked` refuses as `Suppressed` is `expired` too (CON-013: nothing but HELP and the current confirmation reaches a listed number; it is not held for a START), and so is a row whose number has no area-code zone (QH-003: never texted); (5) "one Low alert" is `Severity::Normal`, the weekly-digest level, since `ops` has no Low; (6) the configured homeowner number is the new optional setting `ASKHAVA_HOMEOWNER_NUMBER` (unset: the line has no sender and rows wait, TXT-022), and the footer postal line is optional for the sender (unset: no email copy is queued, and a refused row past its last retry waits 30 minutes more instead of `give_up`, which needs the postal line). The sender is registered whenever the Twilio settings and both vault keys are present. Kind: build. Owner approval: not needed. Source: `app/messaging/src/outbox_sender.rs`, `app/server/src/lib.rs`, `app/core/src/settings.rs`.
- **D-3148** Question (T356, harness, D-2628, D-558; TD-TXT-04, TD-QH-05): how do the done TD-TXT-04 test and the new TD-QH-05 tests prove the fence without a carrier that dedupes? Choice: `tests/integration/tests/outbox.rs`'s killed-worker case is rewritten: the row is a homeowner's `first_quote` with an email on file; the first `send` dies after the fake carrier accepted; a second `send` returns `None` with no call; the sender run 1 minute on leaves it `sending` and 6 minutes on makes it `unknown`, with exactly one carrier call, one `text_failed` email and one `messaging.send_outcome_unknown` alert. Every other assertion in the file is kept. `tests/integration/tests/outbox_sender.rs` drives `messaging.send_due` through `core`'s registry as `askhava_app` on a manual clock, with a fake carrier that counts every call as a delivery and, for the night and refusal cases, the real Twilio client against `stand_ins.server`; a test sets a row's `created_at` to say when it was queued, since `enqueue` takes no clock. Kind: build. Owner approval: not needed. Source: `tests/integration/tests/outbox.rs`, `tests/integration/tests/outbox_sender.rs`.
- **D-3149** Question (T356 fix round, reviewer findings; D-2628, D-3147, D-1688, D-3095, D-493, D-2042; TXT-011, TXT-014, TXT-022, CON-009, CON-030, QH-004): what changes after the review of the outbox sender? Choice. (1) No row may stay at the head of the queue: `models::due` takes the oldest 50 due rows, so a row the sender skipped without changing would, 50 times over, stop all texting. Her phone is now read once per row in `outbox_sender::homeowner_phone`; a read that can never succeed (no such contact, no phone, a bad number, a sealed value that will not open) expires the row with one `messaging.text_expired` audit row, a failure that may pass (the database, the audit write) holds it 30 minutes (`not_before`); after a send, `Recipient`, `RecipientKind`, `BadPhone` and `PastCustomer` expire the row too. (2) `run_send_due` queues the next run first (as `app/server/src/no_handler_alert.rs` does), and a row or stale-sweep step that fails is logged by outbox ID only (`tracing`, already a workspace library, now also a `messaging` dependency) and the row held 30 minutes, never aborting the batch; only the connection, the next run's insert and the batch queries fail the run. (3) `ASKHAVA_HOMEOWNER_NUMBER` is required in test and live, as the Twilio settings (D-1688) and the postal line (D-3095) are: unset there the worker refuses to start with "missing required setting ASKHAVA_HOMEOWNER_NUMBER" (`server::homeowner_number`); unset in dev and CI the line has no sender and rows wait (TXT-022). Without it every homeowner text would wait, and every CON-009 opt-out confirmation would expire unsent after its 5 minutes (CON-030), so the person opting out would get no confirmation text; that is why a silent default is refused. This replaces D-3147 (6)'s optional number. The key stays added to `app/core/src/settings.rs`'s shared list by this task only (D-493: each task adds its own keys). (4) The vault reads per send drop from three to two: `optout::send_checked` hands the number it read for the list check to the claim (`service::send_at`, crate-private, gains an optional number), so the claim no longer reads it again; the sender's own read (needed for the expiry and window checks) stays, since passing it through `mode::send_on_line` would change `app/messaging/src/mode.rs`, which T356 does not own. Public signatures are unchanged. (5) The `text_failed` email copy of an `unknown` row uses the row's stored `language` (`models::mark_unknown` returns it). (6) Gap, not closed here: business texts have no sender. `business_notices::business_notice` queues `Relation::Business` outbox rows (job cards, pick notices) and counts them as texted, so no email fallback goes, but the sender sends only homeowner rows (D-2042: `messaging` cannot read a business phone; the row's `recipient_id` is the phone record). Until a task builds the business-row sender (the composition resolving the business phone, then `send_on_line` with `To::Business` and the business line), business texts wait in the outbox and businesses learn of cards only by email where no text was chosen. The plan needs a task for it; this entry and `docs/for-casey-review.md` name the gap, and no locked plan file is changed here. - **D-3113** Question (T248; INT-048, INT-022, LIC-011; D-1515, D-1518, D-1521): what shape do markets take as reviewed data, and how do other modules read them? Choice: `docs/catalog/markets.yaml` lists markets (`id`, `name`, `state`, `time_zone`, `identity_sources`, optional `decision`, `towns`), each town with its service-area `code`, `name`, `zips` and `extra_zips`. One market, `lake-havasu-city` (AZ, `America/Phoenix`, identity source `city`, the licensing import source of LIC-011's city list), with one town `lake_havasu_city`, the code intake and businesses already use; its `zips` 86403, 86404 and 86406 are the ZCTAs the Census 2020 ZCTA-to-place relationship file links to place 0439370 (86404 is also linked to the Crystal Beach and Desert Hills CDPs, which are not service-area towns, so it is assigned to Lake Havasu City); its reviewed extra ZIP 86405 is the city's PO-box ZIP, which has no ZCTA. `app/catalog/src/markets.rs` compiles the file in and `parse_markets` refuses, each with its own `MarketRefused` variant, a duplicate ID, a town in two markets, a ZIP under two towns, a time zone `jiff` (already allowed, bundled tzdb) does not know, a market with no towns and a state other than AZ without a decision ID (`D-` then ASCII digits only, so `D-` and `D-x` are refused); codes, states and ZIPs are shape-checked. Reads are pure over the compiled-in data (`catalog::api::markets`, `service_area_towns`, `town_for_zip`, `zip_location`, `miles_between`), returning `Result<Option<_>>` so a broken compiled-in file is an error, never a silent "none". `load_embedded` (the catalog sync) now also upserts `catalog.market`, `market_town` and `zcta_centroid` (migration 0162) and never writes `launched_at`: the app role's INSERT and UPDATE on `catalog.market` are both column-level and leave `launched_at` out, so a launch needs the owner's later action; the sync only adds and updates (no DELETE), so rows removed from the files stay in the tables and readers use the compiled-in API, never the tables. The Phoenix metro market is a fixture in `app/catalog/src/tests/markets.rs` only. INT-022's Arizona check reads the towns from this file (`service_area_towns`) and `tests/integration/tests/service_area.rs` runs every one through `intake::api::check_towns`; intake's routing still receives its towns list from its caller, which reads `service_area_towns` when the request route is wired. Kind: build. Source: T248 goal; `docs/spec/intake.md:52`, `docs/spec/intake.md:26`.

One such ZCTA, 86515, has its internal point east of the Arizona line in New Mexico; it is left out (named in the file's header), so it has no location and TD-INT-37's "every row inside Arizona" holds; 416 rows remain, covering every ZCTA of the market's town and of the Phoenix, Scottsdale and Tempe fixture. A ZIP not in the file has no location. Kind: build. Source: T248 goal; `docs/spec/intake.md:52`.
- **D-3116** Question (T248; BIZ-058, BIZ-049, A11Y-010 to A11Y-013, D-1518): where does sign-up ask the base ZIP and radius "beside towns served", when the towns question lives in `app/portals/templates/capability_setup.html` (T155's, not this task's file)? Choice: on its own sign-up screen, `Screen::ServiceArea` in `templates/business_signup.html` (posting to `SERVICE_AREA_ROUTE`, not served yet, D-1709), meant to follow the towns question; one question group per page matches the sign-up's one-thing-per-page shape. `CapabilityValues` reads `base_zip` and `radius` and carries them as hidden fields on every capability screen (the one-page form too), so the check screen (BIZ-030) reads them back after the capability answers when they parse. `businesses::api::ServiceArea::parse` is the one check: the trimmed base ZIP must be exactly 5 ASCII digits (any well-formed ZIP, a ZIP+4 refused) and the radius ASCII digits only, 1 to 100 (blank, 0, `2.5`, `+5`, `-5`, 101 refused); the screen keeps both typed values, opens the title with "Error: ", focuses a summary linking to each field and repeats each message by its field. `save_service_area` upserts `businesses.service_area` (migration 0163; explicit SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE grant; no DELETE) with two audit rows naming `base_zip` and `service_radius`; no location is stored, `service_area` reads the base's centroid from the catalog at read time, so an out-of-state base has none. `portals::api::signup_can_finish` is true only with towns served and a service area. The radius question is draft copy (WORD-028): English "How many miles will you travel for a job?", Spanish draft "¿Hasta cuántas millas viaja para un trabajo?" in `docs/for-casey-review.md` until the page has a Spanish version. The service-area screen posts `base_zip` and `radius` only as its own inputs, never again among the carried hidden fields. Matching by radius and the portal edit stay T249's. Kind: build. - **D-3119** Question (T400; LIC-001, LIC-002, LIC-003, SEC-002; D-3094, D-3100, IC-96): where does the start-up catalog load live and what does a failure do? - **D-3150** Question (T405; FEE-050, FEE-027; D-2204, D-3118): how is a payment's 3-D Secure result read and kept without changing `PaymentIntent` or `PaymentsAdapter`, which ten done test files build or implement? Choice: a separate read. `adapters::api::ThreeDs` (`Authenticated`, `NotAuthenticated`) and the inherent `StripePayments::fetch_three_ds(pi_…)`, on no trait, send `GET /v1/payment_intents/{id}?expand[]=latest_charge` through the existing vendor client (reqwest's `query` feature is off, so the pair is appended to the built request's URL with `build_split` and `RequestBuilder::from_parts`; no new feature or crate) and read only `latest_charge.payment_method_details.card.three_d_secure.result`: `authenticated` is `Authenticated`; any other result, a null or missing `three_d_secure`, an unexpanded or missing `latest_charge` and a card-less method are `NotAuthenticated`, never unknown-as-yes. `ThreeDs::from_result` is public so a fake source maps Stripe's result strings exactly as the adapter does. `payments::api::record_three_ds(conn, source, pick)` reads the pick's `stripe_intent_id` (and whether a row exists) from `payments.charge_evidence` in one statement, asks its `ThreeDsStripe` only when no row exists, and inserts `payments.charge_three_ds` once (`ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING`); no evidence is `MoneyEventError::NothingCharged` and a failed read `MoneyEventError::Stripe` (the existing error type, so `models.rs` is untouched), both storing nothing; it must run outside a transaction (rust brain R11). `three_ds_authenticated` is `true` only for a stored `true`. Only the pick ID and the boolean are stored; nothing logs. Kind: build. Owner approval: not needed. Source: `app/adapters/src/payments.rs`, `app/payments/src/three_ds.rs`, `migrations/0172_payments_three_ds.sql`, `tests/integration/tests/three_ds_record.rs`.
- **D-3151** Question (T405; FEE-050; D-3118, D-2623): how does the stand-in report the charge behind a succeeded PaymentIntent? Choice: as Stripe does. `FakeStripe._succeed` stores a charge object under `ch_` plus the intent's own suffix (so no other fake ID moves) with `payment_method_details.card.three_d_secure` set to `{"result": "authenticated"}` after a passed `authenticate` and null for a card never asked, and sets the intent's `latest_charge` to that ID string; `stripe_fetch` swaps the ID for the charge object only when the query has `expand[]=latest_charge`, so a plain fetch, the confirm answer and the webhook event carry the `ch_` string T352's `latest_charge: Option<String>` will read. Every existing stand-in contract test passes unchanged; `tests/contract/test_stripe_three_ds.py` checks the plain, the other-expand and the expanded fetches with and without `three_d_secure`, the confirm answer and an unpaid intent. Kind: build (harness). Owner approval: not needed. Source: `stand_ins/stripe.py`, `stand_ins/server.py`, `tests/contract/test_stripe_three_ds.py`.
- **D-3140** Question (harness change, November 12, 2026; number reserved from the live counter; Casey's go to speed up the build without harming quality, November 12 about 00:55Z; D-620, D-723, D-1451, D-2886): why did free lanes sit idle with claimable tasks on November 11 between about 22:35Z and 23:19Z, and what is the smallest safe fix? Evidence (`origin/claude/kit-state:kit/runner_log.jsonl`, the state and lease history replayed through `cycle.refill_lanes`, and the Actions step times): (1) at 22:34:58 lane 4's `--after` wrote `BLOCKED` (T317) with `refill` ["4"]; the job's usage reading then wrote the row the chain step reads last (22:35:25), which moved no task, so the chain step started nothing; the rows after it, `keeper_armed: 147 minutes` (22:35:44), `branch_updated` on lane 5 (22:37:54), `merge_pending` on lane 3 (22:38:01), two usage readings and `keeper_armed: 144 minutes` twice (22:38:29, 22:38:38), all named lane 4 in `refill` and none started a run, since only a hand-off started its refill runs itself (D-723) and the keeper sleeps to the soonest live lease's end; lane 4 sat free with 20 claimable tasks until 22:49:18, when a run started by an unrelated merge (PR #516, created 22:35:43) claimed T348. (2) From 22:39 to 23:19 `refill` [] was right by the lane rule: the replay at 22:50, 23:04 and 23:06 finds five tasks in flight (leases on lanes 2 and 4, and lane 1 until 23:04; MERGE_PENDING T232 on lane 3, T388 on lane 5 and, from 23:04:30, T228 on lane 1) beside 19 to 21 claimable ones; lanes 1, 3 and 5 held no lease but a MERGE_PENDING task holds its lane until its pull request resolves (D-620). T388 merged at 22:53:32 yet stayed MERGE_PENDING until 23:19:09, because the merged pull request's run (created 22:52:51) resolves it only in its session's first cycle, after the smoke warm-up (22:55:45 to 22:59:32), the pre-session smoke (22:59:33 to 23:11:23) and the session's start; that cycle freed lanes 1 and 5 (`refill` ["1", "5"]), handed off at 23:21:37 and started lane 1, claimed at 23:24:02. The two `requeued_after_plan_fix` rows at 23:03 (manual sessions) had `refill` [] for the same reason, and a manual session has no job token to start a run. Choice: every run that ends starts one run per refill lane, whatever its result, not only a hand-off (`runner/__main__.py` `lane_report`, `refill_starts`, reusing `refill` and `start_refill`); a `REFILL_STOP` result (`idle`, `paced`, `no_free_lane`, `lease_live`, `lost_race`, `state_invalid`, `smoke_pending`, `smoke_timeout`, `smoke_env`, `main_red`, `fix_main`, `fix_main_blocked`, `requeue_refused`), one that claimed nothing or changed nothing, starts none, so a run that claims nothing never starts another and refill cannot loop; a bookkeeping row (a usage reading, the keeper's record, a renewal, an `--after` status answer) follows its job's last row that tells (`job_row` over the new `GitHubEnv.read_cycle_log`, `keeper.last_result`'s test): none after a `REFILL_STOP` result or with no such row, else only the lanes that row did not start; the row records the lanes in `dispatched`, and the chain step no longer starts a lane its row already started. `cycle.refill_lanes` now names no lane while `main` is red (only FIX-MAIN may be claimed then, and the gate's lane pick places it, the "fix" lane included), besides the pacer's wait (D-723); the lanes stay `lanes.free_lanes` (the effective count, one while `lanes_fallback` is set), and the lease and each lane's concurrency group still keep a second start from claiming twice (a second run on a held lane claims nothing and, with no lane left, starts nothing). No new state value. Not changed: a MERGE_PENDING task still holds its lane (D-620), which caused most of the window's idle lane time; making a merged pull request's run resolve its task before the pre-session smoke would cut about 25 minutes per merge and is a separate harness change for a later review. The keeper stays the backstop. Tests: new `tests/test_runner_refill_after_cycle.py` (9 tests: the November 11 state through `entry.main` with a lane-3 `merge_pending`, `branch_updated`, requeue, plan-fix requeue, hand-in or MERGE_PENDING row starting lane 4, which failed before this change; bookkeeping rows refilling only what their job's row did not; every `REFILL_STOP` result and its job's later rows starting nothing, nor a bookkeeping row with no job row, nor a dry run; the rules of `refill_starts`; no refill while `main` is red or a fix lane is needed; none while the pacer waits, none past the effective lanes under `lanes_fallback`, none with five in flight; two runs for one lane claim once; the chain step's `dispatched` filter; the log reader). One existing assertion changed with this spec change: `tests/test_runner_two_lanes.py` `test_a_cycle_that_hands_off_starts_its_refill_runs_at_once` expected `merge_pending` and MERGE_PENDING rows to start nothing, the behaviour this entry removes; it now asserts they start lane 2, and still that `idle` starts nothing. Rollback: revert this change's commit (the runner, the chain-step line, the tests and docs together); nothing in `kit/state.json` needs undoing. Changed: `runner/__main__.py`, `runner/cycle.py`, `runner/github_env.py`, `.github/workflows/backup-runner.yml`, `tests/test_runner_refill_after_cycle.py`, `tests/test_runner_two_lanes.py`, `docs/architecture.md`, `kit/plan.lock`, `docs/decisions.md`, `docs/for-casey-review.md`. - **D-3141** Question (harness change, November 12, 2026; number reserved from the live counter; D-620, D-723, D-2007, D-2028, D-2560, D-3043; Casey's go of November 12, 2026 to speed the build up without lowering its quality): this number was first reserved for moving merges to a GitHub merge queue. That is not feasible: a merge queue builds its merge groups with GitHub's own merge, which ignores the repository's `.gitattributes` (`docs/decisions.md merge=union`), so two lanes that each append an entry at the end of `docs/decisions.md` would conflict in the queue every time, which the runner's own update merge (`runner/update_merge.py`, a local git that honours the attribute, D-620) does not. The number is reused for the merge hold it was meant to shorten. Evidence: T388's pull request merged at 22:53:33Z on November 11 (`claude/kit-state` `kit/state.json` `merged_at`), and the backup run that merge started (Actions run 43115397861, lane 5) began its job at 22:53:48Z, but `runner/cycle.py` `run_cycle` resolves a MERGE_PENDING task only inside the session's `python3 -m runner`, which `backup-runner.yml` starts after the Rust cache restore (22:54:27Z to 22:55:26Z), the prerequisites, the smoke warm-up (`--warm-smoke`, 22:55:45Z to 22:59:32Z) and the pre-session smoke (`--pre-smoke`, 22:59:33Z to 23:11:23Z); the session then reached its cycle, whose row at 23:19:09Z (`kit/runner_log.jsonl`, result `smoke_pending`) shows `T388: MERGE_PENDING -> DONE`. For those 25 minutes T388 held lane 5 (nothing is claimed on a lane while its task is MERGE_PENDING, `BUILD_BRIEF.md:224`), kept its dependents ineligible, and counted as in flight for every other lane's ownership and stage check. Choice: a new mode `python3 -m runner --resolve-merges` (`cycle.resolve_merged`), run by a new `backup-runner.yml` step "Close merged tasks before the smoke (D-3141)" right after `actions/setup-python`, before the Rust cache, the warm-up, the pre-session smoke and the session, with the same tokens as the after-session steps (`RUNNER_PUSH_TOKEN` for the state push, the job token for check runs and dispatches) and `continue-on-error`. It reads the state once and, for every MERGE_PENDING task whose latest pull request has merged, is not an earlier attempt's (`_earlier_pr`) and has no required check still running (`verify.checks_state` not `pending`), applies `_resolve_pr`, the cycle's own merge step split out of `_resolve_one` unchanged: DONE only from `verify.check_done` (Ci, Twin and Ally green on the merged head and the squash tree equal to it) on a reviewed head, with `mark_owned_gap` and the lane's strike rule (`_lane_outcome`); otherwise BLOCKED and `main_red` with FIX-MAIN queued, exactly as the cycle would. A merged head git cannot place yet (`merge_pending` from `_unplaced_merge`), an open pull request (update merges, closes, the conflict and resync path), a task with no pull request, the inbox, the smoke and every claim stay the cycle's. It pushes once against the state it read; a lost race changes nothing and the session's cycle resolves the merge as before. With nothing to close it pushes nothing and writes no log row (`NO_MERGED` in `runner/__main__.py` `SILENT`); otherwise its row's result is `merges_resolved`. With two or more lanes it starts a run at once for each other lane that a task could now be claimed on (`refill_lanes` with the new `own` argument leaves out the run's own lane, which its session claims on, and the one task that session would take; `lane_report`, `start_refill`), and keeps in the row's `refill` only lanes it could not start; the chain step at the job's end now also counts a `merges_resolved` row of the job as a moved task, so the run's own lane is still refilled when its session claimed nothing on it (a smoke still running, a red smoke). Merged with D-3140 (every run that ends starts its refill runs, `refill_starts`, `job_row`, the `main_red` guard in `refill_lanes`, all kept): the early row is a result that tells and is not in `REFILL_STOP`, so it starts its refill lanes; `lane_report` now also leaves out every lane this job's earlier rows already started a run for (`job_sent` over `job_rows`), so the session's later hand-off never starts a second run for a lane the early step started at minute 1 (that run is still in its warm-up), and the chain step subtracts `dispatched` from every row of this job, not only the last. A MERGE_PENDING cleanup task whose stage proof is not recorded yet is left to the cycle, which records proofs first (`record_proofs`), so the early step never closes one BLOCKED for a proof the cycle would have recorded. Unchanged: the DONE rule (the new tests compare the state `resolve_merged` writes with what `_resolve_merges` makes of the same inputs, byte for byte, for the green, tree-mismatch, failed-check and unreviewed-head cases), the red-main path, the smoke before every claim, one lane per task, the lease. Expected saving: a merge's lane and dependents free about 20 to 25 minutes sooner per merge (T388: 22:54Z instead of 23:19Z), at the cost of one state read, one pull-request read per MERGE_PENDING task and at most one state push per job. Considered and left as a follow-up: giving only the oldest MERGE_PENDING pull request an update merge at a time (first in line), so several branches behind `main` do not each run Ci for an update the oldest one's merge makes stale again. It changes the order in which `_open_pr_step` serves open pull requests and needs a rule for an oldest one that is stuck (red checks, a resync, a conflict) so the others never wait behind it; that is a behaviour change to test on its own, not a safe addition here. Changed: `runner/cycle.py` (`_resolve_pr`, `resolve_merged`, `MERGES_RESOLVED`, `NO_MERGED`, `refill_lanes` `own`), `runner/__main__.py` (`--resolve-merges`, `lane_report`, `SILENT`, `refill` `own`), `.github/workflows/backup-runner.yml` (the new step; the chain step's refill), `tests/test_runner_merge_early.py` (new), `docs/architecture.md` section 12, `docs/decisions.md`, `docs/for-casey-review.md`, `kit/plan.lock`. No state field is added (`kit/state_schema.json` unchanged). Kind: harness change; independent Opus review before merge (its first round found the second refill start, the merge with D-3140, the untested `_earlier_pr` guard and the cleanup-task case, all fixed here). - **D-3157** Question (T339; INT-018, FEE-005, FEE-045; D-2330, D-2210, TD-JOB-17): how are a job's category and candidate job types stored, and what counts as narrowing? Choice: `jobs.job_facts` (`migrations/0164_jobs_job_facts.sql`), one row per change: `job_id` and a per-job `seq` (primary key), the catalog `category` code, `job_types` (a text array, at least one code, no null), `set_at` (the transaction's `now()`, as the plan's four-argument signature takes no time); the app role keeps the `jobs` schema default of SELECT and INSERT and loses UPDATE, DELETE and TRUNCATE. `jobs::api::record_job_facts(tx, job, category, job_types)` locks the `jobs.job` row (`FOR UPDATE`; `FactsError::NotFound` for no job), reads the latest row and applies the pure `narrow` rule: the set is compared as a set (sorted, repeats dropped, stored that way); a blank category, an empty set or a blank code is `Empty`; with a latest row, another category is `OtherCategory`, a code outside its set is `NotASubset`, the same set is `Recorded::Unchanged` and writes nothing; anything else appends `seq + 1` (`Recorded::Written`). The first call may carry any non-empty set. Refusals are a crate-local `FactsError` in `job_facts.rs`, not new `JobsError` variants, because `models.rs` is outside the task's files. Called outside a transaction the lock lasts one statement, so a racing write fails on the primary key (`Database`) rather than writing twice; callers pass their transaction. Kind: build. Owner approval: not needed. Source: `app/jobs/src/job_facts.rs`, `migrations/0164_jobs_job_facts.sql`, `tests/integration/tests/job_facts.rs`.

Choice: as D-3106 and D-3134 plan it. In `side`, after the existing records, each business gets a second job (`quoted_job`) and its page pick (the new `picked` helper, which the first pick now uses too, same calls); `app/server/tests/door_matrix/released_pick.rs` (`release_free`) appends the business's $0 `FreeFirstWin` ledger entry for that job, takes `payments::api::no_fee_release(conn, pick, (business, job))`, settles the pick to `free` with `picks::api::settle` (asserting `Moved`, as `release_sink::PickReleaser` does before minting), mints the proof with `askhava_server::release_minter()` over the homeowner's contact passed in from `door_matrix.rs`, and calls `picks::api::release` with `email_chosen` false and the masked pool built from the probe's own `pairs()`, asserting `Shown`. The submodule names no homeowner mark and `door_matrix.rs` names no `payments` item (TD-FEE-07 unchanged and passing); it is declared with `#[path = r"door_matrix/released_pick.rs"] mod released_pick;`, so Cargo builds no extra test target. `Fixtures` gains `released`; the new `ids_on(template, side)` gives the exact template `RELEASED_PAGE` (`/b/picks/{pick}`) the released pick and every other template the waiting pick, used by `probe_page` (own and the other side's, so the cross-business check compares picks of the same kind), `probe_link` and `probe_csrf`; `ids` and `fill` are unchanged. New case `td_sec_61_each_released_pick_opens_to_its_own_business_only`: `released_view` with each business owner's session proof (`session_minter()`) shows its own side's released pick and answers the other side's not found, and `ids_on` fills as stated. Every other case, judgement, actor and assertion is unchanged; `tests/security/door_cases.txt` unchanged. Kind: build (harness). Owner approval: not needed.
